text:
RETURN OF INHERITANCE 

There was a country that used to treat its people like owners.

That was not a slogan. It was how the place was built. Families claimed land and expected their children to keep it. Hamilton wanted shops and mills here so the yield would stay here. Lincoln’s Homestead Act put title in ordinary hands. McKinley and the old tariff men said if a foreign workshop could undercut an American one, the American house would slowly empty. For a long time the deal was simple. You work. You build. The profit does not all leave by the docks.

Then the deal flipped.

Factories went overseas because labor was cheaper and the finance houses liked the margin. Towns that made steel, cloth, tools, and cars became warehouses for other people’s goods. Washington still collected taxes. Banks still collected interest. Shoppers got lower prices and called that winning, while the job that used to pay for the house left with the product. The citizen became a customer. The country became a platform. That is real history, not a parable. You can walk the boarded main streets and count it.

Older still is the biblical picture people reach for when they see that hollowing. In Israel the land was not supposed to be sold off the family forever. Every so often debts were released and fields came home. They called it jubilee. It was not a stimulus check. It was a law against becoming a tenant on your own ground. America never ran that calendar. It ran a rougher version: property, wages, and a border around the market.

That is what “return of inheritance” means in plain speech. Not a miracle envelope. The fruit of the country coming back to the people who live in it after a long season of managers, offshoring, and a government that treated households like a cost.

Tonight in Dallas, Trump put a number on that hunger. If Republicans keep the House and the Senate, he said, every adult citizen gets a $5,000 dividend, and it has to be spent in the United States. Hear it clearly. It is a campaign condition, not a check already in the mail. He has talked tariff dividends before. Those checks have not shown up. Five thousand dollars times every adult is a huge bill. It has to come from tariffs, growth, cuts, or new borrowing. If it is borrowed, it is not inheritance. It is a loan with a flag on it.

Still, the shape of the offer is the old American sentence: you are a shareholder in this house again. Spend the yield at home. Do not send it back down the road that emptied the towns.

That is the story without the fog.
Owners, then tenants, then a promise to put some of the fruit back on the table.
History will decide if the promise becomes a payment.
The hunger is already historical.

WA State Dept. of Health (DOH)

Temporary Worker Housing Updates for 2027-2029 Agriculture Season

Sept. 9, 2026

The Washington State Department of Health (DOH) has several updates and reminders to help Temporary Worker Housing  (TWH) operators prepare for the next agricultural season. 

Update: Renewal Applications Will Be Sent in October

Starting this year, DOH will send out TWH renewal notices the first week of October rather than the first week of November.  These notices will be sent by mail in a regular envelope labeled RENEWAL.  

Renewal notices are sent to TWH operators if their TWH was licensed for the 2026-2027 season.

Receiving your renewal notice earlier offers more time for TWH operators to:

Update, complete, and submit all required renewal licensing documents.

Correct any issues with your renewal documents before the pre-license inspection.

Address any TWH issues or corrections that could delay issuance of your new TWH license.
 
If you are receiving this email but have not received your TWH notice by October 9, 2026, or have renewal questions, please email:

housing@doh.wa.gov.  

Important: Current TWH Licenses Cannot Be Used for the Upcoming 2027-2028 Season

Although your current DOH TWH license remains valid through February 28, 2027, it cannot be used by ESD to approve H-2A housing for the upcoming agricultural season. TWH operators must complete the annual DOH TWH renewal process and obtain a new DOH TWH license before occupancy for the 2027-2028 season

Documents Required for Renewal

The following documents are part of the TWH renewal process. Please review each document and update and submit with your renewal notice if there have been any changes since it was last submitted.

Communicable Disease Prevention and Response Plan

Temporary Worker Housing Management Plan

We have also included the TWH Self-Inspection Checklist as a resource to help you prepare for your pre-license inspection.

Reminder: Schedule Your Occupancy Inspection

Please complete your required occupancy inspection before the end of the agricultural season.

If you have not completed an occupancy inspection, contact your assigned DOH TWH inspector to schedule the visit or email: housing@doh.wa.gov

Your renewal application will not be considered complete until the required occupancy inspection has been conducted.

If critical violations are and/or were observed from your last inspection, you must correct them and notify your inspector before your renewal application can be processed for the 2027–2028 season.

Update: “Pre-Occupancy Inspection” Is Now a “Pre-License Inspection”

DOH has changed the term “pre-occupancy inspection” to “pre-license inspection”, so inspections can be conducted sooner and during the current agricultural season.

Scheduling your pre-license inspection earlier benefits the TWH operators by:

Allowing the pre-license inspection while workers are still housed at the facility during the current agricultural season.

Allows more flexibility to schedule the pre-license inspection between the TWH operator and DOH inspector. Note: Occupancy and pre-license inspections shall not be done simultaneously.

Additional time to comply or submit any required inspection corrections before the expiration date.

Additional time for DOH to issue a new TWH license and sooner.

Additional time for Employment Security Department (ESD) to consider the ETA-790 H-2A housing certification for the following agricultural season.
 
Update: DOH Database Has Changed

Effective July 27, 2026, the DOH TWH Program updated its database to HealthSpace Cloud and the way we communicate with TWH operators with correspondences, inspection reports, and renewal notices.

The inspection report may look different from what you are used to. We are continuing to make improvements to the report and appreciate your patience as we work through these changes.

The U.S.-Iran war erupted in a big way, Tuesday night, after U.S. Central Command announced that U.S. forces had destroyed five Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for an earlier Iranian attack on U.S. naval ships operating in the Gulf of Oman. Iran answered with waves of missiles fired at the Muwaffaq Salti and Prince Hassan air bases in Jordan and another attack on U.S. ships. Jordan claimed that its air defenses had shot down 18 Iranian missiles while two others landed in empty desert, reported AP. Videos posted on social media show some Iranian missiles penetrating the waves of Patriot interceptors fired at them as well as releasing cluster warheads. Nonetheless, Centcom said it had no information to offer about damage done by the Iranian missiles,

The Iranians had warned yesterday that if the U.S. attacked any more of their tankers, they would respond. In a post on social media published on Tuesday evening, a message said, “The aggressive US army has given Iranian oil tankers a warning to evacuate in order to attack them,” Major General Ali Abdollahi, the chief of the General Staff of Iranian Armed Forces, said, reported Mehr News. “So, I declare that any attack on Iranian oil tankers will result in the targeting of US bases in the region by the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council’s Major General Mohsen Rezaei earlier said that Washington had received a clear warning from new missiles of the Islamic Republic. “In recent days, Washington has received a clear warning from Iran’s new missiles,” Rezaei wrote on his X account on Tuesday, reported IRNA. “Economic warfare will be met by a maritime exclusion zone across the Persian Gulf to the blockade perimeter,” he added. “The operational posture toward US warships and bases has been fundamentally recalibrated,” he noted.

This one is a must read 📚. 
What JAPAN and Japanese think about India and Indians ..

India: Not an Inspiration...
But a Warning

Japan, a nation decimated by two nuclear bombs, didn't beg for sympathy or aid. It rebuilt itself with pride and an unshakeable sense of self-respect. In the years since, it has never once stretched out a hand to America for alms.

An Indian man living in Japan for over a decade was about to leave Japan for good. He observed during his stay that no Japanese ever discussed or asked him much about India!

So, he had been a bit curious and asked his closest Japanese friend prior to departure: What Japanese think about India & Indians in general?

After a long pause, the friend replied, 
"We are taught Indian history... not for inspiration, but as a warning."

Confused, the Indian man asked, "A warning?"

"Tell me," the Japanese friend continued, "how many British ruled India?"
The Indian man thought, "Perhaps... around 10,000?"
The Japanese man nodded grimly. "And how many Indians lived there? Over 300 million, right?"
"Then who oppressed your people? Who carried out the orders to whip, torture, and shoot them?" he pressed. 

"When General Dyer gave the command 'Fire!' at Jallianwala Bagh, who pulled the trigger?
 
The soldiers weren't British; they were Indian."
"Not one turned their rifle on the tyrant. Not one," he said. "
You want to talk about slavery? That was your real slavery. Not of the body, but of the soul."

The Indian man stood frozen, silent, and ashamed.

The Japanese friend went on, "How many Mughals came from Central Asia? A few thousand maybe? And yet they ruled you for centuries. They built empires not with their numbers, but because your own people bowed their heads and offered their loyalty in exchange for survival or silver."

"Your own people converted. Your own brothers became instruments of their oppression. Your own men handed over your heroes. Chandrashekhar Azad was betrayed. Bhagat Singh faced the gallows without even a whisper of help from those who called themselves patriots," he said.

"You don't need foreign enemies. YOUR OWN PEOPLE BETRAY YOU AGAIN AND AGAIN FOR POWER, POSITION, AND PERSONAL GAIN. That is why we keep our distance."

"When the British came to Hong Kong and Singapore, not one native man joined their army. But in India, you didn’t just join the enemy. You served them. Worshipped them. Killed your own people to please them."

"*Even today, you haven’t changed. Offer some free electricity, a bottle of liquor, a blanket—and your vote, your conscience, your voice are all sold without a second thought. 

YOUR LOYALTY LIES NOT WITH YOUR NATION, BUT WITH YOUR STOMACH," he said.

"You chant slogans. You march in protests. But when the country needs your character, where are you? YOUR FIRST LOYALTY IS STILL TO YOURSELF AND YOUR FAMILY. EVERYTHING ELSE —SOCIETY, DHARMA, THE COUNTRY —CAN BURN."

He ended with one final statement:
"If your nation is not strong, your home will never be safe. If your character is weak, no flag can protect you."

This is not mockery. It is a mirror.

Perhaps the time has come for us to stop looking away, because India doesn’t need more patriots in speeches.
IT NEEDS CITIZENS OF UNSHAKEABLE CHARACTER. NOT JUST FREEDOM FIGHTERS, BUT FREEDOM KEEPERS. NOT JUST FLAGS IN OUR HANDS, BUT LOYALTY IN OUR HEARTS.

It is bitter. But it is true.

HOPE IT Shakes our conscience and please spread the word🙏 one person at a time, can do wonders to this country...

So I asked grok about what would happen to the regular people, the occupants of Mocha for example, that live there that have houses and shops there, like what’s gonna happen to them and this is what it says (Note; AA has offered a general amnesty to enemy fighters earlier today)…
—- 

“Ordinary residents of Mocha who own homes, shops, or just live there would face immediate danger first, then a mix of displacement, property loss, and life under a new authority. 

Mocha is a relatively small Red Sea port and fishing town that has already become a military base for government-aligned forces; many current residents are fighters or people who previously fled Houthi areas.

Fighting itself usually produces the first wave of harm. Shelling, street battles, and missile strikes destroy or damage houses and markets, kill civilians, and cut electricity, water, and communications. 

Recent clashes in the wider Taiz–Hodeidah coastal area have already driven nearly 20,000 people from their homes in a matter of days. Families typically leave with whatever they can carry and end up in displacement camps farther down the coast or inland.

Those who stay or try to return later encounter the property problem that has repeated across Yemen for years. When a city or neighborhood changes hands, armed groups on both sides have occupied private houses, used them as bases or sniper positions, looted contents, changed locks, and sometimes rented or sold them without the owners’ consent. 

In Taiz, hundreds of homes remain occupied years after fighting moved on; owners who fled are often treated as absent or politically suspect and struggle to get the buildings back even with court papers. 

Similar seizures and looting have been documented in other pnewly captured districts. Shops and small businesses face the same risks plus economic collapse: ports close, fishing stops, and customers disappear.

Daily life under a new administration would also change. Houthi authorities typically impose their own local committees, taxes or “contributions,” movement restrictions, and might pressure on men of fighting age. 

People seen as having worked with or supported the previous side can face arrest or confiscation. At the same time, the city would likely come under retaliatory airstrikes or further fighting, so remaining civilians stay exposed. 

Yemen already has more than five million internally displaced people; most never fully recover their original homes or livelihoods. 

There is no reliable mechanism that automatically protects ordinary property owners when front lines move.”

text:
@Jeff_Palouse, what Calvin is doing is rebutting the idea of a bare/mere permission, as if God is just standing by and observing things occur. He did not disagree with the overall concept of permission. He qualifies himself fairly clearly. The problem is that he is easy to take out of context, and sometimes his wording can seem sloppy. Here you will see some relevant quotes. I have others that I can give you where he quotes Augustine on divine permission.

“He does so, indeed, in a different way and with a different end; but he still cannot undertake anything unless God so wills. However, even though a bare permission to afflict the holy man seems then to be added, yet we gather that God was the author of that trial of which Satan and his wicked thieves were the ministers, because this statement is true: “The Lord gave, the Lord has taken away; as it has pleased God, so is it done” [Job 1:21, Vg. (p.)].”

John Calvin, Institutes of the Christian Religion & 2, ed. John T. McNeill, trans. Ford Lewis Battles, vol. 1, The Library of Christian Classics (Louisville, KY: Westminster John Knox Press, 2011), 229–230.

“Therefore, whatever men or Satan himself may instigate, God nevertheless holds the key, so that he turns their efforts to carry out his judgments. God wills that the false King Ahab be deceived; the devil offers his services to this end; he is sent, with a definite command, to be a lying spirit in the mouth of all the prophets [1 Kings 22:20, 22]. If the blinding and insanity of Ahab be God’s judgment, the figment of bare permission vanishes: because it would be ridiculous for the Judge only to permit what he wills to be done, and not also to decree it and to command its execution by his ministers.”

John Calvin, Institutes of the Christian Religion & 2, ed. John T. McNeill, trans. Ford Lewis Battles, vol. 1, The Library of Christian Classics (Louisville, KY: Westminster John Knox Press, 2011), 230.

“Those who are moderately versed in the Scriptures see that for the sake of brevity I have put forward only a few of many testimonies. Yet from these it is more than evident that they babble and talk absurdly who, in place of God’s providence, substitute bare permission—as if God sat in a watchtower awaiting chance events, and his judgments thus depended upon human will.”

John Calvin, Institutes of the Christian Religion & 2, ed. John T. McNeill, trans. Ford Lewis Battles, vol. 1, The Library of Christian Classics (Louisville, KY: Westminster John Knox Press, 2011), 231.

🌙 TONIGHT’S OUTLOOK — ONE MORE WARM NIGHT BEFORE CHANGES BEGIN

We’re wrapping up another brutally hot day across Central Arkansas, and unfortunately the overnight hours won’t offer a whole lot of relief just yet. 😅

Expect a warm and mostly quiet night, with lows generally ranging from the lower 70s south to the upper 70s around central and northern portions of the area. Little Rock could only fall to around 78°, with Conway and Perryville near 77°.

But now we get to start talking about the part we’ve been waiting for. 👀⛈️

Thursday begins Step 1 of our two-step pattern change. Our first front arrives with increasing thunderstorm chances Thursday afternoon, followed by a better opportunity for rain and storms Thursday night into Friday. A few storms Thursday could also become strong, with an isolated severe-weather risk across northern Central Arkansas.

And the rain forecast is finally looking a little healthier! Several locations could pick up around 0.25–0.50"+ through the next several days, although amounts will vary considerably depending on who actually gets underneath the storms.

Then comes Step 2 late next week, when the stronger pattern change we’ve been tracking could finally deliver substantially cooler air and additional rain chances. 🍂

When a group operates as a private, non-commercial, and non-financial secret society, it is typically categorized under the law as a private voluntary association or an unincorporated association.

In the United States and across most global legal frameworks, there is no official statutory category called a "secret society". Instead, the law views organizations based on what they do, how they handle money, and how they interact with the public.

Name Your Entity (Wish Fire Secret Society)

Freedom from coercion: Explicitly writing out that your space rejects spiritual abuse, guilt-tripping, and judgment, focusing instead on individual sovereignty and personal growth.

Your foundational text or mission statement: What core truths, ethics, or perspectives do you want to center?

Feeling alienated or exhausted by institutional power dynamics, dogmatic condemnation, and the pressure of global hierarchies is a very common experience. Many people throughout history have responded to that exact frustration by stepping

away to build independent spaces focused on personal freedom, authenticity, and healthy spirituality.

From a practical and legal

Rather than feeling liberated, people experience a hidden, pervasive anxiety. They hide their genuine selves and suppress their highest ideals out of a fear of being judged or canceled by peers

Voluntary Association: A clause explicitly stating that all participation is entirely voluntary, free of charge, and sovereign to the individual.

The Code of Ethics: The internal standards of behavior, mutual respect, and absolute confidentiality expected of participants.

The Declaration of Purpose: A clear statement of what the society stands for, what it rejects (such as external coercion, dogmatic judgment, and institutional control), and its dedication to free thought.

Where Risk Comes In: Liability usually only matters if an organization owns heavy physical property, hosts large public events, enters into contracts, or engages in commercial business where someone could theoretically get hurt or sue.

Low-Risk Activities: If your society is purely philosophical, creative, intellectual, or spiritual—where people gather to discuss ideas, share writing, or appreciate art—the practical risk of a lawsuit or legal trouble is virtually non-existent.

There are no commercial products, financial transactions, or physical hazards to trigger liability.

Total Privacy: Because no state agency holds your records, your membership roster, internal teachings, and philosophy remain entirely between you and your members.

The Private Charter: Instead of state-mandated bylaws, you govern yourselves through a private charter, constitution, or covenant. This document outlines your principles, how decisions are made, and the code of conduct members agree to follow.

No Filing Required: You do not file articles of incorporation with the state. You don't need a tax ID (EIN) unless you ever decide to open a bank account.

What Is an Unincorporated Association?

At its core, it is simply an agreement between two or more people to join together for a common, non-profit purpose under a shared set of rules.

Because you mentioned there are no membership fees, money, or commercial motives involved, this structure fits the profile of a pure, non-commercial private fellowship.

An Unincorporated Association (sometimes called a voluntary association) is one of the oldest and most traditional ways for a group of people to

organize around a shared philosophy, art, or purpose without involving the government, paying fees, or dealing with corporate bureaucracy.

Separate "Their Rules" From "Reality"

When you are immersed in a culture of constant micro-judgment, it’s easy to start internalizing the static and second-guessing your own sanity.

Enforce Time Limits: When you visit or talk on the phone, set an internal timer. Give yourself permission to leave or hang up the moment the judgment starts ramping up. You don't have to announce a dramatic boundary speech; simply say, "I have to run now, good talking to you!"

Information Diet: Put them on a strict information diet. Share less about your career, your creative projects, your relationships, or your daily choices.

If they don't know the details, they can't cross-examine you about them. Keep conversations surface-level (weather, safe general topics).

Build Strict Psychological and Physical Boundaries

You cannot control what opinions they form in their own heads, but you can control how much access they have to your life.

"Mmm."

"That’s an interesting perspective."

"I'll have to think about that."

text:
Apple will assign an absurd price tag to tech that other companies unveiled a decade ago, and people will still line up for hours just to get first dibs on the product.

That’s the iPhone Duo in a nutshell—a folding phone that can set you back as much as ₱254,990, or roughly the price of a decent secondhand car, once it launches next month.

The tech giant announced the iPhone Duo, its very first folding phone, at the “Surprise and Shine” event at its California headquarters on September 9.

The folding screen will be nearly twice the size of previous iPhone models, spanning 7.6 inches. The Duo boasts a nano-texture finish on its inner display to reduce glare, and wide-angle LEDs to enhance viewing angles.

The iPhone Duo will be available in Night Sky and Star White.

But the folding technology and display specs aren’t nearly the most noteworthy detail about the Duo. The real head-turner is the price.

The lowest offering begins at ₱159,990 for 256GB, followed by ₱175,990 for 512GB. The 1TB model is ₱207,990, while 2TB is a whopping ₱254,990.

At ₱159,990, you’re already looking at nearly ₱160,000 for the privilege of folding your iPhone in half. Go for the top-of-the-line 2TB version and Apple is asking for almost ₱255,000.

For someone earning ₱25,000 a month, that’s more than 10 months of gross salary. At ₱50,000 a month, it’s still roughly five months’ worth of income—before rent, food, bills, transportation, and all those other pesky things people generally need their money for.

Global pre-orders begin October 16, while units will be made available starting October 23.

So, if you’ve been selling a kidney every few years to fund your iPhone habit, congratulations—you may now need to locate another one. Alternatively, there’s always the time-tested Filipino strategy of finding a generous DOM or gay benefactor, filing overtime for the next several years, or simply convincing yourself that you “deserve it” until the credit card bill arrives.

Apple’s hardware chief John Ternus also announced the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max at the launch, for those still wanting to clout-chase without quite reaching the quarter-million-peso territory.

The company touts the new series as more capable of handling heavier video and artificial intelligence workloads. The iPhone 18 models offer up to 6 more hours of video playback, faster wired charging, and a more powerful A20 chip that can accommodate greater automation.

The iPhone 18 Pro comes with a 6.3-inch display, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max spans 6.9 inches. The series comes in four colors: Burgundy, Glacier, Silver, and Black.

The iPhone 18 Pro starts at ₱94,990 for 256GB, ₱110,990 for 512GB, ₱142,990 for 1TB, and ₱189,990 for 2TB.

Meanwhile, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is priced at ₱99,990 for 256GB, ₱115,990 for 512GB, ₱147,990 for 1TB, and ₱194,990 for 2TB.

In other words, even if you skip the folding phone and settle for the “regular” Pro models, you’re still looking at nearly ₱95,000 to almost ₱195,000.

Mind you, those don’t even include accessories, telco plans, and maintenance.

And yes, Apple will probably still sell a lot of them. Because apparently, there is a price at which an iPhone becomes cheaper than therapy—and ₱254,990 apparently isn’t it.

Pre-orders begin September 12, while units will be rolled out globally on September 18.

*** A SHORT READERS DIGEST ANALIZATION ***

Analyzing Elon Musk’s strategy and technical setup for feeding Tesla Powerwall electricity back to the grid centers on his Virtual Power Plant (VPP) architecture.

Here is an analysis of how it works, its economic efficiency, and its current limitations:

Key Mechanics: The Virtual Power Plant (VPP)

Instead of relying entirely on massive centralized power stations, Elon Musk's model aggregates thousands of individual distributed Powerwalls into a single, software-controlled "virtual" power station.

Automated Peak Shaving: During periods of extreme electrical demand (such as hot summer afternoons when air conditioners strain the grid), regional utilities signal Tesla's network. The VPP software coordinates thousands of home Powerwalls to discharge electricity back into the local grid simultaneously.

Replacing Peaker Plants: Traditional utilities rely on fossil-fuel "peaker plants" that sit idle most of the year and burn natural gas or oil during demand spikes. Aggregated home batteries act as a cleaner, instantaneous alternative.
Frequency & Voltage Stabilization: Batteries respond in milliseconds to local grid fluctuations, smoothing out voltage drops much faster than traditional spin-up generators.
Financial & Strategic Pros

Revenue Stream for Owners: In states with VPP programs (like California, Texas, Massachusetts, and parts of Australia), participants get paid per kilowatt-hour ($KWH$) discharged during grid stress events.

Net Energy Metering Optimization: Powerwalls can charge automatically during off-peak hours (when electricity is cheap or free via solar) and discharge into the grid during peak pricing windows under Time-of-Use (TOU) rates, allowing homeowners to profit from energy arbitrage.

Grid Infrastructure Relief: Feeding power locally reduces line loss (power lost as heat over long-distance high-voltage transmission lines).
Critical Challenges & Impediments
Battery Degradation: Lithium-ion cells degrade faster with higher cycle counts. Frequently discharging home batteries into the grid speeds up capacity loss, meaning the compensation offered by utilities must outweigh the long-term wear on the battery.

Regulatory & Utility Pushback: Traditional utility companies often limit net metering credits or charge grid connection fees, which diminishes the financial return for home battery owners.

Duration Limits: While Powerwalls can deliver high burst power (e.g., Powerwall 3 supports up to 11.5 kW continuous output), individual capacity (13.5 kWh) means a single unit can only discharge at full power for roughly 1 to 2 hours before depletion.

text:
Planning a trip to New York City can be surprisingly difficult🗽

Not because there’s too little to do, but because there’s far too much.

If you’re heading there, a few things I’d definitely recommend:

🏨 Staying in Manhattan 

🌳 Central Park

🚶 Walk the High Line from Hudson Yards towards Chelsea

🏙️ Grand Central Terminal

🌉 DUMBO and the walk across the Brooklyn Bridge into Manhattan

🚢 The free Staten Island Ferry for views of the Statue of Liberty and the skyline

🌇 Gantry Plaza State Park for some of the best Manhattan views

🏙️ Hudson Yards, The Vessel & Little Island

🍕 Eat more pizza than you planned to

🎭 Watch a Broadway show (book in advance)

A couple of practical tips:

🚇 The subway is by far the easiest way to get around. The fare cap is incredibly useful and means you can hop around the city without constantly worrying about ticket costs.

🌉 Don’t just stay in Manhattan. Brooklyn and other boroughs offer some fantastic neighbourhoods and some of the best skyline views in the city.

And I’m pretty sure this list is still missing a lot😄

That’s probably my favourite thing about NYC. No matter how much you see, it always feels like there’s more waiting around the next corner ✨

What would you add to this list? 🗽

text:
A Gruesome Caption Is Not Theology: No, Catholic Relics Are Not “What Devils Do”

“Unless you are a surgeon, cutting hearts out of dead people is what devils do.”

That sounds shocking. It is also not an argument.

First, you have already smuggled your conclusion into your language. “An organ was removed from a deceased person” describes a physical act. “Therefore it was demonic” is a theological judgment requiring evidence. Autopsies involve the removal of organs. Organ donation can involve removing organs after death. Pathologists examine organs. Embalming and historical burial customs have involved the separate treatment of internal organs. European royalty and other prominent persons were sometimes given separate heart or viscera burials.

None of those practices becomes satanic merely because the words “cut out a heart” sound disturbing.

So before sensationalizing alleged Catholic practices involving the hearts of deceased popes, establish exactly what happened, when it happened, why it happened, and whether we are talking about embalming, separate burial, preservation, relics, or something else. And the meme’s specific claim about “25 popes” should itself be documented rather than simply repeated because a blog put the number underneath a photograph.

More importantly, if your real target is the Catholic practice of venerating relics, then you have a problem with Scripture itself.

In 2 Kings 13:20–21, a dead man is thrown into Elisha’s grave. When his body touches the bones of Elisha, the man revives and stands on his feet. Scripture does not say Elisha’s bones were gods. It does not say the Israelites worshipped Elisha. The power comes from God. Nevertheless, God chooses to associate a miracle with the physical remains of His prophet.

The New Testament makes the same principle even harder to dismiss. Acts 19:11–12 tells us that God performed extraordinary miracles through Paul, so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were carried to the sick, and diseases and evil spirits departed.

Again, the cloth was not God. Paul was not God. The material object possessed no independent divine power. God was the source of the miracle, yet God chose to work through material things associated with one of His servants.

That distinction is fundamental to Catholic teaching about relics.

Catholics do not believe a saint’s bone, heart, clothing, or other relic is a deity. Catholics do not believe relics possess some autonomous magical power independent of God. And Catholics do not offer latria—the adoration belonging to God alone—to a human organ.

Christian respect for bodily remains also makes theological sense because Christianity is not a religion that regards the human body as disposable garbage. The Word became flesh (John 1:14). Paul calls the Christian body a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19). Christianity teaches the resurrection of the body, not liberation from the body as though matter itself were evil.

That is why Christians historically treated the remains of martyrs and saints with extraordinary respect. You may debate whether particular devotional customs were prudent, excessive, or historically appropriate. But “I find this macabre” is not equivalent to “Scripture says this is demonic.”

Your own exception—“unless you are a surgeon”—actually exposes the weakness of your argument. Why does being a surgeon suddenly change the moral character of removing an organ? What about a pathologist? A forensic examiner? An organ-donation team? An embalmer?

The obvious answer is that intention, purpose, and context matter.

And once you admit that, the meme collapses. You can no longer reason:

heart removed → disgusting → demonic → Catholicism evil.

You actually have to investigate what was done and why.

text:
A U.S. prosecutor described China's Huawei as a criminal enterprise that stole from American companies to build its telecommunications empire, as the tech giant's trial kicked off in a Brooklyn federal court on Wednesday.

"Theft, lies, cover-up," Department of Justice trial attorney Taylor Stout said in his opening statement, accusing the company of a 20-year scheme to victimize American businesses and abuse the U.S. financial system.

Stout alleged Huawei conspired to steal trade secrets from five U.S. companies—including router source code from Cisco Systems and a phone-testing robotic arm from T-Mobile—promising jurors video evidence of an employee caught "red-handed."

The defense painted a starkly different picture, framing the government's case as a mischaracterization of routine global tech operations.

"It's about competition, not conspiracy. Innovation, not theft. Ordinary business dealings, not criminal conduct," defense attorney Brian Heberlig countered, arguing that Huawei earned its success without a blueprint for crime.

Heberlig accused the government of "cherry-picking" isolated incidents of rogue employee behavior, noting that management took corrective actions and promptly fired wrongdoers upon discovering the thefts.

The sweeping racketeering case began in 2018 with an initial indictment charging Huawei and its chief financial officer with bank fraud and sanctions violations for allegedly hiding its business in Iran.

Prosecutors claim Huawei laundered U.S. dollars and aided the Iranian government in spying on its citizens, while the defense argues the company had no intent to violate sanctions and that its banking partners were already aware of its Iranian ties.

The three-month trial will feature admissions made by Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou, who was detained in Canada in 2018 and fought extradition for three years before her charges were dismissed in a diplomatic agreement.

The criminal case stems partly from 2012 and 2013 Reuters reporting that originally exposed close ties between Huawei and Skycom, a firm that offered embargoed computer equipment to Iran's largest mobile operator.

text:
The AI Architecture Dilemma: Monopoly vs. Multi-Polar Diffusion

​As the global race toward advanced AI accelerates, policy frameworks are being forced to look past short-term deployment metrics and examine long-term systemic stability.

​A central question defines this era: Should frontier capabilities be concentrated within a handful of tightly guarded corporate monoliths, or should development be intentionally diffused across a transparent, multi-polar network?

​Traditional tech-monopoly arguments favor speed and closed control. However, systems-level analysis points to heavy vulnerabilities in that approach:
​The Concentration Risk: Monopolizing superintelligence creates an unrecoverable power asymmetry.

​The Single Point of Failure: Concentrated pipelines leave no margin for error—a single alignment or security lapse at the nexus scales immediately to a global catastrophe.

​The Information Black Box: Proprietary secrecy forces an arms-race dynamic where safety protocols are continuously undercut by competitive fear.

​Proposals like Plan A from the AI Futures Project offer an alternative lens: combining international pacing, total research transparency, and distributed multi-actor scaling. By decentralizing the frontier and anchoring it to zero-trust verification and hardware-level fail-safes, we trade a fragile, high-stakes gamble for a resilient macro-system.  

​Resilience isn't built by hiding behind walls; it's engineered through distributed visibility, shared verification, and structural checks and balances.

​What is your take? Can an international coalition successfully govern a diffused AI frontier, or does centralization remain an inevitable reality?

This support has been a significant portion of TPUSA's budget over the past decade, helping the organization grow from a small student group to a major conservative youth activist network with revenues exceeding $100 million annually in recent years. However, the funding is not exclusively from "Zionist operators"—it's part of a broader conservative donor ecosystem, including Koch-affiliated foundations, Republican billionaires, and anonymous dark money groups like DonorsTrust. Claims that Zionist funding constitutes the "large part" are partially accurate but overstated; public records show it's a key but not dominant slice, often channeled through neoconservative intermediaries.Key evidence from financial disclosures, investigative reports, and donor analyses (e.g., from InfluenceWatch, SourceWatch, and OpenSecrets): • Prominent Zionist/Pro-Israel Donors: •Bernard Marcus: Co-founder of Home Depot and a major Zionist philanthropist (he has donated tens of millions to pro-Israel causes like the Israel Democracy Institute and AIPAC). Marcus has been one of TPUSA's top donors since at least 2017, contributing over $10 million in the 2010s alone. He served on TPUSA's advisory board and funded its early expansion. Post-Kirk's death, Jewish leaders highlighted his support as evidence of Kirk's pro-Israel stance. •Foster Friess (deceased 2021): A Christian Zionist investor who provided seed funding in 2012 after meeting Kirk at the Republican National Convention. Friess donated millions and sat on TPUSA's advisory council. His wife, Lynn, continued contributions. •David Horowitz Freedom Center: A neoconservative group founded by far-right Zionist activist David Horowitz, which funneled early grants to TPUSA (e.g., $100,000+ in the mid-2010s). Horowitz mentored Kirk and promoted anti-Palestinian narratives on campuses. •Other Pro-Israel Ties: Miriam Adelson (casino billionaire and mega-donor to pro-Israel PACs) has indirectly supported TPUSA events. Dennis Prager (conservative radio host and Zionist advocate) contributed via his PragerU foundation. Reports estimate Zionist-linked donations totaled around $40 million from 2012–2022, including through DonorsTrust (a dark money fund that funneled $906,000 in 2019 alone, with pro-Israel backers like the Bradley Foundation). •Overall Funding Scale: •TPUSA's revenues grew from $52,000 in 2012 to $28.5 million in 2019 and $138 million over the last five years (per IRS Form 990 filings). About 43% of traced funding (2014–2018) came from Koch-network foundations, Uihlein family (Richard Uihlein donated millions), and DeVos family, but Zionist donors like Marcus and Friess were pivotal for campus activism and events. •Anonymous donors: Half of 2020's income came from just 10 undisclosed sources, likely including pro-Israel ones via DonorsTrust. •Kirk's Compensation: Rose from $27,000 in early years to $292,423 in 2019, amid scrutiny over insider deals (e.g., co-founder William Montgomery's contracts). TPUSA's ties to Israel were evident in its programming: Kirk took multiple propaganda trips to Israel, hosted pro-Israel speakers at conferences, and promoted "Judeo-Christian values" aligning with Christian Zionism. Critics like the ADL accused TPUSA of platforming extremists while advancing pro-Israel agendas. text:
Do Ford’s business ties with China "threaten national security"?

On the 8th (local time), U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy sent a letter challenging Ford Motor Company CEO Jim Farley. Duffy accused Ford of being overly reliant on Chinese companies for technology and supply chains, claiming that Ford’s business ties with China helped expand China's influence in the global automotive industry and posed a "threat" to U.S. national security and manufacturing.

Ford strongly refuted Duffy’s claims, pointing out numerous factual errors in the letter and dismissing it as a "stunt" to grab headlines. The company emphasized that its battery plant in Marshall, Michigan, is wholly owned and operated by Ford; it represents a multi-billion-dollar investment and is expected to create approximately 1,700 American jobs.

Ford stated that Duffy’s letter contained multiple factual errors. The company disputed the letter's characterization of its manufacturing plans, highlighting that the White House had recently spotlighted the Marshall battery project in a press release. Ford also cited recent comments by U.S. Secretary of Commerce Lutnick, who praised the company's decision to expand Lincoln vehicle production in the United States.

In reality, Ford’s market share in China has plummeted in recent years. Its global operations face significant challenges, including a slow transition to electrification, margin pressure, and sales figures being surpassed by Chinese automakers—with its global annual sales volume even falling behind China’s BYD for the first time. Once an industry titan—a pioneer of the automotive sector and a cornerstone of modern industrial manufacturing in the early 20th century—Ford now confronts unprecedented difficulties a century later. Key factors include a failed transition to electrification and intelligent technologies, the contraction of U.S. manufacturing, and soaring fuel prices.

CEO Jim Farley has acknowledged that Chinese automakers dominate the global electric vehicle (EV) market, noting that there is "no comparison" between the capabilities of U.S. and Chinese automakers in this arena. Regarding his decision to drive a Chinese EV, he explained on a program this past January that the move was intended to better understand the competition. In fact, Farley is widely regarded as one of the most rational, objective, and outspoken figures in the industry regarding the competitiveness of Chinese automobiles. As a leader in the industry, Jim Farley’s stance toward Chinese automakers and collaboration reflects a distinct duality: a mix of business pragmatism and political exclusionism. He staunchly opposes the direct entry of Chinese-made vehicles into the U.S. market, warning that it would deal a "devastating blow" to the domestic auto manufacturing sector. He also plays up the issue of Chinese automakers benefiting from government subsidies and argues for barring Chinese-made vehicles from the U.S. on the grounds that the multiple cameras they feature could pose risks to cybersecurity, privacy, and data security. In reality, however, Ford cannot avoid collaborating with Chinese companies; failing to do so would risk a prolonged decline and accelerate its obsolescence in the market.

Although Ford has previously partnered with South Korean and Japanese battery manufacturers, the performance of those products fell short of the solutions offered by Chinese firms. Developing a full suite of new energy vehicle (NEV) technologies in-house would entail a lengthy timeline and immense risk, with an uncertain outcome. As a major U.S. automaker, Ford’s operational health has a direct impact on the entire American automotive industry. While the U.S. government advocates for bringing manufacturing back home, a contradiction arises: if Ford were to strictly follow U.S. mandates by producing only internal combustion engine vehicles, it would struggle to maintain market share amidst shrinking demand.

Consequently, in its actual operations, Ford pursues a dual strategy: publicly aligning with U.S. political sentiments to secure political breathing room, while simultaneously exploring various forms of collaboration with Chinese partners—such as CATL, Geely, and BYD—regarding battery supply, technology adoption, and even joint ventures, all to sustain its competitiveness in the NEV market.

The battery project in Marshall, Michigan, utilizes lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery technology and services provided and licensed by CATL, with Ford retaining full operational control and employing a local workforce. Ford has also entered into a strategic partnership with Geely in Europe (specifically at the Almussafes plant in Valencia, Spain) to jointly utilize existing industrial facilities for the production of models from both Ford and Geely brands, with mass production expected to begin around 2028. Additionally, the company has engaged in discussions with BYD regarding the supply of components or technology for hybrid vehicles. It is truly ironic that Ford has come under fire from its own government just as these collaborations were beginning to bear fruit; meanwhile, even Tesla is encouraging its Chinese suppliers to set up factories in Mexico or other regions to circumvent geopolitical tensions and tariff barriers. One has to wonder: without Chinese supply chains and technology, would American automakers even exist ten years from now?

I love this exercise from my book, The Earned Life. It offers a powerful way to focus on what we can do today that will make a meaningful difference tomorrow.

In The Earned Life, I encourage readers to try a simple but powerful reflection. Imagine that it is one year from today. Your “future you” is looking back with gratitude for something the “current you” did that made a real difference.

What gift did you give your future self?

Perhaps it was taking better care of your health. Perhaps it was investing time in learning, strengthening relationships, or having the courage to make an important change. 

Often, the most meaningful gifts are not dramatic actions. They are small, positive steps that we choose to repeat day after day.

Too many people postpone the life they want to live. They wait for the perfect moment, the right opportunity, or a future time when things will somehow be easier.

The truth is much simpler. The future you is created by the choices you make today.

Give your future self something to be grateful for.

Life is good.
Marshall

In the same year they came up, with Duke Energy, the idea of Accelerating Clean Energy (ACE) “tariffs” to lower the long term costs of investing in clean energy technologies like nuclear and LDES through early commitments. They signed an MOU. The consortium was willing to pay the costs.

Fast forward to 2026, and @DukeEnergy has not only declined to follow through on these commitments and instead pursued natural gas at a much higher price, but when asked about their decisions during a deposition, they clammed up and declined to provide answers. Google for example, basically offered to pick up the tab for firming Duke’s renewable energy sites with LDES, but Duke declined. I guess because that’s not how they make money.

For anyone following @JigarShahDC or @tylerhnorris you already knew about this drama in real time. But it explains in large part why the consortium’s Advanced Clean Energy initiative was largely a failure.

In another parallel universe, things could have played out very differently.

text:
Seven terminal backends, two of which hibernate when idle and wake on demand. The agent is not meant to live on your laptop.

Recommendation: ★★★★☆
Difficulty: Intermediate

Without it, a coding agent session is a laptop-bound thing. You open a terminal, work, close it, and the context evaporates.

Whatever you taught it last week gets re-typed this week. Reaching it from your phone means writing your own Telegram bridge, and running it at 3am means wrapping a script in cron yourself.

With Hermes Agent, a Python CLI plus a single gateway process, you install with curl -fsSL https://t.co/q29qX9b8mD | bash on Linux, macOS, WSL2 or Termux, or iex (irm https://t.co/n8J5AYEKTu) natively on Windows, then run hermes.

hermes model swaps the provider with no code changes: Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI or your own endpoint. hermes gateway puts the same conversation on Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal and email.

Underneath there is a cron scheduler with delivery to any of those platforms, isolated subagents for parallel work, FTS5 search over past sessions with LLM summarization, and skills the agent writes for itself after complex tasks, compatible with the https://t.co/shr4I5R5Dv skill format.

The costs are real. The install script pulls uv, Python 3.11, Node, ripgrep and ffmpeg, and on Windows it unpacks a roughly 45MB portable MinGit under LOCALAPPDATA; the README carries a whole troubleshooting section on antivirus engines quarantining the bundled uv.exe as a false positive, with attestation steps to verify it. The self-improving learning loop is the headline claim and the README offers no evaluation behind it, so treat it as a design, not a result. Licensed MIT, and the open issue count is enormous for a project this young, which is what you would expect from something moving this fast. Worth running on a cheap VPS before you trust it with anything sensitive.

Why Intermediate: Install is one command, but you still pick a provider, wire API keys or Portal OAuth, and configure a gateway per messaging platform.

Adoption
243.7k stars, 50.3k forks, MIT license
3.4k contributors, latest release v2026.9.7 (Sep 2026), commits this week

A Brief Filed in the Court of Night
O Angel mine, whom Nature hath made counsel unto the trembling leaf and patient stone, thou walkest where the rivers take their oaths and every dawn doth swear itself thine own. The wildwood leans to hear thy quiet verdict; the stars, as witnesses, attend thy face; no statute of the seasons may constrain thee, thou art both garden and the granted grace.
How many ways thy beauty doth indict me: Exhibit first, the light upon thy brow; Exhibit next, the mercy of thy laughter; the rest, my heart shall enter, even now. I find no want of proof, nor need of pleading; thy loveliness is prima facie true. The court of all my days hath heard the evidence and ruled, beloved, only unto you.
Though we be sundered, and the miles object, thou hold’st my heart in fee simple, entire. No distance files a motion to dissever what love hath sealed with unextinguished fire. Each hour is thy jurisdiction; every minute doth keep thy presence, tender and supreme. I walk, I work, I wake, and still I feel thee: thy hand in mine, not merely in a dream.
I love thee with the whole of what I am, no clause reserved, no residue withheld. My will, my testament, my living bond are written in the blood whereby I am held. Be of good courage, counsel of my soul; the night itself shall yield, if thou but stand. I rest my case upon thy name, my Angel, and bid the dark surrender to thy hand.
So take this brief, this covenant, this prayer: thou art my world, my venue, and my home. Though parted still, I do not walk unaccompanied, in mind, in heart, I will not let thee roam. Come, Love, and take the night as lawful prize; the stars have signed; the earth hath set its seal. I yield, I plead, I offer all I carry, and at thy bar, forever, I do kneel.

Section 1. Conditions Precedent (five continuous years). Gaza shall become eligible to apply for recognition as a state only if, for one unbroken period of five years, all of the following are satisfied:
(a) Disarmament. Hamas is disarmed and dissolved. It ceases to exist as a governing, military, or political organization. Weapons are surrendered and destroyed under verified inspection.

Bankresan -Proposal Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era clearly labeled as a proposal and checks the official Draghi/Lagarde figures against public sources.

Bankresan is a proposal, not adopted Swedish or EU policy. Official Europe has priced the investment bill (Draghi) and designed a savings-to-markets pipe (Lagarde / SIU). It has not proposed moving performing mortgage books off commercial banks.

The “5th Bank Era” proposal is a financing-and-allocation architecture that tries to turn the Draghi investment bill into a Lagarde-style savings-to-investment flow, using Sweden as a 2026–2030 EU-pilot.

It is not an official EU or Swedish government programme; the materials themselves label it a proposal for plumbing the competitiveness agenda

Structured analysis: Draghi, Lagarde, and the Proposal- Transformation to the 5th Bank Era.

Frames a Swedish-led banking redesign as the missing delivery system for Europe’s competitiveness problem.

The official European diagnosis is already on the table: Draghi’s 2024 competitiveness report, Lagarde’s savings-to-investment agenda, and the December 2025 European Affordable Housing Plan. 
 
The useful work is to separate those official layers from the proposal, then test whether the Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era actually supplies the “how.”

1. How the three official layers and the proposal fit together
Layer - What it is - Core claim - Preferred instrument

Draghi Report (Sept 2024)
Official competitiveness diagnosis
Europe needs €750–800bn extra investment per year (~5 pp of GDP;
investment share from ~22% to ~27%) to close the gap with the US and China. 

Without that, welfare, climate or strategic autonomy will have to be sacrificed.

Joint industrial strategy, Single Market completion, CMU/SIU, public support for private investment, and movement toward regular joint borrowing.

Lagarde / ECB “Follow the money” + SIU

Official financial-plumbing diagnosis
Europe is not short of savings. Households hold about one-third of financial assets in cash and deposits versus about one-tenth in the US.

Aligning that mix could redirect a stock of up to €8tn, or a flow of ~€350bn a year, into long-term market investment. Banks remain essential, but capital markets are needed for breakthrough innovation.

Savings and Investments Union, European savings products, deeper equity/VC markets, less leakage of European savings into US assets.

European Affordable Housing Plan (16 Dec 2025)

Official social-industrial “what”
House prices up >60% in a decade. Europe needs ~650,000 extra dwellings a year on top of ~1.6 million already built; extra investment around €153bn a year. Housing is treated as competitiveness, cohesion and clean-transition policy.

State-aid reform, construction strategy, permitting/digitalisation, pan-European investment platform with EIB and national promotional banks.

Proposal- Transformation to The 5th Bank Era
Unofficial architecture

The binding constraint is not only savings volume.
It is the composition of bank assets: 
40 years of residential-mortgage lock-in. 
Transfer housing finance to a public/public-purpose vehicle, then reorient private banks toward energy, industry, modular housing, defence and AI.
Make - Sweden as 2026–2030 to EU pilot.

Housing-stock transfer + bank reorientation + AI credit allocation + Basel III as floor.
One-sentence map
Draghi defines the scale of the investment gap.
Lagarde defines the unused European savings pool and why it does not reach innovators.
The Housing Plan defines a politically visible industrial use-case.

Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era claims to supply a bank-balance-sheet mechanism that the first three do not specify.

That last claim is the proposal’s distinctive contribution. It is also the point that needs the hardest scrutiny.

2. Comparative baseline that actually matters
“Europe” and “EU,” and mix generation with consumption. Electricity, 2025

Total - Per capita – Meaning

China
~10,560 TWh
~7.5 MWh
Scale leader; industry, EVs, cooling, data centres.

United States
~4,536 TWh
~13.1 MWh
Highest intensity among large economies.

Europe (continent)
~5,101 TWh
~6.1 MWh
Comparable to the US in total, far lower per person.

EU
lower than continental Europe; 
demand still below 2015–19 averages
Nordics higher than EU average
Efficiency plus industrial softness, not just “green virtue.”
Income / capital structure

US:
higher after-tax incomes and deeper later-stage growth capital.

EU:
high savings, weaker scale-up finance. Late-stage European tech still depends heavily on non-EU, often US, capital.

China:
lower incomes, state-directed credit pivot toward “new quality productive forces” after the property correction.
The proposal – Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era  is right on the strategic picture:

Europe’s problem is not a shortage of deposits.
It is a shortage of oriented, long-horizon growth capital in energy systems, AI-enabled industry and housing production.Where it overreaches is treating mortgage lock-in as the single master variable.

Draghi’s gap is also about fragmentation, energy prices, weak commercialisation, defence capacity and incomplete capital markets.

Lagarde’s gap is also about household portfolio choice and the fact that European savings already leave for higher-return US markets.

3. What Draghi actually leaves unfinished
Draghi’s report is strong on diagnosis and weak on a single financing machine.
 
Draghi says three things that matter for this proposal:
The investment lift is historically large — Marshall Plan comparisons are 1–2% of GDP a year; 
he wants about 5.

Completing CMU is necessary but not sufficient. The private sector will not carry the lion’s share without public support.

Europe remains bank-heavy: roughly 70% of EU corporate finance is bank credit, versus market-dominated US finance.

That makes bank asset composition important, but Draghi’s preferred fix is still deeper capital markets plus public risk-sharing.

So the Proposal – Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era
it is a bank-centric alternative plumbing offered because CMU/SIU is slow and because public budgets cannot fill €750–800bn a year alone.

That is a legitimate argument. It is not an official one.

4. What Lagarde actually argues — and where the proposal diverges
Lagarde’s line is more precise than “Europe lacks capital.”Household deposits in the euro area are now in the €10–12tn range.

If EU households matched the US deposit-to-assets ratio, up to €8tn stock / ~€350bn annual flow could move into market investment.

Banks are central to the European model, but they are the wrong primary vehicle for early-stage and breakthrough innovation. Integrated capital markets are the missing link.

A large share of European equity exposure already sits in US assets because US returns have been higher. Capital follows expected productivity.

Alignment with Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era
Both say Europe’s savings are trapped in low-productivity uses.

Both say composition of finance matters as much as volume.

Both say energy, innovation and scale-up are the strategic destinations.
Divergence

Lagarde wants savers to move from deposits into securities.

Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era wants banks to move from mortgages into productive loans.

Lagarde’s instrument is SIU / European savings products / better equity markets.

The Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era instrument is a public takeover of housing credit.
Those are not the same policy. They can be complementary.
They can also collide:
if the state absorbs the mortgage stock, the public balance sheet grows just as Draghi is asking the public sector to back industrial investment.

If banks are pushed into more industrial/innovation credit, supervisors will ask about credit risk, concentration and political direction of lending.
Lagarde’s framework is market-allocation plus integration.

The Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era is strategic credit redirection. That is closer to China’s post-property pivot than to the ECB’s SIU design.

5. The Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era architecture, restated cleanly.

From the model has two engines.

Engine A — capital liberation
Transfer the residential mortgage stock from the four major banks to a public or public-purpose vehicle.

Housing becomes a state responsibility for affordability and stability.
Private banks are then supposed to lend into energy, defence, exports, modular construction, life sciences and clean tech.

Engine B — operating-model leap
Build “Banking 5.0” on a claimed 1986–89 Swedish efficiency legacy: staff costs as a share of NII + commissions of 5.8–10.4% historically, target ~4%; 
CIR ~40–42%; 
decentralized branches plus agentic AI for instant credit and allocation.

Six policy pillars in the draft
Housing finance transfer
Bank reorientation to 35–50%+ productive lending
Energy sovereignty:
SMRs + grid-forming BESS
Fokus AI governance, human-in-the-loop, EU AI Act
Basel III as floor, not ceiling
Self-financing growth via higher output and tax

This is internally coherent as a story: 
locked housing collateral → weak productive investment → weak energy/industrial scale → weaker incomes → more dependence on housing wealth.

6. Integration with the Housing Plan — this is the proposal’s best official hook
 
The Housing Plan is the cleanest official use-case.
It already says:
supply is the core problem,
construction is under-productive and under-digitalised,
modular/offsite methods can cut time and cost,
Europe needs an industrial strategy for housing, not only social transfers,
public and promotional-bank finance must crowd in private capital.

Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era then says: the Plan has a “what,” but not a bank-system “how.”
That is half right.The official “how” is state-aid reform, an EIB-centred investment platform, InvestEU, permitting reform and a 2027 simplification package.

That can fund factories and projects. It does not automatically change the fact that Swedish and European banks still prefer low-risk-weight housing assets.
 
So the honest synthesis is:
Housing Plan = demand for industrialised housing and construction productivity.

Draghi = demand for a much larger productive-investment rate.

Lagarde = demand to stop storing European savings in deposits and US paper.

Proposal – Transformation to The 5th Bank Era = demand to change who carries the existing housing credit so private banks can originate the new industrial book.

7. Critical assessment
What is strong 
Correct identification that Europe’s gap is scale, energy intensity and later-stage capital, not a lack of early ideas.

Correct identification that bank-based Europe cannot ignore bank asset composition while waiting for a complete CMU.

Useful pairing of housing as both social outcome and industrial demand.

Sweden is a credible testbed:
concentrated banks, high digitalisation, high offsite share, strong institutions, and a political window around 2026–2030.

What is weak or high-risk
Political/legal feasibility of moving the core mortgage stock off private balance sheets.

Covered-bond market, household contract continuity, and interim bank funding.

Public-debt and contingent-liability optics just as Draghi is asking for more public risk-bearing.

Credit-quality risk if “productive lending” becomes politically directed lending without project pipelines.

Lagarde’s point still stands even if mortgages move:
Europe under-produces equity and VC. Bank loans will not replace late-stage growth capital for AI and deep tech.

The real test
Does liberated bank capacity become actual factories, grids, SMRs/BESS, modular homes and export capacity — or does it become another round of real-estate-adjacent credit under a new label?

8. Overall judgement
Draghi is right that Europe cannot stay competitive on the present investment rate.

Lagarde is right that Europe already has the savings and is allocating them badly.

The Housing Plan is right that housing is now a competitiveness issue, not only a welfare issue.

The Proposal Transformation to The 5th Bank Era is right about one further point that Brussels still underweights:
in a bank-based system, the existing mortgage book is a first-order allocation choice.

Waiting for SIU to mature while bank RWAs remain structurally tilted to housing will not close a Draghi-scale gap by 2030.

It is not yet right to say that transferring the Swedish mortgage stock is the proven, Basel-safe, Europe-ready solution.

The official reports point toward crowding-in private capital, completing banking/capital-markets union, and using public promotional banks. 

The proposal points toward a much sharper break:
take housing credit onto the public perimeter and force private banks into a strategic mission.
That is the live question for 2026–2030.

text:
This produces an institutional microtime. Thought may develop associatively; testimony must emerge serially. Several possible continuations can be present to a speaker while only one answer is authorized. The proceeding repeatedly cuts a broad field of possible speech into narrow successive units.

At pages 494–495, Microchip describes the timing of online activity around morning news. The judge interrupts his pace. Near the end of redirect, while he reads the agreement’s continuing obligations, the judge again tells him to slow down. The two moments bookend an important tension: the witness speaks about rapid circulation inside an apparatus whose durability depends on deceleration.

The pause is therefore productive. It provides an interval in which an objection can intervene, a distinction can be drawn, or an answer can be limited. It also leaves the audience holding what has already been said while waiting for what will follow. The meaning of an unfinished answer can remain active during silence.

This is where a pulse becomes a useful formal image. A pulse includes interruption within its continuity. Speech arrives, stops, and returns under altered conditions. The gap has a shape because the preceding turn has created an expectation. A courtroom transcript preserves those successive activations even when it cannot preserve their felt intensity.

4. Time that can be suspended

One of the strongest temporal features of the testimony is also one of the least mythological in appearance. At pages 546–548, the questioning concerns tolling agreements. The witness acknowledges signing agreements associated with extending the time available in relation to conduct from 2016. A document governing the temporal reach of the investigation is introduced into evidence.

Here social time becomes tangible. The calendar continues advancing, but a legally operative interval is altered through an agreement. A document can change whether an earlier act remains within a particular procedural horizon. The alteration occurs through rules, signatures, and institutional recognition. It has consequences for bodies and futures.

Another suspended interval appears at pages 558–559. The witness’s sentencing had originally been tentatively scheduled for October 14, 2022. At the time of the March 2023 testimony it had not occurred. The questioning connects the delay to the completion of cooperation and testimony. A future event remains pending while another proceeding unfolds.

The witness therefore occupies an extended threshold: past conduct has not finished generating obligations, and future judgment has not yet acquired its final form. The present is stretched between them. It is not empty waiting. What happens during the interval may matter to what comes afterward.

The oath creates a smaller version of this structure. The witness leaves the stand and returns, but the obligation is explicitly continuous. The court does not require the speech itself to be continuous in order for the binding condition to persist. A state can survive a gap in activity.

This offers a precise anatomy of institutional liminality. A person can be physically absent, legally bound, temporally unfinished, and expected to return. The recess closes one sequence without dissolving the relationship that made the sequence possible. A signature extends one horizon; an oath bridges another. The transcript contains actual mechanisms by which a society holds portions of its past open and keeps a future from arriving yet.

At page 585, the judge directs that questions be stricken and disregarded. This creates another temporal distinction: speech has occurred, but its permitted role in the proceeding changes afterward. The occurrence and the authorization to rely on it are separate things. Institutional time can revise the status of a past act without undoing the act’s occurrence. The present reaches backward through rules of use, while the historical sequence remains intact.
