text:
THE DOG-EYED VISITOR OF THE DOCK: THE STORY OF A HARBOR SEAL

The clip lasts only a few seconds. A weathered wooden plank cuts across the bottom of the frame, and beyond it, dark water ripples under grey light. Then, quietly, without any splash or warning, a round spotted head rises just far enough to break the surface: two enormous black eyes, a thick fringe of white whiskers, a small black nose, and an expression that looks, to almost anyone watching, uncannily like a dog peering up over the edge of a pool. It hangs there for a moment, watching the person filming with what seems like open curiosity, before sinking back and drifting a little closer to the dock. This is a harbor seal, and that brief, silent, curious approach to a human standing on a plank of wood is, in miniature, almost the entire natural history of the species compressed into a few seconds of video.

Harbor seals, known scientifically as Phoca vitulina, are among the most widely distributed seal species on the planet, and also among the most familiar, precisely because of behavior like this: an apparently fearless willingness to approach boats, docks, kayaks, and swimmers in places where they are not actively hunted or harassed. Fact: the harbor seal has one of the broadest ranges of any pinniped species, found along coastlines of the North Atlantic and North Pacific across the entire Northern Hemisphere, from the eastern seaboard of North America and the coasts of Alaska and British Columbia, across to the shores of the United Kingdom, Scandinavia, the Baltic and North Seas, and around the North Pacific rim through Japan and Russia. Few marine mammals occupy so much of the map, and fewer still do it while remaining so consistently, recognizably coastal, rarely venturing far from the shorelines, estuaries, sandbars, and rocky haul-out sites where they were born.

That word, haul-out, is central to understanding harbor seal life, and it explains why a dock like the one in the video is such a natural place for one to appear. Fact: unlike many other seal species that spend extended stretches entirely at sea, harbor seals are considered one of the most "terrestrial" of all true seals in their daily habits, routinely leaving the water to rest on exposed rocks, sandbars, mudflats, floating docks, and even, on occasion, the low decks of moored boats, often in the same handful of favored locations day after day, sometimes for years. Researchers who study haul-out sites can frequently identify individual seals returning to precisely the same rock or sandbar on a tidal schedule, which means the animal drifting up beside a particular dock is very likely not a one-time visitor but a local resident with a route and routine of its own, the marine equivalent of a neighborhood regular.

The face itself, the single most striking feature in the video, is doing a great deal of quiet biological work behind that appealing, dog-like expression. Fact: harbor seals lack external ear flaps entirely, having only small round openings on the sides of the head, a trait shared by all members of the true seal family, Phocidae, and one of the simplest ways to distinguish a true seal from an eared seal such as a sea lion or fur seal at a glance. Look closely at the head in the footage and there is no flap or fold of skin where an ear would be on a dog or a cat, only smooth, rounded fur running straight down toward the jaw. That rounded, earless, large-eyed head shape is part of why harbor seals are so often described as looking like a cross between a Labrador and a fish, an impression strong enough that the species has picked up the informal, deeply affectionate nickname "sea dog" or "spotted sea dog" in coastal communities across several countries entirely independently of one another.

Those enormous dark eyes are not simply an accident of cuteness; they are precision equipment. Fact: harbor seals possess exceptionally large eyes relative to head size, packed with a high density of rod cells and a reflective layer called the tapetum lucidum behind the retina, the same structure that makes a cat's eyes glow in headlights, allowing the animal to gather and use available light with remarkable efficiency in the dim, particle-filled water of coastal bays and river mouths where visibility rarely extends more than a few meters even at midday. In murky, sediment-heavy harbor water exactly like the water shown in the clip, a seal's eyesight is doing serious, specialized work that a human observer, squinting into the same water and seeing nothing but darkness a foot below the surface, can barely appreciate.

Vision, though, is only the backup system. Fact: the dense array of whiskers, or vibrissae, fanned out across a harbor seal's muzzle are so mechanically sensitive that laboratory studies have demonstrated the animals can detect and follow the faint hydrodynamic wake left behind by a fish that swam past several seconds earlier and many body-lengths away, using their whiskers alone, with their eyes covered, to accurately track the direction, size, and even the shape of the object that produced the disturbance. This ability, sometimes described by researchers as a form of underwater "wake-following," is considered one of the more sophisticated sensory adaptations found in any mammal, aquatic or otherwise, and it means a hunting harbor seal can often locate a fish it never directly saw at all, guided instead by the fading turbulence the fish's own tail left hanging in the water behind it.

All of that sensory equipment supports an animal built for a genuinely demanding double life, spent partly on land and partly in cold, often turbulent coastal water. Fact: adult harbor seals typically weigh between roughly one hundred and three hundred pounds depending on sex, age, and region, with males generally running somewhat larger than females, and body length in most populations falling between about five and six feet nose to tail, making a fully grown adult a genuinely substantial animal up close, even though the smooth, compact, torpedo-shaped body and the relatively small head often make individuals look deceptively modest in size from a distance or in photographs, right up until one surfaces directly beside a boat and the scale becomes suddenly, unmistakably clear.

The spotted coat pattern visible across the seal's head and back in the footage is not simply decorative; it functions as camouflage against the dappled light and shadow of a rocky or sandy seafloor, and it is also, conveniently for researchers and casual observers alike, close to as individually distinctive as a fingerprint. Fact: the specific arrangement, density, and pattern of dark spots against the lighter background coat varies enough from one harbor seal to another that marine biologists studying particular haul-out colonies frequently identify and track individual animals over multiple years using nothing more than photographs of their unique spot patterns, a non-invasive method sometimes called photo-identification that avoids the stress and cost of physical tagging while still allowing detailed long-term study of specific seals returning again and again to the same stretch of coastline.

Harbor seals are, broadly speaking, opportunistic and highly varied feeders, and this flexibility is a large part of why the species has managed to establish itself so successfully across such an enormous geographic range. Fact: diet studies from different regional populations show harbor seals consuming well over one hundred different species of fish, squid, octopus, and crustaceans depending entirely on what happens to be locally abundant, from herring and anchovies in some regions to flounder, hake, salmon, and squid in others, an adaptability that stands in sharp contrast to more specialized marine predators that depend heavily on just one or two prey species and suffer badly when those populations decline. A seal cruising near a working dock or fishing pier, the exact setting suggested by the plank in the video, has often learned that such locations reliably produce scraps, bait, or an easy meal, and individual seals can become remarkably comfortable approaching people and boats in places where they have repeatedly been fed or where fishing activity consistently produces food.

That comfort around humans, so visible in the calm, unhurried way the seal in the video lifts its head and simply watches, cuts in two very different directions depending on context, and wildlife biologists are generally careful to flag both sides of it. Fact: while an approachable, curious seal often delights onlookers and photographers, most marine mammal protection agencies, including NOAA Fisheries in the United States and equivalent bodies in Canada and Europe, actively discourage feeding wild seals or encouraging this kind of close approach, because seals that become habituated to handouts are measurably more likely to be struck by boat propellers, to become entangled in fishing gear while lingering near vessels, or to develop dangerously reduced wariness around humans that can end badly for the animal even when every individual interaction along the way seemed harmless and friendly. The instinct to interpret a seal's calm, doe-eyed gaze as an invitation to interact is entirely understandable and, according to essentially every marine mammal agency that studies the issue, exactly the instinct visitors are asked to resist.

There is also a formal legal dimension to that guidance in several countries that surprises many people encountering it for the first time. Fact: in the United States, harbor seals and all other marine mammals are protected under the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972, a federal law that makes it illegal to feed, touch, harass, or closely approach wild marine mammals including seals, with real financial penalties attached, a level of legal protection considerably stronger than that afforded to most terrestrial wildlife and rooted directly in earlier twentieth-century population crashes caused by unregulated hunting, culling programs tied to fisheries conflicts, and, in some regions, deliberate extermination campaigns that very nearly eliminated certain local harbor seal populations before protective legislation intervened.

Those population recoveries, where they have happened, count among the more genuinely successful conservation stories in modern marine mammal management. Fact: following protective legislation in the 1970s, several major harbor seal populations, including those along the U.S. west coast, rebounded substantially over subsequent decades, in some regions returning close to the historical carrying capacity of available coastal habitat, a trajectory sharply contrasting with the far more troubled status of many other marine mammal species over the same period. Not every regional population has fared equally well; some harbor seal groups in the Baltic Sea, Scotland, and other localized regions have declined in recent decades due to disease outbreaks, changing prey availability, and localized environmental pressures, a reminder that a species doing well globally can still struggle in specific pockets of its enormous range.

Reproduction in harbor seals follows a rhythm closely tied to the tides and haul-out sites that define so much of their daily existence. Fact: harbor seal pups are born already able to swim, often within hours of birth, an unusual and demanding developmental strategy compared to many other seal species whose newborns remain fully land-bound for an extended nursing period; a harbor seal pup typically nurses for only about four to six weeks on remarkably fat-rich milk before being weaned and left to fend for itself, one of the shortest maternal dependency periods known among mammals of comparable size, a pace of independence that reflects just how exposed and tidally dynamic the sandbars, rocks, and mudflats where pups are born genuinely are.

Underneath the calm surface glide visible in the video lies an animal built for serious underwater endurance as well as speed. Fact: harbor seals are capable of diving to depths exceeding fifteen hundred feet in some recorded cases and can remain submerged for up to thirty minutes at a time, feats made possible by a suite of physiological adaptations including the ability to dramatically slow the heart rate during a dive, a phenomenon called the dive reflex, along with a proportionally large blood volume and high concentration of oxygen-storing myoglobin in the muscle tissue, allowing the animal to function almost entirely without breathing for far longer than any human free diver could safely attempt. The unhurried, almost lazy way the seal in the footage simply floats at the surface, watching, belies an animal that could, if it chose, disappear into the depths of that dark harbor water for the better part of half an hour without difficulty.

None of that underwater athleticism is on display in the clip, of course. What is on display is something arguably more interesting to the average viewer scrolling past it: a genuine moment of mutual curiosity between two very different species, the human on the dock and the seal in the water, each apparently studying the other with roughly equal interest. Fact: several field studies of harbor seal behavior around docks, marinas, and popular haul-out sites near towns have documented what researchers describe as measurable curiosity toward novel stimuli, including human activity, cameras, and unfamiliar objects, behavior consistent with the relatively large brain-to-body ratio found across the pinniped family and with cognitive research showing seals capable of complex problem-solving, social learning, and even, in captive studies, matching tasks and simple rhythmic mimicry that place them among the more cognitively flexible marine mammals studied to date.

It is worth pausing on just how visually deceptive the whole scene is, because the resemblance to a dog is doing a great deal of psychological work on the viewer without most people ever consciously noticing it. Fact: the harbor seal's close evolutionary relatives are not dogs at all but bears, weasels, and other members of a broader carnivore lineage that split roughly thirty million years ago into two branches, one leading toward modern seals, sea lions, and walruses, collectively called pinnipeds, and the other remaining fully terrestrial as the ancestors of today's bears and mustelids such as otters and weasels. The seal's round head, big dark eyes, whiskered muzzle, and even its clumsy, endearing way of shuffling across land on its front flippers all trace back, ultimately, to that shared ancestry with land carnivores, which is precisely why a harbor seal looking up out of the water manages to trigger the exact same instinctive affection in a human brain that a dog does, despite the roughly thirty million years of separate evolutionary history and an entirely different habitat sitting quietly behind that familiar face.

The dock itself, weathered and pale in the frame, is a small but telling detail too. Fact: harbor seals show a strong preference for haul-out and approach sites that offer easy, low-effort access between water and a resting surface, which is exactly why floating docks, low piers, gently sloping sandbars, and boat ramps are so consistently popular with the species across its range, far more so than steep rocky cliffs or high seawalls that would demand more energy and coordination for an animal whose flippers, superbly adapted for swimming, are considerably less graceful once out of the water. A seal willing to approach that particular plank so closely and so calmly is very likely one accustomed to that stretch of shoreline, treating the dock less as an obstacle and more as a familiar, low landmark along a route it has probably swum dozens or hundreds of times before.

A few more details are worth adding here, because harbor seals carry a surprising number of small, specific facts that rarely make it past a quick caption but that make the animal considerably stranger than its friendly, dog-like face initially suggests. Fact: on land, a harbor seal cannot rotate its rear flippers forward under its body the way a sea lion can, which is the real reason true seals move across sand or rock in that distinctive, caterpillar-like wriggle rather than the four-legged walk sea lions manage at aquarium shows; the two groups are often confused, but the hip and rear-flipper structure differs enough that a true seal is physically incapable of the upright waddle-walk that makes sea lions such crowd-pleasing performers. That same trade-off, though, is part of what makes harbor seals such efficient swimmers, since the same fused, paddle-like rear flippers nearly useless on land become a single powerful propulsive fin underwater, driven side to side closer to a fish's tail than to a sea lion's alternating stroke.

The species name itself hides a small etymological joke. Fact: the scientific name Phoca vitulina combines the Greek word for seal with the Latin word vitulina, meaning "calf-like," a reference dating back to early naturalists who thought the vocal calls of harbor seal pups, described as plaintive, bleating cries, sounded remarkably similar to the moo of a young calf, also the origin of the old-fashioned European common name "sea calf" still used for the species in parts of Scandinavia. Underwater, adult harbor seals are considerably quieter than many other pinniped species; unlike the loud, near-constant barking colonies of sea lions, harbor seals tend to be relatively silent on land, communicating instead through underwater growls and low-frequency calls used mainly by males defending breeding territories, sounds rarely heard by anyone standing on a dock above the surface.

Longevity in the wild is respectable for an animal facing so many natural threats. Fact: wild harbor seals typically live between twenty-five and thirty years, with some individuals in protected populations documented living into their mid-thirties, and captive seals in accredited aquariums have occasionally exceeded even that, benefiting from a stable food supply and the absence of predators that shape so much of wild seal behavior. Those predators are formidable: orcas and great white sharks are the primary threats to adult harbor seals across most of their range, and in regions where mammal-hunting orca pods are common, such as the Pacific Northwest, harbor seals make up a significant portion of the diet, while pups hauled out on exposed sandbars face an additional threat from bald eagles capable of snatching a newborn before it is strong enough to reach open water.

Human history with the species has not always been as protective as it is today. Fact: harbor seals were hunted commercially for their fur, meat, and oil for centuries across nearly every part of their range, from Indigenous coastal communities who relied on seals as an important subsistence resource, to large-scale commercial sealing operations in the eighteenth, nineteenth, and early twentieth centuries that, combined with government bounty programs intended to reduce perceived competition with fisheries, drove some regional populations down to a fraction of their historical numbers by the mid-twentieth century. In several U.S. states along the New England coast, bounty programs paying hunters for each seal killed remained active well into the 1960s, a policy stance that reversed dramatically following the 1972 protective legislation and the broader shift in public attitudes toward marine mammal conservation.

One particular harbor seal deserves a mention purely because of how unusual and well-documented an exception he turned out to be. Fact: a rescued harbor seal named Hoover, raised in captivity in Maine in the 1970s after being found orphaned as a pup and later transferred to the New England Aquarium in Boston, became internationally famous for spontaneously learning to mimic short phrases of human speech in a distinctly Boston-accented growl, including his own name and simple greetings, a genuinely rare documented case of vocal mimicry in a pinniped that scientists studied closely at the time. Harbor seals are not generally considered vocal mimics the way parrots or dolphins are, which made Hoover's ability so scientifically notable and so widely reported in the press; visitors reportedly traveled specifically to hear him "talk."

Underwater physiology adds one more layer of genuine strangeness to an animal that otherwise looks, at the surface, so approachable and familiar. Fact: to withstand repeated deep dives without decompression sickness, harbor seals and other deep-diving pinnipeds can deliberately collapse their lungs under pressure at depth, forcing air out of the alveoli and into more rigid airways where nitrogen absorption into the bloodstream is minimized, allowing the animal to dive again and again throughout a single day without accumulating dangerous dissolved nitrogen. Combined with the dramatic slowing of heart rate during a dive and the redirection of blood flow toward the brain and heart, it amounts to adaptations that would be lethal for almost any land mammal, deployed casually, dozens of times a day, by an animal that spends its resting hours looking like an oversized, spotted puppy floating placidly at the surface of a quiet harbor.

That contrast, between the extraordinary physiological machinery running quietly underneath and the disarmingly simple, friendly expression on top, is really the heart of why footage like this travels so easily and charms so many people who see it. A weathered plank, a patch of grey harbor water, and a single curious head breaking the surface do not, on their own, look like very much, yet behind that head sits one of the more sophisticated sensory toolkits in the animal kingdom, wrapped in a face that, purely by evolutionary coincidence, triggers the same warm response in a human brain that a dog's face does.

In the end, the enduring appeal of a clip like this one has very little to do with rarity or novelty. Harbor seals are not an endangered or genuinely rare species in most of their range, and moments of a curious seal surfacing near a dock happen, quietly and largely unrecorded, along thousands of miles of coastline every single day. The appeal instead comes from something closer to quiet recognition: a wild animal, shaped over tens of millions of years by an entirely different evolutionary path than any land mammal familiar to most viewers, that nonetheless returns a human gaze with an expression so easily and instinctively read as warmth, interest, and something close to friendliness that it briefly collapses the enormous evolutionary and ecological distance between a person standing on a weathered plank and a spotted, whiskered predator built to dive fifteen hundred feet into cold, dark water. The seal in the video almost certainly surfaced out of nothing more complicated than curiosity, or the hope of an easy meal, or simple habit built from repeated visits to a familiar stretch of dock. But for a few brief seconds it hung there in the water, dark eyes fixed intently on the camera's lens, it managed, without effort at all, to look remarkably, movingly, like something much closer to home.

text:
You say: Jews are from Judah. Arabs are from Arabia. It's not that complicated.

But it is complicated. And you know it. You are oversimplifying history to hide the truth.

Let us set the record straight.

First: You are confusing religion with ethnicity.
Judaism is a religion. It is not an ethnicity. It is not a nationality. It is not a right to a land. You cannot say I am from Judah because you believe in Judaism. That is like an Italian Christian saying I am from Jerusalem because he is Christian.

And if Judaism is an ethnicity, why are there Ashkenazi Jews from Eastern Europe, Sephardic Jews from Spain and Morocco, Falasha Jews from Ethiopia, Cochin Jews from India, and Kaifeng Jews from China? All of these are Jewish religiously, but they are not one ethnicity. They are a mix of different peoples who adopted Judaism throughout history.

The genetic evidence is clear: Ashkenazi Jews have significant European ancestry, particularly on the maternal line. Mitochondrial DNA studies show that a majority of Ashkenazi maternal lineages are of European origin, not Levantine. This is not my opinion. This is published science.

Second: You say Arabs came from Arabia in the 7th century.
This is a historical error. The Islamic conquests were not a demographic migration. They were military and political conquests. The Arab armies that entered the Levant were small — thousands, not millions. They did not have the numerical capacity to replace or displace the population of the Levant. They did not have the capacity to Arabize the region by force.

What happened is that the indigenous population of the Levant — the Canaanites, the ancestors of today's Palestinians — gradually converted to Islam and gradually adopted Arabic, but they did not leave their land. They were not expelled. They were not killed. They were not replaced. They stayed. And the small number of Arab migrants were absorbed into the indigenous population, not the other way around.

This is not my opinion. This is genetics. The 2020 Cell study analyzed DNA from 93 ancient Canaanite skeletons. The result: Palestinians — Muslim and Christian — derive more than 50% of their ancestry from the Canaanites. A 2025 study found that Palestinians show 75–88% ancestral persistence from the Iron Age Levant.

And the definitive proof: Palestinian Christians. They did not convert to Islam. They did not come with the Islamic conquests. They have been Christian since the early centuries. So why do they carry the same Canaanite DNA as Palestinian Muslims? If we came with Islam, why do the Christians who never converted to Islam carry the same genes as us?

The answer: Because we did not come with Islam. We were here before Islam. And we stayed after Islam. We converted, but we did not leave.

Third: You say Jews were in Judah. Fine. Where were the Jews before 1948?
The official British Mandate table — not a Palestinian document — shows that between 1920 and 1945, 367,845 Jews immigrated to Palestine. In 1935 alone, 61,854 Jews immigrated. These were not returning. These were immigrants from Europe. From Poland. From Russia. From Germany. From Romania. Their language was Yiddish, German, Polish. Their culture was European. They were not Middle Eastern. They were not Palestinian.

Meanwhile, the Palestinians — Muslims and Christians — were living in their towns and villages. Farming their land. Paying their taxes. They did not go anywhere. They stayed.

That is the difference. Not between Jew and Arab. But between an indigenous people and a settler population. Between those who stayed in their land, and those who came from Europe to occupy someone else's land.

Fourth: You say Jews were in Judah, and Arabs came from Arabia. But this applies to you too.
If Arabs came from Arabia in the 7th century, then Ashkenazi Jews came from Eastern Europe in the 20th century. The difference is that the Arabs came 1,400 years ago, and the Ashkenazi Jews came 100 years ago. The difference is that the Arabs were absorbed into the indigenous population, and the Ashkenazi Jews came to replace it.

But even that comparison is flawed. Because the Arabs who came in the 7th century were not a mass migration. They were small military garrisons. They did not settle the land. They did not replace the population. The people of the Levant converted to Islam and adopted Arabic over centuries, but they remained the same people. They remained the indigenous population.

You cannot say I am from Judah while your grandfather was born in Warsaw. You cannot say I am indigenous while your passport is Polish or Russian or German. You cannot say I am from this land while your mother tongue is Yiddish, your culture is European, and your ancestors are buried in European cemeteries.

Fifth: You say Israel occupied the West Bank and Gaza in 1967. But you ignore that Israel planned the occupation before the war.
The Israeli Defense Forces' own archive — not a Palestinian document — documents that the military plans to occupy the West Bank, Gaza, and the Golan Heights were ready before June 5, 1967. Kardom for Egypt. Atzmon for Gaza. Pargol for the West Bank. Makevet for the Golan. These are not reactions. These are premeditated plans.

And Israeli General Mordechai Hod said it himself: For sixteen years, we had been planning what took place in those first 80 minutes. We lived with that plan, we ate with it, we slept with it. We never stopped improving it.

So do not talk about a defensive war. Do not talk about a reaction. Israel planned the occupation. Israel executed the occupation. Israel still occupies.

Sixth: You say settlements are legal.
No. Settlements are illegal. Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention prohibits the transfer of civilians into occupied territory. UN Security Council resolutions 452, 465, and 2334 confirm this. The International Court of Justice ruled in 2004 that the wall is illegal. You cannot use international law as a slogan while ignoring the rulings of international courts.

Seventh: You say Palestinians rejected every offer.
This is a gross simplification. Camp David 2000 did not offer real sovereignty over Jerusalem or a just solution for refugees. Olmert's 2008 offer was better but still insufficient. Palestinians did not reject a state. They rejected a state without real sovereignty.

Eighth: You say the right of return is a myth.
No. The right of return is enshrined in UN General Assembly Resolution 194, which states that Palestinian refugees who wish to return to their homes and live in peace with their neighbors should be permitted to do so at the earliest practicable date. Israel has refused to implement this resolution for 75 years.

And the irony: you say the right of return for Jews is not a myth. Fine. But the Jew who returns after 2,000 years — where does he return from? From Poland. From Russia. From Germany. From Europe. He is not returning. He is an immigrant. A settler. He came from somewhere else.

Meanwhile, the Palestinian who demands to return — where does he return from? From a camp a few kilometers from his village. From a neighborhood in Jaffa. From a house in Haifa. From a field in the Galilee. From a village on the coast. He is not returning from somewhere else. He is returning from exile. From displacement. From occupation.

So who has the real right of return? The one who stayed? Or the one who came? The one born in the land? Or the one born in Europe? The one holding the key to his house? Or the one holding a foreign passport?

The answer is clear. But you refuse to acknowledge it. Because acknowledging it means you are not the rightful owner. It means you are a settler. It means you are an occupier.

Conclusion
You say Jews are from Judah, and Arabs are from Arabia. But the truth is that the Palestinians — Muslims and Christians — are the indigenous people of the Levant. They did not come with the Islamic conquests. They were here before them. They are the Canaanites. They are the Jebusites. They are the Philistines. They are the ones who built the cities of Jaffa, Acre, Gaza, and Jericho. They are the ones who planted the olive trees on these hills. They are the ones who paid taxes to the Romans, the Byzantines, and the Ottomans.

As for you — the Ashkenazi Jew — your ancestors lived in Europe for a thousand years. Your language is Yiddish. Your culture is European. Your genes are European. You are not from Judah. You are from Warsaw. From Moscow. From Berlin. From Bucharest.

And you do not have any legal instrument proving that Palestine became Israel. Not the Balfour Declaration, not the Mandate, not the Partition Plan, not Jordan's annexation, not uti possidetis juris. All of them are lies and flimsy arguments.

Palestine was not a land without a people for a people without a land. Palestine was inhabited. Registered. Cultivated. Its people paid taxes. My grandparents were born there. They were buried there. And I will not give it up.

I do not need to give you legitimacy. You are not the rightful owner. You are a settler. And I am the owner of the land.

I was here before Zionism. I am here now. And I will be here after your occupation ends.

A US State Department grant program for MAGA-aligned groups in Europe will exclude French applicants over fears of appearing to interfere in France’s 2027 presidential election, two sources told Reuters.

The Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights and Labor (DRL) program offers $1–3 million to organizations working on democratic resilience, free speech, national sovereignty, migration, censorship and “lawfare.” Washington has informed French officials of the exclusion, citing the risk to deep US-French economic ties. The US is France’s top foreign investor.

France holds a presidential vote in April–May 2027 in which Marine Le Pen’s National Rally is competitive. Paris has warned against foreign meddling; Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said in July that France and Europe “will not tolerate any attempt at foreign interference.” A French applicant seeking $1 million for anti-censorship work said they were recently told French groups were barred. Officials also worry funding could clash with a pending French bill tightening penalties for disinformation and election interference.

A State Department spokesperson said programs remain under deliberation and declined to confirm an exclusion. Franco-American relations are already strained over tariffs, ambassador accreditation and earlier US outreach linked to Le Pen. Some MAGA officials wanted a harder line on France; others feared blowback for US companies. One applicant said they may relocate, possibly to Brussels, to stay eligible.

Source: Reuters

text:
You don't have to vote for the freebie. You still pay for it.

Indian elections are no longer a contest over what the state will build. They are a bidding war over what it will give. And the invoice lands on people who never asked for the gift.

The New Election Product

Cash to women. Free units of power. Free bus rides. Six gas cylinders. Gold for a wedding. A scooter. A loan waiver. Manifestos now look like supermarket flyers. Every party does it. The party that once called this "revdi culture" now runs the same catalogue under a different brand name. 
The competition is not over ideas or governance anymore. It is over who can promise a bigger monthly transfer. And voters have noticed. Once money hits the account, the next manifesto cannot offer "good roads" and expect to win. That is how a tactic becomes a floor.

First, Draw the Only Line That Matters

Midday meals, vaccines, government schools, primary health centres, targeted foodgrain for the poorest. That is the state doing its job. A monthly transfer to every woman on the voter list, free farm power for a landlord with a 7.5 HP pump, and a pre-poll cash drop six weeks before voting day are not the same thing. 
The Supreme Court has said this out loud. Investing in welfare is not the same as spraying state money on individuals at scale. There is a difference between building a safety net and buying a vote bank.

The Race That No Party Can Sit Out

One state started unconditional cash for women. Twelve states now run it. The bill went from almost nothing in FY21 to about 0.57 percent of GDP in FY26. The Economic Survey put women-focused cash transfers near Rs 1.7 lakh crore for this year. 
In a single budget cycle, twelve states together budgeted Rs 1,68,040 crore just for unconditional cash transfers to women. Maharashtra alone allocated Rs 36,000 crore for its scheme. 
Karnataka set aside Rs 28,608 crore. Telangana topped the list with Rs 56,084 crore for its six guarantees. Once voters have seen the money hit their accounts, you cannot go back. The ratchet effect is real. Moving upward is easy, moving down is politically impossible.

"Free" Is an Accounting Trick

The state does not print the mixer-grinder. It borrows, it cuts something else, or it loads the cost onto the next bill. Combined state fiscal deficit is already above the old 3 percent comfort zone. 
An analysis of 17 major states showed their aggregate fiscal deficit remained high at 3.2 percent of GSDP in FY26. The combined revenue deficit rose to 0.8 percent of GSDP from 0.7 percent a year earlier. 
In several states, half or more of fresh borrowing is no longer building an asset. It is paying for yesterday's promise. States spend over 60 percent of their revenue expenditure on salaries, pensions, interest payments, and subsidies. Many are financing revenue deficits through borrowing. That is not fiscal management. That is a subscription to perpetual debt.

How It Hits You Even If You Refused the Scheme

You pay when the DISCOM is bankrupt and the paying household subsidises the free farm pump. Then you sit through load-shedding while the farmer runs his pump at noon because electricity is "free." 
You pay when the state floods the bond market and your home loan, MSME loan, and corporate capex all get a higher interest rate. State bond yields are already trading at historically elevated premiums. 
Combined central and state borrowing could cross Rs 31 lakh crore, increasing pressure on bond markets and interest rates. You pay when the classroom, the PHC, and the irrigation canal lose the budget line that the cash transfer took. The freebie is a tax with better branding. It just does not show up on your payslip.

The Growth Channel Nobody Puts on the Hoarding

Capital expenditure is the first thing that gets cut because salaries, pensions, interest, and "guarantees" cannot be. The CAG flagged Karnataka's guarantees shrinking infrastructure capex by about Rs 5,200 crore in one year. 
Punjab and Kerala spend a sliver of their budget on building things. Gujarat and Odisha spend several times more. Punjab allocates just 5.5 paise of every budgetary rupee to capital investment. Gujarat allocates 25.3 paise. That gap compounds. 
One path leaves you with a road. The other leaves you with a monthly SMS from the treasury. States may ultimately be forced to squeeze capital expenditure if welfare spending rises while revenues disappoint. Capex remains the easiest item for states to cut.

Power and Credit Are Where "Free" Becomes a System Failure

Free electricity and farm loan waivers do not just cost money. They train the system. Farmers wait for the next waiver. DISCOMs stop collecting. Industry pays a steeper tariff so agriculture can run pumps at noon. The RBI's own language on this is blunt. These schemes undermine credit culture, distort prices, and scare off private investment. 
Frequent waivers weaken repayment incentives. Agri-NPAs rose sharply in waiver-announcing states, reaching 8.44 percent by March 2019. 
The RBI working group noted that eight out of ten waivers since 2014 were announced near election cycles. A state that waives Rs 48,000 crore of farm power arrears in one announcement is not running an energy policy. It is running a campaign.

The Pre-Poll Timing Is the Tell

When the transfer is announced after the election calendar is known, and the amount is a round number that fits a slogan, you are not watching social policy. You are watching vote-buying with public money. 
The Supreme Court has asked this question directly. "Why suddenly schemes are announced near elections?" The Court warned that distributing state benefits indiscriminately, without distinguishing between those who can afford to pay and those who cannot, amounts to appeasement and is detrimental to sustainable development. 
"Not a single penny is left for development because of such policies," the Court told state governments. Bihar's pre-election package was estimated at about 4 percent of state GDP. Larger than its capital outlay. That is not compassion. That is an intergenerational overdraft signed at a rally.

Why "I Didn't Take It" Is Not an Exit

There is no opt-out button on state debt. The woman who never enrolled still lives with worse buses, worse hospitals, and a weaker job market if the state stopped building. 
The salaried taxpayer in a city that "doesn't do freebies" still funds the Centre's extra transfers and still pays the bond-market premium when twenty states borrow at once. 
Collective fiscal choices do not respect your personal virtue. State debt has tripled in a decade from Rs 17.57 lakh crore in FY14 to Rs 59.60 lakh crore in FY23. The combined Centre-State debt is roughly 81 percent of GDP. The prudential ceiling was 60 percent. That debt belongs to every citizen. Whether you took the cash or not.

The Trap for the Next Decade

India needs factory jobs, logistics, power that stays on, and cities that work. That is capex plus competence. Competitive populism buys the next five years of assembly majorities by selling the next twenty years of fiscal space. Growth does not collapse in one Budget. It slows the way a company slows when every spare rupee goes to keep existing customers from leaving. 
The Economic Survey has flagged deteriorating state government finances as a rising threat to fiscal stability, infrastructure creation, and long-term economic growth. Rising revenue deficits among states are crowding out productive investment. 
The question is not whether we can afford these schemes today. The question is whether we can afford what we stop building because of them.

Closing Thought

A republic can feed the poor and still refuse to auction the treasury. The test is simple. Does the rupee create an asset, a skill, or a vote? If the answer is only the third, you are not a beneficiary. You are the collateral.

I dont have to cope harder because i have the truth and facts on my side.

What you have done is dump a list of verses about warfare, treaties, criminals, historical events and a pre-modern institution of slavery, strip away the verses immediately before and after them, then pretend they all say: “Muslims, murder anyone who isn't Muslim.”

They don't. So let's go through your list one by one.

1. Your original meme: paedophilia, rape, beheadings, burning people alive, FGM, oppression, honour killings and hostage-taking.
You haven't produced Qur'anic commands for paedophilia, FGM, honour killings or burning people alive because the Qur'an does not command those things. Armed jihad exists in Islam, just as warfare exists in virtually every civilisation, but jihad does not mean “murder random non-Muslims.” Prisoners captured during an actual war are also not the same thing as taking random civilians hostage. And as I explain below, your “rape” argument simply substitutes the word rape for historical slavery/concubinage without the verses themselves ever saying “rape.”

2. Qur'an 9:5 — the so-called “Sword Verse.”
You conveniently isolate 9:5. Read the surrounding passage. 9:4 explicitly exempts polytheists who kept their treaties. 9:6 orders Muslims to protect a polytheist seeking safety and then escort him to a place of safety. 9:7 commands Muslims to remain upright with those who remain upright with them. Then 9:12–13 identifies people who broke their treaties, plotted to expel the Messenger and initiated hostilities. So no, 9:5 cannot honestly be translated into “kill every pagan wherever you see one.”

3. Qur'an 9:14 — “fight them.”
Who is “them”? Read the verse immediately before it. 9:13 says they broke their oaths, attempted to expel the Messenger and “began the attack” first. You deleted the antecedent and presented “fight them” as though Allah suddenly started talking about every non-Muslim on Earth.

4. Qur'an 2:193 and 8:39 — “fight until there is no fitnah.”
You omitted 2:190: fight those who fight you and do not transgress. You omitted 2:192: if they cease, stop. And even 2:193 itself ends by saying that if they cease, there is to be no aggression except against oppressors. Likewise, 8:38 says if the opponents cease their previous conduct will be forgiven, and 8:39 again says “if they cease.” Classical scholars differed over the breadth of fitnah and the scope of jihad, but none of that magically turns these verses into a private licence for Muslims to murder anyone who doesn't believe.

5. Qur'an 9:29 — People of the Book and jizya.
Yes, this is genuinely a war/jizya verse, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. But notice what the verse does not say: it does not say, “Kill Jews and Christians because they refuse to become Muslims.” Classical Islamic law allowed Jews and Christians to remain Jews and Christians under Muslim rule, with protected legal status, while paying jizya. Historical sources describe jizya as tribute or a poll tax connected with their status under Muslim government and protection.
So if your claim is that Islam commands Muslims to murder Jews and Christians simply for being non-Muslim, 9:29 does not establish that. In fact, the existence of jizya demonstrates that non-Muslim communities could continue practising their religions under Muslim government rather than being given a choice of “convert or die.”

And tribute imposed on conquered or subordinate populations was hardly unique to Islam. The Hebrew Bible itself says in Deuteronomy 20:10–11 that when a city accepts an offer of peace, its inhabitants are to become tributaries and serve Israel. Maimonides later codified Jewish law stating that a surrendering population was required to accept tribute and subjection. That is a very close historical parallel to what you're condemning as uniquely Islamic.

Christian states did it too. Medieval Christian kingdoms imposed special taxes on religious minorities. Jews in medieval England were subjected to extraordinary Jewish tallages, and in Christian Visigothic Spain Jews were subjected to a poll tax from which converts to Christianity were exempt. So discriminatory or religion-linked taxation was certainly not some uniquely Islamic invention.

And yes, Western governments today tax populations to fund government, defence, security and public services. I wouldn't falsely call ordinary modern taxation “jizya,” because modern taxes generally are not imposed specifically because someone belongs to another religion. But if your objection is simply, “People under a government pay money toward the state that governs and protects them,” then every modern state does that.

And let's not pretend Western powers historically stopped at taxation. Britain, France, the United States and other colonial powers invaded or dominated foreign countries, seized land, controlled trade, extracted raw materials and wealth, and imposed economic systems that benefited the colonial power. Britain did it throughout India and large parts of its empire; France did it across Algeria and much of Africa; and Western powers repeatedly intervened abroad to protect strategic and economic interests.

We can even look at Venezuela today. In January 2026, U.S. forces kidnapped Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and transported him to the United States. Legal experts questioned whether the military operation was lawful under international law.

Then, months later, the United States secured a major position in Venezuela's oil industry: a company received 100-year rights to 17 Venezuelan oil fields containing about 65 billion barrels of reserves, while the Pentagon obtained a 35% stake and preferential access to the oil. The White House itself boasts that the arrangement gives the U.S. majority control over those 65 billion barrels.

6. Qur'an 9:123 — “fight those nearest to you.”
Again, this is a military verse. Classical tafsir, including Ibn Kathir, discusses fighting the nearest hostile powers and then farther ones. That can legitimately be discussed as part of classical Islamic warfare; it is still not an instruction for an individual Muslim to attack the nearest Christian, Jew or atheist living next door. Turning state warfare into random civilian murder is your addition, not the Qur'an's.

7. Qur'an 47:4 — “strike the necks.”
You left out the most important words: “when you meet [them] in battle.” The verse is explicitly battlefield legislation. After the enemy is subdued, it says to bind the prisoners and then release them freely or for ransom until the war ends. That's almost the exact opposite of your attempt to portray it as a standing order to behead civilians.

8. Qur'an 8:12 — “strike their necks and fingertips.”
This occurs in the account of the Battle of Badr, and the speech in the verse is Allah addressing the angels supporting the believers in that battle. It isn't “Muslims, go around cutting off unbelievers' heads and fingers.” You took a battlefield narrative and removed the battlefield.

9. Qur'an 8:60 — “terrify the enemy.”
It tells a state at war to maintain military strength so enemies are deterred. Then the very next verse, 8:61, says that if the enemy inclines toward peace, Muslims must also incline toward peace. Funny how the “Qur'an is terrorism” screenshots almost never include that next sentence.

10. Qur'an 4:89 and 4:91.
You again skipped 4:90, which says that if these people withdraw, do not fight you and offer you peace, Allah gives Muslims no authority to fight them. Then 4:91 says force is permitted against those who do not withdraw, do not offer peace and do not restrain their hands. That is plainly more than somebody privately changing religion. Your phrase “apostates = kill them” erases the military qualifiers written directly into the passage.

11. Qur'an 5:33 — killing, crucifixion and amputation.
This became the classical law of ḥirābah: armed brigandage/highway robbery, terrorising the public and violent rebellion, with jurists debating its precise boundaries and punishments. It is a penal-law verse about people who “wage war” and spread violent corruption, not “execute people because they aren't Muslim.” Most classical jurists treated ḥirābah as brigandage.

12. Qur'an 2:191 — “kill them wherever you find them.”
This is one of the most dishonest quote-mines because the preceding verse literally says, “Fight … those who fight you but do not transgress.” 2:191 itself refers to expelling those who expelled you, and even says not to fight at the Sacred Mosque unless they fight you there. Then 2:192 says if they cease, Allah is forgiving and merciful.

13. Qur'an 9:111 — “they kill and are killed.”
Yes, believers fighting legitimately in Allah's cause may kill enemy combatants and may themselves be killed. That's called war. Nothing in the verse says “strap explosives to yourself and murder civilians.” In fact, Qur'an 4:29 explicitly says “do not kill yourselves [or one another].” Martyrdom means being killed while obeying Allah; it does not automatically turn suicide into martyrdom because Bin Laden or ISIS says so.

14. Qur'an 3:169–170 — martyrs are alive with their Lord.
Correct: Islam teaches that people legitimately killed in Allah's cause have a special status with Allah. That says absolutely nothing about permission to murder civilians. Saying “terrorists quote this after attacks” proves something about terrorists, not about what the verse permits.

And simply quoting this verse does not magically make their actions Islamic, mean that Allah condones what they did, or guarantee that they are martyrs who will enter Paradise. A person cannot commit acts forbidden by Islam and then declare himself a martyr simply by quoting a verse. Allah judges whether someone was truly fighting in His cause and whether their actions were lawful.

15. Qur'an 3:110–112 and your Hamas claim.
Even if Hamas quotes these verses, Hamas does not get to rewrite the Qur'an. Verse 3:111 specifically says “if they fight you.” More importantly, you stopped at 3:112 because 3:113 immediately says of the People of the Book: “They are not all the same,” and then praises a righteous community among them. So your attempt to turn this into a racial command against every Jew is contradicted by the very next verse.

16. Qur'an 5:51 — Jews and Christians as awliyāʾ.
The word is rendered variously as allies, guardians, protectors or intimate supporters, and classical tafsir discusses political loyalty and alliances. Whatever interpretation one adopts, the verse doesn't say “kill Jews and Christians.” The same Surah, 5:5, explicitly permits Muslims to eat the food of the People of the Book and permits Muslim men to marry chaste women from among them. Apparently Muslims are supposed to marry the people you claim Islam orders them to indiscriminately murder.

17. Qur'an 5:60 — “apes and pigs.”
It does not say “all Jews are apes and pigs.” It speaks about particular people whom Allah punished. The preceding verses describe people who ridicule the believers' religion and prayer. Once again you convert condemnation of a particular group into a racial statement about everyone.

18. Qur'an 17:4–7 — Children of Israel and “servants of great might.”
This is a narrative about two episodes of corruption and punishment involving the Children of Israel. It isn't a command addressed to Muslims saying “go attack Jews.” You also omitted 17:6, where Allah says He then restored victory to the Children of Israel and increased them in wealth and numbers. Whether Abu Obeida later quoted it is irrelevant to what the passage actually says.

19. Qur'an 5:21–23 — “enter through the gate.”
Did you even read who is speaking? This is Moses speaking to the Children of Israel about entering the Holy Land. It isn't Muhammad commanding Muslims to storm Jewish homes. A modern group's choice to use “gate” imagery doesn't travel backwards through time and change the subject of the Qur'anic story.

20. Qur'an 2:120 and 5:82.
2:120 says Jews and Christians will not be satisfied with Muhammad until he follows their religion. It contains no command to harm them whatsoever. 5:82 describes groups that were particularly hostile to the early Muslims, but the same verse says Christians were among those nearest in affection to the believers, and 5:83–85 praises those among them who recognised the truth. Again: description is not an order to commit violence.

21. “ISIS used it,” “Bin Laden quoted it,” “Hamas quoted it,” “Boko Haram used it,” “Hezbollah uses it.”
This is not an argument. A US/Mossad terrorist organisation quoting scripture does not magically become the authoritative interpreter of that scripture. If a murderer quotes the Bible, Torah, Bhagavad Gita, Buddhist texts, Marx or Nietzsche, we don't conclude that the murderer now owns the interpretation of the entire tradition. You have to establish what the text means from its language, context, the verses around it and the legal tradition, not by saying “bad person quoted it.”

22. Qur'an 23:5–6 and 70:29–30 — “those whom the right hand possesses.”
Here is where I won't play the same dishonest game you are playing: classical Islamic law genuinely recognised slavery and concubinage, as did virtually every major pre-modern civilisation. These verses refer to wives and female slaves/concubines. But the word “rape” is not in either verse. If you want to criticise the historical institution of slavery, criticise it honestly; don't replace “female slave/concubine” with “rape victim” and then pretend you translated the Qur'an.

23. Qur'an 4:24 — married women except those whom the right hand possesses.
Again, this is genuinely one of the Qur'an's pre-modern captivity/slavery passages. Classical law treated lawful female war captives differently from free married women. But the verse does not say “rape them,” and replacing the legal category of captivity/concubinage with the word “rape” is your interpretation, not a translation of the verse.

And you're also leaving out the Qur'an's wider rules concerning captives and slaves. Qur'an 24:33 explicitly allows enslaved people to seek a written contract to purchase their freedom and tells their owners to grant such an agreement when there is good in them, even assisting them financially. The same verse explicitly forbids forcing slave women into prostitution when they wish to remain chaste. Qur'an 47:4 also gives release without payment or release for ransom as outcomes for prisoners of war.

So if you want to criticise the historical institution of slavery, do so honestly. But don't pretend the Qur'an simply says, “capture women and rape them.” It doesn't.

24. Qur'an 4:3.
This verse regulates polygyny—up to four wives, conditioned upon justice—and also refers to those whom the right hand possesses. Again: historical slavery existed and Islam regulated an institution that already existed throughout the ancient world. A command to rape women? No. Those words are not there.

The Qur'an elsewhere gives enslaved people a route to contract for their own emancipation, commands financial assistance toward that freedom, and explicitly prohibits forcing slave women into prostitution.

So you can morally criticise pre-modern slavery all you want, but you cannot simply insert the word “rape” into verses that do not say it and then call that an accurate quotation of Islam.

25. Qur'an 33:50.
This gives the Prophet specific marital allowances and mentions women whom his right hand possessed from captives. Again, acknowledging historical slavery is not difficult. What is dishonest is pretending the verse says “rape captured women,” because those words simply are not there.

26. Qur'an 8:41 and 8:69 — war booty.
Yes, pre-modern armies took war booty. 8:41 actually regulates its distribution and assigns a fifth to the Messenger's administration, relatives, orphans, the needy and stranded travellers. Saying “war booty existed” is historically true. Saying therefore “Islam commands rape” is a non sequitur.

27. Qur'an 33:26–27.
These verses describe a specific wartime event: a People-of-the-Book faction that supported the attacking confederates was defeated; some were killed, some captured, and their property passed to the victors. You can debate that historical event, but a description of one war is not “Muslims are ordered to murder every Jew forever.”

28. ISIS, al-Qaeda and similar groups.
ISIS, al-Qaeda and similar organisations can call themselves “Islamic” all they want. That does not make their actions Islamic any more than someone calling himself Christian while murdering innocent people makes murder a Christian teaching. Their indiscriminate killing, terrorism, torture, enslavement and targeting of civilians have been condemned repeatedly by Muslim scholars, Islamic organisations and Muslim-majority governments across the world.

And before you present these organisations as though they simply appeared because Muslims read the Qur'an, perhaps look into who armed, trained, financed, infiltrated, manipulated and used militant groups throughout the Middle East and Afghanistan for geopolitical purposes.

The United States openly backed, armed and financed the Afghan Mujahideen during the Soviet-Afghan war. Hillary Clinton herself publicly acknowledged America's role in supporting these terrorists.

So when you point at ISIS and say, “Look what Islam created,” you're ignoring decades of proxy warfare, intelligence operations, foreign intervention, weapons transfers, occupations, regime change and deliberate exploitation of militant organisations by governments pursuing their own strategic interests.

These organisations also recruit heavily from populations devastated by war. Imagine someone who has watched his children, wife, parents, brothers or sisters killed, had his home destroyed and spent years living through invasion, occupation or bombing. Extremist recruiters take that grief and rage and redirect it into revenge. In some cases a person's hatred becomes stronger than his iman, knowledge and common sense, making him susceptible to people who convince him that revenge and indiscriminate killing are somehow jihad.

That explains how people can be manipulated. It does not excuse their crimes, and it certainly does not make those crimes teachings of Islam.

And Muslims certainly did not sit quietly supporting ISIS. Muslim-majority governments across the world condemned them. The 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation condemned ISIS and its terrorism. Major Islamic institutions such as Al-Azhar condemned their ideology. More than 120 Muslim scholars from around the world issued a detailed open letter to Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi refuting ISIS point by point using the Qur'an, Sunnah and classical Islamic jurisprudence. Muslim scholars condemned their murder of innocents, torture, forced conversion, enslavement and other crimes.

Muslim armies also fought ISIS on the battlefield and died fighting them. Iraqis, Syrians, Kurds and other overwhelmingly Muslim forces suffered enormous casualties, destroying US/Mossad ISIS's so-called caliphate. And the overwhelming majority of ISIS's victims were themselves people living in Muslim countries.

There is also documented evidence that Israel treated wounded ISIS fighters during the Syrian war, including fighters being transferred across the Israeli-controlled frontier for medical treatment.

So don't hand me ISIS, al-Qaeda, Boko Haram or some other extremist organisation as proof of what Islam teaches while completely ignoring who funded militant proxies, who armed them, who exploited regional wars, who infiltrated organisations, who benefited geopolitically from the chaos, and—most importantly—what Islamic scripture and Muslim scholarship actually say about their actions.

ISIS does not define Islam. Al-Qaeda does not define Islam. The CIA does not define Islam. Mossad does not define Islam. Western governments do not define Islam.

The Qur'an and Sunnah define Islam.

And if your argument depends on terrorist organisations rather than what the Qur'an actually commands, then you still haven't proved your claim.

In some cases this has meant entire settlements have been demolished on court order. Any halfway competent journalist should be aware of these things.

The Palestinian Arabs turned this down, repeatedly. If their stated aim is to be free of occupation and their leaders turn down offers to end that occupation, it begs the question of their repeated refusal to take yes for an answer? On this Andrew has nothing to say.

3. Some settlers break the law and attack innocent Arabs. This is contemptible for sure. Yet what is smuggled in under the category of "settler violence" demonstares that it is another concocted antisemitic libel, for in UN reports Jewish primary school children visiting an historic Jewish site in Samaria is cosidered "settler violence" (presumably becuse they were accompanied by armed security guards). Similarly visits by Jews to the Temple Mount are classified by the UN as settler violence and efforts by Jews to recover livestock stolen by Arabs are also classed as settler violence.

4. The long hoped for two state solution? This is insanity? 

The Palestinian Arab leadership have turned down six offers of partition. Neither have they initiated any peace proposal that envisaged a Jewish state alongside an Arab state.

If the Arabs wanted it, the two-state solution has been on the table for 90 years, they have declined every offer. 

Meanwhile, every inch of the land of Israel given over to Arab self-rule has been used as a base to indoctrinate hatred and to wage war against the jewish inhabitants of the land (which by the way is exactly what Fatah promised in their plan for the staged liberation of Palestine).

Insisting there is still hope for a two state solution- is like insisting there is still hope of a marriage when the girl has already said no on six previous occasions, often voicing violent opposition to the suggestion.

5. Despite all of the above, there is already an Arab Palestine nd had been since 1946. It is called Jordan and it sits on roughly 80% of the territory of the Mandate for Palestine.

This is historically illiterate garbage and my comments relate only to the first 28 seconds of his nonsense. if I heard this from a man down the pub I would be shocked at his ignorance. That this comes from a former senior BBC journalist is at least revealing.
