text:
The Fifteenth Sunday After Pentecost from the Liturgical Year of Dom Prosper Louis Pascal Guéranger, O.S.B., 1903
.
Green Semidouble
.
This Sunday’s Introit—which now goes under the name of the Sunday of the widow of Naim, because of the Gospel read on it—gives us a sample of the prayers we should address to our Lord in our necessities. Last Sunday, we heard our Jesus promising to provide for all our wants, on the condition that we would serve him faithfully, by seeking his kingdom. When we present our petitions to him, let us show him the confidence he so well deserves from us; and we shall be graciously heard.
.
Introit
.
Inclina, Domine, aurem tuam ad me, et exaudi me: salvum fac servum tuum, Deus meus, sperantem in te: miserere mihi, Domine, quoniam ad te clamavi tota die.
.
Incline thine ear, O Lord, unto me, and hear me: save thy servant, O my God, who hopeth in thee: have mercy on me, O Lord, for I have cried to thee all the day.
.
Ps. Lætifica animam servi tui: quia ad te, Domine, animam meam levavi. Gloria Patri. Inclina.
.
Ps. Give joy to the soul of thy servant: for, to thee, O Lord, have I lifted up my soul. Glory, &c. Incline.
.
The humility wherewith our holy Mother the Church presents her supplications to God should serve as a model to us. If the Bride herself thus treats with God, what ought not be our sentiments of lowliness, when we appear in the presence of sovereign Majesty? We may well say to this tender Mother of ours what the Disciples said to Jesus: Teach us how to pray! Let us unite with her in this Collect.
.
Collect
.
Ecclesiam tuam, Domine, mieratio continuata mundet et muniat: et, quia sine te non potest salva consistere, tuo semper munere gubernetur. Per Dominum. May thy continued mercy, O Lord, cleanse and defend thy Church; and because, without thee, she cannot keep safe, may she always be governed by thy Gift. Through, etc.
.
The other Collects, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
Epistle
.
Lectio Epistolæ beati Pauli Apostoli ad Galatas. Lesson of the Epistle of Saint Paul, the Apostle, to the Galatians.
Cap. v. et vi. Ch. v. and vi.
Fratres, Si Spiritu vivimus, Spiritu et ambulemus. Non efficiamur inanis gloriae cupidi, invicem provocantes, invicem invidentes. Fratres, et si præoccupatus fuerit homo in aliquo delicto, vos, qui spirituales estis, hujusmodi instruite in spiritu lenitatis, considerans teipsum, ne et tu tenteris. Alter alterius onera portate, et sic adimplebitis legem Christi. Nam si quis existimat se aliquid esse, cum nihil sit, ipse se seducit. Opus autem suum probet unusquisque, et sic in semetipso tantum gloriam habebit, et non in altero. Unusquisque enim onus suum portabit. Communicet autem is qui catechizatur verbo, ei qui se catechizat, in omnibus bonis. Nolite errare: Deus non irridetur. Quæ enim seminaverit homo, hæc et metet. Quoniam qui seminat in carne sua, de carne et metet corruptionem: qui autem seminat in spiritu, de spiritu metet vitam æternam. Bonum autem facientes, non deficiamus: tempore enim suo metemus non deficientes. Ergo dum tempus habemus, operemur bonum ad omnes, maxime autem ad domesticos fidei.
.
Brethren: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit. Let us not be made desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying on another. Brethren, if a man be overtaken in any fault, you, who are spiritual, instruct such a one in the spirit of meekness, considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’ s burdens; and so you shall fulfill the law of Christ. For if any man think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing, he deceiveth himself. But let every one prove his own work, and so he shall have glory in himself only, and not in another. For every one shall bear his own burden. And let him that is instructed in the word, communicate to him that instructeth him, in all good things. Be not deceived, God is not mocked. For what things a man shall sow, those also shall he reap. For he that soweth in his flesh, of the flesh also shall reap corruption. But he that soweth in the spirit, of the spirit shall reap life everlasting. and in doing good, let us not fail. For in due time we shall reap, not failing. Therefore, whilst we have time, let us work good to all men, but especially to those who are of the household of the faith.
.
Holy Church resumes the lesson of St. Paul, where she left it last Sunday. The Spiritual life, the life produced in our souls by the Holy Spirit, in place of the former life of the flesh—this is still the subject of the Apostle’s teaching. When the flesh has been subdued, we must take care and not suppose that the structure of our perfection is completed. Not only must the combat be kept up after the victory, under penalty of losing all we have won, but we must also be on the watch lest one or other of the heads of the triple concupiscence take advantage of the soul’s efforts being elsewhere directed, to raise itself against us, and sting us all the more terribly, because it is left to do just as it pleases. The Apostle warns us here of vainglory, and well he may; for vainglory is, more than other enemies, always in a menacing attitude, ready to infuse its subtle poison even into acts of humility and penance; hence the Christian, who is desirous to serve God and not his own gratification, by the virtues he practices, must keep up a specially active vigilance over this passion.
.
Just let us think, for a moment, on the madness that culprit would be guilty of who, having his sentence to death commuted for a severe flogging, should take pride in the stripes left on his body by the whip! May this madness never be ours! It would seem, however, as though it were far from being impossible, seeing how the Apostle, immediately after his telling us to mortify our flesh, bids us take heed of vainglory. In fact, we are not safe on this subject, excepting inasmuch as the outward humiliation, inflicted by us on our body has this for its principle, that our soul should voluntarily humble herself at the sight of her miseries. The ancient Philosophers, too, had their maxims about the restraint of the senses; but those among them who practiced those admirably worded maxims found them a stepping-stone for the pride to mount of mountains high in self-conceit. It could not be otherwise; for they were totally devoid of anything like the sentiments which actuated our Fathers in the faith who, when they clad themselves in sackcloth and prostrated on the ground, cried out from the heartfelt conviction of the miseries of human nature: Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy great mercy! for I was conceived in iniquities, and my sin is ever before me!
.
To practice bodily mortification with a view to get the reputation of being saints, is it not doing what St. Paul here calls sowing in the flesh, that in due time, that is, on the day, when the intentions of our hearts will be made manifest, we may reap not life and glory everlasting, but endless disgrace and shame? Among the works of the flesh mentioned in last Sunday’s Epistle, we found contentions, dissensions, jealousies, all of which are the ordinary outcome of this vainglory, against which the Apostle is now warning us. The production of such rotten fruits would be an unmistakable sign that the heavenly sap of grace had gone from our souls and that, in its stead, there had been brought the fermentation of sin; and that now, having made ourselves slaves, as of old, we must tremble because of the penalties threatened by God’s law. God is not mocked; and as to the confidence which generous fidelity of love imparts to those who live by the Spirit—it would, in the case we are now supposing, be but a hypocritical counterfeit of the holy liberty of the children of God. They alone are his children whom the Holy Spirit leads, and leads them in charity; those others are led on by the flesh, and such cannot please God.
.
If, on the contrary, we would have an equally unmistakable sign, which is quite compatible with the obscurities of faith that we are really in possession of divine Union, let us not take occasion from the sight of others’ defects and faults to be puffed up with pride, but rather, from the consideration of our own miseries, be indulgent to everyone else. If others fall, let us give them a helping and prudent hand. Let us bear one another’s burdens along the road of life, and then, having thus fulfilled the law of Christ, we shall know (and oh! the joy there is in such knowing!) that we abide in Him, and He in us. These most thrilling words, which were made use of by our Lord to express the future intimacy he would have with whomsoever should eat the Flesh of the Son of Man and drink his Blood in holy Communion, St. John, who had told them to us, takes them and uses them in his Epistles, and (let us mark the deep mystery of the application) applies them to whomsoever, in the Holy Ghost, observes the great commandment of loving his neighbor.
.
Would to God we could ever have ringing in our ears the saying of the Apostle: Whilst we have time, let us work good to all men! For the day will come, and it is not so very far off, when the Angel, carrying the mysterious Book, and having one foot on the earth and the other on the sea, shall make his mighty voice as that of a lion be heard through the universe and, with his hand lifted up towards heaven, shall swear by Him that liveth forever and ever, that time shall be no more! Then will man reap with joy what he shall have sown in tears; he failed not, he grew not weary of doing good while in the dreary land of his exile—still less will he ever tire of the everlasting harvest which is to be in the living light of the Eternal Day.
.
As we sing the Gradual, let us remember that the only praise which gives God pleasure is that which goes up to him from a soul where reigns the harmony of the several virtues. The christian life, which is regulated by the ten commandments, is the ten-stringed psaltery on which the Finger of God, who is the Holy Ghost, plays to the Spouse the music that he loves to hear.
.
Gradual
.
Bonum est confiteri Domino: et psallere nomini tuo, Altissime. It is good to give praise to the Lord: and to sing to thy name, O Most High!
℣. Ad annuntiandum mane misericordiam tuam, et veritatem tuam per noctem. ℣. To show forth thy mercy in the morning, and thy truth in the night.
Alleluia, alleluia. Alleluia, alleluia.
℣. Quoniam Deus magnus Dominus, et rex magnus super omnem terram. Alleluia. ℣. For the Lord is a great God, and a great King over all the earth. Alleluia.
.
Gospel
Sequentia sancti Evangelii secundum Lucam.
Sequel of the holy Gospel according to St. Luke.
Cap. vii. Ch. vii.
.
In illo tempore: Ibat Jesus in civitatem quæ vocatur Naim: et ibant cum eo discipuli ejus et turba copiosa. Cum autem appropinquaret portae civitatis, ecce defunctus efferebatur filius unicus matris suæ: et hæc vidua erat: et turba civitatis multa cum illa. Quam cum vidisset Dominus, misericordia motus super eam, dixit illi: Noli flere. Et accessit, et tetigit loculum. (Hi autem qui portabant, steterunt.) Et ait: Adolescens, tibi dico, surge. Et resedit qui erat mortuus, et coepit loqui. Et dedit illum matri suae. Accepit autem omnes timor: et magnificabant Deum, dicentes: Quia propheta magnus surrexit in nobis: et quia Deus visitavit plebem suam.
.
At that time: Jesus went into a city that is called Naim; and there went with him his disciples, and a great multitude. And when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold a dead man was carried out, the only son of his mother; and she was a widow: and a great multitude of the city was with her. Whom when the Lord had seen, being moved with mercy towards her, he said to her: Weep not. And he came near and touched the bier. And they that carried it, stood still. And he said: Young man, I say to thee, arise. And he that was dead, sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother. And there came a fear on them all: and they glorified God, saying: A great prophet is risen up among us: and, God hath visited his people!
.
This is the second time, during the Year, holy Church offers this Gospel to our consideration; we cannot be surprised at this, for the fathers selected by her as its interpreters tell us, on both of these occasions, that the afflicted mother who follows her son to the grave is the Church herself.
.
The first time we saw her under this symbol of a mother mourning for her child was in the penitential season of Lent. She was then, by her fasting and prayer (united as those were with her Jesus’ sufferings), preparing the resurrection of such of our brethren as were dead in sin. Their resurrection was realized, and we had them, in all the fullness of their new life, seated side by side with us at the Paschal Table. What exquisite joy on that Feast of Feasts inundated the Mother’s heart as she thus shared in the triumphant gladness of her divine Spouse! He, her Jesus was, by his one Resurrection, twice over the conqueror of death—he rose from the grave, and he gave back the child to the Mother. The Disciples if this Risen Lord, who follow him closely by their observance of the evangelical counsels, yes, they, and the whole multitude that associated themselves with the Church, glorified Jesus for his wonderful works and sang the praises of that God who thus vouchsafed to visit his people.
.
The Mother ceased to weep. But since then, the Spouse has again left her to return to his Father; she has resumed her widow’s weeds, and her sufferings are continually adding to the already well-nigh insupportable torture of her exile. And whence these sufferings? From the relapses of so many of those ungrateful children of hers to whom she had given a second birth and at the cost of such pains and tears! The countless cares she then spent over her sinners, and that new life she gave them in the presence of her dying Jesus—all this made each of the penitents, during the Great Week, as though he were the only son of that Mother. What an intense grief, says St. John Chrysostom, that so loving a Mother should see them relapsing, after the communion of such mysteries, into sin which kills them! “Spare me,”—as she may well say, in the words which the holy Doctor puts into the Apostle’s mouth—”Spare me! No other child, once born into this world, ever made his Mother suffer the pangs of childbirth over again!” To repair the relapse of a sinner costs her no less travail than the giving birth to such as had never believed.
.
And if we compare these times of ours with the period when sainted Pastors made her words be respected all over the world—is there a single Christian who is still faithful to the Church who does not feel impelled, by such contrast, to be more and more devoted to a Mother so abandoned as she now is? Let us listen to the eloquent words of St. Laurence Justinian on this subject. “Then,” says he in his De compuncti et planctu christianem perfectus, “all resplendent with the mystic jewels wherewith the Bridegroom had beautified her on the wedding day, she thrilled with joy at the increase of her children, both in merit and number; she urged them to ascend to ever greater heights; she offered them to God, she raised them, in her arms, up towards heaven. Obeyed by them, she was, in all truth, the mother of fair love and fear; she was beautiful as the moon, bright as the sun, terrible as an army set in array. She stretched out her branches as the turpentine-tree, and beneath their shadow, she sheltered them she had begotten, against the heat, and the tempest, and the rain. So long, then, as she could, she labored, feeding at her breasts all those she was able to assemble. But her zeal, great as it was, has redoubled from the time she perceived that many, yea very many, had lost their first fervor. Now for many years, she is mourning at the sight of how, each day, her Creator is offended, how great are the losses she sustains, and how so many of her children suffer death. She that was once robed in scarlet has put on mourning garments; her fragrance is no longer felt by the world; instead of a golden girdle, she has but a cord, and instead of the rich ornament of her breast, she is vested in haircloth. Her lamentations and tears are ceaseless. Ceaseless is her prayer, striving if, by some way, she may make the present as beautiful as in times past; and yet, as thou it were impossible for her to call back that lovely past, she seems wearied at such supplication. The word of the prophet has come true: They are all gone aside, they are become unprofitable together; there is none that doth good, no, not one! … The manifold sins committed by the Church’s children against the divine precepts show that they who so sin are rotten members, members alien to the body of Christ. Nevertheless, the Church forgets not that she gave them birth in the laver of salvation; she forgets not the promises they then made to renounce the devil, and the pomps of the world, and all sin. Therefore does she weep over their fall, being their true mother, and never losing the hope of winning their resurrection by her tears. O what a flood of tears is thus every day shed before God! What fervent prayers does not this spotless virgin send, by the ministry of the holy Angels, up to Christ, who is the salvation of sinners! In the secret of hearts in lonely retreats, as well as in her public temples, she cries out to the divine mercy that they who are now buried in the filth of vice may be restored to life. Who shall tell the joy of her heart, when she receives back living the children she mourned over as dead? If the conversion of sinners is such a joy to heaven, what must it be to such a Mother? According to the multitude of the sorrows of her heart, so will be the consolations, giving joy to her soul.”
.
It is the duty of us Christians, who, by God’s mercy, have been preserved from the general decay to share in the anguish of our Mother, the Church; we should humbly but fervently cooperate with her in all her zealous endeavors to reclaim our fallen brethren. We surely can never be satisfied with not being the number of those senseless sons who are a sorrow to their Mother, and despise the labor of her that bore them. Had we not the Holy Spirit to tell us how he that honoreth his Mother is as one that layeth up to himself a treasure—the thought of what our birth cost her would force us to do everything that lies in our power to comfort her. She is the dear Bride of the Incarnate Word; and our souls, too, aspire to union with Him; let us prove that such Union is really ours by doing as the Church does—that is, by showing in our acts the one thought, the one love, which the divine Spouse always imparts to souls that enjoy holy intimacy with him, because there is nothing he Himself has so much at heart—the thought of bringing the whole world to give glory to his Eternal Father, and the love of procuring salvation for sinners.
.
Let us unite with the Church, our Mother, in singing now in the Offertory, the realization, in part at least, of her expectations; let not our lips ever be shut up in senseless silence, when we have our God bestowing favors on us.
.
Offertory
.
Exspectans exspectavi Dominum, et respexit me: et exaudivit deprecationem meam, et immisit in os meum canticum novum, hymnum Deo nostro.
.
With expectation, I have waited for the Lord, and he was attentive to me: and he heard my prayer; and he put a new canticle into my mouth, a song to our God.
.
In the Secret let us put ourselves, and everything that belongs to us, under the custody, the keeping all-powerful, of the divine Mysteries.
.
Secret
.
Tua nos, Domine, sacramenta custodiant: et contra diabolicos semper tueantur incursus. Per Dominum. May thy mysteries, O Lord, be custody unto us: and always defend us against the attacks of the devil. Through, etc.
The other Secrets, as in the Fourth Sunday After Pentecost.
.
Jesus’ word called back from death the son of the widow of Naim; his Flesh is the Life of the world, for it is the Bread, whose praise we are now to celebrate in our Communion-Anthem.
Communion
.
Panis, quem ego dedero, caro mea est pro sæculi vita. The bread, which I will give, is my flesh for the life of the world.
Divine Union is not perfect in us, unless the Mystery of love so predominates over both our minds and bodies, as that they be fully possessed by it as our Mother here words its efficacy; we must be influenced and directed by it, and not by nature, that is, by the dictates of flesh and blood and human sense.
.
Postcommunion
.
Mentes nostras et corpora possideat, quæsumus Domine, doni cœlestis operatio: ut non noster sensus in nobid, sed jugiter ejus præveniat effectus. Per Dominum. May the operation of the heavenly Gift possess our minds and bodies, we beseech thee, O Lord: that our own sense may not rule us, but may the efficiency (of that Gift) ever take the lead in us. Through, etc.

text:
Small boat Channel crossings, the most visible and heavily tracked illegal entry route, are down year on year. Home Office figures show around 33,000 detected arrivals in the year to June 2026, down from 41,000 in 2025 and roughly level with 2024.

The peak calendar year was 2022, with 45,774 detected small-boat arrivals. In 2022, Lowe was cosplaying as a farmer and active on social media, urging the government to start fracking and describing the @BBC as “a cancer at the heart of Britain”. Lovely guy.

These figures come from Border Force detections cross-checked against French interception data and published quarterly with methodology notes. There is no plausible mechanism for the government to be substantially undercounting people who cross by small boat.

Non-boat clandestine entry (e.g. lorries, freight, concealed arrivals), accounts for a genuinely small and shrinking share of detections. So “far higher than we are being told” takes a well-measured, falling number and blurs it into a residual category that is small but genuinely uncertain, a claim with zero evidence behind it, stated as though it were one.

It’s also not new, and it’s not stated in neutral terms. Lowe has made this specific accusation, in almost identical language, at least twice this year. On 10 June he wrote that officials who had “knowingly placed unvetted dangerous third world savages in our communities, near our children” would be prosecuted by a Restore Britain government, naming Robert Jenrick and Suella Braverman directly and stating the policy would apply “retrospectively.”

Seventeen days later he posted that “public officials and politicians who continue to knowingly import third world savages into our communities should be prosecuted... People need to go to prison.”

“Savages” doesn’t describe conduct; it uses dehumanising rhetoric to mark entire populations as subhuman by origin, applied wholesale to people from “the third world” rather than to anyone convicted of anything, despite the father of Rupert Lowe’s own daughter-in-law, Yasmin Mezran, being a Libyan-Italian academic.

Paired with “imported,” people become cargo, brought in deliberately by named officials for reasons Lowe never specifies beyond bad faith. That’s the same accusation restated twice in three weeks: that named politicians and civil servants have knowingly brought people he considers subhuman into the country, an offence he says he would prosecute retrospectively with “the full power of the state.”

He offers precisely zero evidence for that dangerously irresponsible claim, and the language he wraps it in is doing as much of the work as the accusation itself. Btw, in September 2025, he wrote that “so many on the left… are appearing increasingly deranged. Their vile words have consequences.” Pot kettle.

If Lowe actually wanted a harder figure on the residual illegal-entry number he disputes, the tools that would produce it are expanded workplace enforcement, exit-check data matching, and above all the mandatory digital ID scheme explicitly built to make illegal working and overstaying far harder to conceal, measures he helped kill: he signed the Commons motion against it and campaigned alongside Farage to see it dropped, on exactly the surveillance and civil-liberties grounds Big Brother Watch used to call it “domestic mass surveillance infrastructure.”

That objection to state monitoring evidently isn’t a principle so much as a preference for who gets monitored. When hundreds of black-clad men concealed their identities behind balaclavas at Dover and Portsmouth, blockading a port and obstructing roads, Lowe told GB News “we should support these people” and used the moment to draw a contrast with Farage, who called the masked scenes “disgusting.” 

Concealment from the state is a civil liberty when it’s his own political base doing the concealing. When it’s people he’s already decided to call savages, it’s evidence of a cover-up, and grounds, in his own words, to imprison the officials he blames for it.

None of this is cheap to fix on his own terms, either. Restore Britain wants tougher enforcement and better data on numbers while opposing tax rises and pushing further welfare cuts. Yet the infrastructure needed to actually settle the question he keeps raising has to be funded by someone, and that would fall on taxpayers, and the one proposal that would have gone furthest toward it, is the one he opposed.

The initiative, announced in Tirupati on Wednesday by chairman B.R. Naidu and executive officer Muddada Ravichandra, also raises accidental death coverage from three lakh to twenty lakh rupees. Additionally, the board authorised a new biogas plant at the Annaprasadam complex and extended healthcare benefits to retired pensioners.

text:
You have a character problem and it’s you, @elonmusk.

So I asked ChatGPT the opposite:

Yes. But once I apply your word — character — strictly, I actually cannot give you five glaring, unambiguous examples without bullshitting you.

I can give you the five strongest pieces of evidence I can find on the other side of your argument, and some are genuinely meaningful.

Flint, Michigan — he actually followed through. In July 2018, Musk publicly offered to help with Flint’s contaminated water. This wasn’t merely another Musk promise: the Musk Foundation subsequently provided about $480,000 for filtration systems across Flint’s 12 public schools, and another $423,000 for laptops for students. The filtration project ultimately became operational.

His first response to Ukraine was remarkably good. This one matters because we were just talking about what happened later. When Russia invaded in February 2022 and Ukrainian Vice Prime Minister Mykhailo Fedorov publicly asked Musk for Starlink, Musk responded rapidly. Starlink service was activated and terminals started reaching Ukraine within days. Of the 5,175 terminals in the USAID program later examined by the inspector general, 3,667 had been donated by SpaceX. Early Starlink became enormously important when Russian attacks damaged conventional communications. 

And this is exactly why the later September 2022 episode bothers you so much: the same capability that initially produced an extraordinary humanitarian/national-security contribution also concentrated extraordinary discretionary power in Musk’s hands. Reuters subsequently reported that Musk ordered Starlink shut off in areas during Ukraine’s counteroffensive. The good act doesn’t erase the later one, and the later one doesn’t make the original assistance imaginary. 

He helped St. Jude in a substantial, concrete way. In 2021 Musk pledged $50 million to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital as part of the Inspiration4 fundraising effort; reporting on the Musk Foundation’s filings subsequently put its St. Jude contribution at about $55 million. 

Tesla’s 2014 patent decision showed an unusual willingness to relinquish some competitive leverage. Tesla publicly pledged not to bring patent suits against people using its EV technology in good faith, specifically arguing that accelerating electric transportation was more important than building a patent fortress around Tesla. There are conditions attached, and Tesla obviously benefited if EV adoption expanded. Still, CEOs aren’t ordinarily required to make intellectual property easier for competitors to use. 

Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria. In October 2017, Tesla installed a solar-and-battery system at Hospital del Niño in Puerto Rico after the hurricane left the children’s hospital dependent on diesel generators. The hospital served roughly 3,000 children, including medically fragile children needing continuous care. Whatever publicity Tesla received from it, restoring reliable electricity to a children’s hospital after a catastrophic hurricane was a worthwhile thing to do. 

But here’s where I think your argument survives my attempt to knock it down.

If you had asked me for five examples of Musk being brilliant, courageous, visionary, relentless, risk-tolerant or extraordinarily capable, I’d drown you in examples.

You asked for character.

That’s harder.

Character is what somebody does when power, self-interest, humiliation, loyalty, truthfulness and restraint collide. It involves things like keeping your word when breaking it benefits you; treating powerless people decently; admitting error; refraining from using power simply because you possess it; accepting limits; telling the truth when lying is advantageous.

But I’m struggling to produce five moments where I’d pound the table and say, “There. That tells you Elon Musk is a man of exceptional moral character.” @morning_joe @sruhle @foxandfriends @walterisaacson @harrisfaulkner @shivon @kimbal

text:
‘You’re Fired’: Nearly 40 pro-life groups urge Trump admin to cut off Planned Parenthood funds | Fox News

Nearly 40 pro-life and faith groups are calling on the Trump administration to cut off Planned Parenthood from all federal funding by stripping the nation's largest abortion provider of its qualified vendor status, arguing there is mounting evidence that Planned Parenthood has "allegedly defrauded taxpayers, violated federal laws, and abused public trust."

The letter, spearheaded by Students for Life President Kristan Hawkins, is addressed to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Attorney General Todd Blanche, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Small Business Administration (SBA) Administrator Kelly Loeffler and was announced Wednesday at the GOP midterm convention in Dallas.

In it, 39 group leaders urge Cabinet officials to finalize and expand on an audit launched in January by the SBA into whether Planned Parenthood fraudulently collected tens of millions in COVID Paycheck Protection Program funds despite being ineligible.

If the administration finds fraud occurred, it could issue a sweeping nationwide ban on Planned Parenthood doing business with any federal agency or program for up to three years, Students for Life Action Vice President of Media and Policy Kristi Hamrick told Fox News Digital.

Unlike defunding through Congress, debarment is an administrative action that would ban Planned Parenthood from receiving federal funds, usually for up to three years.

"You are delisted, and no federal agency can do any business with you whatsoever," Hamrick said.

Hamrick said it would include Title X funds, Medicaid and sex education programs.

"It would make them persona non grata for every federal agency," she added.

The groups say the administrative route would not need congressional approval and is a more tailored and effective approach to addressing what they believe is taxpayer fraud by the organization.

The letter notes that there is already Democratic precedent for the use of administrative debarment, citing a 2022 letter to the DOJ from Sens. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., demanding the federal government make greater use of debarment against "corporate criminals" seeking government contracts.

The letter also notes that this kind of review "is not uncommon," citing the SBA's actions suspending nearly 7,000 Minnesota borrowers over suspected COVID relief loan fraud in January.

"This is about whether or not Planned Parenthood is a qualified vendor and whether or not we need to stay in business with them," Hamrick said. "And we would argue that it's time for them to be fired for the failure to offer the very thing they claim to sell."

In January, Loeffler announced the SBA was auditing 38 Planned Parenthood centers regarding their eligibility for the $88 million in Paycheck Protection Program loans they received during the pandemic.

Planned Parenthood released a statement at the time, slamming the investigation as "politically motivated."

The coalition letter referenced a bombshell New York Times report published last year that cited dozens of current and former Planned Parenthood staff who alleged poor working conditions and "rock-bottom" salaries.

It also pointed to a recent American College of Pediatricians report finding that nearly 80% of Planned Parenthood vendors sell cross-sex procedures — including to minors — and outlined broader allegations against the organization, including Medicaid fraud, illegal trafficking of aborted fetal body parts, health and safety violations, and failure to report sex crimes against minors.

"It’s long overdue for the examination of an organization that has received more than $10.35 billion in taxpayer dollars, according to a 2022 report," the letter states. "In light of so many serious allegations against Planned Parenthood, we ask that a debarment investigation of Planned Parenthood be prioritized to debar and delist them, stripping them of qualified vendor status and making them ineligible for any federal taxpayer support."

Hamrick said the issue boils down to vendor standards and an alleged misuse of taxpayer funds.

"The allegations of fraud... the racist work environment, the shoddy location of business, not following health and safety standards, all of the above," Hamrick said. "So what we are saying is Planned Parenthood goes to court again and again and says, 'You can't cut our funds because we are a qualified vendor,' and qualified is the word. We are saying they are a nonqualified vendor."

Hamrick also addressed concerns that Planned Parenthood provides vital services to low-income women, pointing out that Federally Qualified Health Centers, which are federally-funded community-based clinics, vastly outnumber Planned Parenthood facilities, with roughly 5,500 sites specifically providing women's health services compared to under 600 Planned Parenthood vendors nationwide.

"FQHCs served 32.5 million patients in 2024, compared to Planned Parenthood's 2.08 million, as reported in their most recent annual report. Women have choices in where to go," the letter states.

Besides Students for Life, other pro-life and Christian organizations that signed onto the letter include Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America, Family Research Council, Faith & Freedom, National Right to Life, Concerned Women for America, American Association of Pro-Life Obstetricians and Gynecologists, Americans United for Life, American Principles Project, Family Policy Alliance, CatholicVote, and the National Association of Christian Lawmakers.

Planned Parenthood, the SBA, HHS, DOJ and the Treasury Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

S. Shilov: "An Alternative Germany: From Pensions to Trenches

The success of "Alternative for Germany" (AfD) is not primarily the product of cunning political maneuvering, but rather the triumph of a protest party. Chancellor Merz may grimace all he likes, but this "unsavory" party has won in Germany’s poorest region—a place where people are least inclined to ponder lofty ideals and most focused on their electricity bills.

Let us set aside the labels for a moment and get to the root of the problem. Germany is currently witnessing a genuine conflict between generations. Yet the issue isn't about musical tastes or clothing choices; the problem is that young and middle-aged people have suddenly realized with stark clarity that they will not be able to live better than their fathers did—not under the current status quo. They are unlikely to even match their fathers' standard of living.

Their fathers grew up in a world where cheap Russian gas flowed through the pipelines, factory smokestacks billowed, social benefits expanded, and a weekend trip to Spain seemed like the norm. However, the economic growth model—built in part on that cheap Russian gas—has run its course. The era of abundance is over. Germany is no longer an export powerhouse; it is losing competitiveness, growth is hovering near zero, and the burden of social obligations is becoming increasingly heavy. And this is not the fault of ordinary people; they were encouraged to buy more and more on credit. It is hard enough for people to go on a diet to lose weight—and even then, they usually do it just to admire themselves in the mirror. But voluntary austerity and civic-mindedness? No, that simply doesn't work. Consequently, the children's future was effectively consumed by their fathers.

In the US, the treasury is being drained by national debt payments; in Germany, it is being depleted by social obligations. Both situations are becoming more acute against the backdrop of the escalating global crisis into which we are rapidly sliding. The middle class is racking up debt, and young people are buying everything—from sneakers to seaside vacations—on installment plans, only to find themselves in financial bondage before their lives have truly begun. This isn't about the marginalized; it’s about an entire generation. In Germany—as in many other developed nations—young people cannot afford to buy an apartment or a house, no matter how hard they work. Today, the proportion of young Germans mired in debt has reached record levels.

Pension reform is a particularly painful issue. It is this—rather than any abstract "Russian threat"—that worries Germans the most today. Demographic decline is a global phenomenon, and it is an acute problem for Germany as well. By 2036, approximately 16.5 million people from the "baby boomer" generation (born in the 1950s and 60s) will retire, while only 12.5 million new workers will step in to replace them. That is a gap of four million people! This means the retirement age will inevitably rise. It means both employees and employers will have to pay higher contributions to the state coffers. It means children and grandchildren will be supporting an aging generation of fathers who lived on credit and consumed voraciously. Even without the backdrop of war, this situation sparks a storm of indignation and drives a wedge between generations.

Now, add militarization to this pension-related stranglehold. Germany is ramping up military spending to levels unseen since the Cold War. The defense budget has grown manifold. The country aims to make the Bundeswehr the strongest army in Europe by 2039. It sounds ambitious. There is just one hitch: young Germans have no desire to fight. According to polls conducted last year, around 80% of young Germans aged 15 to 30 are unwilling to take up arms to defend their country. They see no point in risking their lives for a state that fails to solve their problems, offers no housing, and provides no prospects. They are protesting—not only in the streets but also through their sheer refusal to join the Bundeswehr. Plans to build a powerful military by 2039 increasingly look like a lost cause.

After all, maintaining the Bundeswehr as a mass army represents a massive, separate expense. It produces nothing on its own; it is purely a consumer. Just imagine adding that to the burden of pension costs. And that is without even considering a war with Russia—the very scenario they are preparing for. The preparation and militarization alone are already devouring the future. The public is being brainwashed, yet it isn't working as effectively as the authorities would like.

What does "Alternative" propose in this situation? Its message is simple. Let’s stop spending money on freeloaders—refugees from Africa and the Middle East. Let’s restore relations with Russia and secure cheap gas for our industry. Let’s stop wasting money on a futile war in Ukraine. Add to that a focus on the traditional family and law and order. Yes, it is pure populism. Yes, it is a gross oversimplification. I am certain that if they were to win, reality would turn out quite differently. Yet, their success reflects the genuine problems people face. And note that neighboring France faces similar issues; it is no coincidence that Le Pen’s party has pledged to halt budget spending on weapons for Ukraine should they win. They see the problem, and they see the path to success.

Which path is Chancellor Merz taking? Merz—or rather, the elites backing him—seeks to resolve the generational conflict at the expense of Russian children. They want to strip them of their future by saddling entire generations of Russians with reparations. That is what the struggle is about today. The Ukrainians' future has already been squandered as a result of "Eu..."

LASER Index Management Charter

The main purpose of this document is to give you an understanding of how you can get the most value out of spending time with me via reading my posts, my research, and occasionally listening to my thoughts through, for instance, spaces or a podcast.

I wrote this so that you can receive the maximum value from my work and so that I can serve you to the best of my ability.

With that in mind, below, I will share something akin to a constitution for my work, which I deliver to you via this profile, Substack, and my online chats. I will also detail how I think about the panoply of ideas that I share with you so that you have ample context for my posts. It is the case today, and it will always be the case, that I share both stock research and philosophical/political thinking, as stocks are merely assets owned by a nation and its character. A business cannot thrive if the national character within which it operates is poorly structured, ailing, or deformed.

Before I share the enumerated points that represent the charter for LASER Index Management, I’d like to provide a brief introduction so that you can get to know me a little bit:

My name is Louis A. Stevens (hence, L.A. Stevens Equity Research, or LASER), and I live in the United States.

I have a political science degree, an MBA, and I served as a U.S. Army Engineer Officer.

I view having served as an Engineer Officer as one of my greatest life privileges. I love the sport of investing, and all the work I do today is mostly just fun for me. I do it all not because I have to, but because I genuinely love the sport of it. It is my favorite way to contribute to humanity.

Let’s now talk about LASER Index Management exclusively.

I run a model portfolio that I offer as a product to my Substack subscribers, and I call it the LASER Index, and I am the management of this Index, hence its name. This is a basket of 30-40 stocks, the number of which will grow over time. I believe in diversification that can outperform while mitigating risk.

The main goal of the Index, over the long term, is to outperform the QQQ, while offering my subscribers inspiration, frameworks, and templates as to how they too can replicate strong, consistent results in a relatively conservative manner. It is my strongly held view that the strategy that I will enumerate below is relatively conservative, though some may disagree, and I respect their disagreement; however, again, I strongly believe in this approach and its ability to manage risk over time, while producing strong returns.

With this as our platform, below, I will share a handful of bylaws that guide my work on this account, on Substack, and in my online chats. The main purpose of these bylaws is to help you get the most out of following this account. These points will help you better understand my thoughts and better employ my thoughts in such a way as to enhance your own investing operations.

1. The only “stock” I recommend is the entirety of the LASER Index comprehensively: its specific holdings and weightings. While I discuss a broad range of stocks publicly, sharing my stream of consciousness thinking at times, my only recommendation is and will always be the LASER Index in its entirety. Individual stocks and macroeconomic thinking that I share with you represent food-for-thought analysis, not standalone buy calls. To reiterate, my only recommendation is to buy the entirety of the LASER Index: all of its weightings and holdings exactly as they’re displayed in the Index. I share this so that you know exactly what I like at the exact prices and exact weightings at any given time. Zero confusion. No wondering. Direct, straightforward, reliable guidance, with a corresponding ledger of trades, holdings, and weightings. You can access the entirety of the LASER Index on my Substack, whose link is in the description of my profile.

2. I will routinely discuss various stocks, bonds, and macroeconomic perspectives with the intention of providing food-for-thought to my audience, encouraging thoughts for your own investment practices, and generally adding to the body of thought that is the collective consciousness of the market. Most of these thoughts will be with respect to stocks that I extract from the LASER Index itself, such as Amazon as a very basic example; for which I provide in-depth research reports on my Substack, but some may just be stocks that are popular, and to whose body of thought I’d like to add. The spirit of everything I do is serving you to the highest extent possible.

3. My ultimate goal is to deliver the LASER Index as a product to you and to the investment community broadly. That is my main focus. I take managing the index seriously, and I want to deliver a comprehensive, scalable investing strategy to my audience and subscribers. Secondarily, I hope to create the aforementioned content that is thought provoking, salutary, and broadly beneficial to your life. As I continue to reiterate, the spirit of all I do is service to you to the highest, most excellent extent possible.

4. Regarding the LASER Index’s strategy, I use a super straightforward, relatively conservative, exceedingly patient strategy to run the Index. The main pillar of my approach is identifying as many attractive investment setups (asymmetric risk/return setups) as possible. I work to, for instance, identify 30 as-close-to-identical risk/return setups, where I reason that risk is low and return potential is very high. I then allow the positions to grow over time in a survival-of-the-fittest fashion, creating concentration within the portfolio in the process. The businesses that perform well, executing and growing exceptionally, naturally grow into larger positions and begin to command authority over the rest of the portfolio and its returns, as is the natural course of business within a given industry in the economy. As the concentration forms, I mostly do nothing, allowing the best, winningest, and highest quality stocks to carry outperformance of the portfolio over time.

5. While I am a very patient investor, who strives to accumulate compelling businesses that I can hold forever, the reality is that it’s worth trading positions sometimes. Investment theses can change materially. The wheels can come off to an extent that requires either exiting the position or reducing the position’s size. Moreover, new, compelling companies emerge either by way of their own evolutions or via going public, and I may add these to the Index when I deem appropriate. So I do trade from time to time, and there is always a catalogue of all trades made since launch, which you can easily audit and trace with the help of AI.

6. The LASER Index is a generalist portfolio that reflects my view of the future, e.g., humans will continue to develop unique computing platforms such as virtual reality and will build a Space Empire over time. The Index holds restaurants, computing infrastructure, consumer credit, consumer discretionary, and a handful of international companies. I refer to it as a Supercomputer whose price action reflects the state of the global economy, and this is another benefit of the portfolio, i.e., its breadth in terms of industry and geography provides a lot of insight into the state of the global chessboard. It can be as much a macroeconomic signal as it can be a representation of the performance of the businesses it owns.

7. I am not a registered investment adviser, and none of what I say is personalized investment advice. I publish my research, alongside an always available model portfolio, to all subscribers at the same time. Nothing here is tailored to your circumstances, and I don't know your situation, goals, or risk tolerance. I cannot and will not give individual advice. I am not compensated by any company I write about, nor will I ever be. I try to remain skeptical of my companies’ operations so that I remain objective about their performance. I always disclose the LASER Index’s exact positioning via my research notes published to my Substack. All of my incentives are perfectly aligned with the LASER Index and its long term success, as, when it succeeds, you succeed; thereby, I succeed. Choose to follow along if you desire, and remember that stocks are risky. Business is risky. There are no guarantees for any business and its stock, no matter how bullish I, you, the CEO, or the market may be. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Remember to do your own due diligence.

8. Everything I do and share is a part of one overarching thread. Few, if any, ideas are randomly or haphazardly shared. They all weave together into one tapestry. If I share something philosophically or politically on my profile, you can be sure that it weaves into the tapestry of thought into which the LASER Index is woven also.

In summary, I am here to serve you. Everything I do is in service of you. My only stock recommendation is the LASER Index, whose weightings, trades, and holdings are disclosed on my Substack. I will discuss a wide range of topics on my profile, but they all tie together into one valuable tapestry of thought into which the LASER Index is woven also.

And, through this service to you, my goal is to enhance the quality of your life to the highest extent possible and to be an asset to you, so that you can be the best person to those in your life.

Thanks for reading, keep following along, and let me know if you have any questions, comments, or concerns.

text:
Gamified DDoS attacks target NATO nations with psychological warfare, study shows | Hailey Crawford, ScienMag

In an era where cyberattacks are often measured solely by downtime, bandwidth and remediation costs, a groundbreaking study from Finland’s Aalto University School of Business has revealed a chilling new dimension to one of the most persistent digital threats confronting NATO member states. The research examines the inner workings of NoName057(16), the pro-Russian hacking collective responsible for thousands of distributed denial of service, or DDoS, attacks across Europe and beyond, and finds that the group operates not as a conventional criminal enterprise or an idealistic hacktivist movement, but as something far more sophisticated: a gamified, hybrid threat actor waging deliberate psychological warfare against governments and institutions it considers hostile to Russian interests.

The study, published as an open access teaching case in the Journal of Information Technology Teaching Cases, is the first of its kind to dissect the complete modus operandi and operating model of the group. DDoS attacks themselves are not a new phenomenon. By flooding targeted servers with overwhelming traffic, they can shut down public services, knock banking platforms offline and disrupt critical infrastructure. But Assistant Professor Hadi Ghanbari, the study’s lead author, argues that focusing on these technical disruptions fundamentally misreads the threat. The real objective, he contends, is not the outage itself but the erosion of public confidence that follows it.

“NoName057(16) and other such groups actively aim to undermine public trust in governments, institutions, and countries seen as hostile to Russian interests,” Ghanbari explains. “It’s easy to focus on the financial costs, but the more hidden risk is if people lose confidence in large organisations or government services, then the next step is for them to ask what’s the point of having them.” In other words, a website that returns after a few hours is not the point of the attack. The lingering question in citizens’ minds, whether their institutions can protect them at all, is.

Finland has become a particularly instructive case study. Since January 7, 2025, NoName057(16) has launched 23 rounds of DDoS attacks against Finnish targets, affecting 129 public and private organisations. The timing is not coincidental. Researchers note a marked uptick in attacks against the country since it joined NATO in 2023, a move that repositioned Finland squarely within the group’s crosshairs. The targets read like a blueprint of national infrastructure: the Parliament of Finland, numerous governmental institutions, municipalities, banks and financial institutions, and providers of critical infrastructure services. Each attack round serves as both a disruption and a message, demonstrating to the Finnish public and policymakers alike that the country’s digital front door can be rattled at will.

Perhaps the most striking finding of the research is the group’s operational architecture, which Ghanbari describes as genuinely unprecedented. NoName057(16) recruits volunteers through the messaging platform Telegram, cultivating the image of a politically motivated hacktivist movement. Yet beneath this ideological veneer lies an incentive system more characteristic of organised cyber-crime. Evidence drawn from the dark web indicates that members receive cryptocurrency-based rewards of up to USD 1,200 for successful attacks. The group also forms alliances and collaborates with other hacking collectives, at least one of which is linked to the Russian cyber army.

“They claim to be hacktivists but they have an incentive system more common for cyber criminals. They also collaborate and form alliances with other hacker groups,” says Ghanbari. “Essentially, they have gamified their operating model. This is something new—we haven’t seen this hybrid model before.” The gamification is more than a metaphor. By turning attack participation into a point-scoring, reward-earning activity, the group has industrialised the recruitment and motivation of what would otherwise be a loose crowd of sympathisers. Volunteers are transformed into a distributed, paid and ideologically motivated workforce, capable of launching coordinated attacks across multiple countries simultaneously.

The implications of this model place NoName057(16) in a category that existing frameworks struggle to contain. The research identifies a new class of hybrid warfare occupying the grey zone between hacktivism, state-sponsored cyber warfare and cyber-criminality. The group borrows the legitimacy narrative of the hacktivist, the financial machinery of the criminal and, through its alliances, the strategic direction of state-aligned actors. Ghanbari urges that such groups should not be understood as ordinary hackers or conventional hacktivists at all, but as hybrid threat actors functioning strategically to wage geopolitical and psychological warfare. This reframing matters because it changes how defenders should respond, from purely technical incident handling to a broader contest over narrative and public confidence.

Intriguingly, the study warns that the victims of these attacks may inadvertently become their own worst enemies. Ghanbari cautions that when governments and companies attempt to downplay the nature or extent of such attacks in their public communications, they can play directly into the hackers’ hands. “The point is to escalate the psychological cost of their actions. It’s a complex game,” he warns. “Companies and governments can play into the hackers’ hands if they’re not transparent.” A minimising statement intended to reassure the public can instead be reframed by adversaries as evidence of concealment or incompetence, amplifying precisely the distrust the attackers sought to create.

This insight leads to one of the study’s most actionable recommendations: in the aftermath of a reputational or psychological cyberattack, cybersecurity experts should work closely with public relations and communications professionals. Counteracting propaganda and psychological intimidation, the research suggests, requires a joined-up response in which technical teams restore systems while communication teams restore confidence. Treating the two as separate functions leaves the psychological battlefield undefended, which is exactly where the attackers prefer to operate.

The reach of NoName057(16) extends well beyond NATO and the European Union. The group’s recent attacks on Israeli infrastructure illustrate how its targeting follows geopolitical fault lines rather than geographic boundaries. “Nations who have come out in support of the US are getting more DDoS attacks than anyone else,” says Ghanbari. “Anyone considered an ‘enemy of Russia’—which includes those nations who are even discussing joining NATO—have been attacked.” The group has also been active amid the Iran-US conflict, demonstrating how crowdsourced cyber aggression can be redeployed rapidly to whatever flashpoint best serves its strategic narrative. For countries merely debating NATO accession, the threat has already arrived, long before any treaty is signed.

From a societal perspective, the stakes are considerable. DDoS disruptions can block access to essential services for millions of citizens, yet Ghanbari observes that the costs borne by ordinary users rarely receive the attention they deserve. “Not only does it undermine their basic rights, it also undermines the ideological system that underpins them,” he notes. When citizens cannot reliably access government portals, banking services or municipal resources, the damage accumulates not just in lost hours but in the slow corrosion of the democratic and institutional fabric that those services represent. The attack, in this reading, is aimed at the social contract itself.

The study, titled “The blurring lines of hacktivism and crowdsourced cyber warfare: How NoName057(16) weaponises distributed denial of service attacks,” has been made available online as an open access resource, reflecting its value not only for researchers but also for practitioners tasked with defending democratic societies against this evolving form of aggression. As gamified, financially incentivised and ideologically charged cyber campaigns continue to proliferate, the research offers a sobering reminder: the most important battleground in these attacks is not the server, but the mind of the citizen.

🚨 Beti Kamya Set to Launch Late Father’s Autobiography as Museveni Takes Centre Stage

Former Inspector General of Government Beti Olive Namisango Kamya is set to launch the autobiography of her late father, Lt. Col. (Rtd) George Wilson Kamya, in a special ceremony officiated by President Yoweri Museveni.

The book, titled Soldier of Faith, will be launched on Friday, September 11, 2026, at the Kololo Ceremonial Grounds.

Written by George Wilson Kamya before his death in 1993, the autobiography offers a personal account of his life as a Ugandan army officer and accountant during a turbulent period in East Africa.

The memoir traces his journey across four cultures and three countries, capturing the colonial and post-colonial upheavals that shaped the region while highlighting his deep connection to his heritage and Christian faith.

Beti Kamya was born in Kenya in 1955 to Ugandan father George Wilson Kamya and his Kenyan wife, Margaret, before moving to Uganda as a child.

According to the family, the decision to publish the long-kept manuscript was driven by a desire to share a deeply personal story of love, pain, suffering, exile and resilience, preserving the late army officer’s experiences for future generations.

The launch is expected to bring together family members, government officials, friends and other guests to celebrate the life and legacy of Lt. Col. (Rtd) George Wilson Kamya.

text:
Robert Monroe: The Hemi-Sync Tapes

In the 1950s, New York broadcasting executive Robert Monroe began exploring the effects of sound on human consciousness. Fascinated by the idea that audio frequencies could enhance learning and alter mental states, he initiated a series of experiments—what he called “sleep-learning.” 

But during one session, something extraordinary occurred: “I was suddenly enveloped in a bright white light. It was not blinding, but it seemed to shine everywhere. I felt bathed in it, immersed in it.” He experienced a powerful internal vibration, followed by “a sound like a wind, then a roaring, then a feeling of motion. Then, silence. As the light faded I was outside of my physical body, looking down at it.”

That moment marked the onset of what would later be known as an out-of-body experience—or OBE—a term popularized in part by Robert Monroe himself. He went on to develop techniques for deliberately inducing these states using audio frequencies, eventually founding the Monroe Institute and dedicating the rest of his life to exploring the frontiers of human consciousness.

Monroe’s further explorations revealed that these altered states could be reached by harmonizing the brain's hemispheres. While the brain functions as a unified organ, its two halves have distinct roles: the left is typically linked with logic, language, and linear thinking, while the right is more intuitive, creative, and emotionally driven. Each hemisphere tends to operate on different frequency ranges—the left more often in the faster beta range, the right in the slower alpha band. By synchronizing these hemispheres through specific sound patterns, a method known as Hemi-Sync, subjects could enter unique states of awareness—ones that transcend the normal boundaries of the body and even time itself.

Not long after the release of his 1971 book Journeys Out of the Body, U.S. Army Intelligence began exploring Robert Monroe’s Hemi-Sync technology for its potential applications in consciousness expansion, remote viewing, and psi-related operations.

Lt. Col. Wayne McDonnell: “By listening to certain sounds, the Gateway process synchronizes both hemispheres using a technique called Hemi-Sync. Fundamentally, the Gateway experience is a training system designed to bring enhanced strength, focus, and coherence to the amplitude and frequency of brainwave output between the left and right hemispheres so as to alter consciousness—moving it outside the physical sphere so as to ultimately escape even the restrictions of time and space. The participant then gains access to the various levels of intuitive knowledge which the universe offers.”

The Gateway model describes the human mind in two modes: scattered and coherent. In its natural state, consciousness functions like a lamp—diffuse, unfocused, spreading energy unevenly. But with the aid of hemispheric synchronization (often called “Hemi-Sync”), the mind can shift into a laser-like mode—sharp, directed, and capable of high-level focus. According to the Gateway theory, when the brain’s frequency and amplitude become balanced between hemispheres, the vibrational state of consciousness elevates. At these higher frequencies, the mind begins to interface with more intricate layers of reality.

The Gateway Process: The Absolute–God?

With the right training, consciousness can shift perception, reprogram patterns, and influence the energetic framework of what we consider “real.” Quantum phenomena such as entanglement and retrocausality—where a later event influences an earlier one—hint at a deeper truth: reality is not fixed but entangled with the observer’s awareness. Intention, focus, and emotion aren’t merely internal states; they are tools that can subtly shape the unfolding of events across space and time.

If consciousness is a form of energy, then it’s not bound by the traditional limits of space-time. It may act as both transmitter and receiver, interfacing with unseen planes of existence and tapping into data streams beyond physical reality. In this view, consciousness becomes an active participant in a vast, interconnected web of dimensional exchange.

Lt. Col. Wayne McDonnell: “Below the reality we perceive lies a primary energy field—“the Absolute”—from which our individual consciousness arises. Through repeated practice, the individual can return to this Universal Mind and reintegrate with both a shared collective intelligence and their own unique identity—hinting at a kind of neurological immortality. 

The Absolute is the foundational energy field from which all existence originates—a timeless, formless source beyond space and matter. It is pure, undivided consciousness that underlies all realities and dimensions. We are not separate from the Absolute; rather, our individual consciousness is a temporary expression of it. After death—or through advanced altered states—we return to this source, retaining both individuality and connection to the greater collective mind.

Humans are not passive in the face of the cosmos. We participate in the creation of reality. And with sufficient training, we can project our consciousness intentionally to enact change—from the inside out. It's a practical, scientific roadmap to what ancient spiritual traditions have long called manifestation, patterning, or forging reality from thought. Whether you subscribe to mysticism, eastern tradition, or western religion, the Gateway Process could be humanity’s greatest tool for self-discovery and for understanding the universe itself.”

The Gateway Process affirms what mystics have long suggested: that everyone on Earth is part of a collective consciousness, placed here with a shared purpose—to accumulate experiences, learn from one another, and ultimately return that knowledge to the greater energy from which we came. According to the report, we might free ourselves from the prison of separation and individuality—and come to realize that, at the most fundamental level, we are all the same.

McDonnell came to believe that these higher states cannot be accessed through fear or aggression, only through surrender. The true gate, he insisted, is within. Mastering consciousness doesn’t just expand perception—it may redefine who we are and how we interact with everything around us. And perhaps that’s exactly what non-human intelligences are nudging us toward: a shift in awareness, where consciousness becomes central to both human evolution and the nature of contact itself.

Psalm 51:1-19

"Have mercy on me, O God,     according to your steadfast love; according to your abundant mercy     blot out my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity,     and cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my transgressions,     and my sin is ever before me.
Against you, you alone, have I sinned,     and done what is evil in your sight, so that you are justified in your sentence     and blameless when you pass judgment.
Indeed, I was born guilty,     a sinner when my mother conceived me.
You desire truth in the inward being;[a]     therefore teach me wisdom in my secret heart.
Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean;     wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness;     let the bones that you have crushed rejoice.
Hide your face from my sins,     and blot out all my iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God,     and put a new and right[b] spirit within me.
Do not cast me away from your presence,     and do not take your holy spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation,     and sustain in me a willing[c] spirit.
Then I will teach transgressors your ways,     and sinners will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, O God,     O God of my salvation,     and my tongue will sing aloud of your deliverance.
O Lord, open my lips,     and my mouth will declare your praise.
For you have no delight in sacrifice;     if I were to give a burnt offering, you would not be pleased.
The sacrifice acceptable to God[d] is a broken spirit;     a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
Do good to Zion in your good pleasure;     rebuild the walls of Jerusalem,
then you will delight in right sacrifices,     in burnt offerings and whole burnt offerings;     then bulls will be offered on your altar."

Footnotes
aPsalm 51:6 Meaning of Heb uncertain
bPsalm 51:10 Or steadfast
cPsalm 51:12 Or generous
dPsalm 51:17 Or My sacrifice, O God,
