text:
The Asherim: Identity, Cultic Function, and Scriptural Indictment
The Hebrew term Asherim (אֲשֵׁרִים) and its feminine plural Asherot (אֲשֵׁרוֹת) refer both to the ancient Canaanite mother-goddess Asherah (אֲשֵׁרָה) and to the physical cult objects, sacred poles, and living groves erected in her honor. In ancient West Semitic and Ugaritic mythology discovered at Ras Shamra, Asherah (Athirat) was revered as the supreme mother goddess, the chief consort of El (the high creator god), and the mother of seventy deities, including Baal. In popular Canaanite religion and Israelite syncretism, she was frequently paired directly with Baal, the storm and fertility god, governing fertility, sexuality, agricultural bounty, and childbirth. Regionally, she was closely linked to, and often conflated with, other fertility and war goddesses such as Ashtoreth (Astarte) and Anat.
In the biblical historical narratives (as in 2 Chronicles 24:18), the plural Asherim almost always designates man-made cultic poles or carved wooden images rather than an abstract ideology. The Scriptures repeatedly emphasize their wooden construction: they could be carved (1 Kings 15:13), planted like a tree or post beside an altar (Deuteronomy 16:21), and destroyed by being chopped down, cut to pieces, and burned with fire (Exodus 34:13; Judges 6:25–28; 2 Kings 23:6, 15). Set up on hills, under green trees, and alongside altars dedicated to Baal, these carved poles served as localized phallic or arboreal symbols representing female reproductive and cosmic fertility. Under wicked monarchs such as Manasseh, a carved image of Asherah was placed directly inside the Temple of Yahweh in Jerusalem, and ritual prostitutes were housed in the temple complex weaving hangings for her (2 Kings 21:7; 2 Kings 23:7).
The Asherim presented a continuous spiritual snare because they embodied the temptation of syncretism—mixing the pure worship of Yahweh with localized fertility cults. Ancient agrarian survival depended entirely on rain and soil fertility; neighboring Canaanites taught that neglecting Baal and Asherah caused crop failure and barrenness. Carnal Israelite leaders repeatedly hedged their bets by erecting Asherim alongside the altars of God to secure their harvest through pagan ritual. Inscriptions discovered at Kuntillet Ajrud and Khirbet el-Qom reading "To Yahweh and His Asherah" provide historical confirmation of this syncretism, documenting apostate attempts to assign a pagan consort to the holy, uncreated God.
God explicitly commanded the total destruction of these objects prior to Israel entering the land:
"You shall destroy their altars, break their sacred pillars, and cut down their wooden images [Asherim] (for you shall worship no other god, for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God)." (Exodus 34:13–14)
"You shall not plant for yourself any tree, as a wooden image [Asherah], near the altar which you build for yourself to the Lord your God." (Deuteronomy 16:21)
Throughout Kings and Chronicles, a king's spiritual fidelity was measured directly by his treatment of the Asherim. Gideon's inaugural test required tearing down his father's altar of Baal and cutting down the Asherah pole beside it to use as firewood for a sacrifice to Yahweh (Judges 6:25–27). Righteous reformers like Hezekiah and Josiah proved their loyalty by cutting down the Asherim, grinding them to powder, and casting the dust into the Kidron Valley (2 Kings 18:4; 23:6, 14). Conversely, in 2 Chronicles 24:17–18, King Joash collapsed after the death of Jehoiada the priest, succumbing to the flattery of the princes of Judah and abandoning the house of the Lord to serve the Asherim and idols, which brought immediate divine wrath upon the nation.
Contemporary Resurgence: Modern Neo-Paganism and High-Place Rituals
While the names of ancient deities shift across millennia, the underlying spiritual impulse of idolatry and syncretism remains constant. In Europe and across the Western world, nature veneration, hyper-sexualized fertility motifs, and the worship of the created order rather than the Creator have experienced an open resurgence.
Neo-Paganism and Seasonal Cult Festivals: Ancient pre-Christian agricultural festivals have shifted from folklore into mainstream celebrations. In Beltane and Walpurgisnacht rituals across the UK, Germany, and Scandinavia, the Maypole stands as a direct architectural descendant of the ancient sacred tree-pole (the phallic, carved trunk of the Asherah), symbolizing the union of earth and sky for seasonal fertility. Similarly, Midsommar (Summer Solstice) gatherings revive earth-mother deities and nature-communion rituals that prioritize natural cycles over divine moral accountability.
Radical Gaian Earth Worship: Canaanite religion centered on appeasing nature's life-giving forces as an autonomous organism. Contemporary eco-theology and Gaian philosophy mirror this premise: the Earth is conceptualized not as a creation of a transcendent Lawgiver (Genesis 1:1), but as an autonomous mother goddess ("Mother Earth" / Pachamama / Gaia) possessing rights over human conscience. Concurrently, human beings are reclassified from image-bearers appointed to righteous stewardship (Genesis 1:28) into biological intruders disrupting the natural order—fulfilling Romans 1:25: "They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator."
Decoupling Sexuality from Covenant Fidelity: In ancient high places, sexuality was weaponized as a spiritual sacrament stripped of moral restraint, monogamous covenant, or divine design. Modern cultural festivals celebrate an identical worldview, framing unrestrained sexual indulgence and boundary-dissolution as acts of "personal liberation" and "self-actualization," echoing Canaanite rites where sexual experimentation was treated as an avenue to divine communion.
Syncretism Infiltrating Assemblies: The most lethal aspect of the Asherim was that the covenant people brought them into the Temple courts. Today, historic cathedrals and denomination assemblies across nations like Germany, Sweden, and the UK increasingly host ecological "repentance" rituals, pagan ceremonies, and multi-faith installations, while scriptural commands on holiness and judgment are suppressed to appease secular authorities—mirroring King Joash's capitulation to the princes of Judah.
The spiritual blueprint remains fixed: deny the Transcendent Creator, deify nature, dismantle moral law in favor of naturalistic indulgence, and erect public monuments to human appetite.
The Desert Sanctuary: The Architecture of Burning Man
In North America, this ancient impulse finds a concentrated, institutional expression in the Burning Man gathering. While presented under banners of art and counter-culture, its architecture, symbolism, and practices map directly onto the ancient Canaanite high place:
The Geometry of the Desert High Place: Just as ancient cults sought isolated desert wastes and mountaintops to construct temporary sanctuaries away from established civil authority, tens of thousands assemble on the Nevada Black Rock Desert ("The Playa") to build Black Rock City along a precise geometric crescent. This perimeter operates as an ancient temenos—a sacred enclosure where standard civil and moral laws are suspended to commune with primal creative forces.
The Effigy as Modern Asherah: At the epicenter stands a towering wooden colossus ("The Man"), an engineered wooden monument to human autonomy and the deification of the self. On Saturday night, the effigy is incinerated amid mass ecstatic dancing, rhythmic drumming, and sensory delirium, mirroring ancient Celtic wicker-man rites and agricultural purifications that released spirit from matter through fire. Concurrently, a massive non-denominational "Temple" is erected to collect prayers, memorials, and confessions before being burned in total silence on Sunday night—functioning as a pagan priesthood ritual offering grief to an ambiguous universe.
Radical Antinomianism and Pharmakeia: The founding principles of "Radical Self-Expression" and "Radical Inclusion" reject divine moral restraint. Like the fertility festivals of Baal and Asherah, the environment is marked by public nudity, polyamorous exploration, and the institutionalized use of entheogens and psychedelics (pharmakeia) to induce trance states and spiritual awakenings.
Self-Deification (The Edenic Echo): The gathering rejects an external, holy Lawgiver before whom man is accountable. It teaches that the individual is divine, seeking to awaken the dormant godhood within through sensory overwhelm and fire—repeating the promise of Genesis 3:5: "You will not surely die... you will be like God, knowing good and evil."
Elite Patronage: In 2 Chronicles 24:17, the princes of Judah led the apostasy. Similarly, Burning Man's primary sponsors and patrons include Silicon Valley executives, venture capitalists, corporate leaders, and media moguls who absorb this antinomian ethos and inject it directly into the legal, educational, and corporate systems of Western culture.
When a culture rejects the Word of the Living God, it does not become religiously neutral; it returns to the high place, erects a wooden monument in the dust, strips off its clothes, and dances around the fire.
The Apocalyptic Trajectory: Babel, High Places, and Mystery Babylon
The vision of Revelation 17 and 18 unmasks the final, global consolidation of this spiritual architecture, tracing a single lineage designated as "MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND OF THE ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH" (Revelation 17:5).
Across sacred history, this architecture develops through three distinct epochs:
Babel and Canaan: Beginning at the plain of Shinar (Genesis 11:1–4) with human autonomy and sacred ziggurats ("Let us make a name for ourselves"), the system evolved into Canaanite high places marked by carved wooden Asherah poles, fertility magic, and ritual prostitution designed to commune with earth forces and establish regional autonomy from Yahweh.
Modern High Places: Materializing in temporary desert cities, neo-pagan groves, and wooden effigies, this phase operates on "Radical Self-Expression," antinomian hedonism, and chemical trance states (pharmakeia—Revelation 18:23) to dismantle biblical morality and enthrone the autonomous self.
Mystery Babylon (Revelation 17–18): Consolidates into an integrated, globalized megacity network powered by institutionalized occult commerce. Its ethos is defined by universal syncretism, state-sanctioned spiritual harlotry, and the deep cultural intoxication of ruling elites (Revelation 17:2; 18:3). At this stage, humanity is stripped of the Imago Dei, reducing the bodies and souls of men to economic commodities (Revelation 18:13), while becoming a literal habitation of demons (Revelation 18:2; 1 Corinthians 10:20).
The divine verdict demands absolute separation:
"And I heard another voice from heaven saying, 'Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues. For her sins have reached to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.'" (Revelation 18:4–5)
Infiltration of the Assembly: Pergamum and Thyatira
In Revelation 2, Christ addresses how the spirit of the Canaanite high place establishes a beachhead inside the church through two distinct vectors:
Pergamum (The Doctrine of Balaam, Revelation 2:12–17):
Located "where Satan's throne is"—amid imperial altars to Zeus, Asclepius, and Rome—the assembly faced intense political and economic pressure. Refusing to participate in trade-guild feasts honoring patron deities meant financial ruin and civic suspicion. The "Balaamites" inside the church offered a pragmatic theological compromise: outward participation in civic banquets does not defile the inner soul. Christ links this directly to Numbers 25 and 31:16, where Balaam taught Balak to subvert Israel through the women of Moab at Baal-Peor, leading them into idolatry and porneia. Christ demands repentance under threat of the sharp two-edged sword of His mouth.
Thyatira (The Teaching of Jezebel, Revelation 2:18–29):
Rather than outward economic fear, Thyatira was seduced by mystical hubris, spiritual pride, and false prophetic authority. A woman claiming to be a prophetess taught that enlightened believers had the liberty to indulge in trade-guild feasts and sexual immorality without spiritual harm, claiming to understand "the deep things of Satan." Mirroring Queen Jezebel, who imported the state cult of Baal and Asherah into northern Israel (1 Kings 16–21), she normalized spiritual adultery from within the assembly. Christ announces retributive judgment (lex talionis): casting her onto a bed of affliction, throwing her companions into great tribulation, and striking her children with death to demonstrate that He alone searches minds and hearts.
Whether through external economic pragmatism (Balaam) or internal theological seduction (Jezebel), both systems produced the exact same fruit: eating food sacrificed to idols and committing sexual immorality (porneia).
The Apostolic Countermeasure: The Jerusalem Decree of Acts 15
The decree of the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15:19–29 was neither an arbitrary compromise nor an appeasement of legalism; it was a targeted strike against the core machinery of the pagan high place.
The Council codified four specific prohibitions:
"Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols [ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων], from sexual immorality [πορνείας], from things strangled [πνικτοῦ], and from blood [αἵματος]." (Acts 15:19–20; ratified in 15:29)
While liberating Gentile converts from the yoke of ceremonial circumcision for justification (vv. 10–11), the Council drew these four non-negotiable boundaries directly from the Holiness Code of Leviticus 17–18, which applied equally to native Israelites and the resident stranger (gēr):
Things Offered to Idols (Eidōlothutos / Leviticus 17:7–9): Severed Gentile believers from the sacrificial meat of civic banquets and trade-guild feasts dedicated to regional deities.
Things Strangled (Pniktos / Leviticus 17:13–14): Outlawed the consumption of animals suffocated or strangled in chthonic rituals to retain blood-borne animal vitality within the flesh.
Blood (Haima / Leviticus 17:10–12): Banned the ritual drinking or tasting of blood common in pagan covenants and necromancy, preserving blood solely for divine atonement upon the altar.
Sexual Immorality (Porneia / Leviticus 18:6–30): Extinguished the ritual prostitution and libertine ethics foundational to the fertility cults of Canaan and the Greco-Roman world.
Within the perimeter of the ancient high place, these four elements operated simultaneously as a single liturgical package:
Within the perimeter of the ancient pagan high place and its sacred temple banquets, four distinct cultic practices operated in concert as a unified liturgical system. The rite commenced with idol consecration, wherein sacrificial animals were formally dedicated to the presiding regional deity, establishing a legal claim over the meat and the feast. The preparation of the offering followed through the culinary handling of unbled or strangled flesh, a method designed to trap the animal's life-force within the tissue to maximize perceived metaphysical potency. This led directly into the literal drinking or tasting of blood, an act of ritual communion intended to bind the participants directly to the territorial demonic principalities governing the sanctuary. The entire sequence culminated in sacred prostitution and sexual immorality (porneia), where ecstatic sensual release and boundary dissolution were treated as sacramental communion with the fertility forces of nature. Taken together, these four elements formed a single liturgical package through which physical nourishment, spiritual allegiance, and sensual indulgence were joined to demonic worship.
By enforcing total abstinence from these four practices, the Jerusalem Council issued a total severance order: a believer cannot sit at the table of the Lord while partaking of the table of demons (1 Corinthians 10:21). The standard of biblical faith across every covenant remains identical: absolute, uncompromising separation from the intoxicating high places of Babylon.

The evidence compiled across the breadth of Scripture leaves no room for ambiguity: the spirit of the Canaanite high place, the deceptive compromises of Balaam and Jezebel, and the intoxicating machinery of Mystery Babylon are not relics of antiquity, but active, intensifying realities. In light of this, the mandate for the seeker of Truth is neither passive observation nor fearful retreat, but deliberate, uncompromising covenant action.

First, the truth seeker must execute personal iconoclasm. Just as Gideon’s first commission was to fell his father’s Asherah and rebuild the altar of Yahweh, every modern high place tolerated within personal life, home, and thought must be identified and dismantled. This demands an unyielding audit of media consumption, cultural habits, and financial entanglements, rooting out any syncretistic impulse that attempts to blend the holy with the profane. The seeker of Truth refuses to adopt the flattering counsel of worldly princes or hedge bets with the idols of the age.

Second, the seeker of Truth must maintain the apostolic perimeter established in Acts 15. This requires radical separation from the fourfold package of Babylon: rejecting the subtle idolatry of cultural consensus, guarding bodily and sexual purity against the pervasive antinomianism of the culture, and refusing spiritual communion with demonic doctrines and altered states of consciousness. Where modern society glorifies self-deification, unrestrained appetite, and the worship of creation, the truth seeker walks in holiness, modesty, and reverent obedience before the living God.

Finally, the truth seeker must stand anchored in the sovereign court of the Most High, knowing that Babylon’s apparent dominance is brief and bounded by divine decree. When confronted by economic pressures to conform, the seeker remembers the prophetic truth spoken to Amaziah: "The Lord is able to give you much more than this." Rather than seeking refuge in second-hand religion or spiritual pride, the faithful remnant heeds the ultimate divine imperative of Revelation 18:4: "Come out of her, my people." Stand unyielding, preserve an undivided heart, and hold fast to the unadulterated Word until the righteous reign of the Messiah shatters the high places forever.

text:
Darian Mensah threw 25 touchdowns as a senior at Saint Joseph High School in Santa Maria, California, and won his league's Player of the Year.

Recruiting services rated him a two-star.

On the 247Sports composite he was the 2,672nd ranked player in the country. The 161st quarterback. The 383rd best player in the state of California.

One FBS program in America offered him a scholarship. Tulane.

Idaho State offered at the FCS level. Arizona State, Boise State, San Diego State and San Jose State all looked and passed.

He redshirted in 2023.

Then in 2024, as a redshirt freshman, he threw for 2,723 yards and 22 touchdowns against six interceptions and took Tulane to the conference championship game.

Duke came for him with one of the largest transfer packages any quarterback had received.

In one season in Durham he completed 334 of 500 passes for 3,973 yards, with 34 touchdowns and six interceptions. He broke Duke's single-season records for both passing yards and total touchdowns, was named ACC Newcomer of the Year, and won an ACC Championship.

Then he left again, for Miami.

Which is a school that has become a specific kind of place. Cam Ward spent one year there and went first overall in the 2025 draft. Carson Beck spent one year there and took the Hurricanes to the national title game.

Mensah is the third.

Through two seasons he's thrown for 6,696 yards with 56 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. NFL Network's Daniel Jeremiah has floated him as the top quarterback in the 2027 class, and reports this week say multiple scouts believe he could go first overall.

Worth being straight about the other side. He's 205 pounds. He's fumbled 16 times in two years and evaluators have quietly wondered about his hand size. He holds the ball too long. At least one board still has him going in the second or third round.

None of that changes the shape of it.

Three years ago, 2,671 high school players in America were considered better prospects than he was.

text:
Study Notes - (Hastings Dictionary) Death
DEATH
I. In the OT.—1. The Heb. term mâweth and our corresponding word ‘death’ alike spring from primitive roots belonging to the very beginnings of speech. One of man’s first needs was a word to denote that stark fact of experience—the final cessation of life to which he and the whole animated creation, and the very trees and plants, were all subject. It is, of course, in this ordinary sense of the term as denoting a physical fact that the expressions ‘death’ and ‘die’ are mostly used in the Scriptures.
2. The Scriptures have nothing directly to say as to the place of death in the economy of nature. St. Paul’s words in Rom_5:12 ff. as to the connexion between sin and death must be explained in harmony with this fact; and, for that matter, in harmony also with his own words in Rom_6:23, where death, the ‘wages of sin,’ cannot be simply physical death. The Creation narratives are silent on this point, yet in Gen_2:17 man is expected to know what it is to die. We are not to look for exact information on matters such as this from writings of this kind. If the belief enshrined in the story of the Fall in Gen_3:1-24 regarded death in the ordinary sense as the penalty of Adam and Eve’s transgression, they at any rate did not die ‘in the day’ of their transgression; v. 22 suggests that even then, could he but also eat of ‘the tree of life,’ man might escape mortality. All we can say is that in the dawn of human history man appears as one already familiar with the correlative mysteries of life and death.
3. From the contemplation of the act of dying it is an easy step to the thought of death as a state or condition. This is a distinct stage towards believing in existence of some kind beyond the grave. And to the vast mass of mankind to say ‘he is dead’ has never meant ‘he is non-existent.’
4. Divergent beliefs as to what the state of death is show themselves in the OT.—(a) In numerous instances death is represented as a condition of considerable activity and consciousness. The dead are regarded as ‘knowing ones,’ able to impart information and counsel to the living. Note, the term translated ‘wizards’ in EV in Lev_19:31; Lev_20:6, Isa_8:19; Isa_19:3 really denotes departed spirits who are sought unto or inquired of ‘on behalf of the living.’ A vivid instance of this belief is furnished in the story of the Witch of En-dor (1Sa_28:1-25). So also in Isa_14:9-10, where we have a graphic description of the commotion caused in Sheol by the arrival of the king of Babylon, a description with which we may compare the dream of ‘false Clarence’ in Shakespeare’s Rich. III., i. 4. The reference to the dead under the term ‘gods’ (elôhim), as in 1Sa_28:13, is noticeable. Whether in all this we have a relic of ancient Semitic ancestor-worship (as e.g. Charles maintains in his Jowett Lectures on Eschatology) or no, it seems to represent very primitive beliefs which survived in one form and another, even after the stern Jahwistic prohibition of necromancy was promulgated. They may also have affected the treatment of the dead, just as even yet there are usages in existence amongst us in regard to behaviour towards the dead which are probably traceable to very primitive pre-Christian ideas and beliefs.
(b) Jahwism might well forbid resort to necromancers with their weird appeals to the dead for guidance and information, for in its view the state of death was one of unconsciousness, forgetfulness, and silence (see Psa_88:12; Psa_94:17; Psa_115:17 etc.). The present world is emphatically ‘the land of the living’ (Psa_27:13; Psa_116:9 etc.). Those that are in Sheol have no communion with Jahweh; see the Song of Hezekiah in Isa_38:1-22, and elsewhere. Sheol appears inviting to a soul in distress because it is a realm of unconscious rest (Job_3:17 ff.); and there is nothing to be known or to be done there (Ecc_9:10). It is true that here and there glimpses of a different prospect for the individual soul show themselves (e.g. Job_19:25 ff. and probably Psa_16:10 f.); but the foregoing was evidently the prevalent view in a period when the individual was altogether subservient to the nation, and the religious concerns of the latter were rigorously limited to the present life.
(c) Other ideas of death as not terminating man’s existence and interests were, however, reached in later prophetic teaching, mainly through the thought of the worth of the individual, the significance of his conscious union with God, and of the covenant relations established by God with His people (Jer_31:1-40; cf. Ezk_18:1-32). ‘Thou wilt not leave us in the dust.’
5. Death as standing in penal relation to man’s sin and unrighteousness is frequently insisted on. That this is something more than natural death is clear from such an antithesis as we have in Deu_30:15; Deu_30:19 (‘life and good: death and evil’), and this set in strict relation to conduct. Cf. the burden of Ezk_18:1-32, ‘the soul that sinneth it shall die,’ with the correlative promise of life: similarly Pro_15:10. All this points to some experience in the man himself and to conditions outlasting the present life. On the other hand, the thought of dying ‘the death of the righteous’ (Num_23:10) as a desirable thing looks in the same direction. And why has the righteous ‘hope in his death’ (Pro_14:32)?
6. As minor matters, OT poetical uses of references to death may be merely pointed out. ‘Chambers of death,’ Pro_7:27; ‘gates,’ Psa_9:13 (= state); ‘bitterness of death,’ 1Sa_15:32, Ecc_7:26; ‘terrors,’ Psa_55:4; ‘sorrows,’ Psa_116:3 (= man’s natural dread); ‘shadow of death,’ Job, Ps., the Prophets, passim (= any experience of horror and gloom, as well as with reference to death itself); ‘the sleep of death,’ Psa_13:3 (to be distinguished from later Christian usage); ‘snares of death,’ Prov. passim, etc. (= things leading to destruction); the phrase ‘to death,’ as ‘vexed unto death,’ Jdg_13:7; ‘sick,’ 2Ki_20:1 (= to an extreme degree).
II. In the Apocrypha.—The value of the Apocrypha in connexion with the study of Scriptural teaching and usage here is not to be overlooked. Notice e.g. Wisdom chs. 1–5, with its treatment of the attitude of the ungodly towards death (‘Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die’), of the problem of the early, untimely death of the good, and of immortality in relation to the ungodly and the righteous; Sirach, in which no clear conception of immortality appears, the best that can be said, to alleviate sorrow for the dead, being that ‘the dead is at rest’ (Sir_38:23): in which also the fear of death is spoken of as besetting all ranks of men (40), and we are told who they are to whom death comes as a dread foe, and again who may welcome death as a friend (41).
III. In the NT
1. The teaching of Jesus.
(a). It is noticeable that our Lord has nothing to say directly concerning death as a physical phenomenon. He offers no explanation touching those matters in the experience of death which have always excited the curiosity of men, and in this respect His attitude is in strong contrast with that found in Rabbinical writings. He makes no use of the conception of ‘the angel of death,’ so characteristic of the latter, and traceable perhaps in language such as that of 1Co_15:26, Heb_2:14, and Rev_20:13-14.
(b) No stress is laid on death as an evil in itself. In the few stories which we have in the Gospels of His raising the dead to life, the raising is never represented as a deliverance and a good for the person brought back. Compassion for the sorrows of those bereaved is the prime motive: in the case of Lazarus, it is expressly added that the restoration was ‘for the glory of God’ (Jhn_11:4; Jhn_11:40). Still, those aspects of death which make the living and active shrink from it are incidentally recognized. Jesus in Rabbinic phrase speaks of tasting death (Mrk_9:1||) and of seeing death (Jhn_8:51-52): and the feeling underlying such expressions is the very antithesis of that attaching to ‘seeing life’ and ‘seeing many days.’ Death is to common human feeling an unwelcome, though inevitable, draught. This gives point also to our Lord’s promise that the believer shall never die (Jhn_11:26). At the same time, there is no reference in His teaching to natural death as the solemn end of life’s experiences and opportunities, unless an exception be found in the saying about working ‘while it is day’ (Jhn_9:4): but contrast with this as to tone a passage like Ecc_9:10.
(c) Jesus speaks of death as a sleep (Mrk_5:39, Jhn_11:11-13); but the same euphemistic use is found in OT and in extra-Biblical writers. It did not of itself necessarily lessen the terrors of death (see Psa_13:3); but we owe it to Christ and the Christian faith mainly that such a representation of death has come to mitigate its bitterness,—such a use as is also found elsewhere in NT (e.g. 1Th_4:13 ff.). This conception of death is, of course, to be limited to its relation to the activities and interests of this world. It is a falling asleep after life’s day—and ‘we sleep to wake’: but there is nothing here to shed light on such questions as to whether that sleep is a prolonged period of unconsciousness or no.
(d) Natural death is lost sight of in the much larger and more solemn conception of the condition of man resulting from sin, which in the Fourth Gospel is particularly described as ‘death’ (see Jhn_5:24; Jhn_6:50; Jhn_8:21; Jhn_8:24). The exemption and deliverance promised in Jhn_11:25 f. relate to this spiritual death, and by that deliverance natural death is shorn of its real terrors. This condition, resulting from sin and separation from God, may he regarded as incipient here and tending to a manifest consummation hereafter, with physical death intervening as a moment of transition and deriving a solemn significance from its association with the course and state of sin (see Beyschlag, NT Theol., Eng. tr. ii. p. 56 f.). The corresponding language of 1 Ep. of John is not to be overlooked (1Jn_3:14) as exemplifying Johannine phraseology. The conception, however, is not found exclusively in the Johannine writings. Note the saying in 
Luk_9:60 as bearing on this point. In Mat_7:13 f. ‘destruction’ is the antithesis of ‘life’ (and cf. Mat_5:29 f., Mat_18:11, Mrk_8:35, Jhn_3:16 etc.); but the conception of ‘perishing’ covers the deep experience of spiritual death, the loss of all that really makes the man.
(The phrase ‘die the death’ in EV, in Mrk_7:10 and parallel, may be noticed as being not a literal translation of the Greek, but a mid-English emphatic expression,’ now archaic.)
2. The rest of the NT.—We may notice the following points: (a) The Pauline doctrine that natural death is the primitive consequence of sin, already referred to, is to be explained as the common Jewish interpretation of the OT account of the Fall, and finds no direct support in the Gospels. The feeling that ‘the sting of death is sin’ is, however, widely existent in NT. (b) The use of the term ‘death’ as denoting a certain spiritual state in which men may live and he still destitute of all that is worth calling ‘life,’ is quite common (Eph_2:1; Eph_2:5; Eph_5:14, Col_2:13, 1Ti_5:6, Jas_1:15, Jud_1:12, Rev_3:1). (c) A mystical and figurative use of the notion of death as denoting the change from a sinful to a new life is noticeable. The believer, the man spiritually alive, is also ‘dead to sin’ (Rom_6:2, 1Pe_2:24), is ‘dead with Christ’ (Rom_6:8, Col_2:20 etc.). (d) The expression ‘eternal death’ is found nowhere in NT, common as its use is in religious and theological language. It is the correlative, easily suggested by the expression ‘eternal life’ which is so conspicuous a topic of NT teaching, and it serves loosely as an equivalent for the antitheses to ‘life’ or ‘eternal life’ that actually occur, such as ‘destruction’ (Mat_7:13), ‘the eternal fire’ (Mat_18:8), ‘eternal punishment’ (Mat_25:46). Cf. also ‘the second death’ in Rev_21:8. If we substitute for ‘eternal’ some other rendering such as ‘of the ages’ or ‘æonian,’ it but serves to remind us of the profound difficulties attaching to the predication of eternity in relation to the subject of man’s destiny or doom.
J. S. Clemens.

Brazil is no longer only a corridor. It is becoming a shelter.
It can become more complex and more dangerous: a continental landmass, thousands of kilometers of jungle and river borders with Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Bolivia and the Guianas, illegal immigration routes that never close, and a state hollowed out from the inside. When the border stops being a line and becomes a bridgehead, the country is no longer a neighbor in trouble. It is a platform.
@SecRubio’s State Department document on Cuba laid out the method: decades of recruitment, training, documentation fraud, and infiltration not as protest, but as a system. Cuban intelligence has long issued alias passports and used valid documents of other Latin American countries with fabricated entries so travel into and out of Havana leaves no clean trail. That is the same toolkit now sitting on top of narcotics, gold, arms, and money-laundering networks.
Look at the senior pattern, not the slogan. One of the architects of the current political machine was banished after a prisoner exchange, received guerrilla instruction in Cuba, submitted to facial reconstruction so he would not be recognized, crossed back on a false foreign passport, lived for years under a fabricated identity as a “businessman,” then rose into the core of the state. That is not a memoir detail. It is the prototype: seniors formed in Cuba and later aligned with circuits in Russia, Venezuela and other regimes that share the same objective who treat passports, ministries, police appointments and public budgets as operational cover.
Once that class is inside the government, the gangs are no longer only outside the fence. PCC and CV already diversified beyond drugs in the Amazon and the Northeast. They buy routes, corrupt local power, and sit on the same map as Venezuelan and Colombian armed networks. @SecRubio was right to designate those organizations as foreign terrorist organizations. Designation without a functioning partner state still leaves the shelter standing.
The present government cannot police this. Not for lack of speeches for lack of will and resources. Budget cuts, neglected border posts, politicized federal police leadership, and infiltration of the agencies that should be doing the work have produced a predictable result: inability. Negligence is not a side effect. It is the condition that turns a proxy into a sanctuary.
Ordinary Brazilians already know the street-level cost. Public safety is the wound they live with: crime and trafficking rank at the top of voter concern; vast majorities describe criminality as high or very high and believe organized crime has reached politics and parts of the justice system. That is not an opposition talking point. It is the country’s daily climate.
They still cannot say it freely in an election year. October 4 is the first round. One side does not need a militia to silence the other. It uses censorship and a judicial weapon the Inquérito das Fake News (Inquiry 4781), opened by the Court itself in 2019, never given a normal end, and still capable of freezing accounts, dragging citizens, and teaching the rest of the country to stay quiet. Changing the rapporteur does not erase seven years of chilled speech. The other side is not a hashtag. It is a life-threatening organization on the ground, backed by narcoterrorists who already control routes, neighborhoods, and, in too many places, the men who were supposed to stop them.
So the public is trapped: furious about insecurity, afraid of retaliation if they name the cause before they vote. A state that punishes speech while failing to punish armed factions is not refereeing a democracy. Brazil offers depth: ports to Europe and Africa, river systems no satellite watches in real time, and a political shielding.
The pattern is already established. The question is whether we should treat Brazil as a captured territory or simply as a political dispute.

December 3, 2012

My dearly beloved daughter, with all your strength and with all your courage, I call on humanity to prepare for My Great Mercy.

Those of you with a humble heart and a purity of soul, I call upon you to pray for the souls of those who will die during The Warning. How they need your prayers. How I need your suffering. Both gifts, given to Me by you, will help save those who cannot be saved by their own free will.

As My Flame of Mercy will be poured over the whole earth, many will rejoice, but it will be a painful time for sinners who will be unable to ask Me for forgiveness, because of pride.

Their purification will be painful and it will take much suffering on their part in order to be redeemed in My Eyes.

How the wicked hearts of man will be torn inside out, and with terror in their souls, many will fall before Me in agony. Let them know that, although they will undergo much anguish, billions will become pure of heart and soul. Then they will be fully prepared for the great day of My Coming.

My daughter, the trials of My followers will increase and intensify before The Warning.

When you offer Me such suffering I will save the souls of millions. Please do not begrudge Me these torments for great miracles will be given despite those ungrateful men who have no shame in their hearts for the wickedness they are guilty of.

Not one man will be spared the sight of the state of their souls as they appear in My Eyes.

When they see the sorry state of their souls they will be deeply ashamed. Those who are genuinely sorry for their offenses against God will be forgiven. They will be required to undergo a cleansing, which they must accept with humility.

Many, many, souls will accept My Hand of Mercy, but for the souls who have committed mortal sin, they will be so hardened that they will shun My Mercy.  This Crusade Prayer must be recited for souls for after the Warning.

Crusade Prayer (88) for souls after The Warning

O Sacred Heart of Jesus, show Mercy to all of us poor sinners.

Enlighten those hearts of stone, so desperate in their quest for guidance.

Forgive them their iniquities.

Help them, through Your Love and Mercy, to find it in their hearts to grasp Your great Gift of Redemption.

I implore You to forgive all souls who reject the Truth of God.

Cover them with Your Light, Dear Jesus so that it will blind them to the wickedness and snares of the devil who will try to cut them off from You for eternity.

I beg You to give all God’s children the strength to be thankful for Your Great Mercy.

I ask that You open the door to Your Kingdom to all lost souls who wander the earth in a state of helplessness and hopelessness. Amen.

Go, My disciples, and adhere to My instructions to prepare your souls for My Divine Mercy.

Your Jesus

A REFLECTION FOR EMYENDA YA TOORO IN A TIME OF MOURNING
By Omubito Kimome Ruben Araali-Makubebe | Royal and Political Leader

To Emyenda ya Tooro,

I write to you as a Mubito, as your leader, and as a man grounded in both the law of the state and the law of our culture, in this sacred hour when grief and duty meet.

Yes, we are in deep mourning. Omukama Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV Atulize. The drums are silent. The Kingdom weeps.

It is precisely in such a moment that culture must speak louder than emotion.

Our elders, in their wisdom, left us with a profound philosophy encoded in language itself. The number 9 is Mwenda. From Mwenda we get Emyenda, and Emyenda is Love. This is not a coincidence. It is our worldview. The Batooro have endured for centuries not because we are the strongest, but because we are a people bound by love — love for Obukama, love for our customs, and love for one another. That love is our greatest institution.

It is that love that must guide our conduct now.

To bring clarity and to prevent distortion, I offer this intellectual and cultural guidance on the two sacred principles that many are now debating:

1. The Custodianship of the Royal Burial.
In Tooro custom, the burial of an Omukama is not a family funeral; it is a state and spiritual transition. For that reason, tradition is explicit: No one is permitted to bury the King — not the Queen Mother, not the Princesses, not the clan elders. That singular, sacred duty is vested in the New King alone. Why? Because the Crown never dies. The act of burial by the successor is the ultimate proof of continuity. It declares to the world and to the ancestors that the Kingdom lives on.

2. The Philosophy of Mwenda — The Nine Coffee Beans.
Our custom forbids flowers and soil in this rite. The New King buries his predecessor with 9 coffee beans — Mwenda, Omwani. To the outsider, this may look simple. To the intellectual and cultural mind, it is profound: Coffee is life, it is seed, it is continuity. Nine is Mwenda — the number of completeness and of love. It is the seal of Emyenda ya Tooro. It says: what you plant in love shall never die.

Let us be clear: This guidance is not about taking sides. It is not political. It is about preserving the integrity of who we are as Batooro. Culture is not an opinion; it is an institution.

I therefore appeal to all Emyenda ya Tooro, both at home and in the diaspora: Keep calm. Keep love. Keep unity.

Do not let grief become division. Do not let social media become the burial ground. Let us give space and respect to the Office of the Omusuga, the custodian of our rites, and the official burial committee to guide us with dignity and order.

The Kingdom is bigger than all of us. Let us honour our fallen King by honouring the culture he embodied.

Further official communication will follow.

text:
The security order Europe has not named already exists.

👇 A Line of State strategic doctrine essay. Published in @Jerusalem_Post.

That European-Israeli security order runs from the Arctic and Baltic through the Mediterranean and North Africa, into the Levant, the Red Sea and the routes to Asia. Missiles, drones, maritime coercion, cables, energy, cyber and supply chains have already unified what diplomacy still files as separate theatres.

The fault line is no longer alliance. It is veto.

The danger is not American absence. It is American indispensability.

The danger is not Turkey outside NATO. It is Turkey inside it.

Washington converts dependence into jurisdiction. Ankara converts membership into leverage.

Different instruments. Same veto.

Greenland and Cyprus expose the same defect at opposite ends of the map. An ally can exert territorial pressure. A NATO member can coerce European states while sitting inside the consensus mechanism meant to protect them. America can choose its theatres; Europe and Israel cannot choose their geography.

A friendly veto remains a veto.

Israel built American finance, licences, components, replenishment and export approvals into its force structure. The 2016 US Israel MOU subsidised capability while embedding donor control inside the Israeli defence economy.

Aid that dictates expenditure is donor industrial policy inside the recipient’s defence economy.

After 2028, the question is not what Washington offers Israel. It is how much dependency Jerusalem chooses to buy.

Europe faces the same sovereignty test. Defence spending cannot create strategic autonomy while production, modification, integration, replenishment or transfer remain subject to foreign permission. A weapon dependent on foreign consent is possessed, not sovereign.

Autarky is unnecessary.

Substitutability is sovereignty.

Turkey exposes the internal vulnerability. Ankara remains Western enough to preserve protection and access, revisionist enough to monetise its indispensability, and autonomous enough to ease Russian isolation, widen Iran’s latitude and add another defence framework with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a nuclear power, without surrendering its NATO leverage.

Consensus becomes constraint when coercion comes from within.

Lisbon 2.0 leaves NATO as Europe’s principal military instrument against Russia while ending its monopoly over European security. Article 42(7) already supplies the legal core. Turkey is not an EU member. It cannot condition that obligation.

Lisbon 2.0 turns that legal fact into architecture.

Europe brings industrial scale, aerospace and naval depth, lift, space, finance and continental geography; Israel brings wartime endurance, missile defence, intelligence, unmanned systems, electronic warfare and integration.

Europe needs Israeli capability without American permission. Israel needs European depth without American indispensability.

A Europe sovereign enough to defy Washington - even when it opposes Israel - is a strategic asset for Israel.

Diplomatic convenience is not a strategic interest.

That same logic is now visible in Athens. @KalenteridisSav states its operational consequence: Greece must organise around states that share its interests and threats, with Cyprus and Israel at the core.

The architecture already exists in law, procurement, force structure and geography. Declaration lags reality.

Israel is not an adjunct to it. On Europe’s southeastern flank, it is Lisbon 2.0’s principal military pillar outside the EU.

Every European defence euro and every Israeli defence shekel must face one test:

Which veto does it remove?

In 1995, having  paniked because no offers of a university job had materialized,neither from my academic advisor for the Ph.D. Richard Hull,professor of African history at NYU, who SHOULD HAVE gone all out to get me placed, but did not do so,nor from anyone else  at A&S! Thus,I suggested to him that I would be delighted to give a lecture to the faculty on my area of expertise, "social movements in Algeria prior to independence  in 1962, but Hull wasn't having it,perhaps because of my  alleged sympathy for white rule in Africa--witness my article in the NYT "For White Rule in Rhodesia," 10 Aug.1976--and/or my sympathy for parlor fascists like JJ Susini,convicted of the torture slaying of Raymond Gorel, treasurer of the 0AS who had been   suspected of theft of funds from the Organization! A more basic reason was perhaps that I was not black,nor a member of a "victimized" group, but a white conservative. 
Whatever Hull's motives for rejecting my offer, and his standoffish attitude towards me throughout those years, 1972-1980 when he was supposed to help me but did not do so,I found it heart breaking, and so did my parents,since I would have been the first in my family of English immigrants to the US to, not only get a Ph.D.,but to become a college, university professor! And if anyone deserved a second chance, it was ABH.I had made 4 "tournees" to France and Algeria, interviewed over 100 former spooks and gunmen involved in the struggle over Algeria's future,and every interview was in the idiom of Rabelais! How about that?uSo ,did I deserve a second chance to prove  that I was worthy of a second chance? "C'est au lecteur de juger!" 
First,my academic qualifications: BA TULANE UNIVERSITY,M.A.COLUMBIA u. in French,2 M.A.'s from NYU plus a doctorate awarded in 1980, plus 2 certficates in French from the Sorbonne,Fulbright for service in Senegal 1994-5,inclusion of my audio interviews in French at the Hoover Institution,plus 30 years of service as an interpreter for https://t.co/5w8o8mt320 of the Dept. of State and last but not least, 3 published tomes on the end of French  Algeria! 
Who was more deserving of a university post than ABH yet who was treated with less consideration than ABH? ALSO deserves mention that ABH  served 4 yrs. as a relief worker in Muslim Africa, plus many stints in Rhodesia,South Africa and Northern Rhodesia! Do I qualify as an "old African hand?" "Je crois que oui!"
Let me now inform my followers and Dick Hull about my socio economic origins! 
I grew up in a drafty waterfront town called Port Washington, and parents, immigrants from GREAT BRITAIN, worked mainly in the homes of the wealthy in Sands Point and Old Westbury! It should also be added  that the gunmen and spooks whom I interviewed for my dissertation were part of what was called the Organisation de l'Armee Secrete,"formed in 1961 to defend the right of more than a million pieds noirs in ALGERIA which had been French for over 130 years.
I should also add that to enliven my lecture that I had hoped to give to the A &S faculty in 1995,I would have  also ordered 2 bottles of champagne and a bottle of  Calvados for all of us to enjoy, &that I had also hired a videographer to film my lecture! But I never got the chance to do so because my advisor. Richard Hull put the kibosh on what would have been an enlightening intellectual experience for them as well as for Alexander Baden Harrison! They had spent 8 years enlightening me, so I reckoned I would return the favor, but "malheur"I never got the chance. Hull, my advisor had  put the kibosh on my plans!

After Nixon cut the gold link in 1971, the dollar still needed a reason to be wanted. Three years later Saudi Arabia sold oil only in dollars. In return, Washington offered protection. Other producers followed.

If every country needs oil, and oil is billed in dollars, every country needs dollars.

Japan does not pump much. It still has to buy the fuel. First get dollars. Then hold dollar reserves. Then buy US assets so the next tanker can be paid. That loop is petrodollar recycling. Oil money does not sit in a vault. It comes back as Treasuries, companies, property.

That is the object. Not a secret committee. A billing currency that turns energy into demand for one paper.

The advantage is cheap US borrowing and a sanctions pipe that runs through US banks. Cut the invoice and you cut the demand. The last move is a slow shift, not a revolution. Countries drop the dollar where sanctions bite and keep it where it is convenient.

The sin on this side of the screen is treating the dollar as a vibe. You trade the headline. You skip the invoice.

Gold was the old backstop. Oil became the new one.

Not a conspiracy. A settlement rule.

text:
The $5,000 Admission

Donald Trump’s $5,000 “dividend” may be the clearest evidence yet that the White House sees the cost of living as a genuine threat to Republicans in the midterm elections.

A president confident that households already felt prosperous would have little reason to attach a four-figure cheque to continued Republican control of Congress.

Trump says that if Republicans retain both chambers in November, every adult American will receive $5,000.

The offer is a campaign promise. It is also a diagnosis.

For months, the administration has argued that investment is rising, tariffs are strengthening American industry and economic growth will eventually vindicate its programme. Voters encounter the economy somewhere less abstract: supermarkets, rents, mortgages, insurance premiums, utility bills and monthly bank balances.

The dividend compresses that argument into something much easier to sell.

Republicans win. You get $5,000.

For Trump, who will not himself appear on the ballot, that simplicity has obvious value. It gives supporters a personal reason to treat a congressional election as though his own name were still on the ticket.

Yet the apparent simplicity disappears almost as soon as the financing begins.

A programme covering most adult Americans would cost well over $1 trillion, depending on eligibility. Congress would have to approve it. Republican fiscal conservatives would have to accept another large federal outlay at a time when annual deficits are running near $2 trillion and federal debt has reached roughly $40 trillion.

That tension already has a precedent. When Trump floated a smaller $2,000 tariff dividend, congressional Republicans showed little appetite for converting tariff receipts directly into cheques. Some preferred to use the money to reduce the deficit.

Marc Goldwein of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget captured the contradiction in the word “dividend” itself. Companies distribute dividends from profits. Washington is borrowing heavily every year.

“We don’t have surpluses to give away.”

That is the fiscal problem in one sentence.

Tariff revenues could cover part of the cost. They do not make a programme of this scale disappear from the federal balance sheet. Eligibility may therefore have to narrow, and JD Vance has already suggested that wealthier Americans could be excluded — an early retreat from the simplicity of “every adult American”.

A Republican victory would clear only the first hurdle.

The promise would still have to survive Congress, fiscal resistance, eligibility negotiations and the arithmetic of financing.

That matters before anyone receives a cheque, because Trump needs the promise to work politically now.

The public discussion quickly moved from the merits of a new $5,000 payment to the record of earlier promises.

What happened to the DOGE dividend?

What happened to the $2,000 tariff rebate?

What happened to cheaper groceries and cheaper gasoline?

Those commitments were not identical in legal or political terms. Voters rarely preserve such distinctions with much care. They remember being told that something tangible was coming, then compare that memory with what actually arrived.

Trump wants the new promise to move attention forward.

Instead, it has reopened the ledger behind him.

That creates a different kind of problem from the one facing Congress.

The headline value of the offer is fixed at $5,000. Its electoral value depends on how likely voters think they are to receive it.

A voter who regards the payment as highly probable may treat it as a meaningful personal stake in Republican victory. A voter who sees it as another conditional promise will price it very differently.

The discount therefore comes from two directions.

Past promises affect Trump’s personal credibility.

The structure of the proposal affects its institutional credibility.

The White House needs voters to focus on the amount. The debate is increasingly shifting toward the odds.

And if those hurdles are eventually cleared, the nature of the problem changes again.

A transfer exceeding $1 trillion would inject a large amount of purchasing power into American households. Trump has said the money should be spent inside the United States, strengthening its immediate effect on domestic demand.

That would be politically attractive for obvious reasons. It would also be economically awkward.

The administration would be answering anger over the cost of living with another large burst of demand.

How much that matters would depend on the final size of the programme, its financing, the inflation environment and the Federal Reserve’s response. But Treasury borrowing, inflation expectations and long-term yields would all become part of the calculation well before the political memory of the cheques had faded.

The contradiction is temporal.

Trump needs households to feel richer on an electoral clock.

The federal balance sheet operates on a longer one.

Campaigns live in November.

Bond markets do not.

This is why the $5,000 proposal deserves more attention than the usual argument over whether politicians are trying to buy votes.

It reveals where the White House thinks Republican vulnerability now lies. It shows how aggressively Trump is prepared to respond. It also exposes the constraints surrounding the response before a single dollar has been authorised.

The promise could still be effective politics. Five thousand dollars is large enough to make an otherwise abstract congressional contest feel immediate to millions of voters.

But its very existence is already informative.

Trump has put $5,000 on the ballot because the household economy has become too politically important to answer with headline statistics alone.

The number voters see is $5,000.

The election will test how much of it they think is really there.

text:
THE $212 TRILLION ROAD TO SOCIALISM
The promises sound free because the invoice is hidden📷By Francis Gauthier
Two hundred twelve trillion dollars.
That number is so large that Washington hopes your eyes glaze over before your common sense wakes up.
The Democratic Socialists of America promise a country where government guarantees health care, housing, employment, college, utilities, child care, debt cancellation, climate programs, and assorted other benefits. The sales pitch is simple: ordinary Americans receive the benefits, while billionaires and corporations pick up the check.
There is only one problem.
The arithmetic does not come within artillery range of working.
#DemocraticSocialists
#SocialismIsntFree
#212Trillion
#WhoPays
#TaxpayersPay
#LimitedGovernment
#FiscalResponsibility
#SaveTheAmericanDream
📷📷📷 THE COURT OF PUBLIC OPINION IS NOW OPEN 📷📷📷📷
The socialist wish list carries an estimated price tag ranging from $71.2 trillion to nearly $212 trillion over ten years.
They promise health care, housing, jobs, college, utilities, and more. But nothing is free. Doctors must be paid. Homes must be built. Workers must produce. Somebody must cover the bill.
So let’s hear the jury’s verdict:
📷 Can taxing billionaires possibly finance this agenda year after year?📷
📷 When that money runs out, how deeply will Washington reach into working families’ paychecks?📷
📷 How much control over our jobs, homes, health care, and energy should the federal government possess?📷
📷 Are politicians selling benefits while hiding the real invoice?📷
📷Put your verdict in the comments below. Debate the facts, challenge the numbers, and tell us where you stand.

Biblical principle: wise people count the cost before building—Luke 14:28. Demand the full price before Washington signs your name to the bill.📷📷📷📷📷📷📷📷📷📷
Cato Institute tax-policy director Adam Michel estimates that combining the major parts of the socialist agenda would require between $71.2 trillion and $211.6 trillion in additional federal spending over ten years.
The $212 trillion figure is the high end of an estimate—not a bill already passed, not debt already borrowed, and not an official Congressional Budget Office score. That distinction matters. Honest conservatives should state it before anyone else does.
But that qualification does not rescue the agenda.
The low estimate alone would add an average of $7.12 trillion in federal spending every year. The high estimate would average $21.16 trillion every year.
America currently spends roughly $7 trillion annually through the federal government. In plain English, even the low estimate amounts to placing another federal government on top of the one taxpayers already cannot afford.
That is not Scandinavian social spending with a few extra programs. That is a fundamental transfer of American economic life into federal hands.
WHAT IS INSIDE THE $212 TRILLION ESTIMATE?
The largest components reported in the Cato analysis include:
* Universal government health care: approximately $30 trillion to $75.4 trillion
* Slavery reparations: approximately $13.5 trillion to $28 trillion
* A federal jobs guarantee: approximately $4.4 trillion to $60.4 trillion
* Government-guaranteed housing: approximately $3.4 trillion to $16.6 trillion
* Additional spending for climate and energy programs, education, utilities, debt cancellation, food benefits, child care, transportation, and other guarantees
Adding the estimated costs produces Cato’s range of approximately $71.2 trillion to $211.6 trillion over ten years.
The enormous spread between the low and high numbers tells us something important: many of these promises are political slogans rather than detailed legislation. The cost depends on who qualifies, what benefits are included, how many people participate, what wages government pays, and whether the government subsidizes private services or takes them over entirely.
The high number should therefore be treated as a fiscal stress scenario. It shows where the broadest interpretation of the socialist agenda could lead.
The low number is the more conservative warning—and it is still financially staggering.
WHAT WOULD THAT MEAN FOR EVERY AMERICAN?
Spread across approximately 340 million Americans, the estimated cost equals roughly:
* $21,000 per person annually at the low end
* $62,000 per person annually at the high end
Using approximately 132 million American households, the gross federal spending equals roughly:
* $54,000 per household per year at the low end
* $160,000 per household per year at the high end
Those numbers are not proposed household tax bills. Some government spending would replace money people currently pay for health insurance, tuition, housing, or other services.
That is an important qualification, especially with Medicare for All. Under a national health plan, private insurance premiums would largely disappear while federal taxes and spending would explode. Part of the federal expense would therefore be a transfer of existing private payments into government accounts.
But changing the payer does not make the service free.
It changes who controls the money.
Congress sets the taxes. Federal agencies establish reimbursement rates. Bureaucracies decide which treatments qualify, what providers receive, and how limited medical resources are allocated.
A government insurance card can promise care. It cannot manufacture another doctor, hospital bed, nurse, drug, or surgeon.
When demand exceeds supply, somebody must ration the service. The rationing will come through prices, waiting lists, restricted benefits, lower provider payments, administrative rules, or political favoritism. Scarcity does not disappear because Congress passes a resolution against it.
Independent studies of earlier Medicare for All proposals demonstrate the scale. The Mercatus Center estimated that one version would increase federal commitments by approximately $32.6 trillion over ten years. Urban Institute research arrived at a similar federal-spending increase of roughly $32 trillion to $34 trillion.
The analysts disagreed on some consequences, but they agreed on the central fact: shifting nearly the entire health-care system onto Washington’s books would produce an unprecedented increase in federal spending.
THE FEDERAL JOBS GUARANTEE
The proposed federal jobs guarantee produces the widest estimate: approximately $4.4 trillion to $60.4 trillion.
That wide range depends on how many Americans join the program, the wages and benefits offered, and whether analysts subtract savings from unemployment programs and other welfare spending.
A Levy Economics Institute model envisioned roughly 15 million public-service workers. Its authors argued that the program could stimulate the economy and reduce some safety-net costs. Even their favorable analysis estimated a lasting federal budget effect of roughly 1.1% to 1.5% of GDP.
Cato’s $60.4 trillion upper estimate appears to assume far broader enrollment or considerably more generous compensation. It is best understood as a high-end scenario rather than the most probable outcome.
Nevertheless, the institutional danger exists at either price.
A permanent federal jobs guarantee would make government the employer of last resort for millions of Americans. Federal officials would determine eligible jobs, compensation, benefits, workplace rules, discipline, and the distribution of workers.
Private businesses must produce something customers willingly purchase before making payroll. Government programs need only appropriate another pile of taxpayers’ money.
The result would place enormous pressure on private employers, particularly small businesses, which would be forced to compete against federally subsidized wages and benefits. The neighborhood contractor, machine shop, farm, garage, restaurant, and nursing home do not own a printing press.
Washington does.
HOUSING FOR ALL
Government can guarantee a benefit on paper. It cannot guarantee the physical supply needed to provide it.
Housing requires land, lumber, concrete, skilled workers, financing, roads, sewer systems, permits, and years of construction. Government subsidies can change who pays, but they cannot repeal those material requirements.
The estimated cost of “housing for all” ranges from $3.4 trillion to $16.6 trillion because the slogan does not describe one settled program.
Would Washington subsidize rents? Construct public housing? Purchase existing buildings? Guarantee mortgages? Cancel rent? Cap rents nationwide? Establish housing as a legally enforceable federal right?
Each choice produces a different cost and a different economic consequence.
Rent control can appear cheap on a federal budget because much of the cost is pushed onto property owners. But the economic bill arrives through fewer rental units, deferred maintenance, abandoned buildings, and less new construction.
If America wants more affordable housing, governments should reduce unnecessary permitting delays, loosen unreasonable zoning restrictions, encourage infrastructure development, and allow builders to build.
Subsidizing demand without increasing supply simply gives more dollars permission to chase the same number of apartments.
REPARATIONS
Cato estimates the cost of national reparations at approximately $13.5 trillion to $28 trillion.
No final national reparations program exists with fixed eligibility standards, payment levels, or delivery methods. Some proposals call for direct individual payments. Others propose housing grants, community investments, debt relief, business funds, or calculations based on generations of alleged economic loss.
Consequently, no precise national price can be established.
The constitutional problems would be nearly as large as the budgetary problems. Congress would have to classify Americans according to ancestry, determine which historical relationships created eligibility, and decide which present-day taxpayers owe compensation.
That process would generate years of litigation while placing racial classifications deeper into federal law. A nation already suffering from division would be told that justice requires Washington to divide citizens officially by bloodline.
That is not national reconciliation. It is a permanent federal argument over ancestry, money, and inherited guilt.
WHY TAXING THE RICH CANNOT PAY FOR IT
The standard answer is always the same:
“Tax the billionaires.”
Fine. Let us examine it.
Cato reports that the combined wealth of the Forbes 400 richest Americans was approximately $6.6 trillion in 2025.
Suppose Washington confiscated every dollar of it: businesses, stock, homes, farms, equipment, investments, and cash.
Ignore the Fifth Amendment. Ignore the immediate market collapse. Ignore that selling trillions of dollars in assets would drive their prices into the basement. Ignore that pension funds and retirement accounts own shares in many of the same companies.
Even under that imaginary 100% confiscation, the federal government would collect less than enough to finance one year of the low-cost socialist program.
Then what happens in the second year?
Government cannot confiscate the same factory twice.
Wealth is a stock. Federal spending is an annual flow. Permanent programs require permanent streams of tax revenue.
Corporate profits cannot cover the agenda either. Corporate income funds dividends, retirement plans, business expansion, research, equipment, and employee compensation. Taxing it heavily affects shareholders, workers, and customers through some combination of lower returns, reduced investment, smaller wages, and higher prices.
Eventually the government must reach the only tax base broad enough to produce the required money: ordinary working Americans.
That means some combination of:
* Higher payroll taxes
* Higher middle-class income taxes
* A national sales tax or value-added tax
* Higher energy taxes
* Higher business taxes passed through to consumers
* Taxes on investments and retirement savings
* Massive borrowing
* Currency creation and inflation
European welfare states do not finance their programs by taxing only a handful of billionaires. They impose broad payroll and consumption taxes on ordinary workers.
If Americans want European benefits, politicians must admit that American workers will pay European taxes.
Promising Nordic benefits with a tax bill mailed exclusively to Elon Musk is campaign theater.
AMERICA IS ALREADY IN THE HOLE
These socialist promises would not begin with a balanced federal budget.
According to contemporary reporting on the Congressional Budget Office outlook, Washington is already expected to accumulate deficits exceeding $20 trillion over the coming decade. The debt held by the public is projected to reach approximately 120% of gross domestic product by 2036.
Interest payments increasingly compete with defense, transportation, and other federal priorities.
That means the socialist agenda would be piled on top of:
* Existing federal debt
* Annual trillion-dollar deficits
* Social Security’s approaching financing crisis
* Medicare’s rising costs
* Growing interest payments
* An aging population
* Military and national-security obligations
The country would enter this experiment with its credit card already bent from overuse.
And Republicans need to be honest here: the present debt crisis was not built by Democrats alone.
Republican administrations and Republican Congresses have also borrowed too much, expanded spending, and delayed entitlement reform. Conservatives cannot credibly condemn a $212 trillion socialist fantasy while excusing every deficit carrying an “R.”
A ledger does not recognize party affiliation.
Limited government requires more than a flag pin and a speech about Ronald Reagan. It requires spending discipline when our own side controls the checkbook.
THE REAL DANGER IS CONTROL
The fiscal burden is only half the story.
The DSA agenda would make Washington the nation’s:
* Health insurer
* Employer of last resort
* Housing authority
* College financier
* Utility guarantor
* Energy planner
* Debt-cancellation office
* Distributor of essential benefits
When government supplies nearly everything, government can attach conditions to nearly everything.
Political leaders would determine which industries receive investment, which medical services receive funding, which energy sources survive, which housing projects get built, and which groups qualify for special payments.
Economic dependence becomes political leverage.
The traditional American system placed most daily decisions with individuals, families, churches, local communities, states, and private enterprise. Federal power existed for defined national purposes and operated under constitutional limits.
The socialist model turns that arrangement upside down. Washington becomes the center of economic life, while citizens line up for benefits funded with money taken from one another.
That is not merely bigger government.
It is a different relationship between the citizen and the state.
WHAT WOULD BREAK FIRST?
Fiscal capacity would weaken first. Adding even the low-end estimate to current deficits would overwhelm a Treasury already paying enormous interest costs.
Private investment would suffer as government absorbed more available capital and imposed heavier taxes.
Labor markets would change as businesses competed with federally guaranteed employment.
Health care would face rationing pressure as unlimited promised demand ran into a limited number of providers.
Housing shortages would worsen if subsidies and price controls discouraged construction.
Inflation could rise if Washington attempted to borrow or create money instead of imposing the full cost through visible taxes.
Federalism would weaken as national guarantees replaced state experimentation and local accountability.
Finally, America would lose its ability to respond to real emergencies. A government permanently spending at emergency levels has little reserve left for war, recession, pandemic, financial crisis, or natural disaster.
When everything becomes a federal emergency, the country has no emergency capacity remaining.
THE CONSERVATIVE ALTERNATIVE
America does need better health care, affordable housing, reliable energy, useful employment, and honest opportunity.
Conservatives cannot answer every public concern with a shrug.
But the answer is not to nationalize scarcity.
America should expand the supply of doctors and nurses, reform medical licensing, permit interstate competition, demand transparent pricing, and separate routine medical payments from catastrophic insurance.
Government should remove unnecessary construction barriers, speed up permitting, encourage infrastructure development, protect property rights, and allow housing supply to respond to demand.
Tax policy should reward work, saving, domestic production, and family formation.
Washington should eliminate corporate welfare, reduce waste, reform existing entitlements responsibly, and maintain a real safety net for people who genuinely cannot care for themselves.
Public assistance should help people regain independence whenever possible. It should not convert temporary need into permanent political dependency.
Sound money matters. Balanced budgets matter. Local control matters. Private property matters. Work matters.
These are not outdated slogans. They are load-bearing beams in a free society.
FINAL VERDICT
The claim that the DSA agenda will cost exactly $212 trillion is too absolute.
The accurate statement is that Cato estimates the combined agenda could produce between $71.2 trillion and $211.6 trillion in additional federal spending over ten years.
The high end relies on expansive assumptions and should be presented as a warning scenario, not a guaranteed outcome. Some federal spending—especially health spending—would replace private payments rather than represent entirely new consumption.
But the fundamental conclusion remains intact.
Even the low estimate represents an almost unimaginable expansion of federal spending and control. There is no mathematically credible way to finance it solely through taxes on billionaires and corporations.
The middle class would pay.
Workers would pay through payroll and income taxes. Retirees would pay through taxes, inflation, or lower investment returns. Consumers would pay through higher prices. Small businesses would pay through regulation and reduced capital. Children not yet born would pay interest on the debt.
The socialist program offers Americans a remarkable bargain: surrender more earnings, more independence, and more local control today in exchange for federal promises that future taxpayers will somehow finance tomorrow.
The bill is not going to “the rich.”
The bill is going to the machinist, nurse, electrician, truck driver, farmer, retiree, store owner, young couple, and child still sitting in a first-grade classroom.
Freedom has a cost. But dependency carries a larger invoice—and Washington never forgets to add interest.
THE COURT OF PUBLIC OPINION IS OPEN
If confiscating the wealth of America’s richest citizens cannot finance even one year of the low-end estimate, which taxes will ultimately fall on working families?
What happens when promised health care exceeds the available number of doctors?
Who decides which families receive housing when government promises more homes than builders can produce?
How much control should Washington exercise over a citizen’s job, home, health care, energy, education, and income?
And when will both political parties stop borrowing money from children who are too young to vote?
Count the cost before beginning: “For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?” — Luke 14:28. A free people should demand the full price before politicians lay the first stone.
Sources: Cato Institute commentary; Cato estimate reporting; Mercatus Medicare for All analysis; Urban Institute single-payer analysis; Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget; Levy Economics Institute jobs study; 2026 CBO outlook reporting.
