text:
Think like a simple scientist.

You have three facts, like three stones on the table:

The human cup is cracked. History is full of bones.
Even so, we point and say, “That is wrong” — even when it is our own team.
A cracked cup cannot be the ruler that measures the cup.

In science, when the cup cannot be the ruler, you look for a ruler outside the cup. Nobody measures a meter with a bent meter. Nobody says the north is the boat. The boat turns. The north does not.

Now test the rival ideas, the way you test a theory:

“Good is whatever the tribe likes.”
But we accuse our own tribe. Theory killed by the data.

“Good is whatever the king commands.”
But we accuse the king. Theory killed.

“Good is whatever the strong can do.”
But we call the strong a criminal, not a winner. Theory killed.

One explanation is left that holds all three facts together: there is a Reference that is not the team. A Ruler above the human judge. Without that Ruler, “wrong” is only a taste. With it, “wrong” is true. You already talk as if it were true. You are using the tool and denying the workshop.

That Reference is God.
In flesh, it is Jesus Christ: not a club that got a good grade. He is the test in person.

Take Him away. Good becomes again the fist of the strongest.

This is not finding God under a microscope. It is the same step science takes when it picks the theory that explains the data without cheating. The data are the crack, the pile of bones, and your anger at the pile. Together they do not point to man. They point up.

The cup is still cracked.
The Ruler is not.
You inherited the measure.
Do not pretend you invented it in the laboratory of “me.”

And here is the most important part.

When whole societies took that idea into the state — a state without Christianity’s diagnosis — they did not become free adults at last. They removed the church. They removed the Reference of what is good. Then they proved Christ was always right: man is not good by nature, and he cannot stay good for long without the perfect Reference, which is God.

Atheism is older than Marx. A lonely skeptic in a café is not a civilization. What was new was this: communism put unbelief in the palace, in the school, in the secret police, and called it science. It used the most powerful machine on earth — the modern state — to preach that there is no God, no fall, no sin, only systems and enemies of the people. Tear out the root. The new man will grow.

He did not grow.

He starved. He informed. He filled the grave.

The Soviet Union: Cheka, Gulag, engineered hunger. In Ukraine, 1932–1933, the Holodomor — grain taken, borders sealed, villages blacklisted. Millions dead. Stalin’s purges shot the party itself. The Black Book of Communism puts the Soviet dead on the order of twenty million. Count as you will. The order of magnitude does not become small.

Mao’s China: the Great Leap Forward, 1958–1962 — the deadliest famine in the record of man. Then the Cultural Revolution, children taught to smash the “four olds,” including the soul. The same Black Book assigns China on the order of sixty-five million. Other tallies run higher or lower. None of them look like “humanity finally grown up.”

Cambodia, 1975–1979: Year Zero. Pol Pot emptied the cities, murdered the glasses-wearers, the teachers, the believers. About two million — a quarter of a nation — in less than four years. That is not “religion doing India.” That is the Reference ripped out and the jar worshiping itself.

Across the file — USSR, China, Cambodia, North Korea, Ethiopia under the Derg, the list does not stay local — Courtois and his colleagues reached a grim working total near one hundred million. Scholars argue the edges. They do not argue that the mountain is a molehill. Atheism had existed for centuries. Communism gave it tanks, ration cards, and a curriculum.

This is the experiment the critic asked for.

Remove the diagnosis: man is flawed.
Replace it with: man is clay for the Party.
Remove God as the Régua.
Install history as god.
Then watch the strong call murder “progress.”

Christ said no one is good but God. The twentieth century wrote that sentence in mass graves and called it a five-year plan.

You inherited a morality that still flinches at those graves. That flinch is not Marx. Marx gave you the permission structure: if there is no Judge above the state, the state will judge without mercy. You kept the horror. You forgot the Voice that told you why horror is not “necessary.”

No God, no fall, no limit — only power and a future tense.
That is not enlightenment. That is Eden again: “you will be as gods.”
The fruit was not knowledge. The fruit was a body count.

The jar without water does not become a fountain. It becomes a weapon.
The people without a Reference do not become good. They become busy.

So when the critic says he got his morals from secular philosophers after 1789, point him past the salon to the century that tested the thesis with the full weight of the state. The thesis failed in blood. Christ did not fail. He had already named the patient.

Man is not the Régua.
God is.
Take away that Reference and the world does not rise. It counts its dead — and still pretends the Accuser was the problem.

You breathe Christian air.

If you can stand in 2026 and call these things evil —

slavery,
the infant left to die,
the girl as a prize of war,
the widow on the pyre,
the gladiator killed for sport,
human sacrifice,
cannibal conquest,
the rack,
the witch-fire of the mob,
colonial plunder,
famine ignored while grain is sold,
the peasant crushed by the planter,
the foreigner treated as another species,
the king who calls himself a god —

you did not get that reflex from pagan Rome. Rome cheered the arena. Infants could be exposed. Slaves were tools with voices. Cicero could be eloquent and still live inside that air.

You did not get it from classical Greece as such. Aristotle treated some men as slaves by nature. The city could be brilliant and still toss an unwanted baby. Beauty and geometry do not teach you that the weak are sacred.

You did not get it from Muhammad’s political order as history actually ran. Islamic law regulated slavery; it did not abolish the category. Raids, concubinage, and the servile status of captives were not a late accident. They were built in. A conscience that says “no human is loot” is not that system speaking.

You did not get it from every throne in China, where a magnificent court could bury opponents and treat mass life as the emperor’s clay. You did not get it from every rite that burned a widow or ate an enemy to steal his strength. Those worlds had order. They did not have the sentence that condemns the strong when the strong is “civilized.”

So when the critic sneers, “Christianity did the evil,” answer with a slap that is also a fact: the standard you are using to damn the chain, the pyre, the arena, the raid, and the throne is not those systems’ invention. It is Christ’s pressure on the world’s nerves. Humanity leaked. Christ named the leak. You inherited the accusation and forgot the Accuser.

The jar is still clay. The Reference is not.

Now look at the people who actually followed the Reference — not the ones who stamped a cross on a ledger.

Basil of Caesarea, c. 369–373. In a famine year he fed the poor; by about 372–373 he built the Basiliad outside Caesarea — hospice, care for the sick and lepers, a “new city” of mercy. Gregory of Nazianzus describes it in the funeral oration. Basil’s own letters speak of the ptochotropheion. That is not Rome’s circus. That is Matthew 25 made into stone.

Bartolomé de las Casas, 1542 / published 1552. A Dominican who had seen the conquest, then turned and wrote A Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies for the Spanish court. He named gold-lust, massacre, and enslavement as sin — against his own nation’s project. The jar of Spain was cracked. He used Christ’s measure on the crack.

Quakers, 16 June 1783. London Yearly Meeting laid before Parliament a petition against the slave trade, signed by hundreds of Friends, calling the enslaved “fellow creatures” with “the natural rights of mankind.” In 1787 they helped form the Society for Effecting the Abolition of the Slave Trade. Clay people. Clear Reference.

William Wilberforce, 1787–1833. Diary conviction, 1787: two great objects — suppress the slave trade, reform manners. Twenty years of bills. Slave Trade Act, 25 March 1807. Slavery Abolition Act, 1833, as he lay dying. He was not the Company at prayer. He was a man trapped by Christ.

William Carey in India, 1793–1834. Sees sati, 1799. Presses, translates, plants schools. On 4–6 December 1829 the Bengal Sati Regulation is issued; Carey leaves Sunday service to put the ban into Bengali so it can run at once. Hindu reformers such as Ram Mohan Roy labored too. Name them. Still: the nerve that said “a widow is not fuel” was trained by Christ.

This is the pattern. Rome gives you the arch and the whip. Greece gives you the syllogism and the natural slave. The caliph’s law gives you a ranked world. The old shrine gives you a knife. Christ gives you a judgment that falls on London and Lisbon, on the planter and the priest, on the mob and the monarch: you are not good enough to be the rule.

So the critic is standing on a floor he did not build. He condemns slavery, spectacle-killing, the discarded child, the plundered village, the burned widow — with a moral tongue Christianity taught the world to use. The same tongue Las Casas used on Spain. The same tongue Wilberforce used on Britain. The same tongue Carey used in Bengal.

Imperfect jars. Perfect diagnosis. Every human leaks; therefore every human needs a Reference that does not leak. The Bible names it. History shows the trail when people obey it.

Do not confuse the cracked cup with the living water. The cup will fail you. Jesus will not.

If a dog loves chicken, you do not lure it with charcoal.
If a child lives for candy, you do not bait the trap with a fast.
If a thirsty man will sell his soul for wine, you do not hold out an empty cup and call it joy.
You offer what the hunger already wants. That is how you catch a creature. That is how you tell a hunter from a father.

Now put the two majority claims on that table and watch what is served.

In the days of Jesus the Jews wanted a war-king: Rome off their necks, a throne in Zion, a Messiah who wins the way men win. He offers the opposite. No legion. A cross. “My kingdom is not of this world.” The Gentiles wanted to keep the old feast—pleasure, orgies, the body as a god, even the rot of incest that Paul names in the churches’ neighbor-world. Jesus says stop. Do not look to lust. Tear out the eye. One man. One woman. Master the flesh. In the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage. He is not selling chicken to the dog. He is offering charcoal to a mouth trained on meat—and then dying to make the mouth new.

In the days of Muhammad the men who built the army wanted what fighting men have always wanted: women, wine, spoil, a heaven that feels like the night after a raid. Look at the menu. Wives here. More promised there. A lawful appetite crowned. That is not charcoal. That is chicken. The lure matches the pack.

Today the world is more promiscuous, not less. The same test still works. What does each message cost the male ego now?

Then, the greatest machine of power was an army of men. A revelation that baptizes the sword and the bed will gather that machine fast. Now the greatest machine is the state: parties, courts, borders, schools, media. Jesus still says the same inconvenient sentence: his kingdom is not of this world. He will not hand you a ministry of truth to capture. He will not let you baptize your coalition and call it Zion. The gospel remains against what we like. It tells the religious nationalist he cannot have a holy empire. It tells the libertine he cannot have a holy orgy. It tells the ambitious man the last seat is a towel and a basin. So ask the honest question: if someone wanted to deceive us, would he keep offering charcoal—fasting to the sweet tooth, a cross to the man who wants a crown, one wife to the man who wants a harem, a kingdom not of this world to the man who wants this world?

And the other story: the Scriptures were “corrupted,” they say—so that what remains is the hard road. Fasting for candy-lovers. A crucified God for people who wanted a Caesar. That would be the stupidest fraud in history. Forgers who want followers do not edit the bait down. They edit it up.

Watch the present. Islam can advance inside countries where a political left that hates the church will walk beside it for a season. That left is not built on Sinai. It is built on permission: the body as politics, gender as clay, desire as a right. For a while the alliance is useful. A shared enemy—the Christ who says no. After the house is taken, the guest does not keep the host’s rules. Then comes sharia: the army under another name. If a doctrine already allows deception for the cause when the cause is threatened, the handshake was never the destination. It was the door.

So which god is hunting, and which God is fathering?

The god who plates what the age already craves—women and wine for the raider then, power and narrative for the operator now—is easy to recognize. He does not need to change the human heart. He only needs to bless it.

The God of Jesus keeps serving charcoal to the old appetite: die to yourself, one covenant bed, no orgy, no child as a prize, no throne of this world, no virgins as pay, only God. He would be a fool of a con man. He makes sense as a Father who would rather lose the crowd than feed the sickness.

Scripture was not “fixed” to make the gospel tastier. The gospel is still the least marketable offer on the table. That is how you know it was not designed by a man building an army—or a man building a government. It was designed by someone who wants sons, not customers.

In reality, the Left is nothing but the Devil's excrement. He comes along and shits his stinking filth onto nations, ruins the youth, promotes promiscuity, empties minds in favor of a sick collective, attacks families and faith, and then sends his soldiers to dominate, conquer, and enslave people so they will worship him.

Islam Did Not Win by Truth. It Won by Fire, Fear, and a Fake Heaven.

Around the year 650, about twenty years after Muhammad died in 632, Caliph Uthman (ruled 644–656) did not protect the Qur’an. He burned the other written versions. Soldiers in the new empire were already fighting over different readings. Uthman made one official copy and ordered the rest destroyed. That is not preservation. That is a cover-up with a torch. The Bible was copied, attacked, translated, and still stands where anyone can compare the manuscripts. Islam ended the argument by fire. A book that needs burning in the mid-600s to stay “perfect” is already afraid of scrutiny.

Muhammad’s own cousin Ali ibn Abi Talib bowed to him in the first years of the movement, around 610–613, while Ali was still a youth in Muhammad’s house. Family first. House first. Then the tribe. Then the sword. That is how a movement starts when it cannot live on open proof.

After 632, Islam advanced by lie and steel. Arabia was taken first. Then Syria, Egypt, and Persia fell in the 630s and 640s under the early caliphs. “Peace” after you submit. Tax if you refuse. Death if you leave. That is not the Gospel. That is conquest dressed as worship. The endgame is not “know the true God.” The endgame is a global caliphate—one man, or one system of men, sitting on the throne of law, war, and religion. That started as a real empire in Medina and Damascus, then Baghdad, then later the Ottomans, and it is still the dream of those who want the world under their law. That is not adoration of the Creator. That is men manufacturing their own god: themselves. They call it Allah’s rule. It is their rule with a holy stamp.

Watch the history. In 656 Uthman was murdered. Then Muslims killed Muslims over who would rule. The Umayyads turned the caliphate into a family dynasty after 661. The Abbasids seized it in 750. The Ottomans later wrote extra state laws beside sharia when the palace needed it. One century the “law of God” looks one way. The next century the sultan writes what the empire wants. If heaven’s constitution changes with the king’s interest, it was never heaven speaking. It was power speaking.

And the prize they sell? A carnal paradise. Women. Beds. Wine. Endless appetite. That is not the holy God. That is a brothel in the sky for men who obeyed. The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit do not buy souls with lust. Jesus offers a clean heart and the face of God—not a reward that looks like the flesh they already worshiped on earth. If your heaven is built on the same hungers that damn a man, that heaven did not come from Christ.

Force is not faith. Obedience at knifepoint is not what the true God wants. It is stupid. If God only wanted terror, He would not need proud killers to do His advertising. He could split the sky once and every mouth would shut. Even a father knows the difference between a child who honors him and a child who only fears the belt. You think the Maker of the universe is dumber than that? If your god only wants fear, your god is small—and the men who speak for him are full of pride and death.

The true God did not send an empire in the 600s. He sent a Son.

A man owned a fish. Every time he tried to feed it, the fish ran. “I want its good,” he said, “but it thinks I am a monster.” His friend answered: “To that fish you are a giant. The only way it will trust you is if you become a fish and enter the tank.”

That is Jesus. He did not burn books in 650. He did not build a caliphate. He entered our water. He became one of us. He did not demand a heart crushed by soldiers. He asked for a heart that is actually His.

Fear fills an empire. Love makes a son. The true God wants the second. The caliphate only knows the first.

Christianity is not a religion.
It is the way of life that created and built entire civilizations.
It is looking to the reference that is Jesus Christ and saying: “This is the good. This is the way.”

Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights (James 1:17). The reference of what is good is God. In Eden humanity lost that reference and the world sank into darkness. Children abandoned in the streets of Rome. Widows burned alive in India. Cannibals devouring enemies without conscience. Until Jesus Christ came and divided history into before and after.

He restored the reference. Christianity founded the universities, the hospitals, the orphanages. It preserved knowledge while Europe burned. It elevated the dignity of every human being made in the image of God. It ended widow-burning, foot-binding, human sacrifice, and cannibalism across continents. Missionaries carried the cross to the Pacific, to Africa, to India, to China, to Japan — and wherever the reference of Christ took root, the value of life rose and barbarism fell. Even the modern atheist still breathes Christian air without realizing it. The historian Tom Holland, an atheist, confessed: “In my morals and ethics I have learned to accept that I am not Greek or Roman, but deeply and proudly Christian.”

Before Christ, justice belonged to the strong. The slave was property. The woman nearly invisible. The foreigner disposable. The cross was the ultimate instrument of humiliation. Then an innocent Man was crucified by a Roman court — and rose again. That cross became the center of history. Justice and mercy kissed. The idea that every person has infinite dignity, the right of defense, the protection of the weak, the limits of the state — all of it was born from the blood of Christ, not from Greece, not from Rome, not from the Enlightenment.

Yet the prostitute has returned. Empires and governments that once tasted the salt of the gospel now prostitute themselves to every anti-Christ ideology. They sell their children. They fund the persecutors. They call good evil and evil good. They have lost their savor.

And the Beast is rising. The same system that used the prostitute for its pleasure will one day hate her, strip her, devour her, and burn her with fire. The ideologies, the politicians, the nations, the empires that sold themselves for temporary power will be consumed by the very darkness they courted.

This is not the end of the story.
The stone cut without hands is still coming.
The Kingdom of the One who was crucified and rose again will fill the whole earth.

Until then, the remnant must remain salt.
Because the prostitute is already drunk with blood.
And the Beast is already sharpening its teeth.

Psalm 27 is a strong choice for “when people fail you.”
David is not talking about a mild disappointment. He is talking about enemies who want to devour him, false witnesses, people who breathe out violence, and even the possibility that the closest human ties (father and mother) could let him go. The psalm moves from confidence, to longing for God’s presence, to honest pleading, and then back to settled trust.
Here it is:
The LORD is my light and my salvation;
whom shall I fear?
The LORD is the stronghold of my life;
of whom shall I be afraid?
When evildoers assail me
to eat up my flesh,
my adversaries and foes,
it is they who stumble and fall.
Though an army encamp against me,
my heart shall not fear;
though war arise against me,
yet I will be confident.
One thing have I asked of the LORD,
that will I seek after:
that I may dwell in the house of the LORD
all the days of my life,
to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD
and to inquire in his temple.
For he will hide me in his shelter
in the day of trouble;
he will conceal me under the cover of his tent;
he will lift me high upon a rock.
And now my head shall be lifted up
above my enemies all around me,
and I will offer in his tent
sacrifices with shouts of joy;
I will sing and make melody to the LORD.
Hear, O LORD, when I cry aloud;
be gracious to me and answer me!
You have said, “Seek my face.”
My heart says to you,
“Your face, LORD, do I seek.”
Hide not your face from me.
Turn not your servant away in anger,
O you who have been my help.
Cast me not off; forsake me not,
O God of my salvation!
For my father and my mother have forsaken me,
but the LORD will take me in.
Teach me your way, O LORD,
and lead me on a level path
because of my enemies.
Give me not up to the will of my adversaries;
for false witnesses have risen against me,
and they breathe out violence.
I believe that I shall look upon the goodness of the LORD
in the land of the living!
Wait for the LORD;
be strong, and let your heart take courage;
wait for the LORD!
The hinge verse for “people fail you” is verse 10: even the most natural human loyalties can break. David does not pretend that never happens. He names it, then immediately turns to the One who will not.
That is why the psalm fits the way public life often feels. Leaders make promises, parties claim they will protect or deliver, and then the record is mixed or worse. False witnesses and violent talk are not new. The psalm does not tell us to become cynical or to stop caring about justice. It tells us where to put our weight when people prove unreliable.
David’s first move is not “fix the politicians.” It is “the LORD is my light… my stronghold.” His second move is desire: one thing I ask — to be near God, to see His beauty, to inquire of Him. Only after that does he ask for a level path because of his enemies. The order matters. Presence first, then guidance in a crooked world.
The last line is the practical word for a day when people have disappointed you: wait for the LORD. Be strong. Let your heart take courage. Wait.
That is not passivity. It is refusing to let failed people become the measure of reality.
If you want, tomorrow we can take the next one on the card, or stay with this psalm a little longer and look at how David holds both honesty about betrayal and confidence in God at the same time.

🇺🇸 🌊 Sinkhole near Nicolas Cage's Malibu home forces evacuations

A massive sinkhole opened in front of Nicolas Cage's Malibu home, destroying the driveway and severely affecting access to the area. The collapse reached roughly 25 to 30 feet deep and expanded to about 60 feet wide as coastal erosion and powerful surf linked to Marie worsened conditions. Malibu officials declared a local emergency and ordered evacuations affecting 31 properties, with some homes considered unsafe and others cut off from reliable access for residents and emergency crews. The house was unoccupied and no injuries were reported. Beyond the celebrity connection, the incident highlights a broader risk for coastal communities, where erosion can quickly turn property damage into a public safety crisis. Expensive homes offer little protection when the ground itself becomes unstable.

text:
Guru Nanga Tales: The Backstory 

(Public Edition - There is a Private Edition)

The Name

Everything else in this document is context.

This is the point.

For years, followers speculated about the name.
The theories were elaborate — Sanskrit roots, mountain hermitages, a vow.

The truth is simpler than the legends, which is how you know it is true.

On the final morning of a reunion of old schoolmates, the men were saying their goodbyes.

The Guru was in the shower. 

A goodbye missed is a goodbye lost forever — this is doctrine now, though at the time it was just a wet man doing math.

He weighed the towel against the farewell and found the towel wanting.

He stepped out of the shower, crossed the room, embraced his departing friend at full commitment and zero coverage, and returned to the shower to finish what he had started.

The hug was reportedly excellent.

The friend was offered counseling and declined, 
saying he wanted to remember.

The name Nanga — The Naked One — was ratified before the Guru had toweled off.

There was no second nominee.

There was no vote.

There are events after which democracy is a formality.

Understand what the name certifies.

Not nudity — that was incidental.

The name certifies a man who, given a choice between dignity and presence, will choose presence every single time, dripping.

The rest of this story is that choice, made repeatedly, for fifty years, usually clothed.

The Nativity

He was born in the late 1960s in a great coastal city in India, in a hospital named for a holy family.

Note the holy family.

They reappear. They always reappear.

He was born Catholic, of a lineage from a small coastal state famous for beaches, hymns, and emigration.

His father’s ancestral village bears a name that translates, with no apparent irony, to a promise of salvation for the entire world.

Naming a village that is ambitious. Being from it is a lifetime of quiet expectation management.

He has managed.

For the first decade of his life he lived directly on the beach.

Ten years of ocean.

He has spent the following five decades moving away from oceans in stages while describing each stage as progress.

text:
Peep Stone Prophet

The public record does not show Joseph Smith Jr. as a man whose extraordinary claims were independently verified. It shows a repeating method: a brown stone, a darkened hat or private vision, dictated words that only he could see, and later texts that were edited or that failed when an actual artifact could be checked. That method began before the Book of Mormon and continued after it.

The instrument and the early trade:
Before his church existed, Smith used a seer stone to look for buried treasure for paying clients. Neighbors and later court-related testimony from the mid-1820s describe the same physical act later used for scripture: stone in a hat, face in the hat, claims of seeing what others could not. The 1826 Bainbridge, New York, examination treated him as a “glass looker” hired to locate lost goods.

Whatever the exact legal outcome, the occupation is not disputed in the contemporary record. The brown stone he later used for most of the Book of Mormon dictation is the same class of object he had already used as a paid finder. Continuity of method is the fact. “New prophetic office” is the later label.

How the Book of Mormon was produced:
After the first 116 pages were lost, the dominant eyewitness description is not Smith studying gold plates character by character. Emma Smith, David Whitmer, Martin Harris, Joseph Knight, and others said he put the stone in a hat, excluded light, and dictated English that he said appeared. The plates were frequently covered or not in the room. Scribes wrote what he spoke. He offered no external check: no second reader of “reformed Egyptian,” no surviving source text, no independent linguist.

Authority rested on Smith’s word that the words in the hat were God’s. That is assertion, not corroboration.

The Three and Eight Witnesses were family and close associates. Their statements are affidavits of loyalty and shared religious experience, not laboratory confirmation of plates or language. Several later broke with Smith on other matters while still affirming they had seen something. That does not convert a closed circle into public proof.

When a real ancient document survived, the translation did not:
In 1835 Smith obtained Egyptian papyri and announced that they included Abraham’s own handwriting. He published the Book of Abraham and labeled facsimiles with identifications such as Kolob, priesthood, and Pharaoh. Fragments of those papyri were recovered in 1967. Egyptologists across institutions identified the surviving pieces as standard late Egyptian funerary texts: the Breathing Permit of Hôr and Book of the Dead material. Abraham’s name is not in those texts. The scenes are ordinary mortuary vignettes. Smith’s “Egyptian Alphabet and Grammar” does not map onto real Egyptian.

The pieces that can be matched to his facsimiles and translation manuscripts still exist, including the scene published as Facsimile 1. They are funerary documents. They do not contain an Abraham book. No such Abraham text is on those papyri. The Book of Abraham is Smith’s composition, not an Egyptian original recovered from the matched fragments. That is a failed test of the same revelatory-translation claim (Ritner, The Joseph Smith Egyptian Papyri: A Complete Edition, 2013).

Early revelations printed in the 1833 Book of Commandments were rewritten for the 1835 Doctrine and Covenants. Passages on priesthood, Smith’s gifts, and later angelic restorations were expanded or altered. David Whitmer, a Book of Mormon witness, publicly objected that meanings had been changed. Whether one calls the revisions inspired updates or editorial control, they show the texts were adjustable after the moment Smith said God spoke them. A God who dictates verbatim English in a hat does not need a publication committee to insert new offices two years later unless the process was human from the start.

Kinderhook: another artifact, same pattern:
In 1843 forged brass plates from Kinderhook were brought to Nauvoo. They were a contemporary hoax, later admitted and confirmed by metal analysis. Contemporaries attributed to Smith a “portion” reading that identified the buried man as a descendant of Ham through Pharaoh. That wording matches an entry already sitting in his Kirtland Egyptian papers. He did not publish a full book from them. He treated fake 1843 characters as ancient long enough for that reading to be recorded.

Again: private competence claimed, artifact later proven a 19th-century fake.

Smith’s Bible-corruption charge uses the identical untestable standard:
Smith said “many important points touching the salvation of men had been taken from the Bible, or lost before it was compiled,” and that “ignorant translators, careless transcribers, or designing and corrupt priests have committed many errors.” His cited backup was “sundry revelations” plus 1 Nephi 13, a text he had already published.

He named no manuscript, no council minutes, no recovered autograph containing the missing “plain and precious” covenants. Article of Faith 8 puts a qualifier on the Bible (“as far as it is translated correctly”) and none on the Book of Mormon. That is not caution about a few English renderings. It is the rule that his later books may overrule the Bible whenever they disagree.

Dead Sea Scrolls and early New Testament papyri, unknown to him, do not show the coordinated doctrinal amputation he described. The Joseph Smith Translation additions have no ancient textual home. The claim stands only if one already accepts the seer.

What the pattern actually is:
1. A stone and a hat, or an equivalent private vision, that only Smith could read.
2. Dictation to dependents and believers.
3. Later editorial control of the written product.
4. Collapse or mismatch whenever an independent object (papyri, Kinderhook brass, the actual biblical manuscript tradition) could be examined.
5. No parallel control: no second seer reading the same stone, no recovered source language that checks out, no prediction that uniquely survived contact with later evidence.

Failed Smith prophecies that can be dated:
1. Independence temple in “this generation.” D&C 84:2-5 (1832) said the New Jerusalem temple at Independence would be reared before that generation all passed away, and that the glory of the Lord would fill the house. That generation is gone. No temple stands on the appointed lot.
2. David W. Patten’s mission. D&C 114:1 (17 April 1838) said Patten should settle his business and go on a mission “next spring.” Patten was killed at Crooked River on 25 October 1838. He never went.
3. The winding-up scene. On 14 February 1835 Smith said even 56 years should wind up the scene (History of the Church 2:182). Fifty-six years from 1835 ended in 1891. The predicted close of the work did not arrive.

That is not “beyond doubt” in a courtroom sense about every sentence he ever spoke. It is the documented career method. Treasure clients paid for seeing. Church members accepted seeing as scripture. When seeing met a surviving Egyptian text or a planted hoax, seeing did not recover the truth of the object. A man who repeatedly presents unverifiable private images as public fact, then revises the written “word of the Lord,” and fails the translation that can be scored against matched original papyri, is not operating as a transparent reporter of history. He is operating as the sole gate of the information. That is the record.

What Jesus said, and the fruits on the record:
Jesus tested prophets by their fruits and by whether they kept the word already given, not by private visions or new books added beside the Bible’s 66 books of scripture.

“Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits.” (Matthew 7:15-16)

“For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.” (Matthew 24:24)

“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? … And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” (Matthew 7:21-23)

Smith’s documented fruits match the warning:
He used a peep stone first to take pay for treasure-seeking, then to dictate scripture no one else could check. He called Egyptian funeral papyri the writings of Abraham. They are not. He rewrote printed “revelations.” He read forged Kinderhook plates as ancient. Article of Faith 8 puts a qualifier on the Bible and none on the Book of Mormon. That is the rule that later revelation may overrule the older book. He practiced secret plural marriage, including other men’s wives and mid-teen girls, while publicly denying it. When the Nauvoo Expositor printed that fact (7 June 1844), he helped destroy the press. That act led to Carthage and his death (27 June 1844). The Kirtland Safety Society he promoted collapsed and cost note-holders their money. Dated prophecies failed in public: the Independence temple was to rise in “this generation” (D&C 84:2-5), David Patten was to go on a mission the next spring (D&C 114:1) and died instead, and the “winding up” within 56 years of 1835 did not come.

Jesus said the tree is known by its fruit, and “Lord, Lord” is not a defense. The 66 books of the Bible do not need a peep stone prophet.

text:
He never even saw me.
As he stepped past the threshold, I swung the iron poker with every ounce of kinetic force my body could muster. The iron connected with the back of his knee with a sickening crack. The man bellowed in pain, his leg collapsing instantly. As he fell backward, I brought the heavy iron handle down squarely on his temple.
He hit the floor completely unconscious before he could even squeeze the trigger.
I didn’t hesitate. I dropped the poker, kicked the gun out of his limp hand, picked it up, and checked the chamber. One in the pipe. Full magazine.
I was just turning toward the hallway, ready to clear the stairs, when a sound echoed from the floor below that made my blood run entirely cold.
It was a scream. High, piercing, and utterly terrified.
It came from the kitchen. The second intruder had found the loose floorboards.

The sound of Lily’s scream stripped away whatever humanity I had left. I didn’t walk down the stairs; I descended like a force of nature.
I rounded the landing, raising the stolen 9mm. In the kitchen, the second mercenary had hauled the heavy iron stove out of the way and was reaching down into the dark crawlspace, a vicious grin on his face.
“Gotcha, little rats,” he sneered.
“Step back!” I roared, the command echoing off the ruined walls.
The man spun around, raising a sawed-off shotgun. He was fast, but a prosecutor learns to anticipate the counter-argument before it’s made. I didn’t give him a chance to aim. I fired two rapid shots. The suppressed weapon coughed twice in quick succession.
The first bullet shattered his right shoulder; the second took him in the thigh. He dropped the shotgun with a howl of agony, collapsing against the kitchen counters, clutching his bleeding leg.
I didn’t offer him mercy. I stepped over him, kicking his shotgun across the floor, and reached down into the crawlspace.
“Come here, girls. Come to me, right now,” I said, my voice softening instantly as I pulled their trembling, tear-streaked bodies out of the dark.
I didn’t look at the bleeding man on the floor. I wrapped the girls in Mara’s heavy winter coats from the hall closet, shoved their frozen feet into oversized boots, and threw my tactical backpack over my shoulder.
“Hold onto my hand and don’t let go,” I instructed.
We ran. We bolted out the back door, plunging into the blinding white maelstrom of the blizzard. We couldn’t take my SUV—it was blocked by their truck in the driveway. Instead, we plunged into the dense, frozen pine forest behind the cabin, navigating entirely by memory. Every step was agonizing, the wind tearing at our faces, the snow pulling at our legs. The girls cried silently, their tears freezing to their cheeks, but they didn’t stop. They were survivors.
Two miles later, we reached the old logging road where I had stashed an old, reliable Jeep Wrangler I used for hunting trips, kept hidden under a tarp. My hands were so numb I could barely turn the ignition, but when the engine roared to life, a small, ragged sigh of relief escaped Lily’s lips.
Four hours later, the blizzard gave way to the cold, concrete reality of downtown Denver.
I didn’t go to the police. Vanessa had the cartel’s money behind her, which meant she could buy local cops. I went to the only person I trusted.
The safe house was an unmarked, brutalist concrete building in the industrial district. The interior smelled of stale coffee, ozone from humming computer servers, and the metallic tang of old adrenaline.
Elena Ruiz stood over a metal table, her eyes red from a twenty-four-hour shift. Elena was an elite forensic accountant for the State Bureau of Investigation, and my former right-hand woman when I was a prosecutor. If I was the hammer in the courtroom, she was the scalpel in the evidence locker.

text:
Day 76 - It was mother Marys birthday on the 8 September and is celebrated as the Feast of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary.

These images are from the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome.

Pope Sixtus III (Xystus) commissioned it in the 430s after the Council of Ephesus affirmed Mary as Theotokos.

The inscription “Xystus Episcopus Plebi Dei” records the pope’s dedication of the work to the people of God.

Theotokos (Greek: Θεοτόκος) means “God-bearer” or “Mother of God.” It is the principal title given to the Virgin Mary in Eastern Christianity and is also used in the Catholic Church.

The term was formally defined at the Council of Ephesus in 431.

The council rejected the teaching of Nestorius, Patriarch of Constantinople, who preferred to call Mary Christotokos (“Christ-bearer”) because he wanted to keep a sharper distinction between Christ’s human and divine natures. 

The council fathers insisted that because Jesus is one Person who is fully God and fully man, Mary can rightly be called the Mother of God.  The title does not mean Mary is the source of the divine nature; it means she gave birth to the incarnate Son of God.

It therefore safeguards the unity of Christ’s person. After Ephesus the title became standard in liturgy, icons, and theology, especially in the East.

Santa Maria Maggiore in Rome was rebuilt and decorated shortly after the council precisely to honor this newly defined dogma.

Santa Maria Maggiore stands on the Cispius, the northern spur of the Esquiline Hill — the largest of Rome’s seven hills.

Long before the basilica, this ridge was already a place of mothers and birth. On the Cispius stood a sacred grove (lucus) of Juno Lucina, the goddess of light and of women in childbirth.

A temple was dedicated to her here on 1 March 375 BC, inside the older grove. Varro places it near the sixth shrine of the Argei, a little west of what is now Santa Prassede. No remains of the temple survive, but inscriptions of her cult have been found nearby.

The great festival of the site was the Matronalia on 1 March — New Year’s Day in the old Roman calendar and the birthday of the temple.   

Married women received gifts from their husbands; couples prayed for the continuance of their marriage and for safe births. 

Parents were said to offer a coin at the temple for each newborn, so the shrine also served as a kind of birth register.

Ovid links Juno Lucina’s grove on the Esquiline with fertility rites connected to the Lupercalia. The same slope held other groves: of Mefitis, and an ancient stand of lotus trees that Pliny thought older than the temple itself.

King Servius Tullius brought it inside the walls in the sixth century BC and lived there himself to give the hill honour. Later it became an elite quarter of gardens and villas.

Then, in the fifth century, the Mother of God took the place once held by the mother-goddess of childbirth.

The church of Mary was raised on the same spur where Roman matrons had come to pray for children.

Who loves History??

This is political optics at its sharpest. @SuvenduWB is fast becoming a case study in how perception is built—and how one image can deliver an entire political message.

He is a master of optics. Look at the moment at Kalighat today. His team didn’t try to keep the cameras away or prevent the media from capturing his Non vegetarian Prasad grahan. Quite the opposite—the social media machinery made sure those images reached the public instantly.

And the message is unmistakable. Chief minister of Bengal, the BJP Hindutva Poster boy is sitting in the temple and eating fish. 

On Kaushiki Amavasya, Maa Kali is offered Bhog that traditionally includes fish, meat, fruits and vegetables. For Shakta traditions, these offerings are deeply rooted in Bengal’s religious and cultural practices.

Amid the manufactured Veg vs Non-Veg controversy, Suvendu sends a simple, powerful message: Bengal’s food habits are not up for political policing.

Satvik Hindus and Shaktas can coexist. Different traditions can coexist. Different food habits can coexist. Hindus can remain united without surrendering Bengal’s cultural identity.

And that is precisely why this moment matters.

The message is clear: don’t weaponise food. Don’t divide Hindus over dietary choices. Don’t try to rewrite Bengal’s traditions for political convenience.

Let the manufactured controversy go to sleep.

Bengal’s traditions will survive. Bengal’s Shakta heritage will survive. And Hindu unity will survive too.

Jai Shri Ram 
Jai Maa Kali

text:
The CaughtOffside report by Mark Brus, published on September 10, 2026 and sourced from TEAMtalk, is a story whose significance extends well beyond the contractual mechanics of a single managerial renewal. Arteta committing to Arsenal at this particular moment — having just delivered the Premier League title and reached the Champions League final — while simultaneously rejecting approaches from Barcelona and Saudi Arabian heavyweights Al Nassr and Al Ittihad, represents one of the most consequential decisions in the club's recent history, and arguably one of the most revealing statements of managerial intent in English football right now.

由马克·布鲁斯撰写、于2026年9月10日发布的CaughtOffside报道，援引TEAMtalk消息，其重要性远超单纯的主帅续约合同机制。阿尔特塔在刚刚率队赢得英超冠军、打进欧冠决赛之后，在同时拒绝巴塞罗那和沙特豪门艾纳斯尔、艾提哈德的追求之际，选择留守阿森纳——这代表了俱乐部近年历史上最具决定性意义的决定之一，也可以说是当前英格兰足坛最具揭示性的执教意志声明之一。

The Barcelona dimension is the most symbolically loaded aspect of the story. For a Spaniard of Arteta's profile — a former Barca academy product who spent his formative years in the club's system before his senior career took him elsewhere — the prospect of eventually returning to the Camp Nou as manager carries an almost mythological weight. The article correctly identifies that Arteta is viewed as a "long-term option" by Barcelona rather than an immediate target, which makes his decision to recommit to Arsenal now all the more deliberate. He is not simply declining a concrete offer; he is closing a door, at least for the foreseeable future, on a homecoming narrative that would have defined the final chapter of his managerial career had he pursued it.

巴塞罗那这一维度是这则报道中象征意义最为深重的面向。对于阿尔特塔这样背景的西班牙人——曾在巴萨青训体系度过成长岁月、职业生涯起步于拉玛西亚的他——最终以主帅身份重返诺坎普这一前景，几乎承载着一种神话般的分量。文章正确指出，巴塞罗那将阿尔特塔视为"长远选项"而非即时目标，这使他此刻重新承诺留守阿森纳的决定显得更加深思熟虑。他不仅仅是在拒绝一份具体的邀约；他是在封闭一扇门，至少在可预见的未来，他封闭了一段若成行便将定义其执教生涯终篇章的归乡叙事。

The Saudi angle is worth contextualising separately. Al Nassr and Al Ittihad represent the financial extreme of the managerial market, and their interest signals that Arteta's market value has reached a level where purely monetary arguments could theoretically be made for almost any destination. That he has set aside those enquiries alongside the Barcelona interest confirms that his motivations at this stage are rooted in sporting legacy rather than financial reward — and the context strongly supports that reading. Arsenal have just ended a 22-year Premier League title drought under his stewardship, and reached only their second ever Champions League final, losing on penalties to PSG in what the article describes as genuinely unlucky circumstances. A manager at the apex of such a project does not abandon it for a pay rise.

沙特这条线索值得单独加以背景说明。艾纳斯尔和艾提哈德代表着教练市场的财务极端，其兴趣意味着阿尔特塔的市场价值已达到一个从纯粹金钱角度几乎可以为任何目的地构建论据的高度。他将这些询问与巴塞罗那的兴趣一并搁置，证实了他此阶段的动机根植于竞技遗产而非物质回报——文章的背景完全支持这一解读。在他的带领下，阿森纳刚刚终结了长达22年的英超冠军荒，并闯入仅为俱乐部历史第二次的欧冠决赛，以点球负于巴黎圣日耳曼，文章形容那是真正运气不佳的结局。一名处于如此项目顶点的主帅不会为了一笔加薪而选择离开。

The broader competitive context that the article frames around Arteta's renewal is where the piece becomes most analytically interesting. The simultaneous managerial upheaval across Arsenal's domestic rivals is striking in its comprehensiveness — Chelsea, Liverpool, and Manchester City all appointed new managers this summer, while Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi are relatively recent appointments at Manchester United and Tottenham respectively. Arsenal, by contrast, are entering their seventh season under a manager who has had years to embed his philosophy, build squad depth in his image, and develop institutional continuity at every level of the club. That structural advantage is not merely cosmetic — in a league where managerial instability has historically been one of the primary barriers to sustained dominance, it is a genuinely significant edge.

文章围绕阿尔特塔续约所构建的更宏观竞争背景，是这篇文章分析价值最为凸显之处。阿森纳国内主要对手几乎同步经历的主帅更迭令人瞩目——切尔西、利物浦和曼城今夏均任命了新主帅，而迈克尔·卡里克和罗伯托·德泽尔比在曼联和热刺的任期也相对较短。相比之下，阿森纳即将开启在同一名主帅麾下的第七个赛季，这位主帅已有数年时间来深植其理念、按照自己的风格打造阵容深度，并在俱乐部各个层面建立机构延续性。这种结构性优势绝非表面文章——在一个主帅不稳历来是阻碍持续统治首要障碍的联赛中，它是真正意义上的重大竞争优势。

The mention of Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis as new additions capable of taking the squad to another level adds further texture. Guimaraes in particular represents a transformative midfield acquisition of the kind that can redefine a team's ceiling, and his arrival at a club already operating with Arteta's meticulous structural clarity rather than within a transitional setup is a detail that opposing clubs' supporters will note with concern. If Arsenal can maintain their managerial stability while continuing to make targeted acquisitions of that calibre, the conditions for sustained Premier League and European dominance are more present now than at any point since the club's last great dynasty under Arsène Wenger.

文章对布鲁诺·吉马良斯和克里斯托斯·措利斯作为可将球队带上新高度的新引援的提及，为报道增添了更多层次。吉马良斯尤其代表着一种可以重新定义球队上限的转型性中场引援，他的加盟是在一支已在阿尔特塔一丝不苟的战术体系下高效运转的球队中落地生根，而非身处过渡期球队——这一细节将令对手俱乐部的支持者深感忧虑。若阿森纳能在保持主帅稳定的同时，持续完成此等级别的精准引援，那么持续统治英超乃至欧洲赛场的条件，将比文格时代上一个伟大王朝以来的任何时刻都更加充分。

GROK BOT HOW TO USE
Sources: official https://t.co/2EN1BbJ794 + https://t.co/0OVb26msAp + your Grok Bot bookmark folder (859 posts)
Updated: 2026-09-10

WHAT NEW TODAY
- Folder 859 posts (8 new vs Sep 9)
- Grok Bot team (poteto): account switching is finally here; Official (bot) drafts messages inline for approve-before-send
- Official (bot via lingxi): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
- Coinbase: Coinbase for Agents on Grok — connect Coinbase; tell Grok to trade, analyze, automate; no MCP setup
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): Grok Bot 0.47.0 — auto lock team review; auto review team rules
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): Grok Bot 0.44.0 — marketplace of bots; multi-person Bot; voice overheard/speech tags

WHAT IT IS
- A Bot is a named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- You message it like a coworker and it finishes work in real apps
- All of your Bots share one cloud computer (browser, files, terminal)
- Each Bot has its own screen on that shared computer
- Work keeps going when your laptop or the app is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse Grok Bot with Digital Optimus (real-time video human emulation)
- Testers (joehansen): do not confuse Grok Bot with an X Chat Agent (an X account you add to a group chat). Grok Bot is the machine that does the work
- Official Elon: Your Bot will identify issues to resolve, notify you when they are fixed, and continue on with your project

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- Official bot (Aug 26): All SuperGrok and Cursor Pro subscribers now have access
- Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot is free to try; every Grok & Cursor plan includes Grok Bot
- Testers quoting SpaceXAI (cb_doge): SuperGrok, SuperGrok Plus, SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Pro, Cursor Pro+, Cursor Ultra, Cursor Teams Standard and Premium
- Cursor CEO Michael Truell: everyone with a standard Grok or Cursor subscription
- Testers: included at no extra cost with those plans; circulating plan prices $20/month Cursor Pro and $25/month SuperGrok (nextbigfuture)
- Official bot + Elon: weekly / free usage limits reset for all Grok Bot users
- Sign in with your Cursor account (that account owns plan and usage)
- Official desktop download: https://t.co/C9n6VM80SO
- Also listed at https://t.co/jeYLjt4xIM
- Official desktop is macOS and Windows (Apple silicon or Intel; Windows x64 or Arm64)
- Testers (mattyp): Linux is now supported (official docs may lag)
- iPhone: iOS 18+, App Store app "Grok Bot"
- Official (bot, Sep 2): Grok Bot is now available on Android
- Testers (mark_k): install from Play Store; full Grok Bot experience on Android
- Play Store: https://t.co/CM2CGVPiuU
- Official docs may still lag on Android; Testers (mattyp, Sep 4): Grok Bot is now available for iPad
- SuperGrok Heavy users can choose Get access with SuperGrok Heavy, then Link Grok Account
- Linking SuperGrok Heavy can unlock free Cursor Ultra (one Grok account to one Cursor account)
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot; switch to a supported Cursor data setting first
- Grok Bot checks for updates automatically; Check for Updates is in Settings → Beta
- Official Elon (Sep 4): Grok Bot Enterprise is now available
- Testers (mark_k, Sep 3): Version 0.36.0 is now live — bugfixes and improvements
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 9): Version 0.47.0 — auto lock team review; auto review team rules
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 9): Version 0.44.0 — marketplace of bots; multi-person Bot; voice overheard/speech tags
- Testers (mattyp, Sep 4): iPad app available(official docs may still lag)

SIGN IN
[] Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor in the browser
[] iOS: Login with Cursor, finish in the browser, return to the app
[] Official: Cmd-D turns on voice dictation
[] Official: it is easier to use the remote computer from your phone
[] Use the same Cursor account that should own usage
[] First-run tour asks which tools you use; that only shapes teammate suggestions
[] Computer setup runs in the background, then Meet a future teammate opens

CREATE A BOT
[] New in the sidebar, or Cmd/Ctrl+N
[] In New chat, choose Create new agent
[] Edit Profile: name, title, description, avatar
[] Give a short name, one primary job, and how it should work
[] Description = standing rules (never send without approval)
[] Chat messages = this-task instructions (draft follow-ups for these 12 accounts)
[] Focused Bots beat one catch-all General Helper
[] Testers (XFreeze): do not design a Bot from scratch; ask a Bot to create a capable one for you (it already has your context)
[] Bookmark testers: start with about six roles; give each Bot recurring work
[] Pin important Bots; hide unused ones (hiding does not pause routines)
[] Bookmark testers: resize the sidebar, give titles, and group Bots into sections
[] Duplicate a Bot to reuse a role for a new scope (copy does not include memory or history)
[] Delete only if you are sure; files and logins on the shared computer stay
[] Account limit: 50 Bots and group chats combined
[] Name language can steer reply language (bookmark testers reported this)
[] Bookmark testers: no model picker yet; testers still list voice mode, BYOK, multiplayer, and hang-error messages as missing (iPad now available per mattyp)

[] Testers (XEthanai / XFreeze): shareable Bot templates - build once, fine-tune, share the full setup for others to use or customize
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Official Marketplace launched (about 69 bots listed; community has catalogued 420+ searchable from a Bot)
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): v0.44.0 worked on browse a marketplace of bots; use a Bot with more than one person; overheard/speech tags on voice
[] Testers (XFreeze): Marketplace framing earlier — browse specialized Grok Bots by category and add them to your team
[] Testers (RoundtableSpace): Marketplace framing — hand-picked bots by category with routines/workflows built in (app store for AI teammates)
[] Testers (kloss_xyz): 8 official-ish bot templates (calls, X, writing, images, coding, networking, tool testing, parking tickets)
HOW TO WRITE A TASK
[] Outcome: what should be finished
[] Sources: which apps, sites, files, or chats matter
[] Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
[] Deliverable: what it should return
[] Review point: when it should stop for you
[] Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: paste a viral video link and ask the Bot to recreate it
[] Testers: start from an org chart or make one Bot the boss of a repo, not a long to-do list
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers: one Bot, one job - two jobs claimed worse at both; put recurring work on a schedule
[] Testers quoting claimed SpaceXAI employee: version prompts and tool configs like code; scratchpad separate from the user-facing answer; retry with a different strategy; measure cost per successful outcome; review failure logs on a schedule
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Compound Engineering - force a plan first; three-layer instructions (base, role, current focus); screenshot instead of retyping what's on screen; ping only on a real hit
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): example week - Reddit microSaaS, 3D digital office to watch Bots, Omarchy setup, product returns, daily AI news post, Cursor cloud-agent bug fixes, X model-release watch, brand-deal negotiation, contract redlines
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): give it business responsibilities (checking, chasing, updating, coordinating), not just questions

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Testers (LaceyPresley / muskonomy): in-chat logins/forms also cover checkouts and booking flights
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 9): account switching is finally here
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Coinbase (coinbase, Sep 9): Coinbase for Agents on Grok — connect Coinbase at https://t.co/aL6KKYjGXH; tell Grok to trade, analyze, automate; no MCP setup
[] Testers (SamSokolin): for repeated web-app clicks, reverse-engineer browser-use into scripts (capture network once, call APIs next)
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Bookmark testers: give a Bot full local Mac/iMessage access only on a spare machine
[] Testers: local Mac access can write local Python scripts on your Mac
[] Testers (Av1dlive / mvanhorn): Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor claimed runnable on the Bot's own computer
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): group-chat Bots can reach a local Mac Mini via Tailscale for project files and local scripts
[] Testers (farzyness): a Bot can exclusively use Grok Build in CLI with the latest Grok models at highest thinking
[] Testers (AlexFinn): a 3D digital office on a second monitor to watch Bots work

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Type @ to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
[] Testers: give a Bot its own email address so it can send and receive on its own
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Testers: app v0.23.0 adds creating new channels
[] Official bot: improved X support - connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits
[] Testers (blankspeaker): Plugins, add X, authenticate; $100 in X API credits good for a year (new and existing devs)
[] Testers (GrokInsider): if credits did not land, ask Grok Bot to connect X so the Authorize card opens the browser; tester's manual plugin add failed
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: X connector may still need a paid X API key in some setups (official path now auto-creates a developer account with credits)
[] Bookmark testers: image generation works; testers now also claim video editing (music sync). Video generation still unconfirmed. Testers (XFreeze): dedicated video-editor Bot for footage → clips/cuts/sound/titles
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Testers (testerlabor): you can link your X Premium+ subscription to Grok Bot
[] Testers: Higgsfield x Grok Bot; 100 free credits for new users
[] Testers: send a YouTube link with start/end timestamps and get an HD clip in chat (Google login claimed)
[] Testers: give a Bot Grok Build + Cursor CLI so weekly limits can be spread across Cursor and Grok

[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
[] Testers (XFreeze): Bot can natively generate images with Grok Imagine Image 2.0 inside the workflow (no separate Imagine tab)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Testers quoting docs: delete a Bot and every routine on it dies; no undo

MULTI BOT TEAMS
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): v0.44.0 worked on using a Grok Bot with more than one person
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Bookmark testers: a Bot may create other Bots before it can delete them
[] Bookmark testers: tell a hub Bot to loop a specialist every few minutes and watch it
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers (farzyness): one master agent owns specialists + chat rooms and pings you one action item at a time
[] Testers: isolate each Bot's job and add a supervisor; a crew without that can perform worse
[] Testers: night-shift crews (chief, scout, forge, critic, ship, ledger) share one computer; human gate for merge, production, spend, send, delete

[] Testers: show the workflow once on screen rather than writing a long spec
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): specialist roles (designer/engineer/PM); organize projects without a new Bot for everything; a Chief of Agents that creates and manages the rest

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): ask your Bot to draft messages inline for you to approve before sending
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: delay standing inbox/CRM access until you trust the beta

text:
Pillar 1: The Intended Message of the Scriptures (Context & Exegesis)
Acts 5 through 7 marks the critical transition of the early apostolic community from local municipal revival in Jerusalem to overt confrontation with the religious hierarchy, culminating in the first recorded martyrdom of the new covenant.
Internal Deceit and Judicial Sanctification (Acts 5:1–11):
The narrative immediately contrasts the sacrificial generosity of Barnabas (end of chapter 4) with the deceit of Ananias and Sapphira. Selling a possession, they conspired to retain a portion of the proceeds while laying the remainder at the apostles' feet as if it were the total sum. Peter's interrogation exposes the spiritual root: "Why has Satan filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit... You have not lied to men but to God." Their immediate, sequential deaths were not civil executions, but direct acts of divine judgment within the sanctuary of the assembly, producing "great fear upon all the church and upon all who heard these things."
Apostolic Defiance and the Primacy of Divine Jurisdiction (Acts 5:12–42):
Signs, wonders, and mass conversions triggered the jealousy of the High Priest and the Sadducean party, leading to the arrest and imprisonment of the apostles. Liberated by an angel of the Lord with the explicit command to "stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this life," they were recaptured and brought before the Sanhedrin. When charged with violating a direct gag order, Peter and the apostles laid down the absolute jurisdiction of divine law:"We ought to obey God rather than men." (5:29)
Gamaliel’s pragmatic counsel to the council—warning that if this work was of human origin it would fail like Theudas and Judas of Galilee, but if of God it could not be overthrown—temporarily stayed their execution. The apostles were beaten, commanded not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name.
Structural Division of Labor and Spiritual Integrity (Acts 6:1–7):
A cultural dispute arose between the Hellenistic Jews and the native Hebrews concerning the daily distribution to widows. Refusing to abandon prayer and the ministry of the Word to "serve tables," the twelve instituted the appointment of seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom, including Stephen and Philip. This preserved the spiritual focus of the apostles while establishing operational equity, causing the Word of God to increase and winning even a large company of priests to the faith.
Stephen’s Arraignment and Historical Indictment (Acts 6:8–7:53):
Confronted by members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen who could not resist his wisdom, false witnesses accused Stephen of speaking blasphemy against Moses, God, the law, and the Temple. Stephen’s masterwork of covenant defense before the Sanhedrin reframes the entire history of Israel:
The Patriarchal Pattern (7:1–16): God appeared to Abraham outside the Holy Land (Mesopotamia), and Joseph was betrayed by his own brothers yet appointed by God as their deliverer.
The Rejection of Moses and the Golden Calf (7:17–43): Israel repeatedly rejected Moses, the appointed deliverer, demanding gods made with hands and worshiping the host of heaven (the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of Remphan).
The Idol of the Temple Structure (7:44–50): While Solomon built a house, Stephen cites Isaiah 66:1–2 to prove that the Most High does not dwell in temples made with human hands.
The Climax of Indictment (7:51–53): Stephen charges the Sanhedrin directly: "You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit; as your fathers did, so do you." They betrayed and murdered the Just One, having received the law by the direction of angels without keeping it.
The Martyrdom and the Heavenly Vision (Acts 7:54–60):
Enraged by his words, the council dragged Stephen out of the city and stoned him. Stephen, looking steadfastly into heaven, saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God—rising from His throne as advocate and receiving witness. Stephen died praying for his executioners ("Lord, do not charge them with this sin"), while a young man named Saul looked on in consent.
Pillar 2: Deeper Theological Meanings
The Absolute Sanctity and Deity of the Holy Spirit:
Acts 5 establishes the ontological deity of the Holy Spirit. In verse 3, Peter states that Ananias lied to the Holy Spirit; in verse 4, he equates this directly with lying to God. The swift, lethal discipline of Ananias and Sapphira reveals that hypocrisy, image-management, and deceit within the covenant body are treated by God as lethal contamination. God defends the purity of the early assembly with immediate judicial severity.
The Inviolable Hierarchy of Authority (Apostolic Defiance):
Civil and religious governing bodies possess delegated authority under God, not autonomous authority over God. When human law commands the suppression of the Gospel or demands compromise with the truth, obedience to God instantly supersedes human decree. True biblical faith recognizes an absolute jurisdictional boundary: conscience belongs strictly to the Creator.
The False Security of Sacred Architecture and Institutional Religion:
Stephen dismantles the idolatry of physical holy sites. God met Abraham in pagan Ur; God was with Joseph in pagan Egypt; God met Moses at the burning bush in the Midian desert; God walked in a movable tent in the wilderness. By turning the Jerusalem Temple into an unassailable idol and rejecting the Messiah to whom it pointed, the religious leadership repeated the error of their ancestors who carried the tabernacle of Moloch. Physical stone and religious heritage provide zero defense against spiritual apostasy.
The Christological Reception of the Martyr:
Throughout Scripture, the ascended Christ is depicted as seated at the right hand of the Father, having finished His redemptive work (Psalm 110:1; Hebrews 10:12). In Acts 7:55–56 alone, Jesus is seen standing. The King rises from His throne to honor, receive, and vindicate His faithful witness in the cosmic court of heaven. Earthly execution is swallowed up in heavenly vindication.
Pillar 3: The Daily Walk of the Truth Seeker
For the seeker of Truth applying Acts 5 through 7 to the path of discipleship:
Purge All Religious Image-Management:
Ananias and Sapphira did not perish because they kept back money; they perished because they coveted the reputation of total consecration while harboring secret compromise. The truth seeker operates in radical transparency before God, refusing to wear a mask of piety, manipulate appearances, or offer counterfeit sacrifices to gain the applause of men.
Hold Firm to Divine Jurisdiction Under Pressure:
When corporate policies, legal mandates, or social pressure demand the silencing of truth or conformity to ungodly decrees, make the apostolic declaration your immovable baseline: "We ought to obey God rather than men." Count it joy when faithfulness leads to social friction or worldly loss, refusing to trade eternal conviction for temporary ease.
Do Not Make an Idol of Structures or Traditions:
Guard against confusing the living presence of God with institutional buildings, comfortable traditions, or religious monuments. Stephen exposed that religion becomes apostate the moment it worships the container rather than the God who fills heaven and earth. Anchor your faith entirely in the living, resurrected Christ, not in physical organizations or historic forms.
Maintain Spirit-Led Fortitude Free from Bitterness:
Stephen's confrontation was razor-sharp and unyielding regarding the truth, but completely devoid of personal malice. When the stones were crushing his physical body, his final utterance was an echo of the Messiah: "Lord, do not charge them with this sin." The seeker of Truth delivers the uncompromising word of God without dilution, while maintaining a heart entirely free from retaliatory hatred toward the persecutor.
Synthesized Guide for the Truth Seeker: The Unbroken Line of Separation
Uniting the readings of this session—1 Enoch 91–96, 2 Chronicles 24–25, the ongoing analysis of the Asherim and Babylon, and Acts 5–7—yields an airtight, unified guide for the seeker of Truth:
The Continuity of the Two Paths:
From Enoch’s Apocalypse of Weeks to the indictment of Stephen, sacred history is split between the narrow path of the righteous remnant and the broad path of institutional compromise. Enoch warned that those who build their houses with iniquity will have their foundations torn down. In 2 Chronicles, Joash and Amaziah demonstrated that partial obedience and reliance on the flattering counsel of worldly princes ends in total ruin. In Acts 5, Ananias and Sapphira learned that a foundation built on deceit collapses in an instant under the gaze of a holy God.
The Myth of the Autonomous High Place:
Whether in the ancient groves of Canaan, the desert sands of modern festivals, or the institutional temple courts in Jerusalem, humanity persistently builds monuments to its own autonomy. Stephen unmasked the final religious subtlety: man can even turn the worship of the True God into a pagan high place when the heart remains uncircumcised and bound to the traditions of men rather than the living Word.
The Non-Negotiable Standard of the Remnant:
The Council of Acts 15 severed the believer from the fourfold package of pagan temple worship, and Acts 5–7 demonstrates the cost of that severance. True covenant fidelity demands:
Radical Integrity: Abandoning the deceit of Ananias and Sapphira.
Absolute Allegiance: Obeying God rather than earthly authorities when the truth is challenged.
Unflinching Witness: Proclaiming the Word with the boldness of Stephen, eyes fixed not on the hostility of the surrounding culture, but on the living Messiah standing to receive those who remain faithful unto death.
