Three female jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial stoked outrage from many on social media for disparaging the lone male juror who refused to acquit the mother who admitted to strangling her three children to death.

In an interview with NBC10 Boston that aired Tuesday, jurors Paula Devlin, Kellie Farina and Roni Carlson, who served as the jury foreperson, described in unusual detail what happened behind the jury-room door. The case, which ended in a mistrial last Friday, has prompted support for Clancy from many female supporters who believe she was not guilty by reason of insanity or that her ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, was somehow to blame.

Carlson, a retired fifth-grade special needs teacher, said she was initially "so excited" at the prospect of an insanity acquittal when the male juror appeared poised to flip his guilty verdict, but she noted her excitement turned to frustration amid his adamant refusal.

Devlin, who works for a government contractor, called the male juror "very arrogant" because he disregarded input from nurses on the jury about Clancy's toxicology results. Farina, a retired chef, said he "would not interact with us" and "had the hardest time getting off the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children."

The three also criticized the prosecution's tone, describing it as "harsh," "biased," and lacking compassion, while praising defense attorney Kevin Reddington's "funny" and "entertaining" style.

The interview prompted a torrent of backlash from X users, some of whom called for a repeal of the 19th Amendment or mocked the women by posting AI-generated images of them dressed as witches.

Others suggested the women exhibited the end stage of "toxic empathy" and epitomized the stereotype of white female liberals from deep-blue Massachusetts.

Sean Davis, senior editor at The Federalist, pointed out that Devlin unwittingly revealed that multiple nurses on the panel were disregarding the judge's instructions by offering their own interpretations of Clancy's toxicology report during deliberations. Judge William Sullivan explicitly told the jury to disregard expertise that had not been presented at trial.

"There is something of a major bombshell in that interview that the Karen jurors were too stupid to understand while they were bragging about themselves and trashing the holdout," Davis said. "One of the jurors admits that multiple nurses on the jury used their experience and medical background to 'explain' toxicology reports to the holdout juror."

"I showed that clip to a trial attorney who immediately saw it as an admission that the pro-Clancy jurors were using outside information and evidence from outside the trial process to bully a juror toward a particular outcome," he added.

"Absurdity stated with unflinching confidence, with their harshest criticisms reserved for the only man who understood who the real victims were in this case. Feminism and the liberal social justice movement have so distorted the meaning of justice that virtually all of their adherents can no longer recognize it," said Heritage Foundation President Kevin Roberts.

"How strange that the man couldn't get over the fact that she killed her three kids. In a time of mental crisis, we may have to rethink the jury system altogether," said political commentator Dave Rubin.

Author and columnist Buzz Patterson called the comments "disturbing."

"How can a parent, any parent, feel like this? This is not the country I was raised in," Patterson said.

"This is how we got Governor Maura Healey here in Massachusetts. These jurors are her voting base," said Steve Ferguson, a conservative small business owner with a prominent X account.

Healey signed legislation last month permitting abortion in Massachusetts through all nine months of pregnancy.

"These juror interviews are extraordinary. They are admitting openly that they disregarded the law entirely for the sake of letting Clancy off the hook. There's no other way to read it," said Daily Wire host Matt Walsh, who called them "a collection of the most morally obtuse idiots ever assembled."

The issues around the Lindsay Clancy trial and their wider cultural implications have prompted a flurry of reactions from Christian commentators. Earlier this week, Pastor Josh Howerton of Lakepointe Church in Rockwall, Texas, discerned parallels between the Clancy case and the moral depravity of ancient Israel in the book of Judges.

Howerton offered the graphic story of the gang rape of the Levite's concubine from Judges 19, which prompted a civil war among the Israelites, as an example of an event that served as "one flashpoint moment where one specific story of utter degradation circulated throughout the entire nation."

"And God used it to shock the nation into waking up and realizing, 'What have we become?' And it precipitates a moment of repentance in the nation, so that God's judgment doesn't fall in that moment," he said, adding that the Clancy case might serve a similar purpose for many Americans.

Nick Freitas, a Christian father and influencer who formerly served in the Virginia House of Delegates, warned in a viral clip last week that the case threatens to bring long-simmering tensions between the sexes in the U.S. to a boiling point.

"I honestly don't think that women understand what a catalyst moment this is. There's been a lot of conditions set for young men to just be fed up," said Freitas, who went on to observe that men and women are becoming more tribal in their opposition to each other.

text:
After hearing these jurors speak, it occurs to me that the lack of any civics & law education has really screwed our country.

The insanity plea was never meant for perfectly capable nurses. It was intended for the mentally DISABLED; people with IQs so low they can’t know the difference between right & wrong. Or people so neglected in their lives, nobody taught them that violence or murder is wrong and punishable. 

Bad characters have always tried to manipulate the plea to their advantage, of course. It seldom works because they don’t meet the criteria for which it is meant. Multiple personality disorder was born out of criminals trying to manipulate the insanity plea, as was repressed memories. Few psych professionals put weight to either theory, many argue that neither exists, let alone offer any viable explanation for criminal acts.

Jeffrey Dahmer drilled holes in people’s skulls and poured acid into their brains to make zombies he could keep as sex slaves. He tried and FAILED with the insanity plea because he organized, he planned, he concealed and perpetrated. Just like the woman that murdered her kids. 

They found body parts Jeffrey was eating and a head in his refrigerator. Barrels of bodies so wretched that the other tenants had complained about the smell coming out of his apartment for months. That’s insane and psychotic behavior but he was STILL HELD CULPABLE, and rightly so.

Massachusetts uses a different definition for the colloquially named “insanity plea” and they put the burden of proof on the prosecution, meaning the prosecution has to prove the person was sane beyond a reasonable doubt. In most states and historically speaking, the insanity plea is & has always been a burden on the defense, meaning the defense has to prove that the person did not know what they were doing was wrong. It would appear that MA has done this to make it easier to use the plea, even renaming it to “lack of criminal responsibility”. Think that through- you don’t have to prove she was psychotic, the prosecution has to prove she was “sane” so to speak. It’s a dangerous standard & a dangerous precedent because vicious crimes always make us question sanity. Of course we label murdering three children or 17 young boys as psychotic. MA is basically saying, prove it’s not psychotic. 

MA would very likely have let Dahmer walk, and I see it as a failure of suicidal empathy put into place by progressives who never think beyond their own nose. It’s another “feels good” policy where Democrats didn’t consider the precedent or long term repercussions because they never do. It’s one of those most blaring problems I have with liberal ideas - it’s always do what feels good now and worry about the problems it creates later. My conservative nature is the direct opposite - leave it alone until all of the possible consequences have been examined and then write the policy with those “what if’s” in mind.

text:
I'm a lifelong Dodgers fan and I had no idea the history of the Ravine.

Apparently this guy named Zinn invented his own "vibrant community" story of the residents of Chavez Ravine, including the following lies:

- The city cleared the area for the purpose of building a stadium: FALSE - Discussions on clearing that area for future projects like a huge market complex and low-income housing started as early as 1935, and it was ultimately cleared for low-income housing in 1950. When that project failed but the land was already cleared it was THEN in 1955 it was offered to the Dodgers as a site for their West Coast move from Brooklyn

- Generations of Mexican-American's lived there: FALSE - The area didn't start to see structures until 1915 or 1920 and most of them were shacks and barrios. Unpaved roads, no utilities, lots of trailers (you get the idea). At best 1.5 generations of people lived there.

- The owners weren't compensated: FALSE - California law required all land purchased via eminent domain to be appraised 3 times by independent appraisers who weren't allowed to consult with each other, and the government had to pay the amount given by the HIGHEST appraiser. Often times, what the city paid was even higher than the highest of those 3 appraisals.

- One of the resident's homes would be under where 2nd base is now: FALSE - The actual stadium location was the site of an abandoned brick factory. The actual neighborhoods were further North toward the parking lot areas.

Like all Liberal history - the history of Chavez Ravine is painted by modern day social justice warriors as some grand class struggle where "vibrant communities that were there for generations thrived". Their goal? To rally the masses and give undeserved "reparations" to the descendants of those families.

In fact as recent as 2024 a bill was circulating through the California Assembly to do just that - but it ultimately never made its way to the governor's desk - which is good because Newsom certainly would have signed it.

Founder of @craft_ventures- and @Techstars-backed tax compliance startup ComplYant arrested, charged with 15 counts tied to alleged $13 million fraud:

Shiloh Luckey, the founder of startup that purported to offer software to help small business owners track and comply with income tax, sales tax, business licenses, and annual reporting requirements, was arrested yesterday as she attempted to board a cruise ship for vacation.

Luckey's company, ComplYant, raised a $5.5 million seed round in February 2022, led by David Sacks' Craft Ventures.

Techstars, Mucker Capital, Slauson & Co, and Fika Ventures also invested in the company, according to public reports.

But Luckey's company and Luckey herself were not what they seemed. While she told investors she was a licensed certified public accountant, Luckey had never obtained the CPA credential.

Perhaps more importantly, Luckey, the indictment alleges, used investors' funds to pay for personal expenses, including the purchase of her residence, the purchase of a Tesla automobile, and to pay her wedding on the Caribbean island of Anguilla.

She also, the DOJ says, engaged in a check kiting scheme involving the company to buy her Inglewood, California, home.

Per the DOJ, she intentionally wrote a bad $1.5 million check from a company account, deposited it into a company account at a different bank, and then wired the money for the home purchase before the first bank detected the alleged fraud.

Luckey paid off the negative balance using funds obtained from the securities fraud she perpetrated on investors, the DOJ says.

Luckey is charged with nine counts of securities fraud, three counts of wire fraud, one count of bank fraud, and two counts of money laundering. 

The SEC also filed a complaint against Luckey last year stemming from the same underlying fact pattern, alleging she "fraudulently raised over $13 million from venture capital investors using false claims about both the commercial success of ComplYant’s software product as well as her own qualifications to lead the company."

Also charged in the two-count indictment are two petition circulators who worked for Brass: Courtney Price, 49, of Jacksonville, Florida, and Jateisha Herron, 33, of Boron, California. 

All three defendants are charged with one count of conspiracy to commit identity fraud in furtherance of a state felony. Brass and Price are charged with an additional count of identity fraud in furtherance of a state felony.

The charged conduct undermines the confidence voters have in our election systems. We will vigorously investigate and charge anyone involved in corrupting our elections.

text:
Dear Ashley St. Clair,

At this point, I genuinely question your motives.

I know it's a little late in the piece to be saying this, but in February 2025, when you publicly announced that you had a child with Elon, you said you had previously kept it private to protect your child's “privacy and safety.”

You said you intended to allow your child to “grow in a normal and safe environment.”

You asked the media to respect that privacy.

You later said “kids should be off limits for journalists.”

I agreed with you.

But looking at everything being played out publicly now, I have to ask....

What changed?

You're now publicly discussing deeply private matters concerning his father, including financial negotiations. 

You're claiming Elon offered you $40 million, while Jared Birchall has publicly disputed that figure and described a different proposal.

Whether your figure or his is correct isn't even my point.

Why does the public need to be dragged into negotiations concerning your child in the first place?

Whatever issues exist between you and his father, argue about them privately. Fight through lawyers if necessary. Resolve financial arrangements where they belong.

Your son should not become the centrepiece of a public battle between his parents.

Children grow up.

They aren't toddlers forever.

One day your son will have access to every headline, accusation, screenshot and intimate detail placed into the public domain.

He'll form his own opinions about his father, his mother and the circumstances surrounding his childhood.

You once asked the world to respect his privacy.

So why aren't you protecting it now?

Whatever you think of his father, your little boy should come before winning an argument, controlling a narrative or convincing strangers which parent is right.

Let him grow up without inheriting a digital battlefield created by someone who is supposed to be protecting him.

Protect his childhood. Protect his privacy.

Sometimes motherhood means swallowing the satisfaction of winning an argument because protecting your child's future matters more than proving your version of the past.

He didn't choose any of this.

You chose to bring him into this world.

Think about your son.

Be his mother before being his father's public opponent.

text:
Democrats calling this a “bribe” or “illegal” are running a double standard they never applied to themselves. Shocking!! Lol

In the 2020–21 Georgia Senate runoffs, Joe Biden, Jon Ossoff, and Raphael Warnock campaigned on the clear message "elect Democrats and you get $2,000 COVID checks" They won both seats. Congress passed the money. The checks went out. No one on the left called it vote buying then. They called it “relief.” The only difference now is who is making the offer. 

That is the same structure that President Trump used,  if our side keeps power, here is a concrete financial benefit delivered through Congress. Legal experts quoted in mainstream coverage, including election law professors, say it sits in the same category as a tax cut pledge, not a suitcase of cash handed to a voter at the polling place. An adult who votes Democratic still gets the check if the program ever passes. That is not how classic vote buying works. 

Democrats have spent years tying government money to election outcomes. Student loan forgiveness was sold as a reason to vote for Biden. Expanded child tax credits, ACA subsidies, and stimulus rounds were all framed as “what you get if we win.” When they do it, it is “fighting for working families.” When Trump does a larger version of the same thing, it suddenly becomes “corrupt” and “blatantly illegal.” That is not a legal principle. That is team sports.

They also know the practical reality. Trump cannot mail the checks by himself. Congress has to appropriate the money, the same Congress Democrats hope to take. Their real objection is not that a president promised voters a benefit if his party wins. Their objection is that this president did it and they do not want the political credit to go to him.

If promising voters money if your party wins Congress is a crime, then a lot of 2020 Democratic ads were a crime too. They did not believe that then. They do not believe it now. They just do not like the messenger.

Why Architects Choose Premium Siding: Setting the Standard

When architects design homes that blur the boundary between indoors and outdoors, every material choice matters. Siding isn’t just a weather barrier; it’s a design statement. The difference between ordinary cedar and truly premium architectural siding is the difference between a house that looks polished and one that commands presence.

We work with Texas architects who understand that expressive wood creates warmth and character that synthetic alternatives simply cannot match. Your designs demand siding that reflects light differently as seasons change, that weathers with integrity rather than fading into uniformity, and that supports the sustainable ethos central to contemporary practice.
Standard cedar suppliers stock commodity-grade material. They prioritize volume and margin over specification compliance. When you specify a project, you need a partner who understands that vertical grain Western Red Cedar isn’t interchangeable with flat grain, that clear grades serve design intent differently than knotty grades, and that moisture content tolerance affects installation precision.

We’ve built our entire operation around these distinctions. From Clear grade Douglas Fir with its tight, consistent grain to Vertical Grain Western Red Cedar with its minimal cupping tendency, our inventory reflects what architects actually specify. Your next project doesn’t need “good enough” siding. It needs material that performs like you designed it.

Comparing Product Range and Wood Species Availability

The cedar supply conversation typically ends at one or two species. That’s where most suppliers stop because broader inventory requires expertise they haven’t developed.

We maintain active stock in the wood species architects actually specify: Clear and Vertical Grain Western Red Cedar, Yellow Cedar, Hemlock, Douglas Fir, Cypress, and Southern Yellow Pine. Each brings distinct grain character, color development, and performance profiles suited to different aesthetic and functional requirements.
Beyond softwoods, we stock a complete hardwood selection including Ipe, Cumaru, Garapa, Massaranduba, and Tigerwood. Hardwoods offer superior dimensional stability and weather resistance for projects where maintenance-free performance matters more than the softer aesthetic of cedar. Ipe decking, for instance, delivers fire resistance and durability that exceed cedar while maintaining rich, warm tones that complement contemporary design.

Our thermally modified wood catalog includes Ash, Pine, Poplar, and Ayous. These engineered products offer the stability of exotic hardwoods with the workability of domestic species. Architects designing modern homes increasingly recognize thermally modified wood as the solution when they need cedar’s visual warmth but hardwood’s performance reliability.

We also represent leading brands including Arbor Wood, Tantimber, TimberTech, Trex, and Fiberon. This breadth means we can honestly recommend the material that fits your specification, not just what we manufacture or have overstock of. When you’re comparing options with your design team, we provide actual samples and performance data rather than generic marketing claims.

What to do next: Request our species comparison chart. It breaks down grain character, color stability, and typical weathering patterns so you can make informed aesthetic decisions early in design development.

Quality and Certification Differences: FSC and Fire-Rated Options

Architects increasingly face two material mandates: sustainability certification and fire performance. These requirements aren’t negotiable on luxury residential projects or any commercial work.

FSC certification matters because it verifies your material comes from responsibly managed forests. When architects design sustainable homes, they need supply chain integrity that matches their design philosophy. FSC-certified wood supply for Texas isn’t a premium option anymore; it’s standard practice for architects who take material responsibility seriously.
Fire rating requirements vary by project type and location. Texas architects working in Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) zones face Class A fire-rated wood requirements for siding, cladding, decking, and soffits. This isn’t cosmetic compliance; fire performance directly influences insurance, buildability, and homeowner peace of mind.

We supply WUI Class A approved wood products across our entire siding and cladding lineup. Not every supplier maintains these certifications because they require rigorous testing, traceability documentation, and inventory discipline. We treat fire rating as a core capability, not an upsell option.

Standard cedar suppliers often claim fire-rated availability but deliver inconsistent documentation or untreated material they’ve misrepresented. We maintain clear separation between certified fire-rated inventory and standard grade stock, with proper Chain of Custody documentation for every project.

Thermally Modified Wood Innovation and Performance

Thermally modified wood represents a genuine innovation that most cedar suppliers either ignore or misunderstand. This engineered approach changes wood chemistry through controlled heat treatment, eliminating the need for chemical preservatives while dramatically improving dimensional stability.

Think of thermally modified wood as solving a real problem: architects want softwood aesthetics with hardwood performance. Traditional cedar will move with humidity changes, developing cupping and checking over time. Thermally modified Ash or Pine maintains dimensional stability comparable to Ipe while remaining workable with standard tools and finishes.
Projects that demand minimal maintenance benefit dramatically from thermally modified options. A contemporary home with extensive horizontal siding experiences less dimensional movement, fewer finish failures, and longer intervals between refinishing. The upfront material cost difference pays for itself across the building’s lifecycle.

We stock thermally modified products because we’ve seen how they solve real specification challenges. When you’re designing a waterfront home near Lake Travis or a modern estate in the Hill Country where extreme humidity fluctuations occur, thermally modified wood isn’t a luxury consideration. It’s the material choice that prevents callbacks and guarantees performance.

The visual outcome matters equally. Thermally modified wood accepts stains and finishes identically to traditional wood species, delivering the warm, natural aesthetic contemporary design demands without accepting the maintenance burden cedar requires.

Customization Capabilities for Contemporary Design

Contemporary architecture depends on material expression and precise detailing. Stock siding profiles don’t support that vision.

We manufacture custom profiles, thicknesses, and configurations. When your design calls for fluted wall slat paneling with specific dimensions, comb siding with architectural expression, or timber accents that integrate seamlessly with siding systems, we build it. This manufacturing capability sets us apart from suppliers who can only distribute what others make.
Your design team should have material flexibility, not material constraints. We work with architects during the specification phase to develop profile details that enhance the overall design intent. That might mean custom milling of vertical grain material to achieve specific shadow line effects, or developing soffits and trim that integrate with siding in ways that feel integrated rather than applied.

Customization also extends to finish options. Architects designing with darker wood tones, bleached aesthetics, or specific weathered appearances have legitimate expectations that material will perform consistently. We discuss finish strategy during specification, not after installation when surprises emerge.
Our Manufacturing and Supply Advantages

We manufacture siding, cladding, decking, soffits, and timbers. This isn’t a theoretical capability; it’s our core operation.

Manufacturing means we control quality at every stage. We select logs, manage kiln drying to precise specifications, and mill finished product with tolerances that support your installation timeline. This vertical integration eliminates intermediaries and reduces the communication breakdowns that plague distributed supply networks.

Our Texas location means we understand local moisture conditions, seasonal humidity patterns, and weather challenges that directly influence wood performance. We don’t apply generic national best practices; we optimize for Texas climate reality. That knowledge influences how we dry material, what species we stock, and which thermally modified options we prioritize for specific regions.
When standard cedar suppliers experience supply constraints, they compensate with whatever material they can source. We serve the entire state of Texas and all 50 states nationwide. Regional projects benefit from our local operations; national architects benefit from our supply reliability and expertise reaching far beyond Texas borders.

Supporting Modern Architectural Vision

We partner with architects, not just builders. Your design process includes specification decisions that shouldn’t be constrained by what suppliers have in stock.

When your design calls for specific grain character, color expression, or performance profile, we source it. Whether that means vertical grain material with minimal knots for clean aesthetic expression, hardwood species that weather to silver-gray naturally, or thermally modified options that eliminate maintenance concerns, we stock and manufacture solutions.

The architect-supplier relationship succeeds when the supplier understands design intent and translates it into material reality. We’ve worked with practices that emphasize warm wood tones, expansive glass that showcases material character, and contemporary details that demand precision. That experience informs every recommendation we make.
Premium wood siding for Texas projects specifically benefits from suppliers who understand Texas architectural practice, regional climate challenges, and the specific design vocabulary emerging from firms that combine global influence with local environmental sensitivity.

Why US Lumber Brokers Is the Definitive Choice for Texas Architects

When you evaluate architectural siding suppliers, the comparison isn’t complicated. We manufacture and supply the full range of materials contemporary architecture demands. We maintain FSC certification and fire-rated inventory. We offer thermally modified wood innovation alongside traditional species. We customize to support design intent rather than constrain it.

Standard cedar suppliers compete on price and convenience. We compete on material excellence, specification support, and manufacturing capability.

Your next project requires more than commodity siding. It requires material that performs as specified, supports your design expression, and reflects the sustainability values central to contemporary practice. We’ve built our entire operation around those requirements.
Contact us to discuss your project specifications. We’ll recommend material that solves real performance challenges while delivering the aesthetic your design deserves. That’s not a sales conversation; it’s specification partnership based on genuine material expertise and manufacturing capability you won’t find elsewhere.

We supply an extensive selection of softwoods including Clear and Vertical Grain Western Red Cedar, Yellow Cedar, Hemlock, Douglas Fir, Cypress, and Southern Yellow Pine, along with premium hardwoods such as Ipe, Cumaru, Garapa, Massaranduba, and Tigerwood. Yes, we stock a complete line of WUI Class A fire-rated wood products suitable for siding, cladding, decking, soffits, fencing, framing, and pickets. 7. Chuck Colson and Karla Faye Tucker – When Grace Entered the Prison

Chuck Colson reached a very different kind of prison. He had occupied the corridors of political power as special counsel to President Richard Nixon and became known as the administration’s political “hatchet man.” He understood influence, strategy, loyalty, retaliation, and the machinery of government. Then Watergate exposed corruption throughout the administration, and Colson’s carefully constructed world began collapsing. In 1973 he publicly professed conversion to Christianity, and much of the press immediately laughed. Reporters assumed that the conversion was another political maneuver designed to rescue his reputation. That skepticism is understandable, because politicians have been known to discover religion somewhere between an indictment and a sentencing hearing. But Colson’s conversion did not keep him out of court. As a new Christian, he pleaded guilty to obstruction of justice, entered federal prison, and served seven months. Grace did not provide him with a secret tunnel beneath the courthouse. It changed the way he faced his guilt and what he did after paying his debt to society.

After leaving prison, Colson remembered the incarcerated men he had met and founded Prison Fellowship in 1976. The former White House operative spent decades directing attention toward prisoners, their families, Christian discipleship, and the gospel. Whether one agrees with every theological statement, political position, or ecumenical association Colson later adopted is beside the limited point being made here. His inclusion is not a blank endorsement of everything bearing his name. The testimony is that a man identified with ruthless political power entered prison in disgrace and emerged with a burden for prisoners. The world expected him to spend the rest of his life rebuilding his image. Instead, he invested much of it among people who possessed no political power capable of advancing him. His public shame became the doorway into a ministry he would never have chosen from a White House office. Man saw the end of a political career; God opened a prison door in the opposite direction and sent him back inside with a Bible.

Karla Faye Tucker presents an even more severe example. She participated in the brutal murders of two people and received a death sentence in Texas. Nothing about her conversion could restore the lives taken, erase the grief of the victims’ families, or cancel the lawful authority of civil government. While imprisoned, however, Tucker began reading the Bible and publicly professed faith in Jesus Christ. Over the following years, observers testified to an enduring change in her attitude and conduct as she ministered to other prisoners and spoke openly of repentance and faith. She was ultimately executed in 1998. Her story reminds us that eternal forgiveness and earthly consequences are not the same thing. A murderer may receive mercy from God while still facing the penalty imposed by the state. The thief beside Christ was saved, but he was not removed from his cross. He admitted, “And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds.” Then he turned to Christ and received the promise, “To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.” Grace does not pretend the crime was small. Grace declares that the blood of Jesus Christ is greater. If Tucker’s profession was genuine, the glory belongs entirely to God, for only divine mercy could reach into a death-row cell and give hope to someone who could offer no lifetime of public service in return.

text:
MEMORANDUM

DATE: June 26, 2026

TO: DOJ, Civil Rights Division-Voting Section

FROM: @RenoResistance 

SUBJECT: Rights violations in Washoe County’s Elections

Unresolved Complaints, Washoe County, Nevada

A) Sample Ballots: In the 2026 primary, Washoe County’s sample ballots caused widespread confusion because accurate party-precinct information was not mailed to voters, encouraging them instead to follow a QR code to view their mock sample ballot online, which they could then mark, save, download, and print. Civil Rights and federal Voter Rights were violated because thousands of voters who are poor, elderly, handicapped, non-tech savvy, without use of the Internet, without devices to access the Internet and/or print downloaded documents, those who live where Internet is not provided or is unreliable, including Tribal lands, and those who simply refuse to use computers and the Internet, did not receive accurate information as is their right—with the burden shifting to the voter to obtain accurate information, if they could.

B) PII: The mail ballot return envelope in Nevada is designed by each county and approved by the Secretary of State. Arguably, the SOS has relinquished his authority over envelope security features in the process. The mail ballot return envelope violates federal laws intended to protect against ID theft and forgery because a handwritten signature is exposed along with full legal name, address, voter ID #, and precinct #, aka personally identifiable information (PII). Nevada’s policies to protect PII are weak and full of holes. No notice of risk given. No option to opt-out of sharing data with third parties. No information is provided regarding who has access to voter PII data, how such data is stored and secured, or how long their data is retained. Consumer Protection and Commerce laws apply.

C) Precinct Scanner-Tabulator: Voters are forced to violate the law; failure to follow procedure voids one’s ballot. Washoe County voters won a concession when the ROV changed from voting on a DRE to a BMD, which prints out an official paper ballot. However, the voter is now tasked with handing-off their ballot to a scanner-tabulator that sits atop a ballot box, violating NRS 292.365, which states: “no counting board in any precinct, district or polling place in which paper ballots are used may commence to count the votes until all ballots used or unused are accounted for.” Hence, the counting board must have paper ballots, not a digitized version performed by the voter before the polls are even closed. NRS 293.363 outlines directions of how to treat paper ballots in support of ‘paper-only’ counting. Nevada Voters’ Bill of Rights provides for a “uniform, statewide standard of counting and recounting votes…” Other ballots (mail, provisional) have a ballot box whereas the “regular” ballot cast at the polls is scanned by the voter and then placed into a ballot box—clearly an inconsistent act of “counting” covered by NRS 293.2546(10). In addition, there is no screen image or audit trail print-out to prove to the voter that their ballot was accurately recorded by the precinct scanner-tabulator. The solution is so simple: remove the precinct scanner-tabulator and offer a standard ballot box instead.

text:
THE SUPPLIER VERIFICATION SYSTEM — My 5-minute checklist that has prevented every scam in 6 months and 23 orders.

Before I send a dollar to any supplier, I run the same 5-minute check every time. I haven't lost money once.

"Check 1: Verified Supplier badge. This means a third-party inspection firm — SGS, Bureau Veritas, or TÜV — physically visited the factory, confirmed it exists, verified the business license, and checked production capacity. I only buy from Verified Suppliers. Non-negotiable."

"Check 2: Years on the platform. Minimum 3 years. My sweet spot is 5+ years. Scammers don't maintain detailed supplier profiles for 5 years. Established factories do."

"Check 3: Transaction history. I look for consistent order volume — not zero transactions and not suspiciously perfect numbers. A factory with 50–500 completed transactions over 3+ years is legitimate. A factory with zero transactions is a risk I don't take."

"Check 4: Response speed and quality. I message 3–5 suppliers with the same question. The ones that respond within 12 hours with detailed, specific answers — not copy-paste templates — make my shortlist. Slow or vague responses signal disorganization."

"Check 5: Real factory photos. I look for production floor images — machines, workers, assembly lines, quality control stations. If every photo is a polished studio shot or a 3D render with no factory context, it could be a trading company — not a factory. Trading companies add a middleman layer. I want to buy from the source."

"Check 6: Video verification. I ask every shortlisted supplier for a 60-second real-time video of their production line making my specific product — not a generic factory tour. In 2026, Alibaba also offers Verified Factory Video Audits. Suppliers who have completed one have a walkthrough video you can watch before ordering."

text:
ONE YEAR AFTER CHARLIE KIRK WAS MURDERED BY TYLER ROBINSON THE WHEELS OF JUSTICE HAVE BEGUN TO TURN.

One year ago today Charlie Kirk was murdered in front of a crowd at Utah Valley University. He was thirty one. He was answering questions. A single shot from a rooftop across campus ended it. His widow Erika and their children are living with that hole every day. So is the country that watched it happen in public.

The internet filled the vacuum with garbage. Mystery second shooters. Staged footage. Secret handlers. Fake mugshots. A year later the actual case file has done what conspiracy pages never do. It went to court.

Tyler James Robinson is twenty three. He turned himself in the day after the shooting. On September 1 Judge Tony Graf in Provo bound him over for trial on all seven counts and kept the death penalty on the table. Robinson pleaded not guilty through his lawyer. That is not a rumor. That is a probable cause ruling after months of evidence, argument, and a defense team that tried and failed to knock the capital charge out.

The seven counts are aggravated murder, felony discharge of a firearm causing serious bodily injury, two counts of obstruction of justice, two counts of witness tampering, and a violent offense committed in the presence of a child. 

Prosecutors say he fired into an open air event of about three thousand people from more than four hundred feet away. The judge found enough evidence that the shot put other people, including children near the tent, at risk of death. That risk is the aggravator that makes this a capital case instead of ordinary murder. 

Ordinary murder in Utah is fifteen years to life. Aggravated murder is death, life without parole, or a long term of years. Utah still allows a firing squad if a jury returns death.

What happens next is unglamorous and real. Next hearing is October 23. A trial date may be set then. After that comes discovery fights, jury selection in a case the whole country has already tried on social media, a guilt phase, and if there is a conviction on the capital count a separate penalty phase. 

The state still has to prove every element beyond a reasonable doubt. The defense will attack forensics, motive, and the risk to bystanders. None of that is a second shooter. Their own lawyers have not offered another killer. They fought to keep him off death row. That is what a real defense looks like.

If you are still selling a deep state plot, sit down. 

He surrendered. 

A Utah judge looked at the state’s evidence in the light the law requires and sent every count to a jury. Kirk’s family called that an important step toward justice.

Conspiracy content does not have to face a preliminary hearing. Tyler Robinson does.

Honor Kirk by telling the truth about the case. Stop feeding the circus that treats a murdered father like a content drop.

text:
On Tuesday, the Purcellville Town Council met to conduct the business of the town.

It was a long one.

Here's what happened.

- - - - -

6A — Proposed Amendments to Town Code Chapter 82 and Master Tax and Fee Schedule

Staff recommended adopting Ordinance 26-09-01, which modernizes sections of Chapter 82 that hadn't been touched since 1977. The updates cover water service connections, cross-connection and backflow prevention, sewer use, and industrial pretreatment, bringing the code in line with current state waterworks regulations, the Clean Water Act, and new PFAS sampling requirements from recent Virginia legislation. The Master Tax and Fee Schedule was revised alongside it to reflect updated enforcement provisions and penalties. Council voted unanimously to adopt the ordinance.

10A — Appointment of Council Liaison to the Parks and Recreation Advisory Board

The liaison seat on PRAB sits vacant after Councilmember Khalil’s resignation, and the town has already solicited applications from residents to fill that vacancy. Interviews with a possible appointment are set for September 16th. Council concluded that since there is only one PRAB meeting between now and the scheduled appointment, it would be better to wait until after the appointment and appoint a permanent liaison. Council voted unanimously to table the item to the September 22nd meeting, at which point the newly appointed council member can be named liaison to PRAB.

10B — Re-Adoption of Personal Property Tax Rate.

Earlier this year, council adopted the 2026 personal property tax rates by simple majority vote. A recent Virginia Attorney General opinion stated that vote required a supermajority, so Town Attorney Robert Sproul recommended re-adopting the same rates (this time by supermajority) purely to eliminate any legal exposure for the town. No rates changed and no budget impact was expected. CM Rayner, CM Wright, and I were not in favor of the rates themselves when they were adopted earlier this year, since they don't balance the budget. However, we supported re-adopting them as the best available option to minimize legal liability and logistical challenges. Mayor Bertaut and Councilmember Luke, who had backed the rates originally, voted for them again. Council voted unanimously to re-adopt.

11A — Announcement of Candidates for Interim Appointment to Town Council

Councilmember Khalil resigned August 5th, leaving a seat that must be filled under the Town Charter and state code. The town solicited applications, and four residents came forward: Daniel Carvill, Brian Dean, Patrick Jalbert, and Mary Jane Williams. Staff recommended reviewing the applications and scheduling interviews, and Council voted unanimously to hold those interviews in open session on September 16th, with a possible second day on the 17th, before making the interim appointment.

11B — Business License Rates for 2027

Assistant Director of Finance Connie LeMarr brought the annual business license analysis, which staff presents each September so council has time to discuss, hold a public hearing, and act (if desired) before the new tax year starts January 1st. The reports show roughly a million dollars in annual revenue across about nine hundred licensed businesses, with retail the largest category. Staff recommended no rate changes for 2027, and Council agreed the revenue and the rates are healthy, so we did not raise the tax rates.

11C — Collections Update

Assistant Director of Finance Connie LeMarr gave the monthly collections report, covering the town's diversified revenue streams: property taxes, consumer taxes, business licenses, utility fees, and more. Collection rates are strong across the board. Real estate tax collections are on pace to hit one hundred percent, personal property is at ninety-nine percent over the five-year statutory window, business license revenue is running one hundred two percent of budget, and utility collections are expected to continue at roughly one hundred percent. Only two accounts totaling two hundred thirty dollars were written off all year against six point one million in utility revenue.

11D — Review of Committees, Commissions, and Boards

Assistant Town Manager Diana Hays presented the review of the town's volunteer bodies. Council made several appointments: Craig Greco to the Tree and Environment Sustainability Committee as arborist, Julie Di Napoli and Lauren Ren Feliz Durishin to the Arts Council, and former Councilmember Mary Jane Williams and Tara Forsburg to fill additional Arts Council vacancies. Council also reappointed several current members whose terms were expiring.

CM Rayner, CM Wright, and I raised two concerns before the Planning Commission votes: some current commissioners haven't completed their required planning training, and there are open legal questions about how the council currently manages Planning Commission appointments. Our position was that it made no sense to make appointments or reappointments until those issues are addressed. All other appointments and reappointments passed unanimously, but Council took no action on the Planning Commission reappointments.

11E — Amendment/Adoption of Grievance Procedure

Virginia Code requires every locality with more than fifteen employees to have a grievance procedure, and the town's existing one needed updating to meet current statutory requirements. Town Attorney Robert Sproul and HR Director LaDonna Snellbaker brought a revised procedure covering the full process.

A few hours before the meeting, the mayor emailed the town clerk asking that this item be removed from the agenda with no explanation. However, at that time the agenda had been published and it was too late for edits. When we reached this item during the meeting, he simply tried to skip past it, and no agenda amendment was ever brought to remove it. CM Rayner, CM Wright, and I objected. The agenda had been published the week earlier with the item included, the town manager confirmed it was properly before the body, and while no one was telling anyone how to vote, the item deserved consideration. Council voted 3-2 to adopt the updated procedure.

11F — Introduction to the Virginia Cannabis Control Act

Town Attorney Robert Sproul, Finance Director Liz Krens, Assistant Town Manager Diana Hays, and Police Chief Sara Lombrana briefed Council on the Cannabis Control Act, which establishes a regulatory framework for adult-use recreational marijuana in Virginia with retail sales set to begin July 1, 2027. The Act largely preempts local regulation of cannabis itself, but it preserves local authority over zoning and land use, business licensing, taxation, hours of sale, and penalties for public consumption. It also requires the town to adopt a local sales tax on marijuana products at a rate between one and three and a half percent. Staff recommended Council set a timeline for the ordinances the town should adopt before sales begin, including zoning rules for where establishments can operate, the mandatory tax rate, and whether to ban public consumption in parks, playgrounds, streets, and sidewalks. Council voted unanimously to direct the Planning Commission to begin work on cannabis policies and bring them back to Council before December 1st.

11G — Budget Amendment, 0.4 FTE Engineering

Staff asked to convert the Capital Projects Manager from a part-time 0.6 FTE position to full-time, adding 0.4 FTE at a cost of $104,783 in FY27. CM Rayner, CM Wright, and I made the case that there's a difference between lean budgeting and emaciated budgeting. The deep cuts to staffing levels made by the mayor and his allies over the past two budget seasons are exactly why the town is now forced to piecemeal positions together with mid-year budget amendments. We also noted that since the budget was adopted, the town has secured roughly seven million dollars in grant funding for capital projects, including PFAS treatment at the water plants, and that it makes sense to fund a position that can manage and fully utilize that money so the CIP moves forward. Council voted unanimously to approve the amendment.

11H — Budget Amendment, Part-Time Accounting Specialist

After the Senior Accounting Technician resigned, staff reviewed the role and proposed splitting it: utility billing and customer service move to Public Works, while the accounting work stays in Finance as a new part-time Accounting Specialist. The position would cover the front counter, handle accounting duties, and support customer service. Staff requested an additional $21,350 in funding, bringing the total to 0.60 FTE. Council voted unanimously to approve it.

11I — Budget Amendment, Utility Billing Specialist

As part of the same restructuring as the Accounting Specialist, staff proposed moving utility billing and customer service out of Finance and into Public Works, where the work actually lives. The Utility Billing Specialist would become a full-time 1.0 FTE position, funded fifty-fifty between the Water and Wastewater funds — each fund needed an additional $4,077, or 0.10 FTE, to get there. Council voted unanimously to approve it.

11J — Future Town Council Meetings and Agenda Items

A motion to add an action item regarding the special election to the September 22nd agenda passed 3-2. Council took two other votes on how it runs its own business going forward. A motion to keep the future town council meeting agenda topics item on every agenda through the end of the year passed unanimously. Council also added a discussion item to the second meeting in October to talk about next steps for the town manager position, since Interim Town Manager Michael Rogers hits the charter's residency threshold in November, ninety days from his August appointment.

12A — Requests for Proclamations/Recognitions

Interim Town Manager Michael Rogers and Finance Director Liz Krens recommended Council recognize Accounting Manager Paula Hicks for her work on the town's Fiscal Year 2025 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, which earned the Government Finance Officers Association's Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting. The certificate is the highest form of recognition in governmental accounting, awarded for transparency, accountability, and quality in communicating financial information to residents and officials. Council voted unanimously to recognize her.

13A — Closed Meeting, Real Property

Council discussed the acquisition or disposition of publicly held real property, specifically continuing talks on an offer from the County to purchase the town's interest in a property jointly owned by the County and the Town.

13B — Closed Meeting, Investment of Public Funds.

Council discussed the investment of public funds where competition or bargaining is involved, specifically Senate Bill 648, which requires the town to procure a study by a public institution of higher education evaluating the condition and status of the town's debt, infrastructure, utilities, and other significant liability risks. text:
WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN NEPAL ON 26 AUGUST

Two weeks on, the picture is clear enough to set down properly. Much of what circulated in the first days was wrong.

The trigger

At 8:37 am Nepal time, a section of the northern face of Langtang Lirung failed. Seismometers logged it as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. It was not an earthquake. The USGS later re-catalogued the signal as a magnitude 5.2 glacial collapse. The ground shook because the mountain was falling, not the other way round.

The second correction took longer. Satellite images showed missing ice, so the story became a glacier collapse. But seismologist Göran Ekström calculated that a signal that size required hundreds of millions of tons of falling mass — far more than the glacier held. Cloud-free imagery from ISRO and Landsat-9 settled it: a massive rock landslide had occurred beneath the ice. In Ekström's phrase, the glacier just came along for the ride.

This was not a glacial lake outburst flood. No lake has been identified. Where the water volume came from remains genuinely unresolved, and anyone stating it confidently today is ahead of the evidence.

The cascade

Rock and ice failure produced avalanches and debris flows, which blocked the Lhende Khola and released as a surge into the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli. The flow covered its first 22 km at an average of 193 km per hour, per Jeffrey Kargel of the Planetary Science Institute. Downstream, water levels rose nine metres in thirty minutes. Witnesses described something closer to liquid concrete than water.

It reached Gyirong Port, the China-Nepal border crossing, within about seven minutes. The customs building was erased.

Why nobody was warned

This is the part that deserves scrutiny.

At 8:40 am, with the crossing already destroyed upstream, Nepal's water-level station at Syabrubesi read 1.62 metres. The warning threshold is 6 metres. The danger level is 9.

The gauge was not faulty. It measures water that has already arrived. Against a wave travelling at 193 km per hour from 22 km upstream, that is structurally the wrong instrument.

Nepal's Flood Forecasting Division did not learn of the disaster from its monitoring network. It learned by telephone, from the District Administration Office in Rasuwa and staff at the Betrabati station, between 9:00 and 9:05 am. The national alert went out 38 minutes after the collapse.

The signals that did exist

A rapid assessment by HiRISK found pre-event indications. Satellite imagery from 24 August showed a change in the glacier surface, meltwater running visibly brown, and a crack propagating into the bedrock slope. Separately, Manoochehr Shirzaei of Virginia Tech reported in Nature that Sentinel-1 radar showed the glacier and underlying rock accelerating in the weeks beforehand.

Nobody was watching that slope. Nobody watches most Himalayan slopes. That is the honest limitation, and Shirzaei says so himself.

The toll

As of 8 September: 1,357 dead and 5,326 missing in Nepal. On the Chinese side, 43 dead and 519 missing, including 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries. No survivors have been recovered from Gyirong Port. The missing figures have swung by over a thousand in both directions and should be read as open case files, not measurements.

Most bodies have been recovered far downstream. Chitwan 355, Nawalparasi East 218, Nawalparasi West 208, Nuwakot 177 — and Rasuwa, where it began, 127. Early in September, roughly four percent of recovered bodies had been identified.

The cost

Nepal's NDRRMA estimates around Rs 400 billion, roughly 2.9 billion dollars, near seven percent of GDP. Thirty-two bridges and some forty kilometres of road destroyed. Fourteen hydropower and solar projects affected, totalling about 748 MW. Around 84,000 people affected across 17 municipalities, including more than 32,000 children.

What should have been obvious

The same corridor flooded in July 2025. A glacial lake outburst washed away the Nepal-China Friendship Bridge and knocked 211 MW off the grid. Twice in fourteen months.

The customs post, the bridge and the hydropower plants sat in a known debris-flow corridor because the Gyirong valley offers a low, continuous passage through the Himalaya. The feature that made it commercially valuable is the feature that made it lethal. A natural highway is also a natural funnel.

Nepal is now seeking grants for reconstruction and may have to accept loans instead. That is the part worth following.

text:
Independent Ireland Leader Michael Collins TD has slammed the HSE for withdrawing employment offers made to recently graduated nursing students, describing the situation as a disgrace and demanding that it be urgently addressed.

Reports that nursing graduates who had accepted full-time permanent positions at Cork University Hospital have subsequently been told that those offers are no longer valid are deeply concerning.

“These are young people who have spent years training to become nurses, many of whom have already worked in our hospitals throughout their training, and who were told they had secured full-time employment,” said Deputy Collins.

“Now, at the very point when they should be starting their careers, they are being told that those offers have been withdrawn and that some may instead be placed on a staff bank.

“It is simply unacceptable.

“The Government bends over backwards to tell us that Ireland needs inward migration to fill shortages of doctors, engineers, healthcare workers and other skilled professionals.

“And yet here we have recently graduated nurses in Ireland, trained in Ireland and ready to work in our hospitals, being treated like this by the HSE.

“It is a complete contradiction.

“We should be doing everything possible to retain the highly skilled people we train here. Instead, we risk pushing them towards other countries where they will be welcomed and offered secure employment.

“The HSE has apologised and said the original offers were made in error, but an apology is not good enough for graduates who have made plans around these jobs and are now facing uncertainty about their futures.

“The Government needs to get a grip of this situation and urgently establish exactly what happened, how many graduates have been affected and what is being done to ensure that they are given proper employment opportunities.

“I will be raising this issue as one of the first matters when the Dáil returns next week.

“We cannot continue to spend years and significant public money training nurses only to leave them looking abroad for work when they qualify.

“We need to retain the nurses we train, give them secure employment and put the people of Ireland first.

“This is a disgrace and it needs to be addressed urgently.”

@MichaelC_IND_TD

The assessment, made with “strong confidence,” is based on interviews with two former Australian special forces operators and an active-duty reservist who said they were approached to become instructors. 

The main facility identified is Alfa-Metal in Mejdeni, Bulgaria, which offers roughly €4,000 for special forces and advanced sniper courses and has advertised specifically for SAS veterans.

Alfa-Metal denies training Russians since the invasion or ever employing SAS veterans. Senior SAS sources also strongly disputed the allegations, saying the community is small enough that such activity would likely be known.

who comes to Him. God did not save Saul because He saw a useful apostle hidden underneath the persecutor. He saved an undeserving blasphemer by mercy and then made him useful. Years later, the churches were not glorifying Saul’s determination, Saul’s intelligence, Saul’s willpower, or Saul’s ability to reinvent himself. “They glorified God in me.” That is where every real testimony must end.

2. John Newton – When the Slave Trader Learned Amazing Grace

John Newton’s early life was marked by rebellion, profanity, cruelty, and unbelief. He went to sea as a young man, deserted from the Royal Navy, suffered public punishment, and eventually became involved in the Atlantic slave trade. He described himself as an infidel and a libertine, and his blasphemy became so extreme that even hardened sailors were reportedly troubled by it. He participated in a business that treated human beings as cargo and profited from their misery. There is no reason to perfume that record, soften it, or cover it with sentimental music. Sin is ugly when it wears rags, and it is equally ugly when it stands on the deck of a profitable vessel. Newton was not a misunderstood hero waiting for history to recognize his goodness. He was a sinner participating in one of the darkest enterprises of his age. Then, during a violent storm at sea in 1748, with the ship apparently facing destruction, Newton cried out for the mercy of God. That storm did not instantly make him a mature Christian or clear every blind spot from his thinking, but it began a spiritual awakening that Newton would remember for the rest of his life.

Newton’s story should be told honestly because honest grace is more powerful than polished legend. He did not immediately understand the full wickedness of the slave trade, nor did he immediately abandon every connection to it. His awakening developed over time, and years passed before he publicly opposed the trade he had once served. Some people seem to think that admitting this weakens his testimony. It does the opposite. It shows that salvation occurs in a moment, while spiritual understanding and practical sanctification continue as God’s word exposes the darkness a man has carried with him. A newborn child is completely alive, but he does not understand everything the moment he draws his first breath. Newton’s delay in comprehending the full horror of the slave trade was a serious failure, but grace eventually brought him to condemn the evil in which he had participated. He later became an evangelical minister, counseled William Wilberforce during the struggle against the British slave trade, and publicly confessed his part in that wicked business. Grace did not rewrite his past and pretend the ships had never sailed. It taught him to face that past under the mercy of God.

Newton eventually wrote the hymn known throughout the world as “Amazing Grace.” That grace was not amazing because Newton possessed undiscovered virtue. It was amazing because God showed mercy to a man who had no virtue to offer. Romans 5:20 says, “But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound.” That verse does not make sin harmless; it makes grace magnificent. The blacker the background, the brighter the diamond appears, but the glory belongs to the diamond and not to the darkness behind it. Newton did not spend his later years asking men to admire how wicked he had once been. He wanted them to marvel that Christ could pardon such a man. His own chosen epitaph testified that he had been an infidel and libertine but was preserved, restored, pardoned, and appointed to preach the faith he had long labored to destroy. That language sounds remarkably like Galatians 1:23 because the same grace that apprehended Saul on the Damascus road reached a blaspheming sailor on a storm-tossed sea. The testimony was not that Newton found the strength to rescue himself. The testimony was that the mercy of God found Newton.

SITUATION UPDATE — 10 September 2026
Gulf / Levant Theater 📷
Bottom line:
Tit-for-tat strikes on shipping and bases resumed at the highest intensity seen since April.
📷The United States 📷disabled or sank five Iranian-linked crude tankers. Iran fired ballistic missiles at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan and claimed attacks on roughly ten merchant vessels plus two US destroyers. Iranian forces also recovered a US Navy Anduril Dive-LD underwater drone near the Strait of Hormuz.
US tanker strikes
CENTCOM stated that after two days of IRGC ballistic-missile launches toward US Navy 📷ships (including USS John Paul Jones and USS Delbert D. Black), American forces struck five tankers it identified as part of Iran’s shadow oil network. Crews were radioed to abandon ship before the attacks.
•  M/T Riesco (IMO 9251822) — sunk, Gulf of Oman
•  M/T Derya (IMO 9569700) — disabled near Kharg Island
•  M/T Horizon 1 (IMO 9130456) — disabled
•  M/T Kaviz (IMO 9282041) — disabled
•  M/T Charminar (IMO 9318022) — disabled
CENTCOM released video of Riesco burning and sinking.
Washington’s stated policy is now “tanker for tanker”: any Iranian fire that threatens US warships will be answered by attacks on Iranian oil carriers. Secretary of State Rubio repeated that Iran “will lose tankers” for every attempt on US ships. Oil prices briefly pushed above $100 a barrel. https://t.co/kUtPs8TYMW
📷Iranian response 📷
The IRGC claimed it hit ten ships near the Strait of Hormuz (two US 📷destroyers and eight commercial tankers) and launched “fierce missile strikes” on Muwaffaq Salti Air Base (also called Al-Azraq) in Jordan, saying hangars and fighter-jet sites were hit.
CENTCOM said neither destroyer was struck; the ships took evasive action and no Americans were harmed.
Jordanian forces reported engaging 20 ballistic missiles, destroying 18; two landed in unpopulated areas. US and Jordanian officials said there were no casualties from the latest barrage.
Separate US media reporting, citing sources, described damage to one A-10 (wing sheared off) and light damage to about eight F-15s that were later returned to service.
Videos circulating from the area show large numbers of Patriot intercepts lighting the night sky. Some later waves reportedly faced fewer interceptors. https://t.co/mslP65Y4mC
Iran 📷 also claimed attacks on additional commercial vessels; UKMTO and regional officials confirmed several merchant ships received disabling fire or drone strikes, including one incident off Dubai that killed a seafarer.
📷Captured underwater drone
IRGC Navy released photos and video of an intact Anduril Dive-LD autonomous underwater vehicle recovered near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz. The vehicle’s shape, flood holes, short transparent mast, and X-form control surfaces match the US Navy’s Dive-LD, a large AUV used for long-endurance survey, seabed mapping, and mine-countermeasures work.
CENTCOM acknowledged the loss, saying the drone had malfunctioned more than a day earlier, was an older model, and carried neither classified sonar/radar nor sensitive collected data.
It had been “dead in the water.” Iranian officials and state media presented the recovery as a sophisticated capture of a cutting-edge platform.
Defense analysts note the hardware itself still offers reverse-engineering value even if software and sensors were limited. https://t.co/Xs3jd7zy7i
📷Assessment
The “tanker war” phase has intensified. Both sides are now routinely striking commercial shipping as leverage. US interceptor expenditure (especially older PAC-2 missiles, which take more space per launcher than PAC-3) appears high after a single night of multi-wave attacks.
Iran 📷 continues to use saturation tactics. The Dive-LD recovery, even if the vehicle was already disabled, gives Tehran a physical example of current US 📷undersea drone design at a moment when both sides are operating heavily in the same waters.
Further tanker and base strikes remain likely while the current retaliatory cycle continues.

Xi Jinping may not need to invade Taiwan. Taiwanese trust in America is declining, spending on drones is being cut, and China-friendly politicians already hold the largest number of seats in parliament, writes journalist Simon Shuster in The Atlantic.

Shuster visited a factory in Kyiv that produces around 4,000 small drones a day. Taiwan’s Thunder Tiger, one of the island’s leading drone manufacturers, produces roughly the same number in two months. Taiwan’s Defense Ministry estimates that the island needs about 200,000 drones.

Fewer than 25% of Taiwanese voters consider the United States a reliable ally, and only 35% believe America would come to Taiwan’s aid if China attacked. Trump has described U.S. arms sales to Taiwan as a bargaining chip in negotiations with China.

Cheng Li-wun, leader of the party holding the most seats in parliament, said after meeting Xi in Beijing that Taiwan and China share the same blood and are one family. Her party has blocked defense spending on drones and other inexpensive weapons of the kind Ukraine uses against Russia — while China continues preparing its forces for a potential war over Taiwan.

A Chinese attack could begin with cyberattacks against Taiwan’s power grid and communications networks, followed by missile and drone strikes against command centers, air bases and air defenses. Chinese forces could then attempt amphibious landings on Taiwan’s beaches.

Taiwan has more than 200,000 active-duty military personnel. But within weeks of a major war, it would need fuel, weapons and other supplies from the United States, Japan and other partners. China has the world’s largest navy by number of ships and would try to prevent allied vessels from reaching Taiwan.

War games identify essentially one scenario in which China is defeated: Taiwan successfully resists the initial assault and the United States enters the war quickly. Even then, Taiwan could endure weeks of bombardment, while the U.S. and its allies could lose dozens of ships, hundreds of aircraft and thousands of military personnel.

Taiwan holds roughly $600 billion in foreign-exchange reserves. But American weapons deliveries can take years. At the same time, the United States has reportedly used two-thirds of certain air-defense stockpiles in operations against Iran.

Taiwan’s president sought more than $40 billion in additional defense spending over eight years, with roughly three-quarters intended for American weapons. Parliament cut the package to around $25 billion. Almost all of that money will still go toward U.S. weapons, while funding intended to develop Taiwan’s domestic drone industry was removed.

China, meanwhile, is also using incentives. After Cheng’s meeting with Xi, Beijing offered “10 incentives,” including greater access to the Chinese market for Taiwanese farmers and fishermen and permission for certain Taiwanese television programs and cartoons to be shown in China after review.

Only 11 countries formally recognize Taiwan. In April, Beijing reportedly persuaded Seychelles, Mauritius and Madagascar to deny President Lai’s aircraft permission to cross their airspace.

Kinmen, a Taiwanese-controlled island only a few kilometers off China’s coast, once bristled with bunkers, tanks, anti-landing obstacles and mines. Today, tourist ferries travel there from China.

From Kinmen, the Chinese city of Xiamen is clearly visible across the water. Beijing talks about building a bridge between them.

People on Kinmen can look across the water and see Xiamen’s skyscrapers.

China wants them to see their future there.

In the early 1990s, Taiwan’s economy was more than half the size of China’s. Today, it is roughly one-twentieth.

text:
🔹How “Made in Israel” is powering European security

As Europe rearms, governments still buy American platforms at scale, but they increasingly turn to Israel for the systems that decide modern war: sensors, interceptors, C4I, EW, drones and cyber. Direct awards and “technical exclusivity” are locking those capabilities in even as Brussels talks sovereignty and the political relationship with Israel frays.

@AntoanetaRoussi documents the operational fact in @POLITICOEurope.

🔹@ShayGal84 explains the strategic meaning of the security relationship differently: 

“The security order Europe has not named already exists.”

This is not a contradiction. It is the architecture that already exists — and the only one that can reduce the two vetoes constraining Europe and Israel.

The first veto is American indispensability. Washington converts dependence into jurisdiction: licences, components, replenishment, export approvals. Israel’s 2016 MOU subsidised capability while embedding donor industrial policy inside its defence economy.

After 2028 the question is not what Washington offers, but how much dependency Jerusalem still chooses to buy. Europe faces the same test. Spending more does not create autonomy if production, modification or transfer still require foreign permission. A weapon that cannot be replenished without consent is possessed, not sovereign.

Autarky is unnecessary. Substitutability is sovereignty.

The second veto sits inside the alliance. Turkey remains Western enough to keep access, revisionist enough to monetise its position, and autonomous enough to ease Russian and Iranian latitude without surrendering NATO leverage. Consensus becomes constraint when coercion comes from within. Greenland and Cyprus sit at opposite ends of the same map.

Geography has already unified what diplomacy still files separately — Arctic to Red Sea. On that map, European and Israeli interests align more closely than either does with Washington’s current priorities.

The division of labour follows. Europe brings industrial scale, aerospace and naval depth, lift, space, finance and geography. Israel brings wartime endurance, missile defence, intelligence, unmanned systems, EW and integration under fire.

Europe needs Israeli capability not gated by American permission. Israel needs European depth not gated by American indispensability.

A Europe sovereign enough to defy Washington — even when it opposes Israel — is a strategic asset for Jerusalem, not a diplomatic inconvenience. That logic is already visible in Athens, with Cyprus and Israel at the core.

Gal’s test is simple: every euro and every shekel should be judged by which veto it removes.

Europe is already buying the systems. The question is whether those purchases still run through the old permission architecture — or whether they build substitutability on both sides.

Declaration lags reality. The order is already there. https://t.co/I0KMKGWaeM

text:
Dear Manong Teddy,

You are correct in thinking that we should not industrialize just to please Washington. The Philippines should industrialize because Filipinos need higher-productivity work, a thicker manufacturing base, and less dependence on remittances, BPO, and raw-mineral exports. That premise is sound. I agree with you completely. The trouble, however, begins when that premise is treated as if it already were a plan.

You ask what the alternative to Pax Silica is, and you seem to propose one. 

To be sure, a serious alternative would have to beat the proposed project on terms, sequencing, and capacity. What you offered instead was a moral ranking of industries and a historical grievance. Those can inform a strategy, of course. But they are not a strategy in themselves.

Your "alternative" has no numbers. No capital requirement for the steel plant, the petrochemical complex, the farm-machinery industry, or the power system that would have to feed them. There is not even any attempt to find a sourcing of capital. No timeline. No comparison with Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Taiwan, or South Korea. No estimate of how many hand tractors the domestic market can actually absorb, or why a country that has preached “national industrialization” for decades still imports most of the machines on your list. 

The only quantity in your "alternative" is “thousands of jobs,” and even that does not inspire confidence on its own. 

Verily, an alternative without quantities is not an alternative. 

It is a preference.

An actual plan should say what gets built first, who pays, what skill base already exists, what must be imported while local capacity is grown, and what success looks like in 5 years and in 15. 

But your column only says what would feel more patriotic. 

Steel, fertilizers, farm implements, pharmaceuticals, and mass transit are all worth building. However, merely enumerating them is not industrial strategy. It looks more like catechism: agriculture as base, light industry as link, heavy industry as crown, foreign capital only when it completes the domestic circuit. Fine as a north star, as they say, but insufficient as a substitute for the hard problem. 

The Philippines does not presently have the fiscal space, supplier ecosystem, power surplus, or engineering depth to stand that entire structure up from first principles while the rest of Asia is already inside a semiconductor and AI reordering.

That is why, and I say this with utmost respect, that your "alternative" reads more as feelings- and ideology-driven. And its badge is in the causal story that you yourself highlight. 

Pax Silica is dismissed not because its Philippine terms have been shown to be bad, but because it begins with an American interest. You imply that since the origin is impure, the project should be treated as illegitimate—even after the Philippines has rejected extra-territorial jurisdiction, and even though the site is supposed to sit under Philippine SEZ and BCDA law. The state’s own projections, which are still only projections and should be treated as such, run to an initial $10 billion, a full-build range of $40–70 billion, 130,000–190,000 direct jobs, and a large export target. Those figures can be interrogated and tested for truth or doability and risks. But they surely cannot be waylaid with “hand tractors.”

Of course Pax Silica serves American strategy. No one pretends it does not. But the relevant Filipino question should not be - “Does Washington gain?” 

It should be - “Do we extract enough capability, employment, tax revenues, technology, and bargaining power that the bargain is worth the land, power, water, and political exposure?” 

If the answer is yes, the fact that the map was drawn in Washington is not a veto. If the answer is no, reject the deal or rewrite the terms. 

Outcomes are a better guide than origins, don't you think?

text:
Another great evening with the @PMIHouston Chapter!

Last night, we heard from Jim Benvie and Ruqaiya Akbari on two topics that are becoming increasingly important for project leaders: disruption in project management and finding the right balance between AI and human judgment.

As AI becomes more capable and more deeply integrated into how we plan, analyze, and execute projects, the question isn’t simply “Where can we use AI?” It’s also “Where do we need to keep humans firmly in control?”

Both talks offered some great insights and plenty to think about.

But, as is often the case at PMI events, the highlight for me was meeting and exchanging ideas with fellow project managers. There’s tremendous value in getting away from the screen, comparing experiences, and hearing how other PMs are approaching the same challenges.

And it certainly didn’t hurt that this month’s meeting was within walking distance of my house!

Thanks to Jim, Ruqaiya, and the PMI Houston Chapter for another worthwhile evening!
