text:
When one approaches the Book of Mormon with genuine intellectual curiosity, its internal architecture quietly dismantles the casual assumptions of the skeptic. Considered not through the prism of sectarian devotion, but with the steady eye of rigorous analysis, the record presents an astonishing tapestry of antiquity, coherence, and profound spiritual gravity.

The Ancient Semitic Fabric

The Intricate Architecture of Chiasmus. Consider the astonishing inverted parallelism of Alma 36. Across thirty tightly woven verses, the narrative descends into the harrowing abyss of a soul wracked by torment, only to pivot precisely at verses 17 and 18 upon the remembrance of Jesus Christ, before climbing outward in exact reverse sequence. This is not the rambling stream-of-consciousness of a frontier orator; it is the calculated, deliberate symmetry of classical Semitic poetry.

The Natural Gravity of Hebraic Syntax. The text repeatedly employs grammatical forms native to the ancient Near East that were awkward, if not jarring, in 19th-century English. Construct states, cognate accusatives such as "work all manner of fine work," and the ubiquitous connective "and it came to pass" reflect an underlying Hebrew cadence rather than Yankee vernacular.

Intentional Semitic Wordplay. In Alma 27, the converted Anti-Nephi-Lehies are granted a territory called Jershon as their possession. In Hebrew, the root yrsh directly connotes "to inherit" or "inheritance." The text presents an organic, unheralded pun that would have been entirely foreign to the scribe who recorded it.

Ancient Colophons. The opening testament of First Nephi does not begin with modern narrative preambles. It employs the precise biographical formula of ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian inscriptions: lineage, parental blessing, personal witness of afflictions, and an explicit declaration that the ensuing record is true.

The Solemnities of Covenant Renewal. King Benjamin’s tower address in the opening chapters of Mosiah conforms in exquisite, minute detail to the ancient Israelite Feast of Tabernacles and Year-Rite assemblies. The pitching of tents facing the sanctuary, the reading of the law, the sacrifice of firstlings, and the reciprocal covenant-making reflect archaic liturgical rites long buried in history.

Archaic Forms of Parallelism. Beyond simple chiasmus, the pages abound in climactic, antithetical, and introverted parallelisms characteristic of biblical Psalms and the prophets, sustained across diverse narrators without rhetorical exhaustion.

Old World Antiquity and Topography

The Silent Stones of Nahom. In 1 Nephi 16:34, Ishmael is laid to rest at a place which "was called Nahom," employing the passive voice to denote an existing local site. Decades of research in Yemen unearthed 7th-century BC stone altars bearing the Semitic root NHM at the Bar'an temple near Marib, situated squarely along the frankincense trail where an eastward turn toward the sea was required.

The Verdant Miracle of Bountiful. After traveling eastward through barren wastes, Lehi’s exhausted camp arrived at a place they named Bountiful because of its much fruit and wild honey. Modern satellite reconnaissance and field research confirmed that Khor Kharfot and Wadi Sayq in southern Oman uniquely match every specific textual requirement: perennial water, accessible timber, cliffs flanking the sea, and lush vegetation nestled against an otherwise unforgiving desert.

Desert Warfare and Oath Traditions. The swearing of absolute oaths on weapons, the severance of arms as tokens of authority and victory at the waters of Sebus, and the solemn covenant of the Title of Liberty mirror the grim realities of ancient Near Eastern and Bronze Age battlefield conventions rather than the gentlemanly military maneuvers of the 1800s.

The Dissolution of Alleged Anachronisms

The Vindication of Cement. Early critics mocked the record’s claim in Helaman 3 that northern peoples became exceedingly expert in the working of cement. Twentieth-century archaeology subsequently uncovered vast, sophisticated cement and stucco plazas and fortifications across Mesoamerica, reaching their zenith precisely during the late pre-Classic and Classic periods noted in the text.

Barley in Ancient America. Mosiah 9:9 was long assailed for listing barley among indigenous crops. That criticism fell silent when archaeobotanists identified domesticated pre-Columbian little barley (Hordeum pusillum) embedded in ancient American sites, dating squarely within the chronological window of the Nephite record.

The Reality of Metal Plates in Stone Enclosures. The concept of sacred scripture engraved upon thin sheets of precious metal and cached in stone repositories was widely dismissed as absurd in 1830. The later unearthing of Darius I’s gold and silver foundation plates at Persepolis, the copper scroll of Qumran, and the Pyrgi gold tablets established beyond doubt that this was an honored method of preserving sacred texts in antiquity.

Subterranean Repositories. The notion of prophetic records sealed up against the world found dramatic vindication with the discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Nag Hammadi codices, proving that preserving texts in the earth was a recognized ancient practice during times of impending societal collapse.

Textual Architecture and Multi-Author Integrity

Distinct Authorial Personalities. The text resists homogenization. Nephi speaks with the earnest, introspective, structured precision of an exile trained in the scribal arts. Alma the Younger displays the passionate, conversion-centered vocabulary of a seasoned high priest. Mormon writes with the sweeping, grave editorial detachment of a weary military general. Moroni writes as a hunted, lonely remnant, struggling under the weight of an epoch coming to an end. Wordprint and stylistic analyses consistently reflect disparate authorial footprints.

The Intricate Chronological Scaffolding. The Book of Mormon manages three distinct calendar systems: the departure from Jerusalem, the reign of the judges, and the sign of the Nativity. Multiple historical threads, such as Zeniff’s splinter colony departing, enduring two generations of captivity, and reuniting with the main body in Zarahemla, synchronize with the central calendar without a single chronological rupture.

The Embedded Source Plates. The editorial voice of Mormon repeatedly surfaces to distinguish between his primary abridgment, the original large plates of Nephi, the direct transcription of the small plates, and the Jaredite record translated from twenty-four gold plates. The record keeps these distinct metallurgical and historical sources meticulously compartmentalized.

Sun Tzu in the Wilderness. The military engagements chronicled in the war chapters of Alma are remarkably modern in their tactical sophistication. Stratagems involving decoy units, multi-front encirclements, fortifications constructed of earthen timbers, supply line interdiction, and psychological warfare reflect the genuine logistical realities of ancient attrition rather than naive frontier skirmishes.

Philosophical and Theological Majesty

A Coherent Solution to the Paradox of the Fall. In 2 Nephi 2, the text offers a profound theological resolution to the dilemma of Eden. It decouples the Fall from sheer tragedy, framing it as an essential, deliberate step in the architecture of moral agency: "Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy."

The Realism of the Human Heart. The text harbors no illusions about the fragile nature of democratic institutions. It traces with diagnostic precision the ruinous mechanics of the pride cycle: how prosperity breeds class stratification, how systemic inequality corrupts the judiciary, and how secret combinations eventually cannibalize the very societies that nourish them.

Unsparing War Realism. Unlike nineteenth-century romanticized fiction, the conflicts in the Book of Mormon are brutal, gritty, and sorrowful. The narrative captures the devastating psychological toll on righteous leaders, the starvation of civilian populations, the spiritual hardening of both sides, and the catastrophic, slow-motion extinction of two great civilizations.

Universal Divine Regard. Far ahead of its historical era, the text articulates a sweeping, radical equality before God. In 2 Nephi 26:33, it stands firm against the racial, social, and gender prejudices of the day, declaring that the Lord denieth none that come unto him, black and white, bond and free, male and female.

The Historical Miracle of Composition

The Compression of Time. The entire English text was dictated in approximately sixty to seventy-five working days between April and June of 1829. To sustain such pace and narrative velocity without the luxury of preliminary drafts, word processors, or substantial editorial rewrites defies ordinary creative writing paradigms.

The Absence of Physical Reference Material. Witnesses to the translation process, including Emma Smith, consistently affirmed that Joseph used no open books, notes, or manuscripts from which to draw. He resumed dictation after meals and interruptions without reviewing prior lines, never losing the thread of intricate plots or genealogical lineages.

Internal Textual Density. Across hundreds of pages, the text introduces more than two hundred distinct individuals, dozens of geographical relationships, varied monetary and measurement systems, and hundreds of thematic cross-references, maintaining internal coherence without a single irreconcilable geographic or lineage contradiction.

The Weary Failure of Counter-Theories. For nearly two centuries, alternative explanations have been advanced, championed, and subsequently abandoned. From the Solomon Spaulding manuscript conjecture to the View of the Hebrews thesis, secular theories of origin have proven brittle under sustained academic pressure, continually shifting as each in turn fails to explain the comprehensive reality of the record.

University of South Carolina College of Nursing Interim Director of Undergraduate Programs, Instructor, Megan Honaker, DNP, RN, says, "Immersive virtual reality simulation (IVRS) offers a scalable and innovative approach to supporting practice readiness while providing meaningful evidence of clinical judgment development."

Ramapo College of New Jersey Assistant Professor, Amy Pizzulo, DNP, RN, says that successful virtual reality implementation requires more than implementing new technology. "Faculty development is essential and students need a proper orientation and sufficient time getting comfortable with VR technology prior to the VR experience." She also indicated more research is needed on when and how VR adds the most value. 

University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education Instructor, Mamta Shah, PhD, revealed that virtual patient simulations helped nursing students practice key nursing skills and that a new analytical method known as Transmodal Ordered Network Analysis (T/ONA), can help educators better understand how prelicensure students make decisions during simulations.

text:
As we approach the quarter century mark of September 11, the single most agonizing assault on American soil during most of our lifetimes don’t  you find   yourself wondering whether we have forgotten something far more important than the date itself?
We have forgotten how we felt.
For one solitary moment, I wish America could take a collective breath. I wish we could put down the political weapons, silence the partisan shouting, turn off the social media outrage machine, and remember what happened to us twenty five years ago.
The cellular networks were overwhelmed. Millions of us were suddenly unable to reach the people we loved most. Information was scarce. Fear was everywhere.
And yet, amid the dust, confusion and unimaginable horror, something extraordinary happened.
Strangers helped strangers.
People opened their homes. They offered water. They shared information. They prayed together. They searched for missing friends and family members. Nobody asked whether the person standing beside them was a Republican, Democrat, conservative, liberal, rich, poor, Black, white, Christian, Jewish or Muslim.
We were all simply Americans.
That is the part of September 11 I fear we have allowed ourselves to lose.
Twenty five years later, our political discourse has become so poisoned that sometimes  we have to wonder whether we would recognize that America if it appeared before us again.
Whatever someone’s politics, whatever their party affiliation, none of it should matter on September 11.
That day belongs to the dead.
It belongs to the families who never got another phone call.
It belongs to the children who grew up without a parent.
It belongs to the firefighters, police officers, emergency medical personnel and other first responders who ran toward the burning buildings while everyone else was trying to escape.
And it belongs to the thousands of Americans who have spent the quarter century since then dealing with the physical and emotional consequences of what they encountered at Ground Zero, the Pentagon and Shanksville.
The toll did not end when the fires were extinguished. It did not end when the rubble was removed. First responders and survivors continue to suffer from illnesses connected to their exposure at Ground Zero, and the human cost of that day continues to grow.
Memories  cannot simply be ceremonial.
They have to be personal.

It is easy to talk about heroes in the abstract. It is much harder to look into the eyes of the men and women who carried the weight of that day, or the families who continue carrying it, and understand that their sacrifice was not something that happened twenty five years ago.
Over the years I have done that We all have
All should walk at some point through the National September 11 Memorial in Manhattan and you see the enormous reflecting pools occupying the footprints of the Twin Towers. You see the Survivor Tree, battered but alive. In Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the quiet landscape remembers the forty passengers and crew members of Flight 93 who fought back against the hijackers. At the Pentagon, benches commemorate the individual lives taken that morning.
Across the country, smaller memorials carry the same message.
They exist because Americans understood something important: September 11 was not merely a New York tragedy. It was an American tragedy.
What we should remember most about that  day is simply 
remember Americans being Americans.
That is the memory  to preserve.
September 11 should be designated a federal holiday dedicated to remembrance and service. Congress has previously considered legislation to establish such a designation, while New York has continued considering its own public holiday legislation.
New York City has now designated September 11 as a Citywide Day of Remembrance and Service, specifically recognizing victims, first responders, survivors and families.
The federal government already recognizes September 11 as Patriot Day, but I believe California should do something

text:
The Universal Language of "Go Ask Someone Else"

A man in a gray suit wanders into a nighttime plaza and commits the cardinal sin of urban navigation: asking a stranger for directions. What follows is not a simple "turn left at the light" but a full theatrical production, complete with sweeping arm gestures, unsolicited commentary on his English, and a Michael Jackson reference that absolutely nobody asked for. The man just wanted California. He got a one-man show.

This is older than asphalt. The Roman Empire was obsessed with the idea of the peregrinus, the foreigner wandering through Roman territory, expected to assimilate instantly or face the social consequences of their otherness. Senators debated endlessly about what language was acceptable in the Forum, and provincial visitors who showed up speaking anything but Latin were treated as cultural inconveniences rather than people with legitimate needs. The contempt was always dressed up as helpfulness.

What makes this exchange so layered is the Borat energy baked into the name-drop of Azamat Bagatov, a character from a film that was itself a surgical dissection of exactly this dynamic. Cohen built an entire satirical career on the moment when a stranger's foreignness becomes the punchline before they even finish their sentence. That instinct, to clock the outsider and immediately perform superiority rather than offer directions, is as human as the road itself.

The prank is that the man in the suit never got his directions. The guy who refused to help him probably couldn't find California on a map either.

#BreadAndCircuses #HumanNature #HistoryRepeats

text:
As a certified HAZMAT trainer I know that:

Hazardous materials (HAZMAT) response uses four distinct levels of personal protective equipment (PPE)—Levels A, B, C, and D—defined by OSHA to match specific respiratory and skin hazards.
Level A offers the maximum level of skin, eye, and respiratory protection for environments with unknown substances, high toxic vapor concentrations, or severe skin absorption risks. Equipment includes a fully encapsulating vapor-protective chemical suit, a positive-pressure Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA), and chemical-resistant gloves and boots.

For a novel respiratory virus like COVID-19 HAZMAT Level C is the most appropriate standard classification when dealing with active, known response environments.
While emergency responders like me utilize structured HAZMAT levels, hospital healthcare workers like my mother follow CDC Infection Control Guidelines which mirror Level C concepts but are tailored for patient care: NIOSH-approved N95 respirator (or higher, such as a PAPR) to filter out airborne viral particles.
Face shield or goggles to protect the mucous membranes of the eyes from droplet sprays.
Fluid-resistant isolation gown and non-sterile gloves.

While surgeons do not wear HAZMAT suits, they do use the same respiratory technology that defines Level C—specifically Powered Air-Purifying Respirators (PAPRs). text:
Alaska ranks as the single most expensive or second most expensive state in the nation for healthcare, competing only with New York and Massachusetts across federal spending data and private cost indices.
| Cost Metric | Alaska's National Rank | Context & Figures |
|---|---|---|
| Personal Health Spending Per Capita | #1 to #2 Highest | CMS and KFF benchmark data place Alaska at ~$13,600 to $14,000+ per resident, roughly 35% to 40% above the national median ($10,191). |
| Healthcare Cost Index | #2 Most Expensive | Cost-of-living indices benchmark Alaska’s healthcare index at ~130.7 (where the U.S. average is 100), trailing only Massachusetts. |
| Commercial Inpatient & Specialist Prices | #1 Highest | Independent RAND Corporation hospital price studies repeatedly show Alaska private insurers paying over 300% to 400% of Medicare rates for hospital services, the steepest markup in the country. |
| Individual Health Insurance Premiums | Top 3 Highest | Base unsubsidized premiums on the individual exchange regularly rank near the top, softened only by the state’s reinsurance program (which uses federal Section 1332 waivers to subsidize catastrophic claims). |
What Drives Alaska's Costs to the Top
 * Hospital Overhead & Utility Expenses: Extreme winter heating demands, facility structural hardening, and shipping medical technology, parts, and consumables via air or barge create fixed physical operating costs unseen in the Lower 48.
 * Small Risk Pool Over Huge Geography: Spreading specialized capital equipment (like MRIs, surgical suites, and trauma care) across roughly 735,000 residents means individual facility and administrative costs cannot leverage the economies of scale common in dense urban corridors.
 * Physician Compensation & Recruitment: To recruit and retain physicians, surgeons, and nurses in a high cost-of-living environment with harsh winters, facilities must offer substantial salary premiums, signing bonuses, and loan forgiveness.
 * The "80th Percentile" Legacy: For nearly two decades, Alaska enforced a regulation requiring private health insurers to pay out-of-network claims at the 80th percentile of billed charges. This created an inflationary floor that dramatically pushed up in-network contracted rates across both primary care and specialty practices.
 * Medevac & Travel Dependencies: A substantial portion of rural and specialized care relies on aeromedical evacuation and scheduled flights to regional hubs (Anchorage, Fairbanks) or out of state (Seattle), adding thousands of dollars in transport charges to individual episodes of acute care.

text:
Hamas’s leader Sinwar warned Netanyahu about October 7? A new investigative piece by Haaretz has turned the world upside down overnight, but its claims are shaky, contradictory, and in several places simply implausible. It opens with the dramatic assertion that UAE President MBZ warned Netanyahu in September 2023 about Hamas preparing something violent against Israel, risking the destabilization of the region. From there, it veers into far more expansive claims: Israel-Hamas talks to “lift the blockade” through a prisoner swap were allegedly taking place, a supposed message from Sinwar to Netanyahu via UAE-based Palestinian strongman Mohammed Dahlan intermediaries threatened an “earthquake” if Israel didn’t proceed to make a deal with Hamas, and claims that after the 10/7 attack, the terror group offered the “unconditional” release of Israeli civilian hostages shortly after abducting them into Gaza. Here are some thoughts and reactions to the piece:

1. It is likely true that the UAE president warned Netanyahu about intelligence gathered by Emirati services and figures close to Abu Dhabi, including Dahlan, who had maintained contacts with Hamas for years before October 7 after the group reconciled with the controversial Palestinian strongman as part of its effort to counter Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas. Still, according to the Haaretz report, it appears the warning was nonspecific and sufficiently vague so as not to warrant any particular action. Just as Netanyahu reportedly disclosed his UAE visit during the US-Israeli war with Iran, angering Emirati officials, Abu Dhabi may now be returning the favor by leaking this information a month before a consequential Israeli election in which Netanyahu's political survival is at stake.

2. Israel was interested in a long-term truce with Hamas in Gaza. That was partially why it allowed monthly Qatari cash transfers to the terror group, issued 20,000 work permits for Gazans to work in Israel with plans to expand the program, and supported other economic initiatives aimed at improving conditions in the territory. However, the claim that the release of the two Israeli soldiers' bodies from the 2014 war and the two Israeli civilians held by Hamas would have led to the lifting of the blockade is simply not credible. The blockade was structured in a way that made its full removal impossible while a heavily armed terrorist organization with a vast tunnel network remained in control of Gaza. Hamas faced Arab, regional, and international restrictions and sanctions because of its militant ideology and record of violence; no temporary arrangement or “hudna” with Israel would have fundamentally changed that reality. As long as Hamas governed Gaza, a complete lifting of the blockade was never a realistic prospect.

3. The allegation that Hamas genuinely wanted to release the Israeli civilian hostages it captured on October 7 but was prevented from doing so by Israel or then-US Secretary of State Blinken is a false claim the group has repeatedly used to deflect responsibility. Hamas did not offer their unconditional release. As described in the Haaretz report, it wanted any release to occur through an intermediary who could shape the framework for subsequent hostage release negotiations, which by definition was conditional and difficult to reconcile with the chaotic aftermath of the attack. Hamas also adopted a broad definition of who qualified as a non-civilian hostage, often treating virtually any Israeli between 18 and 60, including women, as a soldier. If it had truly wanted to free Israeli civilians immediately, practical options existed. It could have coordinated with Egyptian intelligence and transferred civilian hostages to the Rafah border crossing and handed them over for safe return to Israel. Instead, Hamas quickly escalated its demands, murdered multiple civilian hostages, and held others for hundreds of days. The claim that it had no realistic way to release civilians shortly after their capture defies logic and raises a more basic question: if they were not intended as bargaining chips, why were they taken at all?

4. Approximately two months ago, Prime Minister Netanyahu halted progress on an Emirati-financed, Dahlan-influenced community planned for western Rafah in southern Gaza (beyond the Yellow Line), despite months of work by the Board of Peace and approval from Israeli military and intelligence officials. His last-minute reversal generated frustration among the Board of Peace, the UAE, and Dahlan. Given this context, the timing of the release of the Haaretz piece and references to Dahlan’s man "Coal Eyes" may reflect an effort by Dahlan and a coalition of Arab and Western actors to weaken Netanyahu ahead of a pivotal election that could shape both Israel's future and the broader trajectory of the Middle East.

5. This piece has been extraordinarily damaging, amplified across much of the “pro-Palestine” movement, the pro-Hamas camp, and circles eager to minimize Hamas's responsibility for the October 7 massacre that precipitated the worst catastrophe in modern Palestinian history. Many Israeli leftists, anti-Netanyahu journalists, and activists are so focused on defeating Netanyahu politically that they often portray him as the central culprit behind October 7, at times relegating Hamas, the actual perpetrator of the attack, to a secondary role. The article has fueled conspiracy theories that Netanyahu knowingly allowed October 7 to happen to justify a campaign of "genocide" in Gaza. More broadly, the debate surrounding the piece has further eroded any sense of Palestinian agency, responsibility, or accountability, with some even advancing the claim that Hamas effectively tried to warn Netanyahu about the attack but was ignored, forcing it to launch the attack – almost reluctantly.

6. The idea that Hamas would warn Netanyahu and sacrifice the element of surprise is extremely implausible. Before October 7, Hamas's capabilities remained fundamentally asymmetric, making the element of surprise essential to offset Israel's overwhelming military advantages. It is difficult to believe that Sinwar would have deliberately alerted Israel to the possibility of an operation of October 7's scale just weeks before launching it, particularly given reports that Hamas started planning it in 2022.

7. While ultimately a loathsome and criminal figure, Netanyahu was often defined more by caution than by hawkishness. Before October 7, many Israelis criticized him as indecisive and reluctant to take bold military action. He was grappling with unprecedented domestic unrest over his judicial “overhaul,” pursuing Saudi-Israeli normalization, trying to preserve the Abraham Accords, and struggling to hold together a fragile coalition that included far-right figures like Ben Gvir and Smotrich. Above all, he wanted to keep Gaza quiet while violence was rising in the West Bank and Iran's nuclear program remained a growing concern. That desire for calm at almost any cost likely contributed to the catastrophic negligence that preceded October 7, ignoring multiple warning signals, rather than a deliberate effort to let an attack happen and trigger a war to be used as a political pretext. His resistance to a full investigation of October 7 failures is more plausibly explained by a desire to avoid scrutiny of that negligence, potentially even criminal negligence, than by evidence of a broader conspiracy.

Consider the timing of this piece; consider who’s enthusiastically attempting to absolve Hamas of its responsibility; consider the illogical framing of some of the points being raised; and consider the possibility that while some nuggets of truth may exist in this exposé, there are forces at play very interested in manipulating perceptions of the pre-October 7 reality in which Hamas was deeply unpopular, hated, without options, and run by two psychopaths (Sinwar & Deif) who gambled away the lives and future of two million Palestinians.

text:
One of our buyers received $12,000 back on a $624,900 home in Round Rock, Texas.

That outcome gets at a question I think more consumer companies building with AI should answer:

Who benefits when your business becomes more efficient?

Buying a home involves several distinct jobs: Researching a property → opening a door → structuring an offer → negotiating terms → getting a transaction to closing. Each requires different a skillset.

At @BuyWithHoma, we organize around those differences. AI supports research and analysis. Local specialists handle showings. Licensed brokers review offers and negotiate. Closing coordinators manage paperwork and deadlines.

There’s real operational work in making that feel like one coherent service. Every handoff needs an owner. Buyers need to know where things stand without chasing five people for an update.

That coordination is part of the product.

So is deciding where the economic value goes. Homa Credit returns a portion of the buyer-agent commission to the buyer. On this purchase, that meant $18,800 available at closing.

Companies have choices about how to use efficiency gains: improve margins, fund growth, strengthen the service, lower the cost to customers.

My view is that customers should participate meaningfully in the upside.

For homebuying, that means access to expertise, less work managing the process, and more money retained at closing.

That’s the standard I want us building toward. The customer should be able to point to what got better.

Pygmy Corydoras Care: Everything You Need to Know Before Buying!

Pygmy corydoras are tiny, peaceful catfish that make a brilliant addition to a planted community aquarium. In this pygmy corydoras care guide, I share my experience keeping these nano fish, covering tank size, temperature, filtration, food, plants, and suitable tank mates.

Often sold as Corydoras pygmaeus, and now classified as Gastrodermus pygmaeus, these little fish offer plenty of character.

Mine explore the aquarium, rest on plant leaves, and spend time swimming above the substrate, making them interesting to watch throughout the tank.

I recommend an aquarium of at least 40 litres, or roughly 10 US gallons, with a group of pygmy corydoras, plenty of cover, and enough open space to explore.

Small and medium planted aquariums make it easier to enjoy their behaviour and check that everyone is feeding, although larger community tanks can work too.

A temperature of around 22–26°C suits the setups discussed in this guide, so an aquarium heater will be needed in most homes.

I use Fluval T Series heaters in my fish room, and stable conditions are a priority when keeping these small tropical fish.

Filtration should support good water quality without forcing your pygmy corys to battle a strong current.

Sponge filters and box filters offer budget options, while internal filters and hang-on-back filters can also work well when the flow suits the aquarium.

For substrate, I prefer smooth, rounded sand when choosing a sandy setup, but pygmy corydoras do not automatically need sand to thrive.

I also keep corydoras on aquasoil, and suitable inert gravel is another option.

The condition of the substrate and the overall aquarium deserve attention alongside the material you choose.

Live aquarium plants help create cover and resting places while contributing to the tank's nutrient uptake.

Anubias leaves make useful resting spots, Cryptocoryne and Echinodorus provide shelter, and stem plants such as Limnophila sessiliflora and Hygrophila add dense growth.

You do not need an expensive aquarium light for a simple low-tech planted tank.

An entry-level light can support plenty of suitable plants, although your lighting requirements will depend on the species you want to grow.

Wood, smooth stones, and optional botanicals can add more places to explore.

I have noticed increased activity around botanicals in my own setups, where the fish can investigate surfaces and graze on biofilm.

Pygmy corydoras are omnivores and need deliberate feeding, so don't rely on leftover fish food reaching the bottom.

I use small foods such as Micro Crumb and Fluval Bug Bites, along with mini algae wafers broken into smaller pieces.

Frozen Cyclops and Daphnia offer variety, whereas even mini bloodworms can be too large for their tiny mouths.

Spreading food around the aquarium helps more fish get a chance to eat.

Peaceful nano fish can make good tank mates, and my pygmy corydoras largely ignore their Ember Tetra neighbours.

Neocaridina shrimp have caused no real problems in my tanks, although Amano shrimp can grab food and hog it.

Snails can also gather around larger foods such as algae wafers, making them harder for the fish to access.

Smaller foods spread across the aquarium help reduce competition at feeding time.

If you are planning a pygmy corydoras tank, this video walks through the practical choices that matter when building a comfortable planted home for them.

Subscribe to Glass Box Diaries for more experience-led fishkeeping guides, low-tech planted aquariums, and updates from my fish room.

Kalshi and Polymarket Compared: Fees, Regulation, and Sports Desks

              Get ready for the prediction market showdown. Compare Polymarket and Kalshi platforms on liquidity, fees, and more to see which is best for you as a trader.

I trade both desks weekly, and this Polymarket vs Kalshi guide ranks fees, CFTC status, sports event contracts, and funding so U.S. traders can pick a lane without guessing.

Kalshi holds designated contract market status with wide market categories, while regulated Polymarket us also clears dollars under federal rules after its 2025 exchange path, so the Kalshi vs Polymarket comparison now sits inside the same prediction market industry rather than offshore versus onshore.

        - Key Takeaways

   - Both venues list binary event contracts that settle near $1 or $0, yet fees, depth, and funding rails still diverge in practice.
   - Kalshi usually wins on category breadth, desktop workflows, and payment variety, including debit card and crypto rails.
   - Polymarket US often wins on cheaper taker curves and maker rebates, with an app-first flow for quick tickets.
   - Sports and politics move differently, so I always read overtime rules and official sources before I size up.
   - Holding accounts on both desks beats loyalty when the same game prints two different books.

        - Why I Compare These Desks - Kalshi Vs Polymarket

Prediction markets work as exchanges where traders post prices, not as house books that invent juice.

Kalshi and Polymarket sit at the top of searches when people ask which prediction market is better for dollars in the U.S.

I compare Kalshi and Polymarket on four checks before every ticket: spread, size at the touch, order type, and settlement text.

Difference between Kalshi and Polymarket shows up fastest in fees and how each desk lets users to trade the same headline.

Prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket both allow users to buy and sell contracts on real outcomes, yet the product feel is not identical.

Side-by-side prediction markets compare poorly if you only stare at signup credits and ignore the contract page.

Right prediction market choice depends on whether I need breadth, speed, or the lowest all-in cost that day.

Leading prediction markets still live or die on liquidity, and thin books punish market orders.

US prediction demand keeps rising through 2026 as more fans treat event contracts like a sharper cousin of sports betting.

How should a new trader start without overtrading?
           I fund small, practice limit orders, and only raise size when both the bid and the ask show real depth.

        - Kalshi Vs Polymarket: Regulation, Access, and Platform Type

Kalshi is regulated as a designated contract market watched by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and that CFTC path shaped KYC, reporting, and clearing from day one.

Fiat rails came first in how Kalshi was built, which is why bank transfers feel familiar to brokerage users.

Under federal oversight Kalshi operates cleanly, and Kalshi is available across much of the country for adults who clear age and state checks.

Polymarket is a decentralized crypto-native prediction market in its global chapter, with USDC-style flows that still shape how people talk about the brand.

For local access Polymarket U.S. is the dollar desk I actually fund, and it should not be confused with the offshore app menu.

Polymarket is also a prediction market built for fast social attention, while the U.S. exchange layer adds clearing rules that older crypto fans sometimes miss.

Blockchain-based prediction market DNA still shows up in how Polymarket runs global narratives, even when my U.S. balance is fiat.

Kalshi and Polymarket us both post CFTC-linked credentials, yet state friction can still block a promo or a market.

I read eligibility in-app every month since 2025 taught me that access maps move.

Prediction market platform choice for US users is less about hype and more about which contracts I can legally fund today.

        - Fees, Volume, and Liquidity

Trading fees on both desks peak near coin-flip prices and shrink on long shots, which is the shared math behind a taker fee curve.

Kalshi charges makers a reduced fee on many books, while Polymarket fees on the U.S. side often pay makers a rebate instead.

Polymarket offers a softer touch for high volume accounts that clear monthly volume tiers and earn taker rebates.

Kalshi offers more ways to fund, yet I still shop the live fee page before I assume last month’s schedule.

Trading volume headlines look huge in election years, but I care about volume on Kalshi for the exact sports market I am trading tonight.

Largest prediction market debates online mix global crypto prints with U.S. dollar books, so I separate those ledgers in my notes.

Polymarket tends to move faster on viral politics prints, while Kalshi shows deeper boards across economics, climate, and culture.

Liquidity decides whether my limit rests or my market order walks the book.

Best prediction market for makers is often the desk that pays me to rest size, not the one with the louder timeline.

Smaller tickets come first until depth looks real, and I bet again only after the fill confirms.

Another hedge bet appears when my side runs and a fair exit shows.

Top prediction market status shifts week to week, so I treat screenshots as stale the moment news hits.

Crypto perpetual futures on Kalshi add a separate risk lane that Polymarket US does not mirror today.

I still keep crypto deposits as an option on Kalshi when bank rails lag, but I size event risk apart from leverage toys.

        - Sports, Politics, and Contract Rules

Sports coverage matters if I live inside NFL and MLB calendars, and both desks post sports contracts that look similar until overtime language differs.

Game results can cash on one venue and miss on another when regulation time is the only window that counts, which is why sports outcomes need careful reading.

Sporting events split into moneylines, totals, and props, each with its own official source.

I compare Polymarket and Kalshi wording on the same game before I bet a single share.

Primetime depth is usually fine and thinner on niche props, so I cut size when the ask is lonely.

Politics stays open longer, and the Polymarket debate style of rapid crowd updates can outrun slow poll cycles.

Event contracts pay $1 or $0 after the listed source confirms, which is why I read the hierarchy before I celebrate a TV call.

Skipping the rules tab punishes traders on either desk.

Kalshi lists season-long futures beside single games, which helps when I want a slower thesis.

Polymarket platform screens feel built for quick taps when a lineup drop hits my phone.

        - Funding, Apps, and Day-to-Day Fit

Debit card deposits clear fast on both when the processor cooperates, and ACH remains my default for larger top-ups.

Kalshi wins if I want Apple Pay style wallets or a crypto on-ramp beside wires.

Polymarket US keeps the funnel tighter, which some app-first traders prefer.

I trade on Kalshi from desktop when I line up several tickets, then flip to mobile for live checks.

Use Kalshi when I need breadth and mixed rails; lean the other way when rebate math and phone speed matter more.

Polymarket promo code campaigns and a Kalshi promo code can stack if I am new on each desk, yet I never let credits force a bad price.

Smart ticket habit is still price shopping across books before I click.

Compare Kalshi vs the other board on spread and resting size, not on brand loyalty.

Online threads often blur international crypto books with the U.S. dollar product, so I filter those takes hard.

        - Side-by-Side Snapshot Without a Grid: Kalshi Vs Polymarket Comparison

        - Where Kalshi Fits Me

   - Wider category menus beyond sports and politics.
   - Desktop plus mobile, with more deposit rails.
   - Strong fit when I want one account for many themes.
   - Maker fees exist, so I model cost before resting huge size.

        - Where Polymarket US Fits Me

   - Often lower taker cost near 50¢ prints.
   - Maker rebates that reward patient liquidity.
   - App-first speed when news is hot.
   - Separate international crypto story I do not mix into U.S. balances.

        - Shared Ground

   - CFTC-linked U.S. exchange framing for eligible adults.
   - Order books where people set prices.
   - Binary settlement that can go to zero.
   - State and eligibility checks that can change.

        - Who Should Pick Which Desk

   - Kalshi is better when I need economics, tech, and climate boards beside sports.

   - Polymarket is better when I want rebate-friendly making and a fast phone loop on headline tickets.

   - Kalshi or Polymarket can both be right on the same night if one book is simply tighter.

   - Polymarket or Kalshi should be chosen per contract, not per Twitter argument.

   - Categories come first on my checklist, then I open the other app to hunt a better ask.

   - For politics pace I like Polymarket’s feed, yet I still keep Kalshi for mixed calendars.

   - Kalshi-style funding helps when my bank is slow, and I still check the other fee curve.

   - A single-habit desk will frustrate you if you force every trade through it.

   - Two platforms in my pocket beat one loud favorite.

        - A Final Word

I keep both funded because the prediction market platform race is about price and rules, not team jerseys.

Weekly desk choice for me is breadth and rails on one side, rebate math and speed on the other.

Pick the desk that fits tonight’s contract, then size like a trader who knows a losing share can print zero.

        - Frequently Asked Questions

   - Is Kalshi legal in the U.S.?
Yes for eligible adults on its federally designated exchange path. I still confirm state access in-app before I deposit.

   - Is Polymarket US the same as international Polymarket?
No. The U.S. dollar product has its own markets, fees, and funding rules. I treat global crypto books as a separate ledger.

   - Which desk has lower trading fees?
On many mid-price taker tickets, Polymarket US has looked cheaper in published schedules, and makers can earn rebates there. I recheck live fee pages since schedules change.

   - Do both list sports tickets?
Yes. I compare overtime language, postponement rules, and official sources before I assume two tickets are twins.

   - Can I use debit cards to fund?
Debit card options appear on both when processors allow them. ACH is still my default for larger transfers.

   - Which is better for beginners?
Either works if you start with limits and liquid games. I tell beginners to avoid thin props until they can read depth.

   - Do winning contracts pay $1?
Standard binaries pay about $1 if you are right and $0 if you are wrong, subject to each market’s rules. Settlement can wait on official data.

   - Should I keep both accounts?
I do. Price shopping across desks beats marrying one brand when the same outcome prints two books.

   - Where do promo codes fit?
Credits help new accounts, yet a bad ask still hurts. I claim offers only after I confirm eligibility and read playthrough style rules.

   - How do prediction markets differ from a sportsbook?
I trade against other people on an order book instead of taking a house price. That means better numbers some nights and no fill on others.

Utah judge decides Tyler Robinson will stand trial over Charlie Kirk's killing  

 The murder case against the Utah man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk last year is headed for trial, and the defendant could face the death penalty if he's convicted.

Utah District Judge Tony Graf on Tuesday sided with prosecutors who said they had "overwhelming" evidence that suspect Tyler Robinson shot Kirk once in the neck as the ally of President Donald Trump spoke to a crowd of thousands last September in Orem, Utah.

Robinson's lawyers tried to block a trial, arguing that prosecutors failed to give enough evidence to show Kirk's shooting endangered people around him. That's an aggravating factor under the law that makes Robinson eligible for the death penalty.

Prosecutors said Robinson shot Kirk from a rooftop more than 400 feet (122 meters) away and could have easily missed, injuring or killing other people.

A key factor in charging aggravated murder is whether the shooter knowingly created a risk of death to anyone else as he carried out the killing.

Graf had the option to send the case to trial on a lesser charge of murder, which carries a minimum sentence of 15 years and a maximum of life in prison, said Steve Burton, director of the Utah Defense Attorney Association. The judge said his decision was based on "the documented position of several individuals in and around the canopy area" where Kirk was speaking, among other factors.

"These circumstances support a reasonable inference that defendant was aware that other individuals were positioned near Mr. Kirk when he fired," the judge said.

The hearing Tuesday in state court came after prosecutors in July spent five days presenting what they said was "overwhelming" evidence that Tyler Robinson killed the conservative activist while he was speaking at an open-air event on a college campus.

The 23-year-old defendant turned himself in a day after the shooting at Utah Valley University last September. He has not yet entered a plea, and his lawyers have not offered alternative theories for Kirk's death. They focused instead on blocking the case from proceeding to trial and trying to get the death penalty taken off the table.

Heavy security surrounds the courthouse
Kirk's parents, Robert and Kathryn Kirk, entered the heavily secured facility arm in arm before the hearing at the Fourth Judicial District Courthouse in Provo. Erika Kirk was seated beside them. The family stepped out during part of a prosecutor's argument that described the shooting.

A few local members of Kirk's organization, Turning Point USA, arrived with signs expressing their support for Erika Kirk but were told by security that they could not have them on the court property.

Robinson had no visible reaction to the arguments. His mother, Amber Robinson, watched from the courtroom gallery and his father, Matt Robinson, listened with his head bowed.

Defense says others were not endangered
A "mountain of evidence" shows that Robinson was the killer, including DNA, messages with his romantic partner and posts Robinson made on the communications platform Discord, McBride said.

One of Robinson's attorneys, Staci Visser, argued that the state was trying to "shoehorn" the case into Utah's aggravated murder statute. Prior case law requires prosecutors to show that there was a high probability — not merely a possibility — that other people could have been killed, she said.

Kirk was seated on a stage in an elevated position, not immediately near anyone else, when he was shot from a rooftop more than 400 feet (122 meters) away, she noted.

"There is one shot. There is one bullet. There is one victim," Visser said. "There is zero evidence that there was any action taken towards other people."

The judge said he would rule from the bench at 5 p.m. local time.

Robinson also faces potential sentencing enhancements if prosecutors can show he targeted Kirk for his political beliefs.

According to the magazine, Hayes had been busy in retirement as a vigilante exposing the financial skullduggery and crookedness of various high-level politicians and world leaders. On the cover of the magazine we find Mr. Hayes in front of law library publications and a Great Seal of the U.S. plaque, puffing placidly on a pipe. But what stands out is the mysterious ring with the devilish face, composed of some type of blackish material, inside a circle.

A few months after this issue was published, Charles Hayes was indicted by a federal grand jury and arrested. News reports allege that Hayes was guilty of solicitation of murder. Did the revelations contained in the article in Media Bypass cause the elite to take action to shut him up? Or was something else up? What is the riddle of the mysterious ring with its curious image?

On her right hand is the blue-stoned rectangular ring, and on her left hand is a ring with a strange image, indeed one could even say the ring has a creepy and eerie image. In the accompanying article, the writer acclaims Roberts as "the reigning queen of Hollywood."

Albert Pike, former Sovereign Grand Commander of the Scottish Rite Masons, wrote in Morals and Dogma that the pentagram (pentacle, cabalistic star) on this ring "carries with it the power of commanding the spirits."

Use it, he instructed, to "bind the demons of the air, the spirits of fire, the spectres of water, and the ghosts of the earth." Note that the star atop the ring is encircled by the Oroboros serpent.

text:
🚨BREAKING NEWS IN BROMLEY UK⚔️

Four men stabbed on Bromley High Street this afternoon. One critical. Seven arrested. Air ambulance, fire brigade, an advanced paramedic, the road shut from Ringers Road to Ethelbert Road.

Eyewitnesses described a machete gang running down the high street at quarter past two on a Thursday.

The Met's statement adds that there is no wider threat to the public.

Seven men. Machetes. A shopping street. In daylight.

No wider threat.

Now, the descriptions.

There are none. Seven men in custody and the public has been given precisely nothing to work with, so I am going to have to speculate, which I will do responsibly and with an open mind.

Was it the Scots? Historically the most credible candidate. Long tradition of edged weapons, documented grievances going back to 1296, and a well-established habit of coming south in numbers. Motive, means, and centuries of practice.

The Irish? Also plausible. Considerable back catalogue. Though one notes the modern Irish have generally preferred devices with timers, which suggests a change in methodology that would require explanation.

Vikings? Bromley is only twelve miles from the Thames, and they have form. If they have resumed operations, Britain has bigger problems than a high street.

The Cornish? Watch them. Nobody ever watches them.

Leprechauns? I raise it only because the description released by the authorities fits. Small, fast, notoriously difficult to detain, and if seven are currently in custody, somebody in that station is about to be offered a deal involving gold.

I cannot rule any of it out, because nothing has been ruled in.

And here is the actual receipt.

Britain banned machetes and zombie-style knives in September 2024. It is a criminal offence to possess one in public and has been for two years.

Seven men had them on a high street this afternoon anyway.

Which tells you what a ban is worth against people who were never going to read it, and why a country that arrests thirty-three people a day over things they typed still cannot keep blades off Bromley High Street.

The four men in hospital would have preferred the enforcement went the other way round.

Hon. Gary Stein September 9, 2026 United States District Court, Southern District of New York
Re: Northwest Biotherapeutics, Inc. v. Citadel Securities LLC, et al., No. 1:22-cv-10185— Defendants’ Letter Regarding Documents Confirming the Statements in Defendants’ Declarations
Dear Judge Stein:
We write on behalf of all Defendants pursuant to the Court’s August 27, 2026 Order (ECF 326) concerning the documents Defendants have produced, or are willing to produce, to confirm the statements made in Defendants’ declarations.
As set forth in the declarations, no Defendant used algorithms to trade NWBO stock. With respect to the trading at issue, the declarations confirm that it was overwhelmingly on behalf of clients, explain how it was conducted, and confirm that no algorithm or source code of any Defendant altered the timing, price, quantity, side, or other substantive terms of client orders that were displayed in the market. The declarations further explain that the limited trading that was not on behalf of clients was directed by individual employees and confirm that this trading also did not use algorithms.
Contrary to NWBO’s statements at the hearing, see ECF 327 at 28:12-16, the client-trading nature of the NWBO orders is not a new characterization. Defendants raised it repeatedly, and have explained that “Defendants are market makers and broker-dealers that frequently trade on behalf of clients” and that “it is the clients that set the terms of those orders,” ECF 86 at 16, 24; see also ECF 115 at 14, 21-23; ECF 124 at 13-15; ECF 156 at 5. The trading data Defendants produced to NWBO months ago confirm that the trading is overwhelmingly on behalf of clients rather than on behalf of Defendants’ own proprietary accounts.
Defendants’ confirmatory productions or planned productions are set forth on a per- Defendant basis in further detail below. With respect to algorithms, firms do not typically create records regarding the tools they have not deployed for a given security, and the absence of records concerning the use of algorithms to trade NWBO further corroborates that Defendants did not use algorithms to trade NWBO stock. Defendants remain willing to address any residual questions through the depositions contemplated by the Court’s order, targeted interrogatories, or stipulations.
Citadel Securities LLC
Citadel Securities filed the Supplemental Declaration of Dan Yara, Citadel Securities’ Head of Client Trading Operations, who is responsible for overseeing the electronic trading systems through which Citadel Securities receives, routes, and executes orders (the “Supplemental Yara Declaration”). The Supplemental Yara Declaration states that Citadel Securities did not use algorithms to trade NWBO and that over 95% of the trading was on behalf of clients rather than Citadel Securities’ proprietary trading. See Supp. Yara Decl. ¶¶ 5, 8, 34, 41. As Mr. Yara explains, although Citadel Securities uses algorithms to trade certain other, non-OTC securities, it did not use any algorithms for trading in NWBO.
Confirming Mr. Yara’s statements, Citadel Securities so stated in its sworn responses to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories, served November 5, 2025. See ECF 324-2 at 17, 27. Citadel

Case 1:22-cv-10185-GHW-GS Document 341 Filed 09/09/26 Page 2 of 6
Securities has also produced internal order-level trading data identifying whether the order was a client or proprietary order, together with the order’s complete lifecycle from placement to disposition, as well as trading data from FINRA and OTC Link. Citadel Securities’ internal trading data—produced in April 2026—shows that over 95% of Citadel Securities’ trading in NWBO during the alleged spoofing episodes at issue in this litigation was on behalf of clients; the limited remainder was conducted by Citadel Securities’ individual traders.
Citadel Securities searched for and produced documents concerning Citadel Securities’ compliance programs, policies, and practices pertaining to spoofing of NWBO shares. It also searched for communications related to algorithms or code used to trade NWBO stock, and located no such communications. Citadel Securities also searched for documents describing how it traded securities on OTC Link. Citadel Securities does not, in the ordinary course, create documents detailing how its OTC trading occurs. Trading on OTC Link represents only a small part of Citadel Securities’ broader equities business, which is conducted primarily on exchanges such as Nasdaq and the NYSE. Given the limited role of OTC Link trading within its broader equities business, Citadel Securities located no documentation describing how it trades securities on OTC Link.
G1 Execution Services LLC
G1 Execution Services LLC (“G1X”) filed the Declaration of Brian Rorke (“Rorke Declaration”). Brian Rorke is Chief Compliance Officer at G1X, and is responsible for implementing and maintaining G1X’s compliance program. The Rorke Declaration states that G1X did not use algorithms to trade NWBO. See Rorke Decl. ¶¶ 4, 22.
G1X also stated in its sworn response to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories, served on
November 5, 2025, that it did not use algorithms to trade NWBO stock, which supports the Rorke Declaration. See ECF 324-2 at 44-45. G1X produced available documents from OTC Link of orders and trades in NWBO shares for the specified days of alleged G1X spoofing episodes that remain in the case. G1X also produced all available internal order and execution data showing that all but one of the trades were client orders. As explained in the Rorke Declaration, even the one trade that was not a client order did not involve the use of algorithms.
G1X searched for and produced documents concerning G1X’s compliance programs, policies, and practices pertaining to spoofing of NWBO shares. It also searched for communications related to algorithms used to trade NWBO stock, and located no such communications.
GTS Securities LLC
GTS Securities LLC (“GTS”) filed the Declaration of Joe Pleffner, the Head of Wholesale
Market Making and a Principal at GTS, who is responsible for overseeing the trading desk and traders who facilitate GTS’ Wholesale Market Making line of business, which provides liquidity in over-the-counter securities like NWBO. In his Declaration, Mr. Pleffner states that GTS did not use algorithms to trade NWBO.
Confirming Mr. Pleffner’s statements that GTS did not use algorithms to trade NWBO, GTS so stated in its sworn responses to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories, served November 5, 2025. See ECF 324-2 at 56, 66-68. Further, GTS has produced internal compliance materials that draw a distinction between “algorithms” and “order handling systems.” Those compliance materials also note that GTS’ Wholesale Market Making team may provide automated or manual

order execution in OTC securities like NWBO. Additionally, GTS searched for communications related to algorithms or code used to trade NWBO stock, and located no such communications.
GTS also produced internal trade execution data showing that the vast majority of GTS’ purchases in NWBO on the dates of purported “Executing Purchases” that were effected during the “Baiting Periods,” involved trades effected to facilitate the execution of client orders. Those data include columns denoting related client information.
Instinet LLC
Instinet LLC (“Instinet”) filed the Declaration of Mark Francini (the “Francini Decl.”), Instinet’s Co-Head of Sales and Trading Supervision, who is responsible for supervising the review of trading activity effected through Instinet. The Francini Decl. states that “Instinet did not engage in any proprietary trading of NWBO during the Relevant Period using any algorithm;” “No Instinet algorithm was used in the Remaining Instinet Alleged Spoofs. Any source code of Instinet which was used did not alter or affect the timing, price, volume, or any other characteristic of the client’s orders in the Remaining Instinet Alleged Spoofs.” Id. at ¶¶ 4-5.
Confirming Mr. Francini’s statements, Instinet so stated in its sworn responses to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories, served November 5, 2025. See ECF 324-2 at 74, 88-92. Instinet has also produced internal trading data identifying whether the order used any algorithm or was simply routed as a client directed order (which was reflected by a “G-” in the “route” data field).
Instinet searched for communications related to any algorithms used to trade NWBO stock and located no such communications.
Lime Trading Corp.
As stated in the Declaration of Lime Trading’s Chief Technology Officer, Sergey Bolberov (“Bolberov Declaration”), Lime Trading is an agency-only broker and has never traded NWBO securities for its own account, much less used any algorithms to do so. Lime Trading also does not offer algorithms for trading over-the-counter securities, including NWBO.
The statements in the Bolberov Declaration are supported by Lime Trading’s response to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories which states that Lime Trading did not use algorithms to trade NWBO. See ECF 324-2 at 109-110. Lime Trading also searched for and produced documents pertaining to compliance as well as Lime Trading’s policies and procedures, including Lime Trading’s Compliance and Written Supervisory Policies and Procedures Manual (LIME_0000000007), which further support the statements made in the Bolberov Declaration pertaining to Lime Trading’s role as an agency-only firm that provides DMA access to its clients. See, e.g., LIME_0000000136 (“As a ‘broker/agent’ (executing orders on an ‘agency’ basis for customers on an exchange or in the OTC market), the Firm is compensated via commissions on customer trades.”); LIME_0000000181 (“SPC [Score Priority Corp. d/b/a Lime Trading] is an agency only broker dealer that provides its customers with technology and access to the markets”); LIME_0000000182 (“SPC is an agency only brokerage firm that provides connectivity for others (our clients) to the markets under our exchange membership”). The internal order-level trading data produced by Lime Trading (LIME_0000000190) also reflects that all of Lime Trading’s activity in NWBO during the alleged spoofing episodes at issue in this litigation was made by Lime Trading’s clients, not Lime Trading, and that none of these trades were routed using a Lime Trading algorithm. See, e.g., columns AB and AC reflecting empty “Algo Parent ID” and
3

Case 1:22-cv-10185-GHW-GS Document 341 Filed 09/09/26 Page 4 of 6
“Algo Strategy” fields. Finally, Lime Trading conducted a search for documents pertaining to algorithms or code used to trade NWBO stock—including by running search strings proposed by Plaintiff containing words like “algorithm*,” “high frequency,” “HFT,” and “Sungard,” which located no responsive, non-privileged documents.
Virtu Americas LLC
Virtu filed the Declaration of Robert Verderese, the head of cash trading at Virtu who oversees a team of more than a dozen traders, including eight traders who specifically trade in over-the-counter securities. Mr. Verderese confirms Virtu did not engage in any proprietary algorithmic trading of NWBO during the relevant time period, and that Virtu did not use any algorithm or source code that altered or affected the timing, price, volume, or any other characteristic of Virtu’s client orders in NWBO.
Consistent with the statements in the Declaration of Robert Verderese, Virtu’s sworn responses to NWBO’s first set of interrogatories, which it served on November 5, 2025, stated that “it did not use any automated trading strategy or Algorithm to trade NWBO during the Relevant Period.” See ECF 324-2 at 122-123, 132-133. Virtu has also produced internal order-level trading data identifying whether the order was a client or proprietary order, as well as trading data from OTC Link. Virtu’s internal trading data—produced in April 2026—shows that most of Virtu’s trading in NWBO during the alleged spoofing episodes at issue in this litigation was on behalf of clients.
Virtu searched for documents and communications concerning its trading of OTC securities generally, as well as NWBO stock in particular, and produced responsive custodial emails as well as non-custodial compliance- and training-related materials as well as NWBO- specific order and trade data. Virtu also conducted targeted searches for documents and information concerning any automated trading strategy or algorithm allegedly used by Virtu to trade NWBO stock during the relevant period, including by performing a NWBO-related keyword search through the source code underlying the order routing and management system that Virtu uses for OTC securities, and located no such documents. Virtu is also going to produce its Order Handling and Execution Protocol, which provides a comprehensive description of how Virtu conducts trading in both OTC and NMS securities, including the automation that Virtu utilizes to facilitate routing and handling client orders.

Getting ready for a VA appointment? VA may send you a health questionnaire, via BHL-Screener, to help determine your eligibility for certain national health initiatives and to ensure that you get the right services. 

The BHL-Screener, formally e-screening, streamlines the collection and processing of Clinical Reminder questionnaires by automating Veteran outreach, response capture, CPRS Progress Note generation, and when applicable, completion of the Clinical Reminder. It reduces staff workload, minimizes variability in how questions are asked, and enables Veterans to complete important screenings before their appointments, thereby giving their primary care physician a more complete picture of the Veteran’s medical issues.

BHL Touch, a VA-approved web-based tool supporting measurement-based mental health care, now offers a new mode for Veterans to complete assessments anytime using their own device, in addition to traditional iPad entry in the office. This allows Veterans to receive and answer questions in advance of appointments, increasing the time they have with their primary care physician and reducing the time Veterans spend filling out paperwork when they arrive for their appointment. 

This new feature allows providers to text or email a secure link to a Veteran for convenient completion from anywhere. When the requested assessments are completed, the provider is immediately notified via email, and they can then review the results, track the patient’s progress over time, and seamlessly upload them to the electronic health record.

The benefits of this technology include:
•expanded implementation of MBC
•more accurate and efficient documentation of care
increased overall patient and provider satisfaction

Imagine waking up every day carrying the same worries you carried yesterday… and knowing you will carry them again tomorrow.

Imagine that your biggest goal today is not success, travel, or building a future, but simply finding clean water for your family, a small meal for your children, or a place that offers a little protection from the heat, fear, and uncertainty.
⛺ In Gaza, days are no longer measured by hours, but by patience.

We endure hunger. We endure fear. We endure loss. And we endure the painful feeling of watching the world move on while we struggle just to survive.
💔 Families have lost their homes.
💔 Others have lost the people they love most.
💔 Children have lost the sense of safety that every child deserves.

Yet somehow, every morning, we still wake up and try to smile. We try to hold on to hope, even when hope feels very far away.

The hardest part is not only the lack of food or the harsh conditions. It is watching your dreams come to a stop. It is seeing the simple things that once felt ordinary become impossible wishes.

TURKISH CYPRIOT AND TURKISH REACTIONS: "YOU WILL REGRET IT"

The reaction from the Turkish Cypriot north and Ankara has been sharp. TRNC Foreign Minister Tahsin Ertuğruloğlu accused the Greek Cypriot administration of deepening cooperation with Israel, warning that "the Greek Cypriot side will deeply regret it". He described the partnership as a "dirty alliance against the Turks" and linked it to what he called "shared ideological ambitions," referencing "the obsession with promised lands in Zionist thinking" and the "Megali Idea".

TRNC President Tufan Erhurman alleged that the Greek Cypriot administration has granted Israel privileged use of Paphos Air Base and is pursuing a military balance against Türkiye. "If an alliance with a state that kills children is concluded by violating the will and sovereignty of the Turkish Cypriot people, I will explain this to every part of the international community," he said. He warned that any such alliance without Turkish Cypriot consent would violate Turkish Cypriot sovereignty and that "this is a futile effort. It is not realistic".

Turkish Defence Minister Yaşar Güler confirmed that Turkey is "closely monitoring developments in Cyprus, including Israel's activities in the Greek Cypriot administration," and that military readiness is being "meticulously updated" to ensure the security of both Turkey and the TRNC. Turkey deployed six F-16 fighter jets and air defence systems to the TRNC in March 2026.

WHAT THIS MEANS: THE STRATEGIC PICTURE

The Israeli presence in Cyprus is not simply a property story. It is part of a deliberate strategic alignment that runs from energy cooperation to maritime security to joint military exercises. Cyprus and Greece have become pillars of Israel's "new regional architecture," a counterweight to Iran and a hedge against Turkey. The property purchases and development projects are the visible, civilian face of a relationship that is being cemented in military protocols and joint action plans.

For Turkish Cypriots and Ankara, this alignment represents a threat to the fragile balance on the island and a challenge to their claims of sovereignty. For Greek Cypriots, it offers security guarantees but also raises questions about economic dependence and the long-term consequences of hosting a strategic partner whose regional ambitions extend far beyond the Eastern Mediterranean. The question is not whether Israel has a presence in Cyprus—it does, and it is deepening. The question is what that presence will mean for the island's future and for the wider region.

text:
“Thank you, Margaret,” Luca said quietly, his voice thick with genuine gratitude. “For defending Claire. I was paralyzed… I couldn’t believe they were actually saying those things. Thank you for waking me up.”

I looked at the young man who had just chosen my daughter over a billion-dollar European legacy. He had proven his character in the fire.

“You defended her too, Luca,” I smiled. “That’s all that matters.”

I took a deep breath, filling my lungs completely. The air had never tasted so clean, so pure, so incredibly sweet.

For thirty-one agonizing years, I had rigorously trained myself to be an invisible ghost in my own life. I had learned to expertly navigate the landmines of male ego, to retreat at the slightest raised eyebrow, to apologize for breathing too loudly. I had let my husband convince me that I was a small, insignificant, uninteresting woman.

But tonight, the ghost of my late husband had been permanently, violently exorcised from the house.

I was no longer the frightened, accommodating widow. I was Margaret Doyle. I was the fierce, vibrant, unstoppable twenty-two-year-old woman who had conquered the unforgiving streets of Lyon. I had remembered how to fight, and I swore to the silent night outside the window that I would never, ever allow myself to be silenced again.

Six months later, the bitter, biting chill of the winter had melted into the vibrant, blooming warmth of late May.

The contrast between the disastrous dinner in the Adirondacks and the reality of Claire and Luca’s wedding was absolute, a profound testament to the beauty of excising toxic elements from one’s life.

The wedding was held in a stunning, restored botanical greenhouse on the outskirts of Boston. It was not a multi-million-dollar, highly publicized, performative socialite gala designed to impress investors or secure European status. It was an intimate, warm, incredibly joyous celebration filled with string lights, wild ferns, and seventy-five people who genuinely, deeply loved the bride and groom.

Philippe and Hélène Beaumont did not attend.

Luca had sent them an invitation, extending a final, conditional olive branch, stating that they were welcome to attend only if they issued a formal, written apology to both Claire and me.

Their towering, hollow pride, crippled by the humiliation of being publicly exposed and bested by a “provincial housewife,” would not allow it. They refused to respond.

Their narcissistic arrogance had ultimately cost them their only son. They had prioritized their unearned superiority over their family, and in doing so, they had permanently exiled themselves from Luca’s future. They would not be in the wedding photos. They would not hold their future grandchildren. It was the absolute, most devastatingly poetic punishment they could have possibly inflicted upon themselves.

I, however, was not hiding in the back row.

I did not wear a drab, conservative, off-the-rack navy dress designed to make me invisible.

I stood near the altar wearing a breathtaking, custom-tailored silk gown in a vibrant, rich shade of emerald green. My silver hair was styled elegantly, and my posture was immaculate. I radiated a quiet, unshakeable, profound confidence.

When the time came for the toasts, I did not shrink away. I took the microphone.

I looked out at the sea of smiling faces, at my beautiful daughter and her devoted new husband. I delivered a heartfelt, humorous, and deeply moving speech. I spoke in English, and then, looking directly at Luca, I offered a beautiful, traditional blessing in flawless, fluid, perfect French.

The crowd applauded wildly. Claire beamed, tears of pure joy shining in her eyes. I raised my glass, toasting to a love that required no masks, no translations, and no apologies.

But my resurrection did not end when the wedding reception concluded.

My life back in Rochester underwent a radical, seismic transformation. The quiet, isolated widow was gone.

text:
The Adirondack lake house was supposed to be a neutral ground. A sanctuary where two vastly different worlds could meet, blend, and perhaps find a fragile harmony before my daughter’s wedding. Instead, it felt like a beautifully staged, suffocatingly tense theatre production where everyone knew their lines, but half the cast despised the script.

My daughter, Claire, had spent three agonizing days preparing for this dinner. She was twenty-seven, possessing a fiercely bright, genuine spirit that constantly sought to nurture those around her. When she announced her engagement to Luca Beaumont, I was thrilled for her. Luca was a kind, intelligent architect. But he came with baggage. Specifically, he came with Philippe and Hélène Beaumont.

The Beaumonts were the epitome of European “old money” elitism. They resided in a sprawling estate in Brussels, spent their winters in Gstaad, and viewed anyone lacking a multi-generational trust fund as a quaint, slightly offensive biological anomaly.

Tonight, the expansive, cedar-paneled dining room of the rented lake house was bathed in the warm, flickering glow of candlelight. The table was impeccably set. Claire, her face flushed with the heat of the kitchen and the desperate anxiety to impress, emerged carrying a massive, steaming cast-iron Dutch oven.

She had spent hours meticulously preparing a traditional Boeuf Bourguignon, using a recipe passed down from her grandmother, trying to offer a gesture of culinary respect to the Beaumonts’ Francophone heritage.

“Dinner is served,” Claire announced, her smile wide but undeniably strained.

Hélène Beaumont, draped effortlessly in a minimalist, impeccably tailored beige linen ensemble that screamed quiet luxury, looked at the heavy pot. She didn’t smile. She offered a slight, almost imperceptible tightening of her lips—a micro-expression of profound condescension.

Philippe, wearing a cashmere sweater draped casually over his shoulders and a Patek Philippe watch that caught the candlelight, leaned back in his chair.

“Ah. A stew,” Philippe noted, his English heavily accented but perfectly enunciated. He looked at Claire as if she had just presented him with a bowl of mud. “How… rustic.”

Claire’s smile faltered for a fraction of a second, but she rallied, serving the rich, dark meat and vegetables onto their imported plates.

I sat silently at the end of the table. I was fifty-four years old, wearing a simple, conservative navy dress I had purchased from a mid-tier department store. My hands were folded neatly in my lap. I was practically invisible, and I had spent the last thirty-one years ensuring that I remained that way.

My entire adult life had been an exercise in strategic shrinkage. I had married a man—Claire’s father—who was a master of passive-aggressive psychological warfare. He didn’t hit. He didn’t scream. He used heavy sighs, disappointed glances, and perfectly timed, raised eyebrows to communicate my constant inadequacy. He made me feel clumsy, loud, and uncultured. To survive that marriage, to keep the peace for my daughter, I learned to fold myself into a neat, quiet little box. I learned to apologize for taking up space. I learned that my primary function was to be useful, invisible, and utterly unburdensome.

Even after his death five years ago, the reflex remained. When the Beaumonts arrived, I instinctively slipped into the role of the silent, accommodating background character.

The dinner progressed in agonizing, slow motion.

“Everything okay?” James asked.

Walter smiled.

“Just trying to cut down to my budget.

James offered to pay.

Walter shook his head.

“I’ve spent my life helping others. It’s hard to admit when you’re the one who needs help.”

James asked, “What happened?”

Walter looked down.

“My wife, Margaret, passed away three years ago.”

“She always told me I didn’t have to be strong every day.”
